### Milestone 228 (tentative number) - DONE (`hydo report --html` in plain words: the page says what broke in the user's system, when it happens, whether it is a bug, what hydo saw and how to see it again, and folds everything for specialists into one section at the bottom; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-14)

**In short.** The page of Milestone 220 showed the summary, the schedule, the timeline, and
the diff first. The user read it as a developer who knows their own system and not hydo, and found
it unreadable: every detail was noise. The user approved two mockups: one failing run and one
exploration. This milestone builds the real page to their structure, order, and tone, from the
recorded files only. Two new modules hold the words, so that other outputs can use them later:

- `hydo/crates/hydo-schedule/src/describe.rs` puts every token of the schedule language in words.
  Each token has a sentence and a gloss for the line that explains a command ("`C=12` = cut the
  power before step 12"). It also has a noun phrase for comparing two runs and, for a fault, the
  circumstance it gives a title ("after a power cut"). A manifest setting (`knobs:`) is named with its `name:` and
  its safe value. A word that is not a token gets a neutral sentence that points to `hydo guide
  faults`. `change(a, b)` says how one schedule differs from another ("with a working disk
  instead of a disk with a write cache, and without a power cut before step 9").
- `hydo/crates/hydo-explore/src/advice.rs` maps a failure's class and what failed to a label, a
  title, an explanation, and what to do. The label is "Expected" for a lying disk and a refused
  run. It is "Expected for this setting" for an unsafe setting. It is "Worth a look" for disk
  errors, damaged files, a failed test program, a new error line, and a check the user wrote.
  For a check the user wrote, the words quote the check and say that only the user can decide
  whether it must hold. `class_of` gives a single run (`hydo run` records no class) the
  explorer's class rule.

**The page.** For one run, in this order:

1. The title, from the failed check's description and the fault. An example is "Redis broke your
   rule “every SET the client saw acknowledged reads back with its value” after a power cut, with
   Redis appendfsync set to `everysec`". A lead paragraph says what the workload had confirmed, the
   faults as they happened, and what the check found.
2. "When it happens": the schedule as numbered sentences, and the outcome.
3. "Is this a bug?": the label, the explanation, what a passing neighbour showed, and what to do.
   An example of the neighbour's line is "A second run with Redis appendfsync at `always` instead
   of `everysec` passed every check".
4. "What hydo saw": the confirmed steps, the fault events of the run in words, the restart, the
   services that ended, and what the check found.
5. "See it again": `hydo run "<schedule>"`, the gloss of each word, and the `hydo inspect start`
   command. The command runs in the project's folder when the image is the one `hydo build` wrote
   there.
6. "Details for sharing with hydo or upstream", folded. It holds the verdict, the schedule, the
   class, the fingerprint, the image, the engine, the host CPU, the hydo version, and the epoch.
   It also holds the run folder, `hydo repro`, the failure's findings and diagnosis, the full
   timeline, the diff, the checks and properties, and the versions. Nothing of the earlier page is lost.

An exploration groups its failures by class and signature as before. Then it merges the groups
whose title and label are the same into one problem: Redis's two io-errors signatures (`ERROR redis restart
failed` and `ERROR restart after the faults (redis)`) are one problem, "`redis` did not start
again after disk errors". The problems are ordered by label (worth a look first), then by their
number of runs, each with a bar. New error lines are one problem. "What held" names the passing
runs, the user's checks that held, and the faults the runs did not try. "Next" gives `hydo explore
--seeds <the next 100>`. It also gives `hydo ci accept <key> --reason "…"` with the key of the
first expected problem. A CI run shows the same cards with the state against the base in plain words ("New in
this change", "Already on the base commit", "Fixed by this change") and the accept command for
each finding.

The page finds the project's `hydo.yaml` inside the image when the image file is there, else next
to the `hydo-out` folder that holds the results or the image. Without it the setting names come
from the run's notes (`knob R=everysec (Redis appendfsync)`), and the safe values from the
explorer's fallback rule for `R=` and `M=`.

**Tests.** hydo-schedule's new test program `describe` (8 tests) gives an example of every host
key and every guest letter that no sentence, gloss, noun phrase, or circumstance
uses hydo's own words. It pins the sentences of the Redis power cut, the order of faults by step,
groups, outside services, clock points, and `change`. The advice has four unit tests: what failed
from a verdict, the class of one run, every class with every type of failure, and the titles. The
page's tests check the three goldens (re-recorded), the size bounds, that the page loads nothing,
and that its plain part has none of the words fingerprint, epoch, engine, schedule, token,
invariant, oracle, signature, class, and seed outside commands. The Redis fixtures moved into a
project folder with the example's manifest (`tests/fixtures/report/redis/`).

**Real samples.** The Mac engine's Redis runs of Milestone 220 (`disk=cut | run C=12 R=everysec`
against `R=always`, and the 30-run swarm exploration with 13 failures) rendered as a 34 KiB and an
83 KiB page. The exploration's page shows 3 problems: Redis not starting after disk errors
(worth a look, 5 runs, two signatures merged), the power cut with `appendfsync no` (expected for
this setting, 2 runs), and the lying disk (expected, 6 runs). The voice linter finds no banned
word in the generated sentences; in the details it flags only recorded data (the class name
`unsafe-knob`, the run's notes and the check's shell `echo`). The narrow layout was checked at
500 pixels, light and dark: headless Chrome lays a page out at least 500 pixels wide.

**What is left.** `advice::what_of` knows the error verdicts of a restart that failed; every other error is "The
run stopped early" with the error's text.

**A fresh reader's review.** A fresh agent that played a regular developer read the two real
samples. It found the pages good overall and named 15 places where it stopped. Each is fixed in
the code:

- The single-run page repeated the same facts five times. The title is now short ("Redis failed
  your check after a power cut, with Redis appendfsync set to `everysec`"), and the check's words
  appear once, under the title. "Is this a bug?" no longer repeats the check. "What hydo saw"
  keeps only what the other parts do not say, and it is left out when nothing remains.
- Steps are counted from 1 in every sentence ("after 12 steps, before the 13th step").
- When the failing check's command stops at its first problem (`break`), the page says that it
  reports only the first missing item.
- The `hydo inspect start` line says what it opens and names the run's folder in the project
  (`hydo-out/runA`).
- The replay command says what it needs first, and no machine-specific path is above the details
  (an absolute image path becomes its file name).
- The glosses explain `|` and `run`, and a disk choice kept without a disk fault is "kept so that
  the run is exactly the same".
- Each label has a line that says what it means and what it means for CI.
- The `hydo ci accept` line says what the command writes, where, and what CI then does.
- The links to a problem's runs open the folded details at their target (a small script), and
  the details are called "Details for a bug report".
- A power cut ("a power cut loses the writes not yet flushed to disk") and a lying disk ("a
  faulty disk throws away writes it already confirmed") have clearly different words, and a rate
  change reads "with the disk throwing away fewer writes".
- On the exploration page, the problem of a service that did not start again shows what the
  first run saw. On Redis, `redis` exited with the status 1 during the disk errors, before the
  kill. The page says that hydo did not remove faults from such a problem, and which faults all
  its runs share. The faults the runs never had are in plain words, with `--new-faults`. The
  details' table names the problem of each row.

The page tests check two more rules: no machine path above the details, and every link has a
target on the page.

**Back to the mockups' density.** The user compared the pages after the review with the approved
mockups. The mockups were more concise and concrete, so every visible line now carries a fact of
the run, and general explanations went into the details or were removed:

- The title and the lead use the run's own data. A check that reports something lost (`key k:0
  lost`) gives "Redis lost data it had confirmed", and the lead counts the workload's confirmed
  steps: "Your workload ran 12 steps and Redis confirmed all 12. Then the power was cut before
  the 13th step. When Redis started again, `key k:0` was gone."
- "What hydo saw" has the mockup's four lines: "✔ Redis confirmed `k:0` … `k:11` (12 steps)",
  "⚡ The power was cut before the 13th step", "↻ The machine started again", and "✘ `key k:0
  lost` (the check stops at the first one)". The items are named as the check's output names
  them when its number is a confirmed step.
- Removed from the plain part: the label meanings, the note on steps, the explanation of `|` and
  `run`, the gloss of a token that changes nothing in the run, and the run folder sentence.
- Each exploration card has the mockup's parts only: what happens in one or two sentences, "Is it
  a bug?", the command, and "Open this failure →". The card of a service that did not start
  again says how it exited: "`redis` exited with status 1 during the disk errors, and again after
  hydo restarted it." A command that hydo did not shrink adds one clause on the faults it keeps.
  "What held" is two sentences; the checks that held and the faults the runs never had are in
  the details.

Above the details, the run mockup has 286 words, the run page after the review had 422, and the
new one has 313. The exploration mockup has 318 words, the page after the review had 1,103, and
the new one has 380 (three cards with their commands).

### Milestone 229 (tentative number) - DONE (`hydo onboard` starts onboarding with one command; the Claude Code plugin is `hydo` and its command `/hydo:onboard`; docs/ONBOARD.md with a worked messages example that runs on the Mac engine; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-14)

**In short.** A user who wanted to onboard a message broker found no clear start in the README,
and the plugin install failed for them because they missed `/plugin marketplace add kakoc/hydo`.
The user decided to rename freely and keep no old names (2026-11-14). hydo now has one command,
`hydo onboard`, that starts the folder and installs the skill; the plugin is `hydo` and the skill
`onboard`, so Claude Code calls it `/hydo:onboard`; and docs/ONBOARD.md explains the three parts
with a worked example.

**The plugin and the skill.**

- The plugin folder `plugin/` has Claude Code's standard layout: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`
  names the plugin `hydo`, and `skills/onboard/` holds the skill in the Agent Skills format. The
  marketplace `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` lists it as `hydo` from `./plugin`. The install
  is `/plugin marketplace add kakoc/hydo`, then `/plugin install hydo@hydo`.
- Checked with Claude Code 2.1.323 in a throwaway configuration (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`): `claude
  plugin validate .` and `claude plugin validate plugin` pass, and after `claude plugin
  marketplace add` of the tree and `claude plugin install hydo@hydo` the session's init event
  lists the skill `hydo:onboard`.
- A skills-directory plugin, a folder under `.claude/skills/` with a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`,
  loads as `hydo@skills-dir`. With `SKILL.md` at the folder's root its command was `/hydo`, not
  `/hydo:onboard`; with the standard layout it is `/hydo:onboard`. That is why the skill moved
  into `plugin/skills/onboard/` and why `hydo skill install --agent claude` copies the whole
  plugin folder to `.claude/skills/hydo`. The other tools get the skill folder alone as
  `.agents/skills/onboard`.
- The skill's version is 2.0.0 (a renamed skill, plugin and command), in `SKILL.md`,
  `plugin.json` and the marketplace entry. The skill release archive holds the plugin folder as
  `hydo/`; `hydo skill update` puts the plugin folder into a `hydo` copy and the skill folder into
  an `onboard` copy. A folder counts as hydo's skill only when its `SKILL.md` is named `onboard`
  and has `hydo-min:`, so another tool's skill of the same name is never replaced.
- The releases ship `plugin/` instead of `skill/hydo-onboard/`; `hydo-agents` embeds `plugin/`
  through `embed/plugin`. The repository links `.claude/skills/hydo` to `plugin/` and
  `.agents/skills/onboard` to `plugin/skills/onboard`.
- The old name stays in four places on purpose: the salt `hydo-onboard:` of
  `hydo_build::image::uuid_from` (its UUIDs are inside every image); the comments of the example
  manifests that an earlier `hydo compose` or skill run wrote (compose-voting and miniflux, whose
  bytes are inside recorded images, lago's and libsql-replica's, which the explorer's goldens pin)
  and their schema copies; miniflux's RESULTS.md, a record of its run; and docs/HISTORY.md.

**`hydo onboard [DIR] [--agent NAME ...] [--no-skill] [--no-resolve]`** (`hydo/crates/hydo-cli/src/onboard.rs`):

1. It says what it found: a Compose file and its services, the Dockerfiles, the main language by
   file count, and an existing `hydo/` folder.
2. With a Compose file and no `hydo/`, it runs `hydo compose <file> --out hydo/hydo.yaml
   --images-dir images` and adds the `.gitignore` lines and the `AGENTS.md` section that `hydo
   init` adds. Without a Compose file it runs `hydo init`. An existing `hydo/` is never changed.
3. It installs the skill for the AI tools it finds: a `.claude/`, `.codex/`, `.cursor/` or
   `.gemini/` folder, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, or the `claude`, `codex`, `cursor-agent`,
   `cursor`, `gemini` or `copilot` command on `PATH`. `--agent` names the tools instead, and
   `--no-skill` installs none.
4. It prints the next step: `Next: open Claude Code here and run /hydo:onboard` for Claude Code,
   the onboard skill for another tool, and without a tool the three parts to fill in with
   `hydo guide workflow`.

`hydo onboard --help` answers before anything else (Milestone 210), and the main help lists the
command. `tests/onboard.rs` runs it in scratch repositories with their own `HOME` and a `PATH` of
stand-in tools: a Compose project with `.claude/`, a plain project with `codex`, an existing
`hydo/`, no AI tool, `--agent`, `--no-skill` and `--help`.

**The pages.** docs/ONBOARD.md "Onboard your system" (in `ci/vale.sh` and in the docs test's
user pages) gives the three parts, the three paths (a Compose file, no Compose file, an AI tool),
what a good first result is, what to do when the first run fails, and the worked example.
`hydo guide workflow` starts with `hydo onboard`, `hydo guide` names the new plugin commands, and
`hydo init`'s `AGENTS.md` section names the skill `onboard`. The README was rewritten on `main`
in parallel (`79789388`) and was not changed here.

**The example** `hydo/onboard/examples/messages-tutorial/`: `tinyq`, a queue of 316 lines of Go
(one channel, a log synced before each answer, a resent id stored once, the oldest
unacknowledged message handed out), which is also its client and writes `HYDO-HIST queue`
records. Producers are `parallel_driver_produce` (one in four sends twice), the consumer is
`serial_driver_consume`, and the check is `type: messages` with `delivery: at-least-once`,
`duplicates: {by: message, window_ms: 600000}`, `order: {kind: fifo, scope: key}` and
`after_ack: no-redelivery`. The setting `S=never` makes tinyq answer before it syncs. The fault
kinds leave out `disk`: a first exploration with it found two `io-errors` runs, a drain that
cannot write and a restart on a failing disk, which the tutorial does not check. Runs on the Mac
engine with this branch's `hydo` inside the unpacked 0.3.2 Mac release, Go 1.27.3:

| run | result |
|---|---|
| `hydo run "disk=none \| run"`, twice | `fp=be992f7e466b6db5` both times, OK; no-loss 24 judged, duplicates 8, after-ack 24, order 21 |
| `hydo run "disk=cut \| run C=10 S=never"` | VIOLATION `[queue.no-loss] m10 was acknowledged to process 10 at 0.727 s and never delivered` |
| `hydo run "disk=cut \| run C=10"` | OK |
| `hydo explore --seeds 1-20 --workers 1` | 20 schedules, 1 failure, reproduced; class `unsafe-knob`, shrunk in 29 runs to `disk=cut dseed=362259904816818c \| run C=10 S=never W=:p1,r50,cparallel_driver_produce,1.1.0.1802048978`, two runs `e3b769740bd36ed5`; 2 passing runs with an early power cut judged no order |

**Goldens.** The CLI and agents goldens (the help texts, the skill's paths and names), the
hydo-compose golden (its TODO comment names `/hydo:onboard`), and the explorer's identity and
corpus goldens (the new example) are re-recorded. The full identity golden only grew; the corpus
golden of before still passes with the new example moved aside, so no answer of an unchanged
input moved.

**Open.** The skill release `skill-v2.0.0` is not published (the lead tags it after the merge).
`hydo onboard` ran only on this Mac; the example did not run on Linux, where `build.sh` builds an
x86_64 queue. Claude Code users who installed the old plugin `hydo-onboard@hydo` keep it until
they remove it; the marketplace no longer lists it.

### Milestone 230 (tentative number) - DONE (`hydo report` and the end of `hydo explore` in the terminal say what the page says: the problems in plain words, how often each happened, whether it is a bug and the command that shows it again; the technical report moved to `hydo report --details`; every machine reader keeps its bytes; the README's animated terminal shows the new output from a real run; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-14)

**Why.** After Milestone 228 the web page spoke to a developer who does not know hydo, and the
terminal did not. `hydo explore` ended with a JSON line of timings and counts, and `hydo report`
printed `report.md`: tables of classes and signatures, fingerprints, and the property table.

**`hydo report`.** For an exploration it now prints the problems as the page shows them, from the
same code. `htmlreport::exploration_story` computes the title, the problems ranked by attention,
what held, and the next commands once. `exploration_page` writes HTML from it, and
`htmlreport/text.rs` writes the terminal's words. The text has a headline with the failed runs,
the fault kinds tried, and how the failures replayed. For each problem it gives the title, the
label and the runs, what happens, "Is it a bug?" and the command. Then come "What held" and the
next commands. Sentences wrap at 80 columns and commands never wrap. `hydo report --details`
prints the old text, `report.md`'s. A run directory and an exploration that has not finished
print what they printed before.

**The end of `hydo explore`.** When stdout is a terminal, `hydo explore` ends with two or three
lines, for example `hydo ran your system 30 times: 13 failed, in 3 different ways. Each failing
run failed again the same way when hydo replayed it.` and `See them: hydo report (as one web
page: hydo report --html)`. The count of ways is the report's count of problems, because both come
from the story. When stdout is not a terminal, or with `--json`, it ends as before with the
summary line and `hydo: report: ...`. `hydo_explore::Env` has `plain_end`, and only `hydo
explore` in a terminal sets it. The `hydo-explore` program, `hydo ci run` (through
`delegated::explore_with(.., false)`) and every test keep the summary line.

**Machine readers kept.** They were found by searching the tree:

- `exploration.json`, `events.jsonl`, `report.md` and `result.json` are unchanged; the scripts
  (for example `hv/kvm/smp/turns-check.sh`) read `exploration.json`;
- the summary line on stdout, which hydo-explore's `tests/fake_engine.rs` records as
  `summary.txt`, is unchanged outside a terminal;
- `hydo ci run` and its `report.md` and `junit.xml` are unchanged;
- the skill tells an agent to use the guide's commands and parses no output; its text did not
  change, so its version stays.

**Proof that no other answer moved.**

- The pages of `hydo report --html` before and after are byte-identical for 11 recorded inputs:
  the Redis explorations and runs of Milestone 228, the scripted exploration, two CI runs, the CLI
  test's two exploration fixtures, two Lago explorations and two older explorations. `hydo report
  --details` printed exactly the old `hydo report` text for all of them.
- The CLI golden changed only in its four `hydo report` answers. It gained the two `hydo report
  --details` steps, whose answers equal the old `hydo report` answers byte for byte.
- The explorer's `identity::` and `corpus::` goldens and the scripted-engine scenarios passed
  without a change.

**Tests.** `htmlreport::tests::the_terminal_says_what_the_page_says` checks the scripted
exploration's text: the page's title and problems in the page's order, each command, what held,
the next commands, and no hydo word outside the commands. Its lines fit 80 columns apart from
commands. A directory other than the default one is named in the commands. The test also checks
the end of `hydo explore`. The golden is `tests/golden/report/exploration.txt`.

**A real run.** On this Mac the Redis example ran as a repository with its `hydo/` folder, with
this branch's `hydo` in the unpacked 0.3.2 Mac release. `hydo onboard` found the folder, left it
as it was and installed the skill. `hydo build` made the image `fba2c11e6a371d8b`, Milestone
228's. `hydo explore --seeds 1-30 --strategy swarm` ran in a terminal (`script`) in 35 s. It found
13 failures, all reproduced, with Milestone 228's three minimal schedules, and ended with the two
lines above. `hydo report` then printed:

```text
hydo found 3 problems in your Redis setup (13 of 30 runs failed)
Faults tried: a faulty disk, crashes, power cuts, network faults and disk
errors. Each failing run failed again the same way when hydo replayed it.

1. redis did not start again after disk errors
   Worth a look, 5 of 30 runs.
   redis exited with status 1 during the disk errors, and again after hydo
   restarted it. The command also keeps this run's network faults and crashes.
   Is it a bug? Decide whether your system must survive a failing disk. If it
   must, look at the service's log in the run; if not, accept this finding.
   See it again: hydo run "disk=ioerr:3 dseed=fd403ef8d08fa636 | run K=redis@16+1 N=redis@0-8:loss,7%"
...
What held: 17 of 30 runs passed every check. With a working disk and your safe
settings, none of the 9 runs failed, network faults, power cuts and crashes
included.
```

**The README's terminal.** `docs/img/hero.svg` (10,665 bytes, CSS animation only, no script and no
web font; with reduced motion it shows the last frame) shows that run: `hydo onboard`,
`/hydo:onboard`, `hydo explore --seeds 1-30 --strategy swarm` and `hydo report`. Every line is the
real output, shortened only with `…`, and no line is a comment. The card shows the Redis example,
because no Blnk exploration was kept. Paused frames at 1.5 s, 8.5 s, 14 s and 27.5 s were checked
in headless Chrome. The README's alt text says the same.

**Pages.** Both quickstarts describe the new report and name `--html` and `--details` for the
classes and the property table. docs/ONBOARD.md quotes `--details` where it shows the minimal
schedule. `hydo guide workflow` and `hydo guide faults` list `hydo report --details`.
`hydo report --help` and `hydo explore --help` describe the new output and `--json`.

**Open.** A run directory's `hydo report` is still the technical summary, and the lines that

### Milestone 232 (tentative number) - DONE (Valkey 9.1.3 onboarded with `hydo onboard` on the Mac engine, a primary and two replicas; a new candidate, a backward clock step that delays a replica's full sync by its size, found blind and reproduced natively; the known Valkey issue 5354 found blind; `hydo save` inside the `hydo/` folder fixed; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-14)

**In short.** Valkey 9.1.3, the newest release, runs from its official image in
`hydo/onboard/examples/valkey` (RESULTS.md), as one primary with two replicas. Each server runs
with `appendfsync always`, dual-channel replication, and a replication backlog of 64 KB.
Valkey's repository has no Compose file, so the example has its own, and `hydo onboard`
started the `hydo/` folder from it. The test client `vkc` (Go, standard library only) writes
strings, strings with expiries, and hash fields with expiries. It changes hash fields through
seeded sequences of `HINCRBY`, `HPERSIST`, `HGETEX`, `HSETEX KEEPTTL` and other commands, and
runs `BGREWRITEAOF`. Three final rules check durability on the primary, expiry on every server,
and that each replica holds the primary's keys, values, and expiries. A liveness command waits
for the replicas after the faults. The runs used the Mac engine with this tree's hydo.

**What was found.**

- A new candidate, not reported upstream. `shouldStartChildReplication` in
  `src/replication.c` measures the wait before a full sync (`repl-diskless-sync-delay`, 5 s)
  with the wall clock: `server.unixtime - replica->last_interaction`. A backward clock step of
  D seconds while a replica waits makes the wait D + 5 seconds. hydo found it in 4 of 237
  explored schedules. The regression is `disk=none | run K=valkey3@2+3 T=10:-300`, and the
  kill alone passes. The native run used the official image with its default settings.
  libfaketime moved only the primary's wall clock. The sync took 6 s without a step, 65 s after
  a step of 60 seconds back, and 124 s after a step of 120 seconds back.
  `refreshGoodReplicasCount` computes the lag of `min-replicas-max-lag` the same way.
  Natively, after a step of 120 seconds back, a primary whose only replica was frozen acknowledged writes for 133 s instead of 11 s. Redis's
  `unstable` has the same code. Searches of valkey-io/valkey and redis/redis issues and pull
  requests with 38 phrasings, and of 40 Valkey release notes, found no report.
- A known bug, found blind: `HSETEX KEEPTTL` over the last field of a hash, expired but not
  reclaimed, is propagated as `HDEL` and `HSETEX`. The AOF replay after a power cut deletes the
  key with its expiry and makes it again without one. It is valkey-io/valkey issue 5354 (open).
  Direct probes in Docker of 48 commands on such a field found the same divergence only on the
  `KEEPTTL` paths of that issue.

Reports are drafted in RESULTS.md, not posted.

**Runs.** 237 explored schedules on the Mac engine:

| exploration | strategy | schedules | failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| ex1 | `process --new-faults --cluster-faults`, stopped after seed 17 | 17 | 10, from rules that were too strict; finding 1 in one of them |
| ex2 | the same | 40 | 4: finding 1 twice, a lagging replica twice |
| ex3 | the same | 120 | 2: findings 1 and 2 |
| ex4 | `swarm --new-faults --cluster-faults` | 60 | 28, each with I/O errors or a lying disk: the environment |

The final image gives `fp=d9c2a73b193da94c` twice for `disk=none | run`, and `hydo repro
--regressions` gives 3 of 3 as expected.

**Rules that were too strict.** Three, each fixed in the client:

- An item whose expiry passed before a backward clock step is gone, although its expiry is in
  the future again. The client writes clock marks `t~<ms>` to `$HYDO_ACKED`.
- A lagging replica serves an older value.
- `PERSIST` on an expired key.

**hydo.** One fix: `hydo save` from inside the `hydo/` folder wrote into a nested
`hydo/hydo/regressions`, which no build reads. It now writes into `regressions/` there
(`default_regressions_dir`, a unit test in `hydo/crates/hydo-cli/src/runs.rs`). Five frictions
stay open, listed in RESULTS.md:

- checks get no record of the clock steps;
- `hydo report` on a passing run omits each check's last line;
- the property table marks the project's own checks `[not in catalog]`;
- the import's lock file names a removed path in `generated_by`;
- `hydo setup --archive` from a checkout points `~/.hydo/bin/hydo` at the new version.

**Open.** No Sentinel and no cluster mode, so failover after `WAIT` was not tested. The
`min-replicas-to-write` effect ran natively only. Nothing ran on hvx or KVM.

### Milestone 239 (tentative number) - DONE (what an onboarding of a project's own binaries lacked: `ready: tcp:<port>`, each service's log in the run directory with whole lines in the diagnosis, `hydo run --memory`, the inspect sessions named in a memory refusal, a `--check` warning for missing sources, the guide topic `minimum-path`, the static musl recipe for Rust on a Mac, the messages records' value rules, and the skill's search for an installed hydo; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-14)

**Why.** An AI agent onboarded a user's own system (several services built from
source, no Compose file) into hydo 0.3.1 on this Mac. It reached a passing run with one
fingerprint in about two hours, and about forty minutes of that were hydo's friction. Its
feedback named nine places. Each was checked against `main` first; none was fixed already.

**What changed, each with what a user sees before and after.**

1. The skill's step 0 (`plugin/skills/onboard/SKILL.md`). Before, `hydo: command not found` led
   to "ask the user whether to install hydo", although `install.sh --add-to-path` had installed
   it in `~/.hydo/bin` and only the agent's shell did not read the startup file. Now the skill
   looks in `~/.hydo/bin`, `~/.cargo/bin` and Homebrew's `bin` first. It says "hydo is installed
   at X but not on this shell's PATH; I will call it by that path". It names `rustup target add`
   among the network installs that need the user's yes. `references/install.md` gained the
   `cargo install hydo --locked` and `hydo setup` steps; it still said cargo was planned.
2. `hydo guide workflow`, "Where each program comes from". Before, Rust was "a musl target". Now
   the page gives the `.cargo/config.toml` that links with `rust-lld` and no C toolchain, for
   `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` and `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`. It also gives the check for C
   code (`cargo tree -i cc --target ...`) and three ways for a project with C code (`zig cc`, a
   musl cross toolchain, a Linux container). The recipe was run on this Mac with Rust 1.90.0 on a
   program with a thread and a TCP listener: `file` printed `ELF 64-bit LSB executable, ARM
   aarch64, ... statically linked` and `ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, x86-64, ...
   static-pie linked`.
3. `ready: tcp:<port>` and `tcp:<host>:<port>`, a format-1 addition. The feedback said that the
   guest's busybox has no `nc`. It has: the arm64 busybox lists `nc`, and its symbols
   (`dolisten`, `readwrite`, `oprint`) are the full `nc` with `-z`. `hydo compose` already
   writes `nc -z -w 2 <addr> <port>` for a service without a healthcheck. So the new form needs
   no guest program and no agent change. `hydo_manifest::ready_command` turns it into exactly
   that command, with the service's `addr:` or 127.0.0.1. The host controller's plan
   (`hydo-control/src/plan.rs`) and the image's `manifest.sh` (`hydo-build/src/shell.rs`) use
   it. Every other `ready:` value is returned as written, so every existing image keeps its
   bytes. `hydo build --check` refuses a port outside 1 to 65535. The schema's description of
   `ready` names it. `hydo guide services` and MANIFEST.md ("Readiness by a connect") describe it.
4. Logs and the diagnosis. Before, the `hydo: diagnosis:` line quoted the first 300 characters
   of the failing service's last three log lines joined. A long line was cut at its end, which
   in the onboarding was one character before the error. The log itself was only in
   `result.json`, with terminal color codes, or behind a `hydo inspect` session. Now the
   diagnosis replay reads the last 64 KiB of each service's log and writes it, without color
   codes, to `<run>/logs/<service>.log`. The line quotes whole last lines, at most five, while
   they fit into 600 characters, and at least the last one. It ends with `(the whole log:
   logs/<service>.log in the run directory)`. `result.json`'s `evidence` keeps the last 3,000
   bytes, starting at a line. These reads are part of the replay after the run, so the run and
   its fingerprint are unchanged. A refusal of `hydo run` for the host's memory now names the
   running `hydo inspect` sessions and how to stop them, or says that none runs. `hydo inspect
   start` adds the note "this session holds the guest's memory (guest.ram_mib) until `hydo
   inspect stop <id>`, or until it is idle for 900 s".
5. `hydo run --memory`. After the run, one more replay to the run's end reads `VmHWM` and
   `VmRSS` of every process in the guest, and a service's processes are those whose standard
   output is the service's log. It prints, for the Redis example, `hydo: memory: redis peak 12
   MiB, now 12 MiB (1 process)` and the sum. `hydo guide services` says how to size
   `guest.ram_mib` with it. The flag is opt-in because the replay costs a second boot. A process
   that a fault killed took its peak with it, so the guide says to read a run without faults.
6. `hydo guide messages`. It now gives the values of `s=` (`ok`, `fail`, `info`, as the parser
   accepts them), that `o=` may be any text but `order: log` and the gap explanation need whole
   numbers, which characters `h=`, `k=`, `x=`, `o=` and a message id must encode and how, and
   what to record for "this deduplication id already exists". A retry of the same intent is
   `ok` with the stored message's `o=`. Another message with the same `x=` is `fail`, because
   the system stored nothing of its own for it.
7. `hydo guide services`, the bridge bullet: a program that binds to its own address needs the
   numeric `addr:`; names from `/etc/hosts` work for reaching peers.
8. The guide topic `minimum-path` (`hydo/guide/minimum-path.md`): the binaries, the keys of a
   service, the command kinds and exit codes, the check exit codes and the history record line,
   and the first-run commands, on one page. The skill and `hydo guide workflow` point to it
   first. Its YAML passed `hydo build --check` in a scratch project.
9. Small ones. `hydo build --check` prints `hydo-build: warning: N of M source files of
   root.files are missing (...); the full build will fail until they exist`. `hydo init`'s
   skeleton names every fault kind above its `faults:` line, with `protocol`, `corrupt` and
   `powerloss` and what they need. The skill's step 1 sends a message queue, a stream or a
   pub/sub system to the bundles of `hydo guide messages`.

The skill's version is 2.0.1 in SKILL.md, `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and
`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.

**Five frictions of the Valkey onboarding (Milestone 232), added on request.**

- `hydo report <run dir>` of a passing run named no check's last line. It now ends with "what
  each check said the last time it held", one line per property: the `details.out` of its last
  `HYDO-ASSERT` record that held, read from the run's consoles (`one.log`, `one.recovery.log`;
  `hydo_explore::results::last_held`). For the Redis example it prints
  `redis.acked_writes_survive  acked=20 all present`. `result.json` is unchanged.
- The property table's tag `[not in catalog]` for a property no SDK declared now reads
  `[the project's own check]`. Both quickstarts say so. The 20 report goldens of the explorer's
  scripted-engine scenarios changed in that tag only, at the same line counts.
- The Compose import's lock file says `"generated_by": "hydo compose"` instead of the deleted
  `hvx/onboard/hydo-compose` (`hydo_compose::GENERATED_BY`). The lock file is never inside an
  image: hydo-build copies only the folder's `workload/`, `checks/` and `regressions/`. The
  compose-voting example's lock file has the new line, because a test compares a fresh import
  with it. The older examples' lock files keep their text as records. The explorer's identity
  golden pins only the manifests, and it passed.
- `hydo onboard` and `hydo skill install --agent X` advise committing the copied skill folder

### Milestone 240 (tentative number) - DONE (what a user's first explorations of a message queue taught: a drain that outlasts leases and recovery inside its time limit, with a skeleton in `hydo guide messages`; who retries an `eventually_` command and an `eventually_` check; clock steps against durations kept on the wall clock; `guest.clock_after_cut` for leases; a long clock step also in hours and minutes; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-14)

**Why.** After Milestone 239 the same user explored their own message queue four times, 20
schedules each, about 23 minutes per exploration on one worker. Three of the four explorations
failed because of the plan, not the system, and the minimal schedules showed each cause:

- The `eventually_` command asked the system once. Right after a power cut the system still moved
  its queues between nodes, so the one answer was a redirect. The user had read the command
  table and still wrote the command as if hydo polled it, as it polls an `eventually_` check.
- The drain, the `final:` command of the `messages` check, gave up after some errors in the
  recovery boot. The system serves again only after its old takeover lease runs out. The drain
  also stopped after a quiet window shorter than that.
- The drain was killed by its time limit while it waited.

The fourth failure was real. A clock step back of 10,125 seconds made every message invisible
for that long, because the system stamps leases and visibility with the wall clock. The user
first read the step as 10 seconds, because the report said only "10125 seconds". hydo found the
same class of bug in Valkey on the same day (Milestone 232, valkey-io/valkey#5406).

**What changed, each with what a user sees before and after.**

1. `hydo guide messages`, "Write the drain". Before, the section said only that the drain
   receives until each group is empty and then writes `drained`. Now it gives three rules: the
   quiet window outlasts every lease and visibility timeout; the drain asks again through the
   system's recovery after a power cut and counts the quiet window from each error; and the
   drain's deadline fits inside its time limit. It names that limit and how to raise it. It adds
   a shell drain of about 30 lines (receive, acknowledge, a quiet window, a retry on errors until
   a deadline on `/proc/uptime`, then `drained`).
2. The time limit of the drain. The user reported that `test.command_timeout` killed the drain.
   The controller runs every `final:` read-back under `workload.timeout`
   (`hydo_control::schedule::history::finals` calls `timeout_argv`, which takes
   `plan.workload_timeout`, default 300 s). The guide says that, and that
   `test.command_timeout` limits the composer's commands and the check files instead. The
   user's exit status 137 was not reproduced here; their runs' outputs still on disk show only
   drains that ended themselves (status 1).
3. `hydo guide composer`, `hydo guide checks` and the skill's step 3: an `eventually_` command
   runs once and must retry by itself until its own deadline; hydo polls an `eventually_` check.
   Before, the difference was only implied by the two tables.
4. `hydo guide faults` has the new section "Clock steps and durations on the wall clock", and
   `hydo guide messages` a section of the same name. The number in `T=<step>:<seconds>` is
   seconds, and the shrinker halves it, so a minimal schedule can hold `T=7:-10125`. A system
   that measures leases, timeouts or visibility on the wall clock fails under a step, which is a
   bug of the system. Keep the finding (`hydo ci accept` while a fix is pending) and keep `clock`
   in `faults:`, or say in a comment why it is gone. The messages guide adds that
   `clock_steps:` only decides pairs that a lease, a delay or a window judges, and never excuses a
   message the drain did not receive. The user had expected `clock_steps: strict` to be the
   switch for such systems.
5. `hydo guide faults`, "Clock after a power cut", has a third case: a system that records leases
   or deadlines and serves again only after they run out. Without `guest.clock_after_cut` its
   recovery boot's clock starts before the recorded leases, and it waits longer than a real
   machine would. The skill's pitfalls name both clock items.
6. `hydo_schedule::describe::duration` adds the parts of a length that is not a whole number of
   its largest unit. Before: "the system clock jumps back by 10125 seconds". Now: "the system
   clock jumps back by 10125 seconds (2 h 48 min 45 s)". The function serves the schedule's
   description in `hydo report`, the explorer's advice, and the web page of `hydo report --html`.
   Machine outputs (`--details`, `result.json`, the schedule text) are unchanged. No recorded
   golden held such a length, so none moved.
7. The skill is 2.0.2 (SKILL.md, `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`,
   `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`).

**Tests.**

- `hydo-schedule` `durations_and_clock_points`: 59 s, 90 s, 5,400 s, 93,600 s and 10,125 s, and
  the sentence of `T=7:-10125`.
- `hydo` `equivalence::` and `agents_equivalence::` goldens re-recorded with `HYDO_BLESS=1`. The
  changed answers are `hydo guide composer` (the new paragraph) and `hydo skill install` (the
  version 2.0.2 and the new SKILL.md and pitfalls bytes).
- `cargo test -p hydo --test it` (35 tests), `cargo test -p hydo-agents --test it skill_check::
  public_content::`, `cargo test -p hydo-release --test it`, `sh ci/consolidate-tests.sh
  --check` and `sh ci/vale.sh` pass. No VM ran: the change is text and one description.

**Open.** The shell drain of the guide did not run in a VM. The messages tutorial's own drain
(`hydo/onboard/examples/messages-tutorial/tinyq`) still calls the queue empty at its first empty
receive, with no quiet window. The tutorial's queue has no leases, so that is enough there, and
its bytes are inside a recorded image, so it stays.

### Milestone 238 (tentative number) - DONE (upgrade testing: `services[].versions` and the token `U=` switch a service to another version of itself during a run, as a rolling upgrade or a rollback does, and `hydo explore --upgrades` draws it; an etcd cluster grown with learners reaches etcd issue 19557 with one token, and etcd's documented path through 3.5.26 passes; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-14)

**In short.** Rolling upgrades are a frequent cause of outages: old and new versions run side by
side and read each other's data. hydo had no way to change a service's program during a run. Now
a manifest lists the versions a service can run, and `U=<target>@<at>[/<gap>][+<back>]:<version>`
stops the service, switches its version and starts it again on the same data. The design is
docs/design/upgrades.md.

**The manifest (a format-1 addition).** `services[].version` names the version that `cmd:`,
`setup:` and `ready:` run, and `services[].versions` lists the others, each with its own commands
where they differ. Every command of a service with versions sees `$HYDO_VERSION`; a service
without them gets no such variable. A version name is a letter or digit, then letters, digits,
`.`, `_` and `-`, at most 40 bytes (`hydo_schedule::version_name_ok`). A `{{param}}` may name a
version. Versions of an image service (`image:`) are refused for now.

**The token.** `U=` takes a service, a list or a group selector. A target of several services is
switched one member at a time, the k-th before step `at + k*gap`, each once the one before it is
ready again. `+<back>` rolls each member back `back` steps after its own switch; a downgrade can
also be a second `U=`. The host controller (`hydo-control/src/schedule/upgrade.rs`) sends SIGTERM
to the service's tree, starts a grace thread that sends SIGKILL after 10 s of guest time, waits
for the process's end, switches the version and calls `start_svc`. The switch comes after the
step's `K=` restarts. A service that is down at its switch only gets the version, and its restart
uses it. A service that does not start on its new version ends the run with `HYDO-ORACLE:
VIOLATION [upgrade.started] <svc> did not start on version <v> before step <p> (it ran <old>)`.
The letter `U` is reserved, so no knob may use it.

**Records.** Each switch writes the note `HYDO-UPGRADE {"service","step","from","to","rollback",
"started"}`, and `result.json` lists them as `upgrades` (the results addition `Run.upgrades`,
`UpgradeSwitch`). A run with `U=` declares and reaches `fault.upgraded`. At a power cut (and at
the end of a `cf=` run) the report line `hydo-explore-versions: <svc>=<v> ...` carries the switched
versions; `RecoveryInputs.versions` reads it from the transcript, so the recovery boot starts each
service on the version it ran at the cut. `hydo inspect diagnose` names the service of an
`[upgrade.started]` verdict and collects its log.

**The explorer.** `hydo explore --upgrades` adds a `U=` to 60% of the schedules from its own
stream (`UPGRADE_SALT`): half rolling upgrades of a group whose members all have versions (0 to 3
steps apart), the rest one service, a quarter with a rollback. Version names come from the image's
`/etc/hydo/params` (`Space::with_params`). The class of such a failure is `upgrade`, after the
disk and corruption classes. The shrinker tries the schedule without each `U=`, without its
rollback and without its gap. `--upgrades` without any service with versions is refused.

**The proof: etcd issue 19557.** The example `hydo/onboard/examples/etcd-upgrade` grows a
three-member cluster with learners: `etcd1` starts alone, and `etcd2` and `etcd3` join as learners
and are promoted, one at a time. From etcd 3.5.1 to 3.5.19 a promotion reaches only v2store, so
etcd 3.6 finds two learners in v3store and stops at its start (fixed in 3.5.20; etcd's upgrade
notes ask for 3.5.26 before 3.6). The image holds 3.5.5, 3.6.0-rc.2 or 3.6.0, and 3.5.26. The runs
on hvx, each from a fresh boot, with this milestone's `hydo` in a copy of the unpacked 0.3.2
Linux release:

| image (new version) | schedule | verdict | fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|

`hydo inspect diagnose --evidence` of the failing rc.2 run replays it and reads etcd1's log:

**Blind exploration.** `hydo explore --upgrades --seeds 1-24 --workers 1` on the 3.6.0 image

### Milestone 236 (tentative number) - DONE (rule suggestion, first version: `hydo rules scan` lists what a project promises, `hydo rules check` validates candidate rules on runs without faults, and the onboarding skill proposes rules from the project's own sources and shows the owner only the validated ones; proven on Blnk and Lago and on listmonk, which hydo had never seen; Formance Ledger's rules were proposed but not run; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-14)

The question came from the user's own onboarding of a message broker: did the skill's rule
proposals help? They helped only as far as the lists per domain and the questions to the owner
went. The goal of this milestone is bugs that nobody wrote a test for, found by rules that
nobody wrote, with a method that knows no domain. The design is `docs/design/rule-suggestion.md`.

**The method.** The skill proposes rules from five sources: the database schema (constraints,
unique keys, foreign keys, CHECKs, state columns), the API, the documentation's promise words,
the project's tests, and the client library. Each rule has a plain statement, its evidence (file
and line), a kind (`sql`, `command`, `messages`, `history`) and a confidence. hydo validates every
rule on runs without faults before the owner sees it, and the skill shows the owner only the
rules that hold, with the ones that failed without faults apart. Four kinds of evidence give
rules that a database cannot enforce by itself, and they are the ones the method prefers:

- a constraint that only the application checks (a model validation, a check in a service);
- a partial unique index, taken to all the rows that mean the same thing;
- a total across tables, instead of a constraint that the database already enforces;
- a state that the documentation says leads to an action (an eventually rule).

The rule over the client's acknowledged operations is proposed for every project.

**`hydo rules scan [DIR] [--kind K] [--json] [--max N]`** (`hydo/crates/hydo-cli/src/rules.rs`)
lists the evidence in five kinds: `schema`, `state`, `api`, `docs` and `tests`, each line with
its file and line number. It reads `.sql` files, migrations, model and schema files, OpenAPI,
`.proto` and GraphQL files, Markdown, reStructuredText and AsciiDoc files, and test files of
common languages. A file of documentation or tests gives at most 40 lines. A schema dump gives
all of its lines: with a limit of 40 lines, Lago's `db/structure.sql` lost every partial unique index.
A query's `LIMIT` and `OFFSET` are no evidence; before that rule, listmonk's `queries.sql`
listed its paging clauses.

**`hydo rules check <candidates.yaml> [IMG] [--runs N] [--schedule S] [--mutate] [--keep-checks]
[--timeout S] [--out DIR] [--write-checks DIR]`** runs the image's workload without faults on
the schedules `disk=none | run W=00000001` to `W=0000000N` (default 3; `W=` takes 8 hex digits
in its seed form). An image without composed commands gets one run of `disk=none | run`. The
image is not rebuilt. The command changes the image's plan in the host controller
(`runs::run_with_plan`, a `PlanEdit` hook on the run path): the project's own checks
(`compose.sh check N`) leave, the composed commands' invariants (`compose.sh verdict`, the
`eventually` and `finally` commands) stay, and each candidate becomes a final invariant
`rule.<id>`. Each candidate runs in a shell wrapper:

- `sql`: `hydo-sql none <store> '<query>'`, its `cases` through `hydo-sql read sql`;
- `command`: the command as written;
- `within: N`: the rule is tried every 2 s of guest time until it holds or N s pass;
- the wrapper's last line is `hydo-rule exit=S mutate=M cases=C :: LAST`, and it fails only when
  the rule failed, so one rule that cannot be evaluated does not make the run an error.

The command reads each rule's result from the `HYDO-ASSERT` records and a failing rule's rows
from the `HYDO-CHECK-OUT` notes of Milestone 225. The statuses are `holds`, `vacuous` (it held but
its `cases` count was 0 in every run), `fails-clean`, `unevaluated` and `not-run`. `--mutate`
makes one more run of the first schedule: each rule that holds and has a `mutate` runs, its
change is made, and it runs again. It must fail then (`caught`); else it is `blind`. A rule that
already fails before its own change (an earlier rule's change broke it) gets a run of its own.
`--schedule S` runs another schedule instead, for example a saved regression's. The results are `rules-check.json`, and
`--write-checks DIR` writes each rule that holds as `final_<id>.sql`, an executable `final_<id>`,
or an `eventually_` check with `within=N after=commands`.

**The guide and the skill.** `hydo guide rules` holds the facts: the scan, the kinds of evidence
that give strong rules, the candidates file's format, the statuses, and the commands.
`hydo guide workloads` ("Business rules: ask the owner") and `hydo guide workflow` point at it.
The skill (2.1.0; SKILL.md, `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and
`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) no longer asks the owner to confirm a domain's list in step 1.
Step 3 proposes the rules with the new reference `references/proposing-rules.md` into
`hydo/rules.yaml`, step 4 validates them with `hydo rules check --mutate` and shows the owner the
ones that hold, and step 5 reports them, plain words first. The domain lists are a last check for
rules the sources did not give.

**Tests.** The unit tests of `rules.rs` (12): the candidates file and its errors, the commands of
a `sql` rule, the wrapper in a real shell (the summary line, its exit status, `within` and the
planted change), the reading of the records, every status and mutation verdict, the plan edit
(the project's checks leave, the commands stay), the check files, the store of
`helper_sql.conf`, and the scan's kinds by file and by line. `hydo/crates/hydo-cli/tests/rules.rs`
(`hydo::rules`, fast) runs `hydo rules check` on the scripted engine end to end: six rules give
each status, the four runs, the failing rows, both mutation verdicts and the check files; a bad
file runs nothing; and the scan by kind and as JSON.

**The proof runs.** Blnk and listmonk ran on the bare-metal machine with hvx, through
`~/bin/hvx-run`, with this branch's `hydo` in a copy of the unpacked 0.3.2 Linux release; their
images were built there from the manifests (Blnk's programs from `build.sh`, its six pins
checked). Lago ran on this Mac's engine with this branch's `hydo` and an image built from the
example's manifest: on hvx its `api` service exits during start (open item 110). The rules were
proposed from each project's sources (`hydo rules scan` and the files it names) and the
example's workload, without reading the example's checks. The author knew which rules had found
the known bugs (the task named them), so the proposal is not blind; each rule's evidence is in
its candidates file. The files are in `docs/design/rule-suggestion/`.

| project | scan (the final `hydo rules scan`): lines of evidence in files | proposed | hold | vacuous | fail without faults | changes caught |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Blnk `67d88333` (hvx) | 586 in 228 | 9 | 8 | 0 | 1 (a wrong rule) | 5 of 7 tried |
| Lago v1.57.0 (Mac) | 4,217 in 1,325 | 11 | 11 | 0 | 0 | 8 of 10 tried |
| listmonk v2.5.1, never seen before (hvx) | 204 in 58 | 5 | 4 | 0 | 1 | 1 of 4 tried |
| Formance Ledger v2.4.18 | 760 in 793 | 6 | not run | | | |

A change that was not caught was `blind` (a change that hit rows the rule does not judge: 1 in
Lago, 2 in listmonk) or failed itself (an `INSERT` or `UPDATE` that the database refused: 2 in
Blnk, 1 in Lago). Before the fallback of a run of its own, three Blnk rules and one listmonk rule
were broken by an earlier rule's change; with it, the three Blnk rules were caught. Formance's
six rules were proposed only: its ledger's Go link hung twice on the shared machine, and no
image was built.

*Blnk.* The rule over the client's acknowledged operations failed without faults in all three
runs: 14 of 76 operations had no transaction, every one a commit or void of a hold. The rule was
wrong, not Blnk. Blnk gives a hold's commit the reference `<leg>_commit_<reference>`
(`transaction_inflight.go:637`, `inflightActionReference`). The second version looked for that
name in `transaction_id` and failed the same way. The third looks in `reference`, holds in the
three runs (173, 170 and 146 cases), and catches its planted change. This is the loop of the
skill for a rule that fails without faults: read the rows, fix the rule, validate again.

Then the saved regressions of Blnk's three findings (Milestone 224) ran with `--schedule`
against the proposed rules:

| finding | its schedule | the proposed rule that failed |
|---|---|---|
| 1. a draw ignores its overdraft limit (Blnk bug) | `disk=none dseed=62b1aba8e728944c \| run W=e48d5d25,p3,q1,r200,o...`, no fault | `no_balance_below_its_floor` |
| 2. an atomic bulk keeps its first transfer (Blnk bug) | `... \| run P=redis@9+4 W=3e71cf9e,p5,q3,r800` | none of the nine (below) |
| 3. acknowledged commits of holds lost with Redis's defaults | `... \| run K=redis@21+1 N=worker-*@14-20:delay,100ms W=a36fcf62,...` | `acked_operations_recorded` (1 of 39) |

The overdraft rule held on the seeds 1 to 3 and failed on finding 1's composition. The bug needs
concurrent draws that Blnk's worker coalesces, and the three default compositions had none. So
a rule that holds on clean runs is ready for exploring; it has not been checked yet.

Finding 2 was missed. The proposed `atomic_bulk_whole_or_refunded` looked for a rejected
transfer next to an applied one, but in finding 2 the second transfer is never saved. Two later
proposals, written after the miss, show what the method lacked:

- `failed_operations_not_applied`, the generic rule's second half, held on finding 2: the
  client did not learn the bulk's outcome (a timeout), so the operation was `unknown`, not
  failed. It also matched references without Blnk's `_q` suffix (below), so it judged less than
  it says.
- `atomic_bulk_all_or_none` (`blnk-bulk.yaml`; an atomic bulk ends with both transfers applied
  or neither) first held on finding 2 too. It counted the queued rows, whose references are
  `k5.1`. Blnk applies a queued transfer as a copy with the reference `<reference>_q`
  (`transaction_queue.go:424`). Its `cases` counted the bulks, not the rows it judged, so the
  check did not show that it judged nothing. The second version counts the `_q` copies, holds
  on the seeds 1 to 3 (17, 6 and 8 applied transfers judged), and fails on finding 2 with
  `db: 2 rows where none may be`, as the example's own rule did.

The lesson for the skill and the guide: a rule's `cases` must count the rows that the rule's
query judges, not the operations the rule is about.

*Lago*, on the Mac engine (a clean run takes about 17 s of guest time). All 11 rules held, none
was vacuous, and 8 of the 10 planted changes were caught. The planted change of
`closed_period_usage_invoiced` deleted a row of a subscription without usage in a closed month
(`blind`), and that of `one_invoice_per_period_any_reason`, an `INSERT`, failed. Then the
example's four saved regressions ran with `--schedule` against the 11 rules:

| finding (Lago's RESULTS.md) | its schedule | the proposed rules that failed |
|---|---|---|
| 8. a subscription cancelled before the billing tick is invoiced twice | `disk=none \| run T=3:@:10-2s O=db-api@1-3:resp:loss,74% W=740c6cfa,...` | `one_invoice_per_period_any_reason` (1 row) |
| 1. lago-api 6901: cancelled while Redis is down, never invoiced | `disk=none \| run K=redis@1+4` | `terminated_subscription_invoiced`, `closed_period_usage_invoiced`, `in_advance_fee_once_per_event` |
| 2. Lago issue 354: a clock step over the billing day | `disk=none \| run T=0:86400` | `closed_period_usage_invoiced` (2 rows) |
| 1 (fees). a power cut loses queued in-advance fees | `disk=cut dseed=629bfb2777cb6c08 \| run C=10 P=api_worker@5+5 T=0:300 W=340bcd65,...` | `in_advance_fee_once_per_event` (4 rows: the 4 transfers never charged) |

The double invoice came from generalizing two partial unique indexes
(`index_uniq_invoice_subscriptions_on_charges_from_to_datetime` covers only periodic invoices,
`index_unique_terminating_invoice_subscription` only termination invoices) to overlapping charge
periods of any reason. Each found failure ran on one schedule; no exploration ran with these
rules.

*listmonk* had never been onboarded. Its onboarding for this milestone is in
`docs/design/rule-suggestion/listmonk/`: the release's static program, PostgreSQL 16, a client
`lmc` in Go, and four commands (subscribe, hard bounce, unsubscribe, blocklist). A clean run takes
about 5 s. One rule failed without faults, in two of three runs:
`blocklisted_has_no_live_subscription`. listmonk's own blocklisting (`queries.sql`,
`blocklist-subscribers`, and the comment of `unsubscribe-by-campaign`) unsubscribes the
subscriber from every list. A blocklisting by hard bounces (`record-bounce`, `block1`) changes
only the subscriber's status, so two base subscribers stayed `confirmed` on the double opt-in
list. listmonk's campaign query leaves blocklisted subscribers out, so no mail goes out. Whether
this is a wrong rule or a bug is the owner's decision; `record-bounce` on listmonk's `master`
of 2026-11-14 is the same. The planted changes of two rules picked a row that the rule does not
judge (the first blocklisted subscriber, who had no bounces), and `blind` showed it. With the four
rules that held written as checks (`--write-checks`), `hydo explore --seeds 1-150 --strategy
process --new-faults` ran 150 schedules in 410 s with the manifest's fault kinds (kills, pauses,
network faults, power cuts and clock steps) and found no failure.

**Checks.** On the bare-metal machine, in a synced copy of the tree: `cargo fmt --check`,
`cargo clippy -D warnings` (`hydo`, `hydo-config`), `cargo test -p hydo --test it` (37 passed,
with `docs::` and `rules::`), `cargo test -p hydo --bin hydo` (123 passed; the one failure,
`skillupdate::tests::each_agent_gets_its_folder`, needs the repository's git and passes in a
checkout), `cargo test -p hydo-agents` (with `skill_check::` and `public_content::`),
`cargo test -p hydo-config` (with the inventory), and `hydo-release`'s `test_tiers::`. On this
Mac: `sh ci/consolidate-tests.sh --check` and `sh ci/vale.sh`. Re-recorded goldens: the CLI's
help (`tests/golden/cli.jsonl`: the line for `hydo rules`), the agents' answers
(`tests/golden/agents.jsonl`: the guide's topic list has `rules`, the skill is 2.1.0) and
`INVENTORY.md` (`HYDO_SCRIPTED_RULES`). No recorded value of an example moved; no example
