### Milestone 271 (tentative number) - DONE (two small fixes: every test removes the folder it makes in the temporary directory, also when it fails, and `HYDO_KEEP_TMP=1` keeps them; and open item 127, a `cf=` cut at the flush of an `L=`'s mount: in a `cf=` run busybox mounts and reads in a child process instead of the agent, so the run reaches its recovery boot; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-16)

**What was asked.** On this Mac the temporary directory (`getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR`) had
filled with 10 GB of folders that hydo's tests left. Make every test remove its folder when it
ends, also when it fails. Then fix open item 127 without a module change, and keep every
recorded value.

**1. The folders the tests left.** One run of `cargo test --release --workspace` with an empty
`TMPDIR` left 269 folders (25 MB). Each folder came from a test helper that never removed it:

| Folders | Prefix | Made by |
|---|---|---|
| 235 | `hydo-kvm-engine-` | `hydo-kvm` tests, `engine.rs`: one engine folder per scripted run |
| 18 | `hydo-grpc-client-` | `hydo-grpc-gen` tests, `client.rs`: the plan and state folders |
| 4 | `hydo-hvx-abi-` | `hydo-hvx` tests, `abi.rs`: the C probes |
| 4 | `hydo-world-test-` | `hydo-world`'s unit tests, `world.rs` |
| 3 | `hydo-agents-eq-` | the `hydo` program's `agents_equivalence`: the release roots |
| 2 | `hydo-manifest-messages-` | `hydo-manifest` tests, `messages.rs` |
| 1 | `hydo-docs-help-` | the `hydo` program's `docs.rs`: the folder of `hydo <command> --help` |
| 1 | `hydo-eq-` | the `hydo` program's `equivalence.rs`: the `PATH` without `debugfs`, kept in a `static` |
| 1 | `hydo-store-rw-` | `hydo-image`'s unit tests, `store.rs`: a store with read-only entries |

On a developer's machine every run adds that many again. The 10 GB were about 135 release roots
of `agents_equivalence`, 74 MB each when the plugin folder was larger, and 22,000 engine folders
of `hydo-kvm`. Most other helpers removed their folder as the last line of the test. So a
failing test left it in these test programs: `hydo-world`, `hydo-compose`, `hydo-manifest`, `hydo-build`, `hydo-control`,
`hydo-composer`, `hydo-errors`, `hydo-bench`, `hydo-contracts`, `hydo-image`, `hydo-grpc`,
`hydo-sql`, `hydo-hvm`, the explorer's scripted engine, and the Rust SDK's tests. The SDK tests in
other languages left theirs too. The JavaScript `unit` and `history` tests left one folder per
run each (`hydo-js-unit-`, `hydo-js-hist-`), and the Python history tests seven per run
(`hydo-hist.`, one per test that records, and two without a prefix).

- The fix. Each test program that makes such folders has a support module `tests/tmpdir/mod.rs`
  with the type `TmpDir`. A `TmpDir` is a folder that is removed with its contents when the value
  is dropped. A test that fails unwinds, so its folders go too. A helper that made a folder now
  returns a `TmpDir`, which reads as a path. A folder that a `static` keeps for the whole test
  program (the `PATH` folder of `equivalence.rs`) is removed when the program exits
  (`tmpdir::at_exit`, with C's `atexit`). The unit tests in `src/` have a small guard of their
  own in their test module. The JavaScript tests remove their folder at the process's exit or in
  a `finally`, and the Python ones with `atexit`.
- `HYDO_KEEP_TMP=1` keeps every folder, to look at it after a test; the guard then prints the
  folder's path. It is a test switch in `hydo_config::registry` and `INVENTORY.md`. The guards of
  `hydo`'s and `hydo-errors`' unit tests in separate files under `src/` (`htmlreport/tests.rs`,
  `cache/tests.rs`, `skillupdate/tests.rs`, `src/tests.rs`) remove their folder always, because
  only `hydo-config` may read a variable in a crate's `src/` (the `inventory` test).
- `own_help` of `docs.rs` named its folder by the process alone, and the tests that call it run
  as threads of one process. Its folder now has a counter in its name too, so that one test
  cannot remove another's folder.
- The proof. The same run with the fix and an empty `TMPDIR` left 0 folders, and every test passed. The JavaScript
  tests (`node --test` of the four files) left 2 folders before and 0 after; the Python history
  tests left 7 before and 0 after.

**2. Open item 127: a `cf=` cut at the agent's own mount.** Milestone 261 cuts the power of a
`cf=` run at the first stop after its data disk lost power. The cut freezes the workload and the
services and reads the ids through the agent. An `L=` (the power loss of one service) mounts the
service's file system again with the agent's own `mount` command, and a `G=` flip reads a byte
with the agent's own `read`. When the k-th flush came from that mount (its journal replay), the
agent waited on the dark disk in the `mount` call and answered nothing. The run then ended 200,000
stops later in `ERROR the disk lost power at its flush of cf= while the agent itself waited on it`,
without its recovery boot.

- The fix (`hydo/crates/hydo-control/src/schedule/storage.rs`). In a `cf=` schedule's run, the
  storage faults' mounts and reads are made by busybox in a child process. The mount is
  `$BB mount -t <type> -o <flags and data> <device> <dir>`, with the agent's flags written as
  their mount options. The byte read is `$BB dd ... | $BB od -An -tx1`. When the disk loses power
  under the child, only the child waits. The agent answers the power cut, and the recovery boot
  gives the verdict. A run without `cf=` sends the agent's own commands as before, so its
  transcript and its values stay. The agent and the module are unchanged.
- The test (`hydo-control`, `tests/drive.rs`):
  `a_cf_cut_at_the_mount_of_an_l_reaches_the_recovery_boot`. The scripted engine's disk now
  loses power at the next mount when a test asks for it. With the agent's own mount the agent
  answers nothing after it, as the real agent does. With the agent's own mount, as before the
  fix, the test fails. Now the run ends with the power cut and the reported ids, the recovery boot
  gives a verdict, and the same schedule without `cf=` still sends the agent's `mount`.
- The runs on hvx. They ran on the bare-metal machine, one VM at a time through `~/bin/hvx-run`.
  The programs `hydo` and `hydo-hvx` were built from this branch over the 0.3.4 Linux release.
  The image is a copy of Milestone 261's final RAUC image. "Before" is `main`'s `hydo` at
  `588c76dd`.

| Schedule | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `disk=cut dseed=b867e156d88e8c87 cf=83 \| run T=12:-300 L=device@6+2` (seed 37 of M261's exploration) | `ERROR the disk lost power ... while the agent itself waited on it`, `ea37cda227ebf2cb`, 229,181 stops | `OK invariants=6 held (device.boots: booted slot A v3 after 4 boot(s))`, `0cad7c03d59862fa` on two runs, 35,073 stops |
| the same without `cf=` | `OK`, `71a6a8ff2ef5db3e` | `OK`, `71a6a8ff2ef5db3e`, the same control transcript |
| `disk=cut dseed=72b4b958fb4479ee cf=34 \| run T=12:-30` | `88efb2c07865ffab` (M261) | `88efb2c07865ffab` |
| `disk=cut dseed=9f14bde427152010 cf=83 \| run G=device@13:zero,len=512,seed=3a12608b` | `6db779f596d5296e` (M261) | `6db779f596d5296e` |

The run's control transcript shows the busybox `mount` of `/dev/vda5` on `/data/part`, the note
`the disk lost power at its flush of cf=: the power cut is now`, and the recovery conversation's
verdict. A flip of `G=` with `cf=83` (`G=device@13:flip,n=2,seed=5`) was cut before its step
13, so no run here reads a byte in a child.

**What moved.** Nothing in `hydo/onboard/recorded.json`: it has no `cf=` run and no `L=` or `G=`.
The pinned reproducers give `a76d7fe857fdb37c` (VIOLATION) and `efbde7b57264be0f` (OK) on the
images in `~/hydo/build/m204`. `hydo-bench rebaseline --check --only stack-fix,stack-old --jobs 1`
on the bare-metal machine built the six images of the two stages and ran their 31 schedules in
1,726 s. The report says: verdicts unchanged, 0 images with new bytes, 0 runs with a new
fingerprint or `ctl` value. Each hvx run with `cf=` and an `L=` gives other values and another
transcript, and so does each run with `cf=` and a `G=` flip. This holds also when the disk did not
lose power during the mount.

**Checks.** On this Mac, on `main` at `47df6fee` with this milestone on top: `cargo test --release
--workspace` (every test program, the CLI golden `equivalence::cli_matches_golden` and
`agents_equivalence` among them), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo
fmt --all --check`, `hydo-config`'s `inventory` after `HYDO_BLESS=1`, the Rust SDK's tests,
`node --test` of the JavaScript tests and the Python tests, `hydo-schedule`'s `language::`,
`hydo-agents`'s `public_content::`, the `hydo` program's `docs::`, `sh
ci/consolidate-tests.sh --check` and `sh ci/vale.sh`.

### Milestone 270 (tentative number) - DONE (open item 131, a recording that shows the failing run: a walk with `rec` repeats the actions that the same schedule without `rec` took, by the same role and accessible name, instead of choosing them again; five Memos recordings repeated their run's 72 actions exactly, the reaction finding and web-shop's two planted bugs kept their verdicts under recording, and the share-link finding could not be filmed, because the new walker's image changes the walks that reached it; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-16)

Open item 131 said that a recording replay does not show the failing run. With `,rec` on, the
walker chose each action again from what the page showed. Recording slows the browser, so the
pages answered later, and the walk took other actions: in Milestone 267 two Memos walks that
failed with the share link took other actions with `rec0` and `rec4`, and passed. The design is
the new bullet "The recording repeats the failing run" in the section "The evidence of a failing
walk" of `docs/design/ui-exploration.md`.

**The change.**

- **The walker prints a script.** Every run prints each action it takes as one console line,
  `hydo-web: walk-act <step>.<k> <json>` (`hydo-manifest/src/browser/walk.mjs`). The JSON holds
  the kind of action, the control's role, its accessible name, its place among the controls of
  that name (and among the controls of its role, for a control without a name), the value
  typed, the option chosen, the button that committed a form, or the time waited. An action
  that did not finish is marked `failed`. The human line `hydo-web: walk <step>.<k>: ...` stays
  as it was.
- **The schedule.** `,rec` implies the script: `I=<walk>,rec<s>` means the actions that the same
  schedule with `I=<walk>` takes, with step `s` recorded. hydo runs that schedule
  deterministically, so a schedule with `rec` reproduces exactly, and no new token is needed.
  `hydo_schedule::describe` says so in plain words.
- **The host gets the script.** `hydo explore`'s recording replay takes the `walk-act` lines from
  the console of the minimal schedule's confirmation run, which is the run of the same schedule
  without `rec` (`walk_replays` in the `hydo` program's `delegated.rs`). `hydo run` and `hydo
  repro` of a schedule with `rec` run it without `rec` first, into `walked/` of the run directory,
  and print how many actions that run took and its verdict (`walk_script_for` in `runs.rs`).
  Every recording's run directory keeps the script as `walk-script.txt`.
- **The guest gets the script.** The host sets the new field `hydo_control::Plan::walk_script`,
  which is not a manifest key. Before the walk's first step range, the controller writes it to
  `/tmp/hydo/web/walk-script.txt` in parts of at most 1,200 bytes, because a part's JSON is
  escaped once more inside the agent's command. A run without `rec`, or without a script, sends
  exactly the commands it sent before.
- **The walker repeats the script.** An action finds its control by the same role, name and
  place, and waits up to 10 s for it to be visible, because a recorded page answers later. A
  name with a time in it may read otherwise when the clock moved on; then the control with the
  same name without its times and the same place among them is the same control, by Milestone
  264's rule. A control that is not on the page is left out: the walker's line says that it was
  not on the page and that the replay takes no other control. An action that the script lacks
  is left out with its own line. Each step ends with `hydo-web: walk <step>: the recording replay
  repeated every action of the run it replays`, or the number it left out. `hydo explore`'s line
  about a recording names each action that it left out.
- **An older image.** An image built before this milestone prints no `walk-act` lines. Its
  recording then chooses again, and `hydo run` says so.

**Proof on hvx.** Every run used the 0.3.3 Linux release with this milestone's `hydo`, in a folder
of its own on the bare-metal machine, one VM at a time. Two images were built with this
milestone's walker: Memos and web-shop's `hydo-walk.yaml` (buggy). One more Memos image has
Milestone 267's first walker (`img-memos-e`, the one whose walks of seeds 31 and 42 clicked a
share link's copy button) with this milestone's change on top, built only for this proof. Its
walker is not in the tree.

Each `hydo run` of a Memos schedule with `rec` ran the schedule without `rec` into `walked/` and
then the recording. In all five, the recording's `walk-act` lines are byte for byte those of the
run without `rec`, `failed` marks included. Every step printed "repeated every action".

| walk | image | run without `rec` | the recording | video of the recorded step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| seed 31's share-link walk (r31), `rec4` | first walker | OK, `67e323efabc3d44e` | OK, `801d602b4ba3782d` | 370,979 bytes |
| seed 42's share-link walk, `rec0` | first walker | OK, `2da85e0ae10297f9` | OK, `eced80b58b29bed0` | 490,565 bytes |
| the reaction walk (r2), kill at 3000 ms, `rec4` | this walker | OK, `9de8e41696feb816` | OK, `bccafcfbdad63486` | 151,884 bytes |
| the reaction walk, kill at 4500 ms, `rec4` | this walker | finding 2, `b367255eab3296bb` | finding 2, `6ba714fd0f786c41` | 363,359 bytes |
| the reaction walk, kill at 2000 ms, `rec4` | this walker | finding 2, `ae741082e88b5c3a` | finding 2, `2446b6a2b1ac4fa6` | 362,800 bytes |

The schedules are r31's `disk=none dseed=d7599677879feaea | run
N=memos@3-5:corrupt,6%,delay,20ms,reorder,29% P=memos@1+1 T=2:3600 I=4faa1d8cb3256a54,rec4`, seed
42's `disk=none dseed=bdd732262feb6e95 | run I=36c25063a25340e7,rec0`, and the reaction walk's
`disk=none dseed=7daf7bd7b0085fd2 | run X=memos@4~<ms> I=8690c91dedf1a78f,rec4`. Finding 2 is
`browser.failures_shown`: "POST /memos.api.MemoService/UpsertMemoReaction got no answer
(net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED) during the test "walk step 4"". On this walker the reaction comes at
actions 4.2 and 4.3 with the kill at 3000 ms. That is before the server dies, so both runs pass.
With the kill at 4500 ms the walk adds a reaction while the server is down. A recording is still
a run of its own with its own fingerprint, but now with the same actions and, in all five, the
same verdict.

**What the proofs show, and what they do not.**

- The recording replay repeats the run it replays exactly, by the record of every action, in
  all five Memos recordings and both web-shop recordings.
- The reaction finding (finding 2) fails the same way when recorded. Its video is
  `walk-step-4.webm` of the recording at 4500 ms.
- web-shop's two planted bugs, found blind and recorded, show their bugs. The exploration of
  seeds 1-20 with `--protocol-faults` (one worker, 2,630 s) failed seeds 7 and 17, as Milestone
  267's final walker did, and confirmed both. Its two recordings ended with the minimal
  schedules' verdicts, and each repeated every action of its run:
  - `I=a0d28305209409f6,n7,x0.0-6,x1.0-6,x2.0-6` with `H=api.get_order@3-4:reset`: the

### Milestone 272 (tentative number) - DONE (the Mender client 5.2.0 in standalone mode on a device with A/B root partitions, U-Boot's redundant environment and Mender's data partition on one eMMC, with real reboots; two new Mender candidates: Mender syncs an Artifact's state scripts before the scripts' version file has its content, so a power cut soon after an install leaves an update that can be neither committed nor rolled back; and an interrupted `mender-update commit` makes the next commit roll the update back and exit 0, which undoes an update that U-Boot had made permanent; a tooling candidate in mender-artifact; both Mender candidates found blind on the Mac engine; what hydo lacked; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-16)

**In short.** `hydo/onboard/examples/mender` (RESULTS.md) runs Mender 5.2.0's `mender-update`,
built statically from its release archive for arm64 (the x86_64 build did not finish), with mender-flash 1.1.0,
libubootenv 0.3.8 and Mender's rootfs-image Update Module. The device has one eMMC with a volatile
write cache, laid out as meta-mender lays out a storage device. U-Boot's redundant environment is
at 4 and 8 MiB, root file systems A (Mender's partition 2) and B (3) follow, and an ext4 data
partition holds Mender's database at `/data/mender`. The slots hold real root file systems, and
every Mender command runs in a chroot on the booted slot. So the module's check of the mounted
root sees the slot that U-Boot booted. U-Boot is an emulation of Mender's U-Boot integration with
U-Boot's boot counter (`bootlimit=1`). The operator runs 8 standalone deployments: install, a
real reboot, commit. The broken v4 is rolled back with `mender-update rollback` after its health
check. On the Mac engine the eMMC is an added disk (`hydo-devices.yaml`); on hvx it is a file on
the data disk (`hydo.yaml`). Every Artifact carries state scripts that print console events, the
events of the reactions; with `--set artifacts=plain` the operator installs the same Artifacts
without them. Seven checks: a complete slot boots; the booted version is one the outcomes allow;
`mender_boot_part` holds a complete image; Mender's database names the running version when no
update is in progress; the synced records survive; every reboot and every commit that exited 0
held; and the operator's commit after the run keeps its promise.

**What was found.**

- **Mender, new as far as the search found: an empty version file of the Artifact scripts.**
  `Parse` in `src/artifact/v3/header/header.cpp` writes the scripts' `version` file with an
  `ofstream`. It calls `path::DataSyncRecursively` while the stream still holds the file's one
  byte in its buffer. The byte reaches the page cache when the stream closes, and nothing syncs
  it. The commit that added the sync (`b8a032e0`, 2023) says it is there "so that we don't risk
  half written scripts in case of a spontaneous reboot after the installation has begun". After a
  power cut between an install and the next writeback, the version file is empty: the agent logs
  `the version file 0 bytes`. Then every Artifact state's scripts fail ("Error reading the
  version number from the version file"). `disk=cut | run C=4`: the healthy v3 that booted
  cannot be committed; the error path's rollback fails too; Mender names the artifact
  `v3_INCONSISTENT`; and U-Boot returns to v2 (`e06faa5d58198d94`, 2 runs). `C=6`: after the
  broken v4, the rollback after its health check fails, and Mender names `v4_INCONSISTENT`
  while v3 runs (`780103d63e23cd06`, 2 runs). `disk=none | run C=4` fails as `C=4`
  (`006c3b078505d65d`). Artifacts without state scripts pass both schedules.
- **Mender, new as far as the search found: an interrupted commit rolls back and exits 0.**
  `SetStartStateFromStateData` in `src/mender-update/standalone/standalone.cpp` resumes the saved
  state `ArtifactCommit_Enter` on the rollback path. `ResultHandler` in `cli/actions.cpp` reports
  a completed rollback as success. A power cut or a kill inside `ArtifactCommit` leaves that
  state; the next `mender-update commit` (or `resume`) rolls back, prints `Rolled back.` and
  exits 0. When the cut came after the module's `fw_setenv upgrade_available 0`
  (`A=mender.commit_started@3+7:cut`, `d86603abb67442fe`; the kill, `837445ed6cac8646`; 2 runs
  each), U-Boot had made v2 permanent, and the rollback sets `mender_boot_part` back to v1's
  partition while v2 runs. A cut before it (`@3:cut`, `f84173ba7aaf1f25`) leaves v1 booted by
  U-Boot's boot counter, and the commit still exits 0. `+8` passes (`f23c37c27bf666d1`). Without
  state scripts the same happens 8 to 10 ms after the agent's own event, and `+11` passes.
- **mender-artifact 4.4.2, a tooling candidate:** `Scripts.Get` returns the scripts from a Go
  map, so an Artifact with two or more state scripts gets them in a random order, and two runs
  give different bytes. Its `master` merged `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` for the archive times (pull
  request 848) and still has the map. The example's build sorts them
  (`build/mender-artifact-script-order.patch`) and copies each Artifact's outer tar with fixed
  times (`build/retime.go`). Two builds then give the same bytes.

The searches covered Mender's Jira through its public API, mendersoftware/mender's and
mendersoftware/mender-artifact's issues and pull requests, and Mender Hub. They found no report
of either Mender candidate; RESULTS.md lists the terms. Nothing was posted. Neither candidate was
reproduced without hydo, because each cause is plain in a few lines of code.

**The runs.** The Mac runs used this tree's hydo over the 0.3.4 Mac release, one VM at a time, on
the image `explore-ob-mender-ota-devices-arm64.cpio.gz` (sha256 `31df3901bb65554e…`).
`disk=cut | run` runs 8 deployments with 10 reboots and holds every check (`d854f95e3fe00126`,
2 runs). The blind exploration, `hydo explore --seeds 1-24 --workers 1 --strategy process
--reactive fault` with the eight console events, gave 9 failures in 24 schedules, each reproduced
(128 runs per hour). The shrinker gave `disk=cut dseed=4127cc1347fae6ba | run C=16` (the failed
commit, `1b083708a8690666`), `disk=cut dseed=581cc68c71772e2c | run K=device@14+1 C=16`
(`v4_INCONSISTENT`, `49aaa2aa7d4bbe25`) and `disk=cut dseed=c054734a6f769762 | run
A=mender.commit_started:cut` (the commit that exits 0, `7c6a84af1e182056`). An exploration of an
earlier image (seeds 1-17, stopped there) gave the same signatures at seeds 6 and 10. hvx did not
run the example: the x86_64 tools build under emulation in Docker on this Mac, and the first
build stopped at a compiler segmentation fault, the second when the Docker VM stopped. The
x86_64 programs and `hydo.yaml` are untested (open item 136). KVM did not run either.

**What hydo lacked** (RESULTS.md, "What hydo lacked"; AGENTS.md open item 136):

- a power cut at a point a millisecond after an event: the explorer draws a reaction's delay from
  six fixed values, and the example swept the delay by hand;
- reactions while a service starts, where a device's boot service commits or rolls back;
- a restart after a reaction's kill, which keeps the service down until the heal;
- a service's own log in an OK run;
- a `/dev/loop4` in the Mac engine's guest kernel.

**What moved.** Nothing recorded: the example is not in `hydo/onboard/recorded.json`, and no
engine, controller or guest program changed. The new manifests are in the explorer's identity
and corpus goldens (`identity-quick.txt`, `identity-full.txt`, `corpus-full.txt`) and in the
control corpus (`corpus-quick.txt`), re-recorded on this Mac with `HYDO_BLESS=1`. The CLI golden and
`agents_equivalence` pass unchanged.

**Checks** (on this Mac, `main` at `47df6fee` with this milestone on top): `hydo-schedule`'s
`language::`; `hydo-agents`'s `public_content::`; the `hydo` program's `docs::`,
`equivalence::cli_matches_golden` and `agents_equivalence`; `hydo-explore`'s `identity::` (also
with `HYDO_IDENT_FULL=1`) and `corpus::`; `hydo-control`'s `corpus::`; `sh

### Milestone 274 (tentative number) - DONE (guest loops without VM exits on the Mac and KVM engines: on GitHub's runners only the Xeon 6975P-C hosts have a counter of the guest's branches, exact with `0x11c4`, with a skid of 26 branches; the KVM engine's branch tick, `guest.branch_tick`, an opt-in format-1 key, interrupts code without exits after 2^26 user-mode conditional branches at the exact count, so kine's loop gives way; the Mac engine has no such counter, and refuses the key; its spin observer now resolves TigerBeetle's polling loop, so the single replica boots on the Mac; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-16)

**Why.** The Mac and KVM engines count the guest's time in VM exits and deliver interrupts at
exits. A loop that makes no exit gets no timer interrupt. Milestone 256 found kine's watch loop
in k3s: Go's `select` on a closed channel changes the runtime's random state in every pass, so no
spin observer proves a cycle, and k3s stopped with `ERROR boot: SPIN` on both engines. The Mac
could not boot TigerBeetle (open item 13). hvx's PMU branch clock interrupts such loops. The design
is `docs/design/exit-free-loops.md`.

**The options measured.** The interrupt must come at a point that the guest alone fixes, so it
must follow from a count of the guest's work since its last exit.

- A host counter of the guest's branches on KVM. `hv/kvm/pmu/pmuprobe.c` gained the tests `info`
  and `readcost`. The one-off workflow `tmp-exitfree-kvm` (branch of that name, run 43903881480)
  ran it on eight runners. Three Xeon 6975P-C hosts had a counter. With `0x11c4` it counted 3,000
  of 3,000 runs of 1,000 branches and 50 of 50 runs of 10^6 exactly. `0x01c4` counted only taken
  branches, and `0x00c4` the loop's jump too. The overflow stopped the guest 26 branches late (once
  28), never early. A trap-flag step cost 17.0 µs. An exit cost 10.6 µs, 14.4 µs with the counter
  on, and 16.1 µs with a read of it. The Xeon Platinum 8573C host had "no PMU driver", and the four
  AMD hosts (EPYC 7763, 9V45, 9V74) "PMU not available due to virtualization".
- A guest PMU that the guest kernel programs: KVM offers version 2 with 8 counters on the 6975P-C,
  but its overflow interrupt needs KVM's in-kernel local APIC, which the engine does not use, and
  it has the same skid. Not built.
- Single steps from the last exit: a stretch is known to be long only from the host-timed kick, so
  the count must cover what a fast host runs in 5 ms, about 2.5·10^7 instructions. One tick would
  take about 425 s on the runners (17 µs per step) and 60 s on the Mac (2.4 µs): not built.
- The Mac: no counter of the guest. The guest PMU traps with nothing behind it (`hv/hvm/PROBE.md`),
  the host counters count host work too (Milestone 48), and the emulated guest PMU needs guest EL2,
  which an M2 lacks.

**Built: the branch tick on KVM** (`hydo/crates/hydo-kvm/src/branches.rs`, the `bt_` functions of
`vmm.rs`, `PerfBranches` in `sys.rs`). `guest.branch_tick: true` (a format-1 addition, the schema
and MANIFEST.md "Loops without VM exits") makes `hydo build` write the period 2^26 into
`/etc/hydo/branch-tick`. hydo-engine passes it as `HYDO_BRANCH_TICK`; the Mac engine refuses the
image before any VM ("guest.branch_tick needs a counter of the guest's branches, which the Mac
engine does not have"); hvx ignores it.

- The rule: after 2^26 retired conditional branches in user mode of one vCPU without one of its
  exits, the engine stops the vCPU right after the branch that makes the count, and treats the
  point as a proven loop. The clock jumps to its next event, as at an idle HLT; with several vCPUs
  the turn ends when another vCPU can run.
- The count: a pinned `perf_event` (`exclude_host`, `exclude_kernel`) on the engine's thread, read
  after every `KVM_RUN`, its difference given to the vCPU that ran. An exit sets the vCPU's count to
  0, so the count is in no snapshot and no fingerprint. The raw event is `0x11c4` from Ice Lake on
  and `0x01c4` for Skylake to Comet Lake; AMD is refused.
- The overflow: the watchdog's first kick of a stretch arms it 256 branches before the tick
  (`HYDO_KVM_BRANCH_MARGIN`); its signal is the watchdog's. A count past the tick ends the run as a
  SPIN.
- The landing: trap-flag steps to the exact count. `PUSHF`'s pushed word loses the flag; `SYSCALL`
  and `POPF` are run over to a breakpoint; breakpoints at the guest's #DE, #UD, #GP and #PF
  handlers let the engine take the flag out of a fault's frame. `INT`, `INT3`, `UD2`, `IRET`,
  `SYSENTER` and `SYSRET` end the run as a SPIN.
- The observer: with the tick on, a kick whose count advanced skips the spin observer, and a look
  whose steps advanced it proves nothing, so a cycle with branches is always the tick's.

**Built: the Mac observer at the return address** (`hydo/crates/hydo-hvm/src/spin.rs`). The Mac
observer compared the pages a pass writes, so TigerBeetle's loop was a cycle it could prove. Its
breakpoint sat at the kick's instruction, inside `memset`, which one frame calls twice per pass;
consecutive arrivals never matched, and every look gave up after 64. After 16 arrivals without a
repeat a look now moves its breakpoint to `x30`, up to three times. Where a look is armed decides
only whether a cycle is found, not the canonical state it is resolved at.

**Proof on the Mac** (an M2 Pro; the 0.3.4 Mac release's guest files and this milestone's
programs; one VM at a time). TigerBeetle 0.17.9's single replica (`hydo/hydo-single.yaml` without
`cpu: v3`, `--set tb=0.17.9-aarch64`, image `4f8e200c…`): before the change `ERROR boot: SPIN`
(43 looks, 36 gave up, at exit 18,043); after it, each schedule twice from a fresh boot, every
command and the three invariants OK, one fingerprint per schedule: `disk=none | run`
`ac51e985c3361285`, `K=tigerbeetle_0@5+3` `35357e63660b2d80`, `disk=cut | run C=10`
`dc817c32c558ba2c`, `P=tigerbeetle_0@5+5` `6908fd6ad74d193a`, `T=6:3600` `290308a7857401d1`. The
first run resolved 175 loops and moved to a return address 160 times. An image with
`guest.branch_tick` was refused before any VM. `hydo-bench rebaseline --check --platform hvm
--only hvm/redis,hvm/ledger,hvm/ledger-spin --jobs 1`: 16 of 16 schedules with the recorded
fingerprints and verdicts, the counter-loop example `hvm/ledger-spin` among them.

**Proof on KVM** (the one-off workflow `tmp-exitfree-kvm`, branch of that name, deleted after the
runs; the published 0.3.4 Linux release, this milestone's `hydo`, and the containers kernels of
Milestone 256's run 43698484545, whose bytes are the pins).

- Nothing moved. The 0.3.4 release's own `hydo` built the quickstart image with the recorded bytes
  `f3a152d6…` (`kvm/release-redis`), and this milestone's `hydo` ran it without the key. In runs
  43910568187, 43916305446 and 43917522895, all 24 jobs gave the published values: on Intel
  (Xeon 6975P-C, Xeon Platinum 8370C) `2d059466fb87a253` and `8af0c14d4ec2c470` (`disk=cut | run
  C=11 R=everysec`, VIOLATION), on AMD (EPYC 7763, 9V45, 9V74) the recorded `fb237d7eebbf8b83` and
  `6a76d87a7dd2d6f2`. On every host with a counter the same image with `guest.branch_tick` gave OK
  and one fingerprint twice.
- kine's loop gives way. k3s-lease's `containers/hydo.yaml` with the key on 2 vCPUs: without the
  key the boot stopped with Milestone 256's `ERROR boot: SPIN`; with it, 32 to 63 ticks per boot,
  each landed by about 1,500 trap-flag steps (90 ms) with the default margin. Run 43913419444, on
  five 6975P-C hosts, gave one fingerprint (`a0a7c82d991b1b99`) on every run, with margins of 256
  and 3000 branches (up to 18,136 steps in one landing) and with `HYDO_KVM_DIAG`. Its verdict was

- k3s on KVM (run 43917522895, one Xeon 6975P-C host; the other seven jobs were AMD, without a

**Goldens and what moved.** Nothing recorded moved: an image without the key builds the same
bytes and runs the same code paths. Re-recorded on this Mac: `hydo/schema/project-v1.json`, the

### Milestone 275 (tentative number) - DONE (function fuzzing from contracts: `hydo fuzz` tests one Rust function at a time, natively, with inputs generated from its `requires` and `input` lines and each call judged by its `ensures`; a broken clause or a panic shrinks to a small input that replays; it found the contracts-ledger example's planted bug from the contract alone and one candidate in Qdrant's `common` crate; the run inside the VM with faults is designed, not built; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-16)

**What and why.** The same `// hydo: requires` and `ensures` comments that a whole-system run
checks at every call (Milestones 241, 255 and 260) now also drive the testing of single
functions. `requires` and the `input` lines describe the valid inputs, `ensures` judges each
result, and a panic, a call that does not return, or a process that ends is a finding too. A
property that needs a call, such as a round trip, is a function that returns `bool` with
`// hydo: ensures result`. The design is `docs/design/function-fuzzing.md`.

**The prototype.** `hydo fuzz [CRATE_DIR] [--fn NAME] [--cases N] [--seed S] [--input ...]
[--release] [--list]`, in the new module `fuzz` of `hydo-contracts`:

- hydo reads the package with `cargo metadata` and its sources as text (comments and literals
  masked, brackets matched): each contracted function's signature, its `impl` block, the
  crate's structures and type aliases. It refuses generic, `async` and trait functions, and
  parameters of types it cannot generate (floating-point values, enumerations, references
  inside structures), with one reason each.
- It copies the package to `--out` (default `hydo-out/fuzz`), writes the copy's manifest from
  `cargo metadata` (with the workspace's lock file, profiles, patches and toolchain file), and
  writes one test module per function on the line of the function's closing brace. The module
  is a child of the function's own module, so private items and binary crates work, and every
  line keeps its number. `cargo test --no-run` builds it.
- hydo generates the inputs from a seed. The first input is the smallest values, the second the
  largest, the rest random with edges: type and domain bounds, 0, 1, -1, the clauses' constants
  and their neighbours. Pairs of paths that a clause compares are made equal or one apart in
  1 of 4 inputs. Inputs that break `requires` are not run.
- The harness reads each input as text, calls the function under `catch_unwind`, and writes the
  result and the `&mut` parameters after the call, or the panic's location and message. A panic
  in the standard library is placed at the crate's own frame of the backtrace. hydo judges the
  clauses on those values with the language's meaning (`old()`, reads through references after
  the call, exact integers).
- Each failure kind shrinks once (integers towards 0 or the domain's bound by halving steps,
  lists and strings shorter, options `None`), and the smallest input runs once more. The same
  seed writes the same `fuzz.json`; `--input 'name = value, ...'` replays one input.
- An `input` line may name a field path (`input l.balance in 0..=1_000_000`); the plan's compiler
  checks only its root.

**Proof on the contracts-ledger example.** `hydo fuzz hydo/onboard/examples/contracts-ledger/rust
--toolchain 1.90.0`, 1,000 inputs of `apply`, 5.1 s with the build, the example's files
unchanged:

- `ensures req_id > old(l.last_req) || l.balance == old(l.balance)` broke on 96 inputs; the
  smallest is `l = Ledger { balance: 1, last_req: 1, applied: 0 }, c = Conn { last_req: 0 },
  req_id = 1, amount = 1`. This is the planted bug: a request that the ledger applied is applied
  again on a new connection. The whole-system run reached it only under a pause or a lost answer.
- `ensures req_id <= old(l.last_req) || l.balance == old(l.balance) - amount` broke on 159
  inputs, with a connection that saw a higher request id than the ledger, which the server never
  makes. The contract lacks `requires c.last_req <= l.last_req`.
- Two panics: `attempt to subtract with overflow` at `src/main.rs:46` (a debit larger than the
  balance, 180 inputs) and `attempt to add with overflow` at line 48 (`applied` at
  `u64::MAX`, 13 inputs).
- `ensures result == l.balance` held on the 807 calls that returned. A second run wrote the same
  `fuzz.json` (`16c3e7aa3b43882da574d275bbe29dac56058219114d45bc4597c51b9c1fb9a4`), and the first
  smallest input replayed with `--input`.

**Proof on Qdrant.** Contracts on 12 functions of Qdrant's `lib/common/common` at `222b2e44`
(the commit of the example `qdrant-flaky-10200`): 10 of Qdrant's own and two round trips in the
test module of `delta_pack.rs`. The contracts are
`docs/design/function-fuzzing/qdrant-contracts.patch`. With Rust 1.99.0, 1,000 inputs each,
7.8 s with a built copy:

- Nine functions held every clause: `bytes_to_human`, `thread_count_for_hnsw`,
  `compress_sequence`, both round trips, `prefetch_windows`, and `U24::new_wrapped`, `get` and
  `try_from`.
- `default_cpu_budget_unallocated` broke `ensures result <= 0` for `num_cpu =
  9223372036854775808` (`num_cpu as isize` wraps). No machine has that many CPUs.
- `delta_pack` panicked on `[1, 0]`: its comment says that the input is sorted, which the
  language cannot state.
- `decompress_sequence` panicked on `[57]`, a header that asks for 65 bits per value and that
  `compress_sequence` never writes. `StoredSparseVector::decode_untrusted_bytes` says that a
  malformed blob from outside the storage is a user error and never a crash, and it reaches this
  function. The test profile stops at a debug assertion. With `--release` no input panicked,
  and the decoder returns values without an error. What the caller does with them was not
  checked. Nothing was posted upstream.

**Inside the VM.** Designed only (docs/design/function-fuzzing.md, "Inside the virtual
machine"): the harness built for the guest, a runner that makes an image per batch and reads
the answers from the console, and the schedule's faults (`disk=ioerr`, `T=`, `P=workload`,
`pct=`). A hidden `fsync` error or a lost write shows only after a recovery boot, which needs a
second phase of the harness. Open item 139.

**Tests and checks.** New: `hydo-contracts`'s `fuzz::` (10 tests, with one end-to-end run of the
fixture `tests/fuzz-crate`, five functions with four planted bugs, about 5 s). The CLI's main

--all-targets -- -D warnings`; every test of `hydo-contracts` and of the `hydo` program;

### Milestone 281 (tentative number) - DONE (the onboarding playbook: one written process for every onboarding of a real project, from the choice of a target to the upstream report and the retro, built from the onboardings of Milestones 215 to 275; skill 2.3.2 links it; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-16)

**What and why.** About 15 onboardings of real projects (Formance Ledger, Lago, Blnk, Temporal,
Valkey, River, Hatchet, Saleor, NATS JetStream, etcd, TigerBeetle, the web-shop example, Memos,
RAUC, SWUpdate and Mender) each found their own way through the same steps. The lessons were in
the examples' `RESULTS.md` files and in the working rules of the maintainer who ran them. The
new page `docs/ONBOARDING-PLAYBOOK.md` writes them down as one how-to guide that a maintainer
of hydo or an agent follows from top to bottom. The skill writes the `hydo/` folder; the
playbook adds what comes before and after it.

**The page's sections.**

1. Picking a target: GitHub issues, a simple setup, a promise about state, and a reproduction
   with released hydo; the red flags (a tracker that needs an account, a device-style setup,
   memory over the guest's limit, kernel features, documented behaviour).
2. The promises of each type of system, with the rule shapes that worked: queues and job
   runners, ledgers and billing, key-value stores and databases, update tools and devices, and
   web apps.
3. Which faults found which findings, from power cuts to storage faults.
4. The five phases with their time limits (scouting 45 minutes with no VM, setup to a first
   clean run 3 hours, exploration and shrinking 4 to 5 hours, the write-up 1 hour), the two
   checkpoints, and the commands.
5. Judging a finding: the labels, the required duplicate search with its phrases recorded,
   separating the faults, the conditional native reproduction, and `hydo versions`.
6. The write-up: the sections of `RESULTS.md`, the regressions, the milestone, the open items,
   and the checks before a merge.
7. The upstream report: its fixed format with the one sentence about hydo, where to post,
   attachments by hand in the browser, and following the threads.
8. The retro in a fixed form, with reference values from the onboardings.
9. Throughput of hvx, the Mac engine and GitHub's KVM runners, and sharding by seed ranges.
10. Fifteen common setup problems with their fixes, from the examples' lists of what hydo lacked.

**The five lessons that matter most.**

- The generic rule over the client's acknowledged operations found more than any domain rule.
  In Lago it failed in all 11 runs that broke a business result, and in Formance and Blnk it
  was the only rule that saw a lost acknowledged operation.
- The first failures of an exploration are mostly the rules' own mistakes: five kinds in River,
  all 10 failures of Valkey's first exploration, and TigerBeetle's false loss at every power
  cut.
- Clock steps against durations measured on the wall clock gave the most new upstream reports
  (Valkey, Temporal, River), so the clock audit runs before the exploration.
- A crashed consumer that held acknowledged work lost it in Hatchet, Saleor and Lago, so a kill
  aimed between the acknowledgement and the completion belongs in every queue's exploration.
- Disk errors and lying disks broke hydo's disk model, not the systems, in every onboarding
  that drew them; `--durable-only` keeps them out once that is seen.

**Other changes.** `ci/vale.sh` checks the new page (60 documents). The skill
`plugin/skills/onboard/SKILL.md` links it in one line, with an absolute link because the
published plugin has no `docs/` folder; the skill's version is 2.3.2 in its frontmatter,
`plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`. `docs/ONBOARD.md`
links it under "Where to read more". The CLI golden and `agents_equivalence` were re-recorded
for the skill's new text and version.

**Proof.** On this Mac: `sh ci/vale.sh` (no findings); `cargo test -p hydo --test it docs::`,
`equivalence::` and `agents_equivalence::`; `cargo test -p hydo-agents --test it skill_check::`
and `public_content::`; `cargo test -p hydo-schedule --test it language::`. No VM ran: the page
cites the recorded runs of the examples. Nothing recorded moved: no engine, image, guest program
or example file changed.

### Milestone 280 (tentative number) - DONE (an evaluation of `hydo fuzz` as a Rust developer new to hydo would meet it, on six crates from crates.io: semver, base64, fixedbitset, memchr, num-integer and byteorder; the harness does not build on `#![no_std]` crates or on a structure with private fields in another module, runs that test nothing report `every clause held`, and short generated values miss real code paths; two bug candidates, nothing posted; the verdict is that a developer would not keep using it yet; no code of the feature changed; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-16)

**What and why.** Milestone 275 built `hydo fuzz` and proved it on hydo's own example and on
Qdrant. This milestone asks whether a developer who has never used hydo would keep using it.
The evaluator learned the feature only from `hydo fuzz --help`, `hydo guide`, and the design
document that the help names. They wrote contracts on 8 to 14 functions per crate from each
crate's documentation, and ran `hydo fuzz` natively on this Mac with Rust 1.90.0 and hydo at
`9294778e`. The full report is `docs/design/function-fuzzing-evaluation.md`.

**What happened per crate.**

- semver 1.0.28: `--list` said `can be fuzzed` for the five functions, and the harness did not
  build. It names the private fields of `Identifier`, a structure of another module. The nine
  properties ran; four of them tested nothing, because 0 of 2,000 generated strings were
  versions.
- base64 0.23.1: four functions and seven properties held. `Alphabet::new` with `requires
  len(alphabet) == 64` ran 2 inputs after 49,998 rejections and still exited 0.
- fixedbitset 0.5.9: `#![no_std]` stops the harness's build until the crate says
  `#![cfg_attr(not(test), no_std)]`. `insert` and `grow` were refused (a pointer field). Ten
  properties held. `with_capacity` without an `input` line ran for 23 minutes, at up
  to 2 GB per call, with no output, until it was stopped by hand. With an `input` line it
  held in 2 s.
- memchr 2.8.3: five functions and seven properties held, 20,000 inputs each in 4 s. A planted
  bug in the 64-byte vector loop was caught only by a property that builds a long haystack.
  memchr's own quickcheck tests caught it too.
- num-integer 0.1.47: both contracted functions are generic and were refused. Eleven
  properties over concrete types found the known negative gcd (rust-num/num-integer#55) and
  one candidate.
- byteorder 1.5.0: a trait implementation's method was fuzzed, and a default method of a
  trait was refused. Six properties over `Cursor` and a failing writer found one candidate.

**Bug candidates.** Each was searched for in the crate's open and closed issues; nothing was
posted.

1. num-integer 0.1.47: `i64::MIN.nth_root(1)` panics with `attempt to negate with overflow` in
   a debug build, although the documentation allows a negative value with an odd root. The
   answer `i64::MIN` exists, and a release build returns it. No issue names it.
2. byteorder 1.5.0: `ReadBytesExt::read_uint` panics for `nbytes` of 0 or more than 8, while
   its documentation lists only the errors of `read_exact`. Issue #230 is the same kind of gap
   for `write_uint`; no issue names this one.

**The problems, in order.** The harness does not build on `#![no_std]` crates (three of six) or
on a private field of another module, and one such function stops every function. `every
clause held` hides runs that tested nothing. Strings and lists have at most 16 elements, and
`input` takes no length or character set. A run with a large size parameter looks hung. Most of
a crate's API is generic or a trait. The replay line drops `--release`, `--json` starts with a
progress line, a panic in macro code is placed at the harness, and `hydo guide` has no topic on
fuzzing. Each has a fix proposal in the report, and the first five are in open item 139.

**The guide.** `hydo guide manifest` (MANIFEST.md, section on contracts) gained a list of the
limits that a first run meets, so `cli.jsonl` was re-recorded for `guide manifest` on both
platforms.

**Tests and checks.** On this Mac: `sh ci/vale.sh` on its documents and on the new document; the `hydo`
program's `docs::` and `equivalence::`; `hydo-schedule`'s `language::`; `hydo-agents`'s
`public_content::`. Nothing recorded moved: no engine, image, guest program, or example file
changed.

### Milestone 276 (tentative number) - DONE (open item 136's hvx part: the Mender example on hvx with `hydo.yaml`, the eMMC in a file on the data disk; the x86_64 tools built on the Mac under QEMU, with a retry of each compile command and no mender-artifact in the emulated image, and two builds that differ in `mender-update` because crashed CMake checks turn libarchive features off; finding 1's two regressions give their Mac verdicts, finding 2's two give their violation in the earlier form, and a cut 69 to 87 ms after the event gives the Mac's form; one fingerprint over two runs for each; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-16)

**What was asked.** Milestone 272 ran the Mender example (`hydo/onboard/examples/mender`) on the
Mac engine only, because the x86_64 tools did not build in Docker on this Mac. Build them, run
`hydo.yaml` and the four saved regressions on hvx, each twice, and say whether each regression
gives its Mac verdict with one fingerprint. If a timing-sensitive one does not reach its bug,
scan the points near it.

**The build.** `sh build.sh amd64` builds the x86_64 tools under QEMU's user emulation in Colima
(2 vCPUs, 8 GiB). There the compilers end with a segmentation fault at a random source file now
and then. `cc1plus` stopped the Mender build three times at three different files. `cc1` stopped
libarchive's once, and Go's compiler stopped mender-artifact's at once. Two changes, both in the
example's build:

- `build/retry.sh` (`retry` in the image) runs a compile command again, up to 10 times. make then
  builds only the files it has not built yet. A compiler that crashed wrote no object file, so the
  program's bytes are those of one run. Every `make` and `cc` of `build/Dockerfile` runs through
  it.
- The Dockerfile has a stage `tools` without mender-artifact, which writes the Artifacts on the
  build host only. `build.sh` builds the other architecture's image to that stage.

Results of the build:

- The arm64 tools of the changed Dockerfile have the bytes of Milestone 272's (every file of the
  old image's `/out` compared).
- Two x86_64 builds gave the same busybox, `fw_printenv`, loopdio, `mdb_dump`, mender-flash and
  rootfs-image module. They gave two `mender-update` programs, `e3bcd860…` (the first) and
  `ad400115…` (the second), and with them other slot images and Artifacts. A third build of
  the Mender step, on the second build's libraries and without a compiler crash, gave the
  second's bytes in every object file.
- The cause is libarchive's `config.h`. A check of CMake compiles a small program, and a check
  whose compiler crashed reports a missing feature. The first build's libarchive (a layer
  cached by an earlier attempt on this Mac) lacks `HAVE_OPENAT`, `HAVE_MBRTOWC` and
  `HAVE_TZSET`. The second's lacks `HAVE_WCHAR_T`, `SIZEOF_WCHAR_T` and `SIZEOF_INT`. So an
  x86_64 build on a Mac gives the same bytes only by chance (open item 136). A build on an
  x86_64 host with Docker was not tried: the bare-metal machine has no Docker.

**The runs on hvx.** On the bare-metal machine, in the tree `~/hydo-mender-hvx`, with `hydo`,
`hydo-hvx` and `hydo-build` built from this tree over the 0.3.4 Linux release (`04ccae1f…`),
one VM at a time through `~/bin/hvx-run`. The loop module came from `fetch-modules.sh`. Two
builds of `hydo.yaml` gave the image `explore-ob-mender-ota-disk.img` with the sha256
`6d46a6a1b4ea1a6d…`; with `--set artifacts=plain` it is `d12f74e89b593aef…`.

| schedule | verdict on hvx | fingerprint, 2 runs each |
|---|---|---|
| `disk=cut \| run` | OK, 7 checks held, v5 after 10 reboots | `43a98c8ee471b072` |
| `C=4` (regression) | the Mac's verdict, VIOLATION `[mender.commit_permanent]` with `v3_INCONSISTENT` | `a5450ade5f9535cc` |
| `C=6` (regression) | the Mac's verdict, VIOLATION `[mender.state_matches_slots]` with `v4_INCONSISTENT` | `bc2380c4573776f9` |
| `C=4`, `artifacts=plain` | OK | `2323dea1290f9937` |
| `C=6`, `artifacts=plain` | OK | `2a3e428b780f6fd5` |
| `A=mender.commit_started@3+7:cut` (regression) | VIOLATION `[mender.commit_permanent]`: the commit exited 0, Mender's artifact is v1, and v1 runs | `216a4d3c4eaf41f7` |
| `A=mender.commit_started@3+7:kill-device` (regression) | the row before's violation | `a6ad6d8ee0e65e9f` |
| `A=mender.commit_started@3:cut` | the row before's violation | `85acf4397831368d` |
| `A=mender.commit_started@3+80:cut` | the Mac's `+7` violation: the commit exited 0 on v2, and U-Boot boots v1 next | `45683a8ad6f64cfa` (3 runs) |
| `A=mender.commit_started@3+80:kill-device` | the same | `d129e303c1b8e8db` |

So finding 1 gives its Mac verdicts on hvx. Finding 2's regressions break the same check on
hvx, so `expect: violation` holds on both engines. But they break it in the earlier form: 7 ms
after the event, hvx has not reached the module's `fw_setenv upgrade_available 0`. A scan of
the delay, with one run each, gave these results:

- the earlier form at 1 to 63 and 65 to 68 ms;
- the Mac's form at 64 ms and at 69 to 87 ms;
- OK at 88 to 1,000 ms;
- at 2,000 and 5,000 ms, a step that ended before the cut was due.

So finding 2's window is about 88 ms of guest time on hvx, against about 8 ms on the Mac. Why
64 ms gives the later form and 65 to 68 ms do not was not investigated. The regressions keep the
Mac's 7 ms. The section "On hvx" of the example's RESULTS.md has the tables.

The table's values come from the first x86_64 build. The second build's image (`c7d80b2a…`)
gave the same verdicts for the fault-free run and the four regressions, with other fingerprints
(`06c8329b0209afa7`, `f98d56872f1b5cf3`, `6e23979a26e77df2`, `86a3b37807b3f007`,
`89b1a9247bd07ff8`), each twice. Its later form of finding 2 came at 65, 70 and 75 ms, and
80 ms gave OK. So the window depends on the program's bytes; 70 ms reaches it with both builds.
