### Milestone 273 (tentative number) - DONE (a second web app for the walk through the pages: Vikunja 2.8.0, a self-hosted task manager on SQLite, onboarded with `hydo compose` and explored blind on hvx with walks and backend faults; the walk records the ids of a REST API's answers, and `watch.failures_of` matches the method; two new candidates, not posted: a power cut loses the tasks Vikunja acknowledged in the last seconds, because its SQLite runs in WAL mode with the driver's `synchronous=NORMAL`, and a task of the quick action bar that the server refuses is lost and leaves its rejection unhandled; what the walk lacked on this app; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-16)

The user asked for a second popular open-source web app for `browser.explore`, after Memos
(Milestone 258), with a real backend and data whose integrity users care about. The example is
`hydo/onboard/examples/vikunja`, and its RESULTS.md has every run and the duplicate searches.
Every hvx run used the 0.3.3 Linux release with this milestone's `hydo`, in a folder of its own on
the bare-metal machine, one VM at a time.

**The choice.** The candidates weighed were Actual Budget (about 30,000 stars), Docmost (about
22,000), Mealie (about 14,000), Linkding (about 11,000) and Vikunja (about 6,100). Actual keeps
the budget in the browser, syncs binary messages, and needs a secure context, which the guest's
plain HTTP is not. Docmost saves a page's text over a WebSocket that the walk does not see.
Linkding saves with HTML forms answered by a redirect, which the walk does not record. Vikunja
was chosen: one Go server with its frontend built in, SQLite by default in the documentation's
Docker example, a REST API, and tasks whose loss a user notices.

**What the walk needed (built here).**

- The acknowledged writes of a REST API. The walk wrote words for resource names of the shape
  `memos/<id>` only, and Vikunja's answers name a new task by a number (`{"tasks":[{"id":6,...}]}`).
  Since this milestone each acknowledged write also adds `<METHOD>:<path>=<id>` for every id of
  the objects that its JSON answer returns (its `id`, or the `id` of each object in a field), or
  `<METHOD>:<path>` without an id: `POST:/api/v2/projects/1/tasks/bulk=6`,
  `DELETE:/api/v2/tasks/6` (`walk.mjs`, `idsOf`). The old words stay, so Memos's rule reads the
  same words as before.
- The writes of an API whose reads use the same paths. Vikunja reads a task with `GET
  /api/v2/tasks/4` and saves it with `PATCH` on the same path, so a pattern over the path cannot
  name the writes. `watch.failures_of` now matches the path or `<METHOD> <path>` (`walk.mjs` and
  `check.mjs`), so `^(POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE) /api/v[12]/(projects|tasks|labels|teams|filters)`
  names them. A pattern that matched a path matches it as before. The validator still compiles
  the pattern with Rust's `regex`, so a lookahead such as `(?!user/token)` is refused.

The reference is MANIFEST.md, section "A walk through the pages that hydo makes", and `hydo guide
web-apps`; the design is the section "Faults and rules" of `docs/design/ui-exploration.md`.

**The onboarding.** `hydo compose` of the documentation's Compose file started
`hydo/onboard/examples/vikunja/hydo/`. The image runs as uid 1000, and the documentation has
`chown 1000` of both volumes: without it the server stopped at its start ("Could not init file
handler: ... permission denied"), so the service's `setup:` gives both volumes to uid 1000. The
workload became `browser.explore` (6 steps of 12 actions, the account's registration as
`setup`). Two rules in `page-rules/vikunja.mjs` read the walk's words and the database, with
`node:sqlite` in the browser's service:

- `vikunja.saved_work_survives`: every task, project, comment, label, saved filter and team that
  Vikunja answered as created is in its table, unless an acknowledged write deleted it.
- `vikunja.kanban_matches_done`: on every Kanban view with its own buckets, each task is in one
  bucket, and in the done bucket exactly when it is done.

`disk=none | run I=1` saved five tasks and held, with one fingerprint twice (`e6e35a2ab56471e5`).

**The blind exploration of all faults.** `hydo explore --seeds 1-20` (kills, network faults,
power cuts and disk faults) ran in 106 minutes with one worker. Four schedules failed, and each
reproduced:

- Finding 1 (new candidate), seed 18: a power cut lost a task that Vikunja had answered as
  saved. `disk=cut dseed=1120b3d00955f032 | run N=vikunja@0-1:reorder,29%,delay,17ms C=6
  I=d94729ae6c47c1f6` shrank in 40 runs to `disk=cut dseed=1120b3d00955f032 | run C=6
  I=d94729ae6c47c1f6,n4,x0.0-3,x1.0-3,x2.0-3,x3.0-3,x4.0-3,x5.0,x5.1,x5.2`, a walk of one action
  after the registration: it types a task and presses Enter, and the power is cut after the step
  (`14dd446ea98dd932` twice). Vikunja opens SQLite in WAL mode and sets no `synchronous`, and
  `mattn/go-sqlite3` compiles SQLite with `SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_SYNCHRONOUS=1`, so a commit is
  not synced until a checkpoint. The WAL mode came with commit `98f2893f`, first released in
  v2.2.0. On the second image, `disk=none | run C=5 I=1` lost the two tasks of step 4 (tasks 4
  and 5) and kept the three of steps 0, 1 and 3 (`b9c4ca304679f322` twice).
- Finding 2 (new candidate, small), seed 9: under disk I/O errors the quick action bar's "New
  task" failed, the page left `ApiError: unexpected error occurred` unhandled, and the typed
  title was gone. `onEnter` calls `doCmd()` without a `catch`, and `newTask` does not catch the
  create's error. The shrink took 81 runs (`65f8e47405e63d25` twice). A Playwright test with a
  `page.route` 500, `walk-repro/quick-add-new-task.spec.ts`, fails the same way on this Mac
  against Vikunja in Docker.
- Seeds 1 and 8 ended in ERROR: under disk I/O errors the rule could not read its copy of the
  database. Not findings.

**The exploration with every fault kind but the lying disk.** `hydo explore --seeds 21-60
--new-faults --durable-only` ran in 114 minutes on the third image (14 kills, 19 network faults,
2 one-way network faults, 16 pauses, 10 clock steps and 19 power cuts). Five schedules failed,
all with finding 1 (seeds 24, 49, 55, 59 and 60), and lost 9 of the 21 objects that they had
saved. The 35 passing walks saved 65 objects, and all were in the database at the end. The five
failures had one signature, so one shrink ran: seed 24, in 47 runs, to `disk=cut
dseed=aac8c00000a81e44 | run C=4
I=772ff9303a3b7ac5,n2,x0.0,x1.0,x1.1,x2.0,x2.1,x3.0,x3.1,x4.0,x4.1,x5.0,x5.1`
(`a6607ec0eb8fce80` twice). Its one action types a task with Markdown, and Vikunja's quick add
makes a label and three tasks of it; the cut loses all four. The Kanban rule held in all 40.

The second image's exploration of the same seeds was stopped after 5 schedules. Its rule named
every lost object in the verdict, so losses of four and of two objects had two signatures, and
each would have been shrunk on its own. The third image prints the list on a line before the
verdict, whose words stay the same.

**What the walk lacked on Vikunja** (open item 137): it never marked a task done, because
Vikunja's done check boxes are hidden inputs that take no trial click; it did not sign in again
after the session ended; and the recording replay of a walk that a power cut ends recorded
nothing. Under disk I/O errors the rule could not read its copy of the database.

Both candidates were searched for in Vikunja's issues and pull requests (the terms are in
RESULTS.md), and none names them. Finding 1's cause is plain in the code, so no reproduction
without hydo was made. Nothing was posted.

**A mistake in the runs.** The runs went through chain scripts, each a list of commands run one
after another, and a chain waited for the line that ends another chain's log. One chain was
stopped and started again with a new list, and the stopped one still wrote its end line into the
same log. The chain that waited for it then started five runs of the second image while the new
chain's own runs and the start of an exploration ran: for about ten minutes two VMs of this
milestone ran at once on the shared machine. Each run had its own VM, and the minimal schedule
of finding 1 gave one fingerprint on both of its runs then; the `disk=none` form, `disk=cut |
run C=6 I=1` and the quick-add schedule ran once each. The script now reads its list once and gives every command
`/dev/null` as its input.

**Goldens, tests and what moved.** Nothing recorded moved: Vikunja is not in `recorded.json`,
and a manifest without `browser.explore` builds the same image as before. Every walking image
gets other bytes (the walker), so the walks' fingerprints change. Re-recorded on this Mac for the
new example manifest: the explorer's identity goldens (quick and full) and corpus golden (full;
the quick one did not change), and the core controller's corpus golden. The full goldens only
gained the new manifest's lines; the quick identity golden samples every fifth manifest, so its
sample moved by one. Re-recorded: the CLI's two `guide manifest` answers (MANIFEST.md changed)
and `hydo/schema/project-v1.json` (the description of `failures_of`). New test: the expansion's
unit test takes a `failures_of` over `<METHOD> <path>`.

**Checks.** On this Mac, on `main` at `8b1f87c3` with this milestone on top (the runs above used
a tree on `47df6fee`, before Milestones 270 to 281): `cargo fmt --all --check`; `cargo clippy
--workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; every test of `hydo-config`; every unit test of
`hydo-manifest` and its `format::`; `hydo-explore`'s `identity::` and `corpus::` (also with
`HYDO_IDENT_FULL=1`); `hydo-control`'s `corpus::`; `hydo-schedule`'s `language::`;
`hydo-agents`'s `public_content::`; the `hydo` program's `docs::`,
`equivalence::cli_matches_golden` and `agents_equivalence`; `sh ci/consolidate-tests.sh --check`
and `sh ci/vale.sh`.

### Milestone 278 (tentative number) - DONE (Dragonfly 2.1.0 with one primary and two replicas on hvx; a new Dragonfly candidate: Dragonfly loads the snapshot whose files have the latest modification time, so after a backward step of the wall clock a restart, also a clean shutdown that saves first, loads a snapshot from before the step and loses every write since; found blind and shrunk to one clock step; a power cut loses snapshots that SAVE acknowledged, known as dragonflydb/dragonfly#8646; Dragonfly's Lua interpreter needs AVX, a known requirement; REPLTAKEOVER kept its promise; what hydo lacked; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-16)

**In short.** `hydo/onboard/examples/dragonfly` (RESULTS.md) runs Dragonfly 2.1.0, the newest
release, from its official image as one primary and two replicas on `network: bridge`, imported
with `hydo compose` from the example's own Compose file. Each server runs two threads, so a key
space has two shards and a transaction spans both; snapshots use the default file name
`dump-{timestamp}`. The Go client `dfc` writes keys and waits for the replicas (`WAIT 2 500`),
sets three keys in one `MULTI`/`EXEC` or one Lua script, sets keys with expiries, and makes the
primary save a snapshot: `SAVE`, `BGSAVE`, or `SHUTDOWN` and the wait for the restart. With
`--set takeover=yes` a serial driver moves the primary with `REPLTAKEOVER 10` and checks the
documented promise at once: the new primary holds every key the old primary held just before.
Four final rules check that a write a completed snapshot holds survives, that transactions are
whole on every server, that the replicas converge, and that no server returns a key after its
expiry. Error logs are findings (glog's `E` and `F` lines).

**What was found.**

- **Dragonfly, new as far as the search found: a restart after a backward clock step loads an
  older snapshot.** `FileSnapshotStorage::LoadPath` in `src/server/detail/snapshot_storage.cc`
  sorts the files that match `--dbfilename` by `last_modified` and loads the latest. After a step
  of D seconds back, every snapshot of the next D seconds has an older time than the last one
  from before the step. So a restart in that time loads the old snapshot, also after a clean
  `SHUTDOWN` that saves first, and every write since is lost although a `SAVE` answered `OK`.
  The name's `{timestamp}` comes from the same clock. Dragonfly's `main` has the same choice.
  hydo found it blind in 25 of 120 schedules of the default image (16 without a power cut), from
  the fourth schedule on. The shrinker reduced it to one step of 18 s back, `disk=none
  dseed=9836c546baaf0b5 | run T=8:-18 W=48c2cbb5,p5,q2,r300,oanytime_read`: 17 of 21 saved writes
  lost (`4e00723d70706c54`, 2 runs), and without the step OK (`31d217a68cbef3d0`). After a kill
  instead of a shutdown, `K=df1@21+9 T=12:-150` loses a saved key before its expiry
  (`ec06181c11e9c87d`; without the step `d8e3cca2145b739f`). In ex1's shrink (`T=10:-81000`),
  `hydo inspect exec` showed the restarted primary load `dump-2026-11-16T00:00:05`, although it
  had saved `dump-2026-11-15T01:30:06` and `01:30:07` after the step.
- **Dragonfly, known: a power cut loses snapshots that `SAVE` acknowledged.** The files are
  renamed into place without an `fsync` of the files or the directory, so a power cut takes the
  newest snapshots away (dragonflydb/dragonfly#8646, open). Six failures of the first
  exploration had a cut and no backward step; `disk=cut dseed=9f14bde427152010 | run C=30
  W=07713d5d,p1,q2,r150` loses 9 writes (`dc90bf5a49ea5252`, 2 runs), and the same schedule
  without the cut passes (`7db895511e57586c`).
- **Dragonfly, known: its Lua interpreter needs AVX.** On hvx's default x86-64-v2 guest the first
  `EVAL` ends Dragonfly with "An attempt to execute an instruction failed". Dragonfly's own code
  is built for Core 2 with SSE4.1, but its Lua fork (`dragonflydb/lua`, tag `Dragonfly-5.4.6a`)
  is built with `-march=sandybridge`: `lua_newstate`, `luaV_execute` and about 60 other functions
  of the 2.1.0 binary contain AVX instructions and no CPU check. hydo's v2 CPUID offers no AVX,
  XSAVE or OSXSAVE, so the guest behaves as a CPU without AVX. The maintainers require Sandy
  Bridge (issue #163); the closed issues #3166 and #5197 report the same message. The example
  uses `guest.cpu: v3`.
- **REPLTAKEOVER held.** With `takeover=yes` and kills, pauses, partitions and one-way faults (no
  clock steps or power cuts), `REPLTAKEOVER` answered `OK` at least once in 73 of 80 schedules,
  and after every `OK` the new primary held the old primary's keys.

The searches covered dragonflydb/dragonfly's issues, pull requests and discussions; RESULTS.md
lists the terms. Nothing was posted. Finding 1 was not reproduced with a real clock step without
hydo, because its cause is plain in the code; `native/` shows the choice by modification time in
Docker with `touch`.

**The runs.** Every run used hvx on the bare-metal machine with the 0.3.4 Linux release, one VM
at a time, in the tree `~/hydo-dragonfly`. The final image `explore-ob-dragonfly-disk.img`
(sha256 `7cb07d1af0499bb3…`) gives `aba00945721586e9` for `disk=none | run` twice, and `hydo
repro --regressions` gives 5 of 5 as expected, twice. The explorations, each `--strategy process
--new-faults --cluster-faults --workers 1`:

| exploration | image | seeds | failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| ex1 | the first image | 1-60 | 26: 18 finding 1, 6 finding 2, 2 a rule that was too strict |
| ex2 | the final checks, error logs on | 61-120 | 13: 7 finding 1, 6 finding 2 |
| ex3 | `takeover=yes`, faults `[kill, pause, network, oneway]` | 1-59, stopped | 4 liveness failures of the client's takeover bookkeeping |
| ex3b | the same, the client fixed | 1-80 | 0; `REPLTAKEOVER` answered `OK` in 73 |

ex1 ran 299 schedules an hour, ex2 286 and ex3b 588. A run of an image at `guest.cpu: v2` showed
the Lua cause: the primary stopped 6 times, no Lua transaction was acknowledged and 7 failed,
while 5 `MULTI` transactions were acknowledged.

**What hydo lacked** (RESULTS.md, "What the onboarding needed from hydo"; AGENTS.md open item 141):

- the cgroup2 file system in hvx's guest: Dragonfly exits at start when `/proc/self/cgroup` is
  empty, which it is until a cgroup2 file system is mounted, so each service's `setup` mounts one;
- a restarted service's earlier log in the run directory: `logs/df1.log` held only the last
  start, and the reason of the first crash needed `hydo inspect`;
- `guest.cpu` as a parameter: `{{cpu}}` passes `hydo build --check`, and the explorer's corpus
  test refuses it;
- a way to leave a fault kind out of one exploration: the takeover search needed a copy of the
  manifest with a shorter `faults:` list;
- the faults' clock steps and restarts in a check: the client records the primary's process id
  with every write.

**What moved.** Nothing recorded: the example is not in `hydo/onboard/recorded.json`, and no
engine, controller or guest program changed. The new manifest is in the explorer's identity and
corpus goldens (`identity-quick.txt`, `identity-full.txt`, `corpus-full.txt`) and in the control
corpus (`corpus-quick.txt`), re-recorded on this Mac with `HYDO_BLESS=1`. The CLI golden and
`agents_equivalence` pass unchanged.

**Checks** (on this Mac, `main` at `03fdacb9` with this milestone on top): `hydo-schedule`'s
`language::`; `hydo-config`; `hydo-agents`'s `public_content::`; the `hydo` program's `docs::`,
`equivalence::cli_matches_golden` and `agents_equivalence`; `hydo-explore`'s `identity::` (also
with `HYDO_IDENT_FULL=1`) and `corpus::`; `hydo-control`'s `corpus::`; `sh
ci/consolidate-tests.sh --check`; and `sh ci/vale.sh`.

### Milestone 277 (tentative number) - DONE (SurrealDB 4.0.1 on SurrealKV, onboarded with `hydo onboard` and hunted on hvx and the Mac engine; one new SurrealKV candidate: when a damaged value of the value log belongs to the WAL's newest large record, the next open drops every later acknowledged commit and starts with a warning, while one more large record after it makes the open refuse; found blind 7 times in 167 schedules and reproduced with Docker; two known SurrealDB bugs reached; the experimental upgrade from 3.3.5 on RocksDB held; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-16)

**In short.** SurrealDB 4.0.1 (2026-11-09) keeps its data in SurrealKV 1.2.0, its only disk
engine since RocksDB was removed in 4.0. `hydo/onboard/examples/surrealdb` (RESULTS.md) runs one
server from SurrealDB's image with the default `sync=every`, started with `hydo onboard` from a
one-service Compose file. The test client `sdbc` (Go, `client/`) sends SurrealQL to `/sql` and
registers live queries on the WebSocket endpoint `/rpc`. Eight drivers and nine checks state
SurrealDB's documented promises:

- list-append transactions, checked at `strong-snapshot-isolation`, and registers with
  compare-and-set, checked for linearizability;
- a bank whose total stays 800;
- records of 1 byte to 20 KiB, half of them in the value log, that must survive, with no failed
  creation applied, and the changefeed of their table, complete and in the order of the
  acknowledgements;
- an `ASYNC` event, a `UNIQUE` index and a plain index, and a graph of `RELATE` edges;
- live queries, whose commits of one client must arrive in order and only when committed.

SurrealKV's directory is a file system of its own (`storage:`), so `G=` and `L=` apply. Two
known clock bugs are kept out of the blind explorations by the build parameter `feeds=no` (no
changefeeds and no event) or by a copy of `hydo.yaml` without `clock` in `faults:`.

**What was found.**

- **SurrealKV, new as far as the search found: a damaged value drops the commits after it.** At
  an open, `TailCheck::run` in `wal/tail.rs` holds every value-log pointer of the WAL's last
  segment to its entry. When an entry fails, the open refuses only when a later record of the
  segment points to a value that passes, and a sync mark claims the failed record
  (`holds_a_value` and `synced_to`). Otherwise it ends the segment before the failed record. So
  when the damaged value is the newest large one, every later commit is dropped: also the small
  ones, which share no byte with it, and also when sync marks say they were synced. SurrealDB
  logs `WARN surrealkv::lsm: WAL segment 1 ends before record 76 ... 12 record(s) ... were left
  out` and starts. The blind explorations found it 7 times: hvx seeds 3, 10 and 32 (zeroed bytes,
  a cut tail, one flipped bit of `vlog/00000000000000000001.vlog`) and Mac seeds 111, 121, 150
  and 156. The explorer shrank hvx seed 3 to the `G=` token alone, which failed on both hvx runs
  of its image (`fp=aa638ed17df30148`). The saved regression `G=surrealdb@40+1:trunc,file=vlog`
  fails on the explorations' image on hvx (`fp=6b6e85bf41bea7d4`, twice) and on the Mac engine
  (`fp=8f77af7e6cb5a8b7`, twice), and on the committed folder's image (Mac
  `fp=63e1ed905f64c9b8`, hvx `fp=7d5ebcc3b9ac3b16`, twice).
  `native/vlog-tail-cut.sh` reproduces it with Docker in seconds: 11 small acknowledged records
  are lost. With one more large record after them (`LATER_BIG=1`) the open refuses, naming "a sync
  mark says that the segment was synced past record 76". surrealkv's `main` at 1.4.0 has the same
  condition. Nothing was posted.
- **SurrealDB, known (#7606, open): changefeed versionstamps go back after a backward clock step
  and a restart.** `T=20:-3600 K=surrealdb@25+1` gave 21 creations a versionstamp below one
  acknowledged before them, on every Mac run. It is saved as a known regression.
- **SurrealDB, known (pull request #7672, open): writes to a table with a changefeed or an
  `ASYNC` event wait for the length of a backward clock step.** Steps of one day and 30 days back
  ended Mac runs with `ERROR workload: exit budget exhausted`.

**What held.** In 167 blind schedules (40 on hvx, 127 on the Mac engine) and the hand
schedules, no acknowledged commit was lost to a kill, a pause, a power cut at a step or at the
k-th disk flush, a power loss of the service or disk I/O errors. The list-append history showed
no anomaly at strong snapshot isolation, the registers stayed linearizable, the indexes and the
graph agreed with their tables, every acknowledged event was marked, and every live query
reported its client's commits in order. With `feeds=no`, 20 schedules with clock steps of 30 s to
30 days passed. Damage that SurrealKV detects at the open (its manifest, a value with a later
large one) stops the server with an error, which the explorer classifies as `corrupted-files`.

**The upgrade from 3.x.** `upgrade/` runs SurrealDB's experimental in-place upgrade
(`SURREAL_EXPERIMENTAL_UPGRADE_FROM_3X=true`). The service's first start runs 3.3.5 on RocksDB,
and every later start 4.0.1, so the first kill or power cut of a run upgrades the store with the
workload running. The 3.3.5 program comes from the root of a second image service, a job that
only sleeps, because versions of an image service are refused (open item 109). On hvx: two clean
runs on 3.3.5, two runs with `K=surrealdb@30+1` (the server's log shows the conversion, "301
version(s) in 1 table(s)", and the data migrations to 4.0.1), and two with `disk=cut | run C=40`
held every check. Twelve power cuts at the 84th to the 128th disk flush with
`K=surrealdb@3+1` held too: 11 of them came after the restart began and before the server was
ready, inside the 4.0.1 open, and each recovery boot finished the upgrade. Which of them cut the
conversion itself was not separated.

**What hydo lacked** (open item 140; RESULTS.md, section "What hydo lacked"):

- An exploration cannot leave out one fault kind. `faults:` with a build parameter
  (`"{{clockfault}}"`) stopped `hydo explore` and the explorer's corpus test with `faults: unknown
  kind`, so the example keeps `faults:` literal and explores through a copy without `clock`.
- No way to keep a known bug out of a blind exploration: half of the drawn clock steps go back,
  and each reached a known finding.
- The explorer shrinks every `ERROR ... restart failed (its files were corrupted)`: detected
  corruption, which is right. Seed 3's shrink took an hour on hvx, then wrote nothing for 25
  minutes, and the exploration was stopped before its report.
- A failed check gives no service log when no service exited; the cause of the finding is a
  `WARN` line, which `hydo inspect logs` and Docker showed.

**Onboarding retro** (RESULTS.md): the first clean run passed 18 minutes after the start; the
first new finding came in about the 10th blind schedule, 44 minutes after the start.

**Checks.** Before the commit, on this Mac: `cargo test -p hydo --test it
equivalence::cli_matches_golden` and `agents_equivalence`, `hydo-schedule`'s `language::`,
`hydo-config`, `hydo-agents`'s `public_content::`, `hydo`'s `docs::`, `sh
ci/consolidate-tests.sh --check` and `sh ci/vale.sh`. The explorer's identity and corpus goldens
and the control corpus golden were re-recorded for the new example's files only. Nothing
recorded moved: no engine, guest program or recorded example changed.

### Milestone 279 (tentative number) - DONE (Redpanda v26.2.7, three nodes in one hvx guest, against what Redpanda promises its producers and consumer groups: the durability promises held under strict power losses of one node and whole-guest power cuts, with write caching off and on; three new candidates: one partition's damaged snapshot stops its whole node at every start, a transaction that the coordinator still records as `empty` is never aborted, so `read_committed` consumers stall for good, and a committed transaction is visible on only one of its two partitions; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-17)

**In short.** `hydo/onboard/examples/redpanda` (RESULTS.md) runs three nodes of Redpanda
v26.2.7, the latest release, from its Docker image on hvx. Each node has one core, 1 GiB of
Seastar memory and its own 384 MiB file system for its data directory. The cluster takes the
sizing properties of `rpk`'s development mode without the two that change durability: fsync is
not bypassed, and write caching stays off (`--set bootstrap=bootstrap-write-caching.yaml` turns
it on). A static Go client on franz-go produces with the idempotent producer, writes two-record
transactions that commit or abort, and consumes as group `g` with offset commits. All of it is
one `type: messages` history, with the claims `no-loss`, `no-phantom` (no aborted record read
with `read_committed`), `duplicates: forbidden`, `order: log` per partition, `fan-out` to the
full read and to `g`, and `after-ack` (no redelivery after an acknowledged commit). The
`eventually` invariant `tx.no_hanging` says that no transaction stays open after the heal.

**What the guest needed.** Seastar reads `/proc/self/cgroup` at start and failed with
`std::out_of_range (sstring out of range)` on the empty file of hvx's guest: Linux shows the
cgroup v2 line only after cgroup2 was mounted once. Each node's `setup:` mounts it. The first
clean run came 35 minutes after the start.

**What was found.**

- **Redpanda, new as far as the search found: a damaged `tx.snapshot` stops its node.**
  `persisted_stm_base::start()` in `src/v/raft/persisted_stm.cc` turns any error of the local
  snapshot's load into `vassert(false, "... Can't load snapshot from ...")`. A zeroed or
  bit-flipped `tx.snapshot` (53 bytes) of one partition stops the whole node at every start,
  although the same function rebuilds a missing or rejected snapshot from the log. Seed 6 of the
  blind exploration found it; `G=n1@1+2:zero,len=4096,file=tx.snapshot,seed=626bd178` stops n1
  on every run, and Docker shows the same assertion (`native/zero-snapshot.sh`). A truncated
  snapshot is handled. Pull request 24662 (2025) says that a snapshot that cannot be loaded
  "should trigger log replay"; the merged code throws again.
- **Redpanda, new as far as the search found: a transaction that the coordinator records as
  `empty` is never aborted.** `do_try_abort` in `src/v/cluster/tx_gateway_frontend.cc` handles
  `tx_status::empty` like `ongoing` and asks for `preparing_internal_abort`, which the state
  machine (`is_state_transition_valid`) allows only from `ongoing`. A partition that times out
  such a transaction asks every 10 seconds and gets an error each time, so the transaction
  stays open and the last stable offset stops. The `empty` record comes from
  `do_add_partition_to_tx`, which starts the transaction on the data partitions before it stores
  them. Seed 9 found it after four leader changes of the coordinator partition; it reproduced
  three times on its image (explorer, `--schedule`, `repro --transcript`), and a harmless file in
  place of the seeded corruption gives the same hang. Seed 37 of the fourth exploration reached
  the same `empty` record after a whole-guest power cut, as a `VIOLATION [tx.no_hanging]`. The
  code is unchanged on `dev` (2026-11-12).
- **Redpanda, new as far as the search found: a committed transaction visible on one partition
  only.** Seed 24 of the third exploration: the client's commit of a two-record transaction
  returned no error, `read_committed` readers read one record and never the other, and a
  `read_uncommitted` read showed the missing record in its partition's log. The explorer shrank
  it to `disk=none dseed=2aa0ad4523ae213f | run K=nodes.primary@66+1 P=n2@42+11
  W=02ecd045,p2,q2,r500` (a pause of n2 and a kill of partition 0's leader, 50 steps before the
  transaction), which fails on every run of that image, also from a fresh boot. A single kill
  of a node at the moment a transaction adds its partitions (`A=rp.txn_add@20+3:kill-n1`) breaks
  it too, in five of nine runs, and is the saved regression. A raw `read_committed` fetch of
  each partition showed the cause's shape: producer 9 at epoch 7 has a commit marker on one
  partition and an abort marker on the other. Two commands with one transactional id ran at
  once; epoch 8's start on the second partition aborted epoch 7's transaction there, after the
  coordinator had already answered epoch 7's commit (`do_commit_tm_tx` answers at
  `preparing_commit`). Why the coordinator let epoch 8 start before epoch 7's commit reached
  every partition was not found: the nodes logged nothing about it at the default level. Three
  tries under Docker did not reproduce it. The closest report is issue 17921 (v23.1.7, closed
  as stale).

The durability promises held: with write caching off, `disk=cut | run C=60`, the shape of
Jepsen's NATS finding 3.5 with a strict power loss, and two more strict power losses lost
nothing; with write caching on, two whole-guest cuts lost no record. The searches covered
redpanda-data/redpanda's issues, pull requests and discussions and Jepsen's Redpanda analysis;
RESULTS.md lists the terms. Nothing was posted.

**The runs.** Every run used hvx on the bare-metal machine, one VM at a time, with this branch's
`hydo`, `hydo-build` and `hydo-hvx` over the 0.3.4 Linux release, at the fingerprint epoch 3.
A clean run takes about 2 minutes of the machine; a schedule of the explorer took 3 to 14
minutes, on one worker, because the guest has 4,608 MiB. Four blind explorations
(`--strategy process --more-faults --new-faults --storage-faults --cluster-faults`) ran 37
schedules, seeds 1 to 37, on three images; six failed: findings 1 (seeds 6 and 35), 2 (seed 9;
and seed 37, the same `empty` record after a power cut), 3 (seed 24), and records deleted by retention after
a clock step of a year (seed 25, by design). The image of the committed folder gave
`hydo repro --regressions` 2 of 2 as expected; its clean run, on the image before its last
`expect` line changed, gave `dbe6a8ebad1212ca` twice. RESULTS.md lists every image and value.

**Tests and checks.** The explorer's `identity-quick.txt` and `corpus-full.txt` were re-recorded
for the new manifest (`HYDO_BLESS=1`): its inputs are added, and the chunks after it in the
sorted stream move. The control corpus `corpus-quick.txt` gained the manifest's two lines. On
this Mac, on `main` at `9294778e` with this milestone on top: `cargo test -p hydo --test it
equivalence::cli_matches_golden` and `agents_equivalence`, `hydo-explore`'s `identity::` and
`corpus::`, `hydo-control`'s `corpus::`, `hydo-schedule`'s `language::`, `cargo test -p
hydo-config`, `hydo-agents`'s `public_content::`, `hydo`'s `docs::`, `sh
ci/consolidate-tests.sh --check` and `sh ci/vale.sh`. Nothing recorded moved: no engine, guest program or existing
example changed.

**Finding 3's cause (a follow-up in this milestone).** An image with Redpanda's `tx` logger at
trace level (`65b1c401…`) passed the saved regression, and five of the nine reaction variants
still broke the claim. The trace of `A=rp.txn_add@20+3:kill-n2` shows the cause in
`src/v/cluster/tx_gateway_frontend.cc` (v26.2.2, the same on `dev` at `d9944871`):

- `do_init_tm_tx` aborts an `ongoing` transaction for a second producer with the same
  transactional id, and `do_abort_tm_tx` finishes it without the epoch bump.
- The first producer's next AddPartitionsToTxn, at the old epoch, passes `get_latest_tx`.
  `init_add_resource_to_tx` then starts a new transaction (`reset_transaction_state`) with only
  that partition.
- The first producer's commit commits the new transaction and returns no error, and its earlier
  partition keeps the abort marker.

Apache Kafka bumps the epoch in that abort (`prepareFenceProducerEpoch`), so the old producer
gets `PRODUCER_FENCED`. The earlier reading (epoch 8's start aborting a commit in flight) was
wrong. `native/half-commit.sh` reproduces it without hydo under Docker. In the program's
`steps` order, 10 of 10 commits returned no error and lost their record on partition 1. Two
producers racing with no fault lost a record in 5 of 205 commits. Against Apache Kafka 3.9.1
the same program got `PRODUCER_FENCED` and lost nothing. RESULTS.md, finding 3, has the trace and
the commands.

**Finding 4, from KVM (a follow-up in this milestone).** On GitHub's KVM runners (run
44046143553 of the one-off workflow of the branch `tmp-redpanda-kvm`, the image built from
`main` at `7944ad08`), `disk=none | run A=rp.txn_add@20:kill-n3` broke `rp.duplicates` and
`rp.order` the same way on two AMD EPYC 9V74 hosts and one Intel Xeon 6975P-C host
(`fp=ff1ea63a6c2f966f` on the first). Transaction 28's promise gave `m28b` offset 5, which holds
transaction 11's `m11a` of the same transactional id, and every reader read `m28b` at 15.
franz-go 1.22.2 takes a record's offset from the answer that ends its batch (`sink.go`,
`handleReqRespBatch` and `finishBatch`), so the offset is Redpanda's answer to franz-go's retry
after the kill. The cause is in Redpanda v26.2.2, the same on `dev` at `d9944871`:

- A partition's cache of a producer's 5 newest requests matches a request by its sequence range
  only, without the epoch (`requests::try_emplace` in `producer_state.cc`).
- A transactional producer starts its sequences at 0 in each epoch.
- Only the leader clears the cache, at a transaction's first batch (`do_transactional_replicate`
  in `rm_stm.cc`, the fix of pull request 5026 in 2022). A follower applies a transaction's begin
  batch without a reset (`apply_transaction_begin`), so after a change of leader the earlier
  epochs' entries match.

`native/stale-offset.sh` reproduces it under Docker (arm64, v26.2.7) with a move of the leader
through the admin API. A resent request got the earlier batch's offset in 20 of 20 rounds. A new
request in the same place got the earlier batch's offset and was not written in 20 of 20 rounds,
and each commit returned no error. Without the move, 0 of 20 in both modes. Apache Kafka clears
the batch metadata on every epoch change (`ProducerStateEntry.maybeUpdateProducerEpoch`). The
messages check's `duplicates` message called the record "stored twice". It now says that the
acknowledgement named another id when every delivery carries one id
(`hydo-history` `messages/claims.rs`, with a test in `tests/messages.rs`). No issue or pull
request of redpanda-data/redpanda or twmb/franz-go describes the case. Nothing was posted, and
nothing recorded moved.

### Milestone 282 (tentative number) - DONE (what the evaluation of `hydo fuzz` found, fixed before 0.4.0: the harness builds on `#![no_std]` crates and reads results with private fields of another module; each function whose harness does not build is reported and the others run; each function ends with one verdict, `held`, `broken`, `vacuous` or `too few inputs`, and the last two exit with status 3 with a `to fix:` line; `input` lines take lengths, character sets, example strings and list elements; lists grow to 256 with edge sizes to 4,096; sizes stay within 2^20 without an `input` line, with progress lines and a stop after 3 calls that do not return; `with T = i64` for a generic function; `hydo guide fuzz`; the six crates again: every harness builds, the planted memchr bug and num-integer#55 are found from the functions' own contracts; nothing new found and nothing posted; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-17)

**What was asked.** Milestone 280 found that a new Rust user would not keep using `hydo fuzz`.
The gate for 0.4.0 was to fix its first four problems, with tests, and to run the six crates
again. The full report is the section "After the fixes" of
`docs/design/function-fuzzing-evaluation.md`.

**The harness.** The test module that hydo writes declares `extern crate std` and names
`self::std` paths, so it builds in a `#![no_std]` crate and in a crate of the 2015 edition. hydo
now reads each structure's module and which of its fields are `pub`. A field that the
harness's module cannot see is a new fuzzing type, `FTy::Hidden`. The harness writes `X` (not
read) for it without naming it, and a parameter with such a field is refused with the field's
name. The build uses cargo's JSON messages. An error whose place is a harness module's columns
leaves that one function out with the compiler's first line, and the others build again. An
error elsewhere is checked by a build without any harness. Constants such as `ALPHABET_LEN`
give an array its length.

**The verdicts.** `requires` rejections are counted per clause. A clause `a || ... || z` counts
the calls on which `z` decided, and a property that returns `Option<bool>` counts its `Some`
answers. `too few inputs` (fewer calls than `--min-inputs`, default a tenth of `--cases`) and
`vacuous` (fewer decided calls than `--min-reach`, default 1 % of `--cases`) exit with status
3. Each prints a `to fix:` line: an `input` line from the clause's bounds (`input alphabet len
64`), `input s like "hydo"` for a string compared with a literal, or `like` for a parser.

**The generator.** An `input` line takes `in`, `len`, `chars` (a named or a quoted set) and
`like` (examples, used as they are in a third of the inputs and changed in the others), for a
parameter, a field or a list's elements (`v[]`). The longest list or string grows from 4 to 256
over the inputs, and one input in eight after the first 100 has an edge size up to 4,096. One
long list in four repeats one value with a few others. A value that a clause compares with a
list's element is put into the list in one input of four. An input holds at most 65,536 values.
A list's shrink now reaches its first 256 elements, every element's simplest value first.

**Long runs.** A `usize` or `isize` value without an `input` line stays within 2^20, its
edges too. A progress line comes on standard error every 5 seconds. After 3 calls that do not
return, a function's other inputs are not run, and a shrink stops after 3 such calls or 60
seconds. With the rest of the fix, `FixedBitSet::with_capacity` without an `input` line took
under a second, against 23 minutes before.

**Smaller fixes.** `// hydo: with T = i64` fuzzes a generic function with that type, called
with `::<i64>`. The `again:` line keeps `--release`, `--toolchain`, `--target-dir` and
`--timeout`, and names the function by its path. `--json` prints only JSON on standard output.
Names keep their module and type (`memchr::memmem::find`). `--list` says when no function has a
contract, and a panic's place is shown relative to the package also for a relative `--out`.

**The evaluation again.** The crates are the same archives as in Milestone 280, unpacked fresh.
The contracts were written again, because Milestone 280 did not save them; they are
`docs/design/function-fuzzing/m282-contracts.patch` and `m282-contracts-b.patch`. Phase A used
Milestone 280's language only, on the old code (`hydo-contracts` at `7944ad08`) and the new:

- semver: before, no harness built; after, 13 functions, 12 held and `Version::parse` is
  `vacuous` (0 of 1,000 strings parsed). With `like` examples, 486 of 1,000 parsed and all 13
  held.
- base64: before, `Alphabet::new` held on 2 inputs with exit status 0; after, 1,000 calls and
  `vacuous`; with two `like` alphabets, 875 of 1,000 calls built one.
- fixedbitset and memchr: before, no harness built without `#![cfg_attr(not(test), no_std)]`;
  after, 11 and 12 functions in 6 and 7 seconds with the crates unchanged.
- memchr with the planted bug: before, every contract held; after, memchr's own contract broke
  on 10 of 1,000 calls, shrunk to 80 bytes of 0 with a 3 at index 50.
- num-integer: the same two failures as before without the workaround; with `with T = i64`,
  `gcd`'s own contract finds rust-num/num-integer#55.
- byteorder: the same two `read_uint` panics; the trait's default method stays refused.

Nothing new was found, and nothing was posted. The verdict: a developer would now keep `hydo
fuzz` for functions over integers, strings and lists, but not yet for APIs built on traits or on
types that hold pointers. The contracts were written by the one who fixed the tool, so a fresh
evaluator before 0.4.0 would give a less biased view.

**Tests and checks.** `hydo-contracts` gained the fixture `tests/fuzz-nostd`, a `#![no_std]`
crate with one function per problem, and tests of the `input` syntax, the generator, the
clause's parts, the harness without `std`, and private fields. The guide gained the topic
`fuzz`. `cli.jsonl` was re-recorded on purpose for `guide`, `guide --list` and `guide
manifest` on both platforms, and `agents.jsonl` for the guide topics after `fuzz` (`HYDO_BLESS=1`). Nothing recorded moved: no engine, image, guest
program or example changed.

### Milestone 269 (tentative number) - DONE (open item 132, the first item of release 0.4.0: the saved regressions leave the image; `hydo build` writes them beside it as `<image>.regressions.json`, so saving or editing one no longer changes the image's bytes, and an `# expect: fp=` line can hold its own image's value; the fingerprint epoch is 4; an image built before keeps its regressions inside and is replayed from them; every image built at epoch 4 has new bytes, and its values wait for the pass before 0.4.0; 2026-11-16)

**What was asked.** Milestones 251 and 268 showed that a saved regression changed the image it
tests. `hydo build` copied the folder `regressions/` into the image as `/hydo/regressions/`,
comments included, and put each schedule and `# expect:` value into `/etc/hydo/compose.json`,
and each `W=@<key>` composition into `/etc/hydo/compose.saved/<key>`. So saving the second
Saleor regression moved the gift card schedule's run, and an `# expect: fp=` line could not name
its own image's value. The task: find what reads regressions inside the guest, move them to the
host side, prove with a test that an edited regression leaves the image's sha256 alone, and raise
the fingerprint epoch.

**What reads regressions.** Nothing in the guest. The agent runs only primitives, and the copy
under `/hydo/regressions/` was read by nobody. The host read them out of the image:

- `hydo repro --regressions` and `hydo ci run` (`runs::replay_regressions`) read the entries and
  the plan meta from the image's `/etc/hydo/compose.json`;
- the host controller took the compositions that a `W=@<key>` names from the same entries
  (`ComposePlan::of`, the `compose.saved` of the image);
- hydo-build read the folder's files for its search of the programs a manifest uses
  (`uses_program`: `hydo-sql`, `hydo-read`), and the plan meta for manifest.sh.

The test composer's guest calls, `hydo ci`'s input key and the explorer read no regression from
the image. The explorer reads the plan meta for its commands only.

**The change.**

- `hydo_image::EPOCH` is 4, and `hydo_image::defaults` has `regressions_in_image`, true before
  epoch 4. `hydo_image::regressions_path`, `regressions_text` and `read_regressions` name, write
  and read the file beside an image: `{"regressions": [...], "type": "regressions", "v": 1}`,
  with the plan meta's entries as an image before epoch 4 carried them.
- hydo-build (`stage::take_regressions`, called by `prepare` when the epoch says so) takes the
  regressions out of the manifest it stages: the plan meta's `regressions` is empty, the folder's
  `regressions/` is not copied, `test.regressions` leaves the validated manifest, and a plan of
  only regressions is no plan (no `compose.json`, no composer lines in manifest.sh). What stays is
  what the same project gives without any regression. At the end of a build `write_regressions`
  writes `<image>.regressions.json`, or removes a stale one.
- hydo-control: `agent::regressions_of_image` gives the entries and the plan meta by the image's
  epoch, from the image before epoch 4 and from the file beside it from epoch 4.
  `agent::plan_of_image` takes the `W=@<key>` compositions of an epoch-4 image from that file
  (`schedule::composer::saved_of`). A missing file means no regressions; a file that is not a
  regressions file is an error that names it.
- The `hydo` program's replay reads `regressions_of_image`. For an epoch-4 image without the
  file, `hydo repro --regressions` says that no file is beside the image. The help of `hydo
  repro` and `hydo save` says where the regressions go.
- MANIFEST.md "Regressions" and "Stable compositions", and `hydo guide composer`, say where
  `hydo build` writes the regressions and that a `test.regressions` entry in hydo.yaml stays part
  of the manifest the image carries.

**The proof.** The composed Redis example, with its regression `lost-update.schedule`, built
three times in one folder: as committed (a), with a new comment and `# expect:
fp=0123456789abcdef` (b), and without `regressions/` (c). Each build by the 0.3.4 release's
`hydo` and by this milestone's.

| platform | hydo | a | b | c |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| x86_64, the bare-metal machine (`-disk.img`) | 0.3.4 | `98aff836…` | `27b2ae22…` | `fc2b75c4…` |
| x86_64, the bare-metal machine (`-disk.img`) | this milestone | `ff17a4b4…` | `ff17a4b4…` | `ff17a4b4…` |
| arm64, this Mac (`.cpio.gz`) | 0.3.4 | `8ca1cae5…` | `d363baf9…` | `6357f21a…` |
| arm64, this Mac (`.cpio.gz`) | this milestone | `f96995ac…` | `f96995ac…` | `f96995ac…` |

The arm64 data disk was `d47e86f7…` in every build. The new builds of a and b wrote
`<image>.regressions.json` beside the image, and the build of c wrote none.

`hydo repro --regressions` on the new images, one VM at a time (hvx through `~/bin/hvx-run`):

- On hvx, image a: PASS `expect ok`, `948119c545e7ae2e`. Image b: FAIL `expect
  fp=0123456789abcdef` with `948119c545e7ae2e`, the same run. Image c: "has no saved
  regressions: there is no ... .regressions.json beside it".
- A fourth build with `# expect: fp=948119c545e7ae2e` gave the image `ff17a4b4…` again, and its
  replay passed: an `# expect: fp=` line now holds its own image's value.
- On the Mac engine, image a: PASS, `414cc2e809d104ac`; image b: FAIL with `414cc2e809d104ac`.

The tests are hydo-build's `regressions_beside::` (an edited, a new and a removed regression
leave the staged manifest, the composer's files in the root, manifest.sh and the prelude the
same; a plan of only regressions stages no plan) and hydo-control's `regressions_beside::` (on
small arm64 images: an epoch-4 image's entries and `W=@<key>` composition come from the file
beside it, an epoch-3 image's from inside it, and a file beside an epoch-3 image is not read).

**What moves.** Every image built at epoch 4 has new bytes, because its record says epoch 4, and
an image whose plan has saved regressions loses them too. The values of `hydo/onboard/recorded.json`
are not re-recorded here (AGENTS.md "Re-recording runs in batches"): open item 105 lists them for
the pass before 0.4.0 (docs/REBASELINE.md section 26). The pinned reproducers' epoch-2 images
keep their values. Re-recorded goldens, each diff read:

- hydo-build's equivalence answers: six. The `--print-shell` of three manifests with only a
  `regressions/` folder (the RAUC example and the SWUpdate example's two manifests), on both
  architectures, lost the composer's lines, because such a plan is no plan for the image now.
  A `W=` on such an image was refused before and is refused now, with the message for an image
  without a test composer plan.
- hydo-manifest's equivalence answers: one input digest, of the Saleor example's `hydo/`
  folder, whose regression Milestone 268 edited. No answer changed.
- The `hydo` program's CLI goldens: ten answers on the two platforms, `hydo guide composer` and
  `hydo guide manifest` (the text above) and `hydo save`'s last line, which says that `hydo
  build` writes the regressions beside the image.

No answer names a host path. The epoch's literal in hydo-image's unit tests is 4.

**Checks.** On this Mac, on `main` at `47df6fee` with this milestone on top: `cargo fmt --all
--check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; every test of hydo-image,
hydo-build, hydo-composer, hydo-compose, hydo-control (its full-tier `m123`, `features` and
`corpus` included), hydo-engine, hydo-agents, hydo-release and the `hydo` program; the `hydo`
program's `equivalence::cli_matches_golden` and `agents_equivalence`, with `HYDO_BLESS=1` for
the guide's new text; `HYDO_BLESS=1` for the equivalence answers of hydo-manifest and
hydo-build; hydo-schedule's `language::`, hydo-agents's `public_content::`, the `hydo`
program's `docs::`, `sh ci/consolidate-tests.sh --check` and `sh ci/vale.sh`. On the bare-metal
machine, in a folder of its own under umask 022: the x86_64 builds and the hvx replays above,
with this tree's `hydo` over the 0.3.4 Linux release.

### Milestone 283 (tentative number) - DONE (the guest mounts cgroup2 on `/sys/fs/cgroup` at every boot, from the fingerprint epoch 4: the host controller sends the agent's existing `mount` before the S0 snapshot, so the agent pin and the images' bytes stay; `guest.cgroup2: false` turns it off, and an image of an older epoch mounts nothing; the Dragonfly and Redpanda examples start without their `setup:` mounts; the pinned reproducers keep their values on hvx; every epoch-4 run moves and waits for the pass before 0.4.0; 2026-11-17)

**What was asked.** Dragonfly (Milestone 278) and Redpanda (Milestone 279) both stopped at start
until each service's `setup:` mounted cgroup2. Linux writes the `0::/` line of
`/proc/self/cgroup` only after the first mount of a cgroup2 file system, and Dragonfly (`Failed
to parse cgroupv2 format`) and Seastar (`sstring out of range`) exit on an empty file. Every
program that sizes itself from cgroups meets the same blocker. Mount cgroup2 by default from the
fingerprint epoch 4, keyed on the image's epoch, with an opt-out key, on all three engines, and
make the thread pause agree with it.

**Where the mount happens, and why there.** In the host controller's boot prelude
(`boot_prelude` in `hydo/crates/hydo-control/src/schedule.rs`), after `lo` is up and before the
phase line, the network namespaces and the S0 snapshot. The request is the agent's `mount`
primitive, which the controller already uses for the data disk: source `cgroup2`, type `cgroup2`,
destination `/sys/fs/cgroup`, no flags and no data. The choice:

- The agent is inside every image and has its own pin. A mount in the agent's own start would
  move the agent pin and give every image new bytes, also an image that turns the mount off. The
  controller's request is part of the boot conversation only.
- S0 is taken after the prelude, and a recovery boot after a power cut and a boot after a reboot
  start from S0, so one request covers every boot. `hydo run`'s solo conversation runs the same
  prelude.
- A service enters only its network namespace (`nsenter -n`), so a mount in the guest's root
  mount namespace reaches every service with `network: bridge` too.
- When the agent refuses the mount (a guest kernel without cgroup2), the controller logs
  `cgroup2 not mounted on /sys/fs/cgroup: <reason>` and the boot goes on. Every engine's kernel
  for an epoch-4 image has cgroup2: hvx's `bzImage`, and the epoch-3 kernels of the Mac and KVM
  engines (`Image-explore-cg`, `bzImage-kvm-cg` and their variants).

**The epoch and the key.** `hydo_image::EpochDefaults` gained `cgroup2`, on from epoch 4.
`guest.cgroup2` is a format-1 addition (hydo-manifest's model and validation, the schema
`hydo/schema/project-v1.json`, `hydo-schema-compat` passes). `Plan` keeps the manifest's value,
and `agent::plan_of_image` puts in the image's epoch default when the key is absent. A plan read
from a manifest without an image mounts nothing unless the key says `true`, so the controller's
recorded corpora and the explorer's goldens stay the same. Epoch 4 is not published yet (it came
with Milestone 269 for 0.4.0), so this milestone adds a second default to it and does not raise
the epoch.

**The thread pause.** Its script (`schedule/threads.rs`) mounts cgroup2 only when
`/sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.controllers` is missing. On an epoch-4 image the boot's mount is there, and
the pause mounts nothing. On an older image, or with `guest.cgroup2: false`, it mounts cgroup2 as
before. No change was needed.

**An image service.** Its root gets `/sys` from hydo-build's launcher by `mount --bind`, which is
not recursive, so the cgroup2 mount does not reach the image's root. Its programs read the `0::/`
line, which is all Dragonfly and Seastar need. The examples' `setup:` mounts gave the same, and
Dragonfly logs `Failed in deducing any cgroup limits` either way (its `known-errors.yaml`). Open
item 144.

**The proof on the Mac engine.** A probe project: a service writes its `/proc/self/cgroup` to the
data disk, the workload writes its own and `grep cgroup /proc/mounts` and times a `sleep 2`, and a
check reads its own `/proc/self/cgroup`. Built with this hydo (epoch 4), with `guest.cgroup2:
false`, and by the 0.3.4 release (epoch 3). Run with this hydo unless named:

| image | schedule | verdict | fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| epoch 4 | `disk=none \| run` (twice) | OK: `svc=0::/ wl=0::/ check=0::/`, `cgroup2 /sys/fs/cgroup cgroup2 rw,relatime` | `81d8e6edfc902e11` twice |
| `guest.cgroup2: false` | `disk=none \| run` | VIOLATION: no line, no mount | `5027afc8ff2dbbfc` |
| epoch 4 | `disk=cut \| run C=1` | OK in the recovery boot: `svc=0::/ check=0::/` | `bc02bb06a9898d98` |
| epoch 4 | `disk=none \| run P=workload/busybox@0~500:3000` | `PAUSED workload/busybox`, then VIOLATION `probe.slept` (`slept=3`): the pause stopped the threads | `caf14ebea83cdcbf` |
| epoch 3 | `disk=none \| run`, this hydo and 0.3.4 | VIOLATION: no line | `f915c2f25935a5a8` under both |
| epoch 3 | `disk=cut \| run C=1` | VIOLATION: no line in the recovery boot | `10263c4ccb44d4fa` |
| epoch 3 | the pause above | the pause mounted cgroup2 itself: `check=0::/`, `slept=3` | `36ba223b66cccd10` |

The workload's threads are all named `busybox` (busybox runs `sleep` as an applet), so the pause
names `busybox`. A pause whose script fails replies with an `E` line, and the controller then
ends the run with `HYDO-ORACLE: ERROR P=...`. No run did. The script's own text, error messages
included, is in the transcript's `send` record of the pause, so a search of the transcript for
`cannot mount` finds that record and not a reply.

**The proof on hvx** (the bare-metal machine, a tree of its own under umask 022, this tree's
`hydo`, `hydo-hvx` and `hydo-build` over the 0.3.4 Linux release, every VM through
`~/bin/hvx-run`). The same probe built for x86_64:

| image | schedule | verdict | fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| epoch 4 | `disk=none \| run` (twice) | OK: `svc=0::/ wl=0::/ check=0::/` and the mount | `8725e9cb1054854d` twice |
| `guest.cgroup2: false` | `disk=none \| run` | VIOLATION: no line, no mount | `41315e3d7aee5731` |
| epoch 4 | `disk=cut \| run C=1` | OK in the recovery boot: `svc=0::/ check=0::/` | `27d6141ef1646ecc` |
| epoch 4 | the pause | `PAUSED workload/busybox`, VIOLATION `probe.slept` (`slept=4`) | `773e765fda76e831` |
| epoch 3 | `disk=none \| run`, this hydo and 0.3.4 | VIOLATION: no line | `2a0fe290804411d6` under both |
| epoch 3 | the pause, this hydo and 0.3.4 | the pause mounted cgroup2 itself: `check=0::/`, `slept=4` | `5ee84b6090c5fdd7` under both, `ctl=8e00a68cf8d4d0e7` |

The two examples without their `setup:` mounts, `disk=none | run`:

| example | built at | verdict | fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dragonfly 2.1.0 (`f2c26003…`) | epoch 4 (this hydo) | OK, 6 invariants held, 71 commands, 13 s | `33ed7bed7b566eb8` twice |
| Dragonfly | epoch 3 (0.3.4), the control | `ERROR service start (df1)`: `Failed to parse cgroupv2 format, got:` | `30e5fc7c35551213` |

So both examples drop the mount from `setup:`. Their RESULTS.md files keep their epoch-3 values,
measured with the mount, and say so. Open item 141 loses its cgroup2 point.

**The pinned reproducers** on hvx, `disk=none dseed=4d5cb825dfaab05b | run K=redis@11+1 C=24`,
before (this tree at Milestone 269) and after (with this milestone), each once per image:

| images | old (VIOLATION, order 11) | fix (OK) |
|---|---|---|
| epoch 1, `~/hydo/build/m155` | `1dc3677fb94053cf`, `ctl=e873020651036931` | `ba0aa0612502a1df`, `ctl=07c598044a68e5be` |
| epoch 2, `~/hydo/build/m204` | `a76d7fe857fdb37c`, `ctl=84a3f0619a00b9e2` | `efbde7b57264be0f`, `ctl=087df49b7b36b10a` |
| epoch 3, `~/hydo/build/m244` | `a76d7fe857fdb37c`, `ctl=84a3f0619a00b9e2` | `efbde7b57264be0f`, `ctl=087df49b7b36b10a` |

Before and after gave the same `fp`, `wfp`, `inh` and `ctl` on all six; only the wall time
differed.

**KVM.** The bare-metal machine never runs KVM. `.github/workflows/tmp-cgroup2-kvm.yml` runs the
probe on four GitHub runners with this tree's `hydo`, `hydo-build` and `hydo-kvm` over the 0.3.4
release, with 1 and 2 vCPUs (`bzImage-kvm-cg` and `bzImage-kvm-smp-cg`). It also checks that the
Redis release example built by 0.3.4 gives the published values. Its first run, 44066203730, had
four Intel hosts: one Xeon Platinum 8370C and three Xeon 6975P-C. Every host gave the same values:

- These checks passed: `0::/` in the service, the workload and the check; one fingerprint over
  two runs; the opt-out; the recovery boot; 2 vCPUs; no mount at epoch 3; one fingerprint for the
  epoch-3 image under 0.3.4 and this hydo; and the Redis example's published values
  (`2d059466fb87a253`, `8af0c14d4ec2c470`).
- Two checks of the probe failed, and neither is a failure of the pause. They expected the Mac's
  exact `slept=3`. The KVM engine's clock gave `slept=4` on the epoch-4 image
  (`7c824ab78d040db9`, after `PAUSED workload/busybox`) and `slept=5` on the epoch-3 image
  (`fb1ae17ed4c8754c`, `check=0::/`). The `cannot mount cgroup2 on $G` line that the run printed
  is the script's text in the `send` record (above), not a reply.

The workflow now accepts any `slept` of 3 or more. It reads the pause's outcome from the
controller's `PAUSED` note and from the absence of an `ERROR P=` verdict. It also runs the
epoch-3 pause under 0.3.4 and requires one fingerprint, as hvx gave. The second run is open item
144.

**What moves.** No image's bytes change with the mount itself. Every image built at epoch 4 sends
one more command in its boot conversation, so every epoch-4 run gets another control transcript
and another fingerprint on all three engines. Those values wait for the pass before 0.4.0 with
Milestone 269's (open item 105, docs/REBASELINE.md section 26). The Dragonfly and Redpanda
images change with their manifests; neither is in `hydo/onboard/recorded.json`. Re-recorded
goldens, each diff read:

- the schema `hydo/schema/project-v1.json`: the key `guest.cgroup2`;
- hydo-manifest's equivalence answers (17) and hydo-build's (10): the refusal of an unknown
  `guest` key, whose list of known keys names `cgroup2`. Only those answers were replaced. A run
  with `HYDO_BLESS=1` would also draw the mutant corpus again over the examples of Milestones
  277 to 279, which `main` added without a recording, and change about 8,000 answers that this
  milestone does not move;
- the `hydo` program's CLI goldens: `hydo guide manifest` on both platforms (the new section).

**The rebase of Milestone 269.** Milestone 269 was rebased onto `main` at `7944ad08` (Milestones
270 to 281). AGENTS.md and this file kept both sides, `main`'s text first. The explorer's
identity-quick and identity-full and corpus-full, and the controller's corpus-quick, passed
without a new recording. The `hydo` program's CLI golden took `main`'s answers, and its ten
answers of Milestone 269 were recorded again. hydo-manifest's and hydo-build's equivalence
answers passed. M269's two new test files now remove their folders when they end (Milestone 271's
`TmpDir`).

**Checks.** On this Mac, on `main` at `7944ad08` with Milestones 269 and 283 on top: `cargo fmt
--all --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; hydo-image's unit tests;

### Milestone 285 (tentative number) - DONE (value history: `// hydo: key` and `// hydo: record` lines next to a function record chosen values at every call through the contracts' plan and breakpoints, and `hydo inspect values` shows each key's values in the run's order with each change marked; new readers for floating-point values, strings, a Go interface's dynamic value and a Go map's value by a constant key; on Blnk's overdraft regression the history shows the limit at 50.0 in the API, absent from the saved metadata, and 0.0 in the worker's coalesced copy of the two draws past the limit; one fingerprint with and without the plan; first version on the Mac engine; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-17)

**In short.** The user's idea was to follow one field of a structure through the program under
faults. A value history does it for the fields a developer names. `docs/design/value-history.md`
is the design, and `hydo guide values` the how-to.

```go
// hydo: key persistedTxn.Reference
// hydo: record persistedTxn.OverdraftLimit as overdraft_limit at entry
// hydo: record persistedTxn.MetaData["overdraft_limit"] as meta.overdraft_limit at entry
func createQueueCopy(persistedTxn *model.Transaction, originalRef string) *model.Transaction {
```

**The parts.**

- The language (`hydo-contracts`, `lang.rs`): `record <expr> [as <name>] [at entry|at return]`
  (both by default) and `key <expr>` (at entry, one per function); floating-point literals.
- The plan (`plan.rs`): `Function.values` (a `Show` per value at entry and at return),
  `Function.ret_addr` (the entry read of the return address) and `Program.calls` (the direct calls
  of each recording function, found by a scan for `BL` on arm64 and `CALL rel32` on x86_64, with
  the calling function). `Ty::F` and `Expr::Float`. `Record.boot`, the boot of a call (each power
  cut or reboot starts the next), which the Mac and KVM engines set. Every addition is skipped
  when empty, so a plan or a record of before reads and writes as it did.
- The readers (`compile.rs`): a `float64` or `float32` in memory; a string's length and first 32
  bytes; a Go interface's dynamic value (`runtime.eface`'s type word, or `runtime.iface`'s itab
  and its type at offset 8), compared with the runtime type descriptors of 11 types, each at
  `.go.type` plus the type's `DW_AT_go_runtime_type`; and a Go map's value by a constant string
  or integer key in a map of one group (8 slots), from the `map<K,V>`, `table<K,V>` and group
  types that Go's linker writes. A test builds `tests/go-values` for arm64 and amd64 and checks
  each descriptor's size and kind in the program's file.
- Clauses compare floats now (`V::Float`; `requires t.Limit > 0.5`).
- The host (`values.rs`): each recorded call's entry and return as points in the run's order, a
  history per key (a key that extends another after `_`, `-`, `.`, `:`, `/` or `#` is its
  copy), and each change of a value between two points.
- The view (`hydo-cli`, `inspect/values.rs`): `hydo inspect values <run dir> [--key K] [--name N]
  [--changes] [--plan FILE] [--limit N] [--offset N]`, the results type `values` (a results
  addition: `ValueHistory`, `ValueKey`, `ValuePoint`, `ValueChange`; `hydo-schema-compat`
  passes) or `--text`. Each point names the run's stop (`run:8007`), the workload's step range
  from the transcript, the function, the caller and the values. `hydo inspect events` adds them
  as events of the kind `value`, and `hydo report --html` adds the section "How the recorded
  values changed".
- `hydo build` prints `10 recorded values` beside the functions and clauses when a plan has
  them. `hydo run` prints `hydo: recorded values: N calls recorded` for a plan without clauses,
  and a function stopped at its entry only no longer counts as a call without its return.

**The proof on Blnk.** `hydo/onboard/examples/blnk` (RESULTS.md, "The overdraft limit's
history"). `values.patch` adds only comments to `setTransactionMetadata`, `createQueueCopy` and
`canProcessTransaction`; `hydo-values.yaml` is `hydo.yaml` with that program. The first choice,
`restoreTransactionFlagsFromMetadata`, has no copy of its own: the Go compiler inlined it into
its three callers. All runs used the Mac engine with this tree's hydo and engine over the 0.3.4
Mac release's guest files, on `explore-ob-blnk-values-arm64.cpio.gz` (`431e374d…`) and its build
with the fixes (`8533608f…`):

| image, schedule | with the plan | without it | verdict | calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| buggy, `overdraft-limit-concurrent-draws` | `f3cbeb9c85945f5c` twice | `f3cbeb9c85945f5c` twice | `VIOLATION [no_overdraft]` | 98 |
| fixed, the same schedule | `31feeab9f802ef32` twice | `31feeab9f802ef32` twice | OK | 100 |
| buggy, `disk=none \| run` | `e688c9f3241219f1` | `e688c9f3241219f1` | OK | 283 |
| buggy at epoch 4 (`62d83259…`), the regression | `ddb6f1730f6854ea` twice | `ddb6f1730f6854ea` twice | `VIOLATION [no_overdraft]` | 97 |

The first three rows ran on `7944ad08` with this milestone on top, at the fingerprint epoch 3.
The last row ran after the rebase onto `64950f8f` (Milestones 269 and 283, epoch 4); its records
were the same in both runs with the plan (`eaf3d5fb…`), and its decisions for `c27_q` and `c29_q`
saw 0.0, the rule's two rows.

The two runs with the plan of each regression wrote the same records (`f1067232…`, `86a7df98…`).
On the buggy regression 2 of 22 keys changed, `c27` and `c29`, the draws past the limit. Their
history: `setTransactionMetadata` returns with the limit 50.0 and `meta.overdraft_limit =
absent`; the API's copy for Redis has 50.0; the worker's coalesced copy, called from

sees 0.0. On the fixed build no key changed, and the metadata holds 50.0. In the passing run 3 of
65 keys lost the limit in their coalesced copy, and one of them reached the decision with 0.0.

**The cost.** The regression stopped at 98 entries and 44 returns, 142 breakpoint stops, each
with its single step; a stop makes at most 115 reads. The engine's time was 5.5 s and 5.1 s with
the plan and 5.2 s and 5.5 s without it, the same 10,288 stops each; the records are 59 KB.

**Tests and checks.** New: `hydo-contracts`'s `values::` (the lines, floats, each reader's
evaluation on synthetic reads, histories and copies, a return not reached) and
`types::go_values_on_arm64_and_x86_64`; the results example
`hydo/schema/examples/results/v1/mac-blnk-values/values.json`, recorded from the regression's
run. Re-recorded for the new guide topic and manifest: `hydo`'s `equivalence::` and
`agents_equivalence::` goldens, and the explorer's `identity-quick.txt` and `corpus-full.txt`.

-p hydo-contracts`, `-p hydo-hvm`,
`-p hydo-config`, `-p hydo-results`; `hydo-schedule`'s `language::`; `hydo-agents`'s
`public_content::`; `hydo`'s `docs::`; `hydo-explore`'s `identity::` and `corpus::`;

### Milestone 286 (tentative number) - DONE (hydo in a team's CI, what makes a team keep it after the first try: `hydo ci page`, the history store as one web page that loads nothing; `comment.md` and `hydo ci comment`, the pull-request comment of only what the change did, edited in place by `action/comment.sh`; the `workflow_run` recorder `action/examples/hydo-record.yml` for pull requests from forks; `seeds_from: history`, budgets turned into seed counts; proven on this Mac with the Mac engine on a throwaway repository of four commits and two pull requests; nothing ran on GitHub; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-17)

**Why.** Open item 67 listed what stage 2 of `docs/design/ci.md` left after M223. A team that
tried hydo once still had no view of its findings over time, and a pull request's comment listed
every finding of the run, also those the change did not cause. A pull request from a fork got no
comment at all, because its token cannot write. These are the parts a team meets every day.

**Built** (`hydo/crates/hydo-cli/src/ci/`, `src/htmlreport/history.rs`, `action/`, `hydo guide ci`
sections 3, 10, 12, 13 and 14):

1. **The history page.** `hydo ci page --store DIR [-o FILE]` writes `DIR/index.html` with the
   style sheet and the copy script of `hydo report --html`; the page loads nothing. It folds each
   branch's recorded runs again with `history::fold`, so it shows what each run did to each
   finding. Per project it has:
   - a card per finding: its state on the main line (`main`, `master`, else the branch with the
     most runs), the commit where it was first seen and when, the commits where a replay proved
     it fixed and where it came back, the acceptance and its reason, the minimal schedule, the
     replay line, the `hydo ci accept` line, the link to the report page of the run that last
     saw it, and its state on each branch;
   - a timeline per branch, one column per run (the latest 30), with `new`, `fails`, `fixed`,
     `back`, and `·` for a run that did not find a finding that stays open;
   - the runs, the latest first (at most 200): time, branch, commit, trigger, seeds, budget,
     engine, runs, findings by state, result, and links.

   A pull request's first run of a finding that its target branch had fixed shows `back`. Every
   text is escaped, and a run's job link is kept only when it starts with `http://` or
   `https://`, because a fork's run can name any text.
2. **The store keeps the order and the report pages.** `hydo ci record` adds
   `CiLedgerBranch.recorded`, the runs in recording order with the time in UTC (a results
   addition, `CiLedgerRun`). With `--report` it also writes the run's report page, made by
   `hydo report --html`'s code from the run's directory, to `v1/<project>/reports/<id>.html`; it
   never copies a page from the run. A store written before has no order; the page then takes
   the run files in name order.
3. **The comment of only what the change did.** `hydo ci run`, `hydo ci merge` and `hydo ci
   compare` write `comment.md` (src/ci/comment.rs). It lists the findings in the states `new`,
   `reappeared`, `changed` and `fixed`, at most 10 per state. Each has its minimal schedule, the
   `hydo run` line in a shell block (`--backend kvm` on KVM, shell quoting when the schedule
   needs it), the commit where the history fixed a finding that came back, the first difference
   from the base, and the `hydo ci accept` line (the head's key for a `changed` finding, none for
   a `fixed` one). The other findings are counted in one sentence. Text from a run goes into code
   spans and fences one backtick longer than any backtick run in it, so a title cannot add
   Markdown, links or mentions. `hydo ci comment <ci-run.json | DIR> [-o FILE]` makes the same
   text from a recorded run. `CiImage.set` (a results addition) keeps the `--set` values, so that
   the comment names the `hydo build` line without the run's settings.
4. **The comment edited in place.** `action/comment.sh REPO NUMBER MARKER FILE` finds the comment
   whose first line is the marker `<!-- hydo-ci: <project> -->`, which the action used before, so
   an existing comment is kept. It edits that comment or posts a new one with `gh api`. The
   marker is compared in the shell, not put into a jq program, and the body goes from a file
   (`-F body=@FILE`). A token that cannot write gives a warning and exit status 0. The action
   posts `comment.md`, or `report.md` for a hydo older than 0.4.0.
5. **The `workflow_run` recorder.** `action/examples/hydo.yml` runs `hydo ci run` with a read-only
   token and reads the history branch `hydo-history` into a temporary directory (the action's new
   `history` input). `action/examples/hydo-record.yml` starts on `workflow_run` of `hydo`, in the
   default branch's context, with `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write`, in the
   concurrency group `hydo-history`. It downloads the artifact `hydo-ci-<run id>-<attempt>`. It
   finds the pull request from the event: the event's own list, else the open pull request whose
   head is the event's head commit, which must be hexadecimal. The action's new `recorded` input
   makes the comment with `hydo ci comment` and runs no VM, and `pull-request` names the pull
   request. The workflow then records the run with `hydo ci record --report`. A pull request goes
   on the line `pull/<number>`, and a push or a scheduled run on its own branch. It writes the
   page and pushes the branch, which it creates as an orphan the first time.
6. **Budgets from history.** `seeds_from: history` per mode in `hydo/ci.yaml` (a format-1
   addition, with the example `seeds-from-history.yaml`) or `--seeds-from history`, with a
   budget and `--history`. `history::measured` averages the seconds per seed of the last 10
   recorded runs with the same engine, strategy and options: `CiBudget.explore_s` over the seeds
   explored, and `base_explore_s` when the base is explored too. `hydo ci run` then explores the
   first seeds of the range that fit into the time left after the image builds (85 % of the
   budget, as before), at least 1 and at most the range. The time limit stays on. `ci-run.json`
   gets `budget.seeds_from` (`history`, or `range` when nothing was measured), `seconds_per_seed`,
   `measured_runs`, and `range` for the range the seeds came from. The report says which it
   used. A shard keeps its part of the range. `hydo ci merge` adds the shards' `explore_s`.

Results-format additions: `CiBudget.explore_s`, `base_explore_s`, `seeds_from`,
`seconds_per_seed` and `measured_runs`, `CiImage.set`, `CiLedgerBranch.recorded` and the type
`CiLedgerRun`, with examples from the proof in `hydo/schema/examples/results/v1/mac-redis-ci-page/`.
`hydo/ci.yaml` format 1 adds `seeds_from`. The schema checks pass against the released schemas. Two small report fixes: a run without a base no longer counts a fixed finding
in its headline (`1 finding` became `1 fixed`), and `hydo ci comment --help` and `hydo ci page
--help` print their usage.

**Proof, on this Mac** (an M2 Pro, the Mac engine, this tree's hydo over the 0.3.4 Mac release,
one VM at a time under the session's VM lock, `workers: 1`). A throwaway git repository holds the
0.3.2 release's Redis example with `push` and `pr` set to `{seeds: 1-8, strategy: swarm}`. Its
clean base has no lying disk in `faults:` and no `R` setting, because each loses acknowledged
writes with `appendfsync always` too; the first two tries found them. The store is a plain
directory:

| Commit or run | Line | Result |
|---|---|---|
| c1, the clean base | `main` | 8 runs, no finding, 19 s |
| c2 as a pull request against c1 (`appendfsync everysec`) | `pull/1` | `hydo: 1 new finding (failed)`: `VIOLATION [redis.acked_writes_survive] key k:# lost` (`f1:invariant:5ef675c8c9`), minimal schedule `disk=cut dseed=eac0b527c5ac67d9 \| run C=20`, the base passes it; 17 runs, 2 replays, 48 s |
| c2 on `main` | `main` | the event `new` |
| c3, a change elsewhere, and `hydo ci accept` of the key | `main` | `hydo: 0 findings, 1 accepted (passed)`; the event `accepted` |
| c4, `appendfsync always` again and the entry removed | `main` | the exploration did not find it; the history's schedule passed on replay: `fixed` |
| c5 as a pull request against c4 (`everysec` again) | `pull/2` | `hydo: no new findings, 1 reappeared (failed)`; the comment's section "Back again" names c4 as the commit where it was fixed |
| c4 with `--budget 3m --seeds 1-200 --seeds-from history` | `main` | `budget from history: 153 s left at 2.5 s per seed (6 recorded runs): 60 of the 200 seeds of 1-200`; all 60 explored in 71 s, so the estimate was high by a factor of 2 |

The comment of each pull request lists only that finding, with its schedule, its replay line,
its first difference from the base, and its accept line. `hydo ci comment out/pr2` gives the
same bytes as the run's `comment.md`. The page (15 KiB) was checked by its text: the finding is
`Fixed` on `main`, first seen at `ac7ab56821`, fixed at `eb12f87641`, accepted before the fix
with its reason, `Open` on `pull/1` and `Back again` on `pull/2`. The timeline of `main` reads
nothing, `new`, `fails`, `fixed`, nothing. The runs table has all seven runs with a link to each
report page. The page has no `http` text and no `src` link. A screenshot by headless Chrome
showed the same. The 0.3.4 release's hydo read the new `ci-run.json` (`hydo ci compare`) and the
new `state.json` (`hydo ci record`), and dropped `recorded` when it rewrote the ledger.

Tests: `ci::comment::` (only what the change did, a run's text kept inside its span, the limit
per state, and `comment.sh` against a fake `gh` over files: it posts the first comment, edits it
on the next call, leaves a person's comment and another project's alone, warns on a read-only
token, and refuses a number that is not one before any call), `htmlreport::history::` (the page
of four commits and a pull request, escaping, the dropped `javascript:` link, the UTC dates) and
`ci::run::a_budget_becomes_a_seed_count_from_history`. actionlint 1.7.12 and shellcheck report
nothing for `action/examples/` and `comment.sh`, nor shellcheck for the action's scripts.

**Checklist for the trial on GitHub** (it needs the lead: a repository and a fork):

1. Release 0.4.0, or point the examples' `hydo-version` at a build of this tree.
2. In a throwaway repository, add the Redis example, `hydo/ci.yaml` with `pr` and `push` seeds
   `1-20` and `engine: kvm`, and both files of `action/examples/` in `.github/workflows/`.
3. Push to `main`, and check that `hydo record` creates the branch `hydo-history` with
   `index.html`.
4. Open a pull request from a branch with `appendfsync everysec`. Check one comment with the
   new finding, and that a second push edits it.
5. Open the same change from a fork. Check that `hydo` passes without writing, and that
   `hydo record` posts the comment and records the line `pull/<number>`.
6. Merge, then fix the setting on `main`, and check `fixed` on the page.
7. Turn on GitHub Pages for `hydo-history`, and open the page.
