## Milestone 310 (tentative number): three fixes of explorations on many runners

Open item 153 named three gaps of M304's sharded explorations. A part's commands and an error
path count were lost on the way to the user.

**What changed.**

- `hydo explore --merge` adds up the parts' error paths (M306): the run counts and each place's
  runs add up, and a place's first run is that of the earliest part that ran it. Before, the
  merged exploration kept the first part's paths only. A unit test in `merge.rs` checks the sums
  and the first run. No sharded run watches error paths yet, because only the Mac engine watches
  them and the parts run on KVM.
- The report's command for more runs (`hydo report`, its page, and `report.md`'s "Next") names
  the image by its file name when the project has no folder, as the replay lines already did.
  A merged exploration's image path is the runner's (`/mnt/w/up/img/...`).
- `ci/remote-explore.sh` runs `hydo report` and `hydo report --html` again on the downloaded
  folder, so their commands name that folder. Without a `hydo` on `PATH` the runner's text stays.
- `explore.yml` copies the example's `known-errors.yaml` (next to its manifest, or in its
  `hydo/` folder) into the build's files, and each part passes it with `--known-errors`. The
  Dragonfly and Redpanda runs of M304 had reported their expected error kinds as new.

**Evidence.** On the downloaded merge of M304's Redis run (seeds 1-40 in 8 parts), `hydo report`
now ends with `More runs: hydo explore --image explore-ob-redis-disk.img --seeds 41-140` and the
local folder in the page's command; before, both named the runner's paths. The workflow passed
actionlint and the script shellcheck. No workflow run used the changes yet. Nothing recorded
moved.

**What is left.** Open item 153.

## Milestone 308 (tentative number): a third evaluation of `hydo fuzz` by a new user

A fresh evaluator, a coding agent that played a Rust developer new to hydo, tried `hydo fuzz`
natively after Milestone 307. The evaluator learned the tool only from `hydo guide fuzz` and
`hydo fuzz --help`, read the two earlier evaluations (M280, M288) only for their method and their
crates, and did not read hydo's source. The binary came from `main` at `bc91ab75`. The page is
`docs/design/function-fuzzing-evaluation-3.md`. No code of hydo changed.

The crates were heck 0.5.0, half 2.7.1, either 1.19.0, humantime 2.4.0, percent-encoding 2.3.2
(a member of the `rust-url` workspace) and arrayvec 0.7.8, each from its latest release. The
evaluator contracted 73 library functions and 54 property functions. hydo fuzzed 57 of the
library functions. It refused 13: 12 methods of arrayvec for their const generic parameter, and
one method of either that takes a closure. It could not build the harness of 3: humantime's
`parse_duration`, and percent-encoding's two encoders, which take a `&'static AsciiSet`. Each
crate's first useful run came 1 to 2.5 minutes after the first look at its source.

hydo reproduced 9 bugs that were already reported upstream, and found no new candidate:

- heck: issues 36, 70 and 71 (case conversions that are not idempotent, at `"a_a"`, `"ﬄ"` and
  `"İ"`);
- humantime: issues 67, 68, 69, 78 and 82 (an offset read as UTC, a panic in the year 10000, a
  space inside a number, bytes after `Z`, a refused fraction of an hour);
- percent-encoding: `rust-url` issue 1132 (`AsciiSet::add` panics at `byte = 128`).

The worst problems, in order:

1. A false `broken` verdict: an element of a list of built values compares as its constructor's
   arguments, so half's `result[0] == self[0]` broke with `self = [f16::from_bits(7)]` and
   `result = [7]`.
2. heck's eight trait methods return `Self::Owned`, which hydo does not read. Each was `vacuous`,
   with a `to fix:` line about the inputs.
3. humantime has two enumerations named `Error`. hydo read `duration::Error` as `date::Error`, so
   `parse_duration` could not be fuzzed.
4. Const generics, `&'static` parameters and closures are refused or do not build.
5. The default strings hold three characters outside ASCII. heck's title case bug held for 50,000
   calls until the evaluator named `ß`, `İ`, `ﬄ` and a combining mark with `chars`.
6. A `read` line by `to_string()` does not build in a `#![no_std]` crate, `by collect()` needs a
   type, and a turbofish or a generic type name is refused.

A bug planted in arrayvec's `swap_pop` broke the evaluator's model property on 4 of 1,000 calls,
and the shrink gave 11 operations. Open item 139 lists the fixes. Nothing recorded moved.

### Milestone 309 (tentative number) - DONE (open item 154's fourth point: with `--kill-now`, half of the fault reactions, drawn from a stream of their own, kill any service at the event's moment, and the schedule's `K=` or `P=` on that service is left out; on Meilisearch, which has one service, 101 of 360 schedules carried a `kill-now-` reaction against none of 24 before, and finding 1, the index swap that runs twice, was found blind at seed 101 and shrunk to one reaction without other faults; explorations without `--kill-now` draw the same schedules; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-18)

**What was asked.** Open item 154's fourth point. `hydo explore --reactive fault --kill-now`
drew a `kill-now-<svc>` reaction only on a service that the schedule's `K=` and `P=` did not
name, as the plain `kill-<svc>` reactions do since M139. On a manifest with one service the
process strategy puts a `K=` or a `P=` on that service in most schedules. So 24 seeds of the
Meilisearch example with `--kill-now` drew no `kill-now-` reaction (Milestone 305), and a blind
exploration could not reach finding 1: an index swap that runs twice when the server dies
between its two commits. The task was a fair share of `kill-now-` reactions also on such a
manifest, without a change to any schedule that an exploration without `--kill-now` draws.

**The design.** With `--kill-now`, the reactions take one more draw from a stream of their own
(`NOW_SALT`, in `hydo_explore::gen`): a coin with a probability of 50 % (`NOW_TAKE_PCT`) and a
service. When the coin is up and the schedule has a fault reaction (60 % of the schedules), the
reaction is `kill-now-<v>` of the drawn service `v`, with these rules:

- `v` is drawn from all the services, as for a pause. With `cf=` it is only the bug benchmark's
  order service, as before, and a manifest has no such service, so no reaction is taken there.
- The schedule's `K=` on `v` (also a list that names `v`) is left out. The schedule's `P=` on
  `v` is left out, and with it a heal reaction `cont-<v>` of that pause.
- The reaction keeps the event, the step it is armed at and the delay that the reaction stream
  drew. A reaction armed at the start of the `K=` or `P=` that it replaces stays armed there.
- A taken reaction is never a power cut or a stop, so the disk stays as the strategy drew it.

When the coin is down, the schedule is the one of Milestone 305: each drawn kill is
`kill-now-<svc>`. Without `--kill-now` the new stream is not read, so every other draw keeps its
value: `reactive::the_reactive_stream_is_pinned` and every golden of `hydo-explore` pass
unchanged.

**Why not the other options.**

- Draw the reaction first and the process faults on the rest of the services: on a manifest
  with one service there is no rest, so the strategy's faults would all go. The take leaves the
  other half of the schedules as the strategy drew them.
- Keep the `K=` and `P=` and kill the service anyway: a kill-now reaction on a service that a
  `K=` already keeps down, or that a `P=` stops, is a schedule with two meanings. The rule of
  M139 that a reaction does not act on the `K=` or `P=` service stays true.
- Change the process strategy itself: its draws are pinned by the identity goldens, and the
  change is for `--kill-now` only.

**Tests.** hydo-explore's `reactive::kill_now_changes_only_the_drawn_kills` now checks both
kinds of schedule. When the coin is down, the schedule is the one without `--kill-now` with each
kill made `kill-now-`. When it is up, the schedule is the one without `--kill-now` with the fault
reaction replaced by `kill-now-<v>` at the same event and step, the `K=` and `P=` on `v` left
out, and nothing else changed. The new `reactive::kill_now_reaches_the_only_service` draws 1,000
seeds on one service. With the process strategy, 306 schedules carry a `kill-now-` reaction,
against 11 with the rule of Milestone 305. The random strategy gives 377, and swarm gives 380.
No such schedule also has a `K=` or `P=` on the service.

**Meilisearch on the Mac engine.** The example's image built with this tree (`--set
arch=arm64`, initramfs `dddbbcab…`, the image of Milestone 305), 0.4.0's guest files, one

The seeds 61 to 360 ran as a second exploration with the same options.

| 1-60 | 15 | none | none |
| 61-360 | 86 | seeds 101, 138, 158, 160, 183 and 307 | seeds 117, 123, 185, 198 and 318 |

So 101 of the 360 schedules (28 %) carried a `kill-now-` reaction: 33 after a swap's event, 34

## Milestone 315 (tentative number): `hydo update` updates hydo and every copy of its skill

A user's coding agent tried to move a hydo 0.3.1 to 0.4.0. It downloaded every asset of the
release, two sources archives of about 1.2 GB among them, found that the old hydo cannot install
a newer one, and needed three steps by hand. On the same Mac, Claude Code had the skill from
hydo's plugin marketplace at 2.0.0 while 2.3.3 was out, and `hydo skill update` does not reach a
marketplace install: it updates only the copies in `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`. The
user's requirement: "`hydo update` should update everything without any need to do any other
harder things".

**What changed.**

- `hydo update [--check] [--yes] [--version V] [--offline]` (`hydo/crates/hydo-cli/src/update.rs`).
  It reads the release list (`HYDO_RELEASE_API`) once. The target is the newest `v<x>.<y>.<z>`
  release that is neither a draft nor a pre-release, or `--version V`; the newest skill release
  comes from the same list. How hydo was installed comes from its own program's real path:
  - a Homebrew keg (`<prefix>/Cellar/hydo/...`): `brew update` when `brew info --json=v2` names
    an older formula, then `brew upgrade kakoc/tap/hydo` and the new hydo's `hydo doctor`;
  - cargo (`<root>/bin/hydo` with cargo's `.crates2.json` naming `hydo` in `<root>`): `cargo
    install hydo --locked --version V --root <root>`, then the new `hydo setup` and `hydo doctor`;
  - an `install.sh` tree (`SHA256SUMS` around `bin/hydo`): only this platform's
    `hydo-<mac|linux>-V.tar.gz` and the release's `SHA256SUMS`, over TLS, the archive accepted
    only with the sha256 that file names, unpacked in a temporary folder, and its `install.sh
    --prefix <tree>`. On Linux it adds `--no-module` unless the module `hvx` is loaded, and says
    first that the module's install asks for `sudo`; with the udev rule it adds `--udev
    --udev-group <the rule's group>`;
  - a version of the install cache (`<HYDO_HOME>/versions/<own version>`): the same download,
    then the new hydo's `hydo setup --archive <archive>` and `hydo setup --get V`;
  - anything else, such as a checkout's build: nothing of hydo changes, and the commands to
    update it are printed.
- The skill is brought to the newest skill release, downloaded once and checked as `hydo skill
  update` checks it, in every copy found:
  - the copies that `hydo skill update` knows;
  - `skills/hydo` of each Claude Code configuration folder: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `~/.claude`,
    and every other `~/.claude*` folder with `plugins/` or `settings.json`
    (`hydo_agents::copies::claude_config_dirs`);
  - every copy in the new registry `~/.hydo/skill-copies.txt` (`<version>\t<path>` lines), which
    `hydo skill install`, `hydo skill update`, `hydo onboard` and `hydo update` write. A line
    whose copy is gone is dropped. A copy inside the temporary directory is not recorded: the
    first run of the whole test program recorded the scratch copies of `tests/readme.rs`, which
    runs `hydo onboard` with the user's home, in the real `~/.hydo`. Those lines, and the
    doctor's `update-check.json` of the doctor tests before they set `HYDO_UPDATE_CHECK=0`, were
    deleted again; both files exist only since this milestone.
- Claude Code's marketplace installs: in each configuration folder whose
  `plugins/installed_plugins.json` lists `hydo@hydo`, with `claude` on `PATH`, `claude plugin
  marketplace update hydo` once, then `claude plugin update hydo@hydo --scope <scope>` for each
  install (in the project's folder for a project or local install), all with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`
  set to that folder. The commands' syntax is that of `claude plugin --help` of Claude Code
  2.1.327. A managed install is left alone. Only the `hydo@hydo` entries are read; nothing else
  of these folders is read or printed.
- The plan lists hydo and each copy and install with its version before and after, the way hydo
  is updated, and the "Before you upgrade" section of each newer release's notes (the release's
  body in the list). `--check` changes nothing and exits 0 or 3. Without `--yes` a terminal is
  asked once; elsewhere the plan is printed, nothing changes, and the exit status is 3. At the
  end it lists what changed and says that a new session of the AI tool loads the new skill.
- `hydo doctor` prints one line when a newer release exists, with `hydo update`. It looks at most
  once a day, with one attempt of at most 3 s (`fetch::Options::quick`, the new `timeout`), and
  keeps the answer, also a failed look, in `~/.hydo/update-check.json`. `HYDO_UPDATE_CHECK=0`
  (new, in hydo-config) and `HYDO_OFFLINE` turn the look off. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is registered
  in hydo-config too.
- The skill 2.4.0: its step 0 runs `hydo update --check` and, when something is newer, asks the
  user and runs `hydo update --yes`. A hydo without the command (0.4.0 and older) prints its usage
  text; the skill then offers the one manual upgrade of `references/install.md`, which now says
  to fetch only this platform's archive. `hydo-min` stays 0.1.0, because the skill still works
  with an older hydo. The facts are in the new guide topic `hydo guide update`;
  `docs/INSTALL.md` has the section "Upgrading".

**Evidence.** `tests/update.rs` (12 tests) runs this tree's hydo against a local HTTP server
with a fake release 0.9.0 (an archive whose `bin/hydo` and `install.sh` are scripts that record
their arguments, its `SHA256SUMS`, a `-sources` asset, and a skill release 2.9.0), and fake
`brew`, `cargo` and `claude` programs that record theirs. The hydo under test runs where cargo
built it (a checkout build) or copied into a Homebrew keg, a cargo bin folder, an `install.sh`
tree and a version of the install cache:

- the archive tree ran `install.sh --prefix <tree>`, and the server served only `SHA256SUMS`
  and this platform's archive; the plan quoted only the newer release's "Before you upgrade";
- a `SHA256SUMS` with another sha256 ended with exit status 1, no `install.sh`, the same
  `bin/hydo` bytes and an empty temporary folder;
- the install cache ran the new hydo's `setup --archive <archive>` and `setup --get 0.9.0`;
- Homebrew ran `brew info`, `brew update`, `brew info` and `brew upgrade kakoc/tap/hydo`, then
  the new hydo's `doctor`, and nothing was downloaded;
- cargo ran `cargo install hydo --locked --version 0.9.0 --root <root>`, then `setup` and
  `doctor` of the new program;
- the checkout build changed nothing and printed the commands;
- `--check` exited 3 with an older copy and 0 when everything was current; without `--yes` and
  without a terminal the plan exited 3 and changed nothing; `HYDO_OFFLINE` and a release list
  that cannot be reached exited 1 and changed nothing;
- in a home with two Claude Code folders (one with a skill copy, one with a user and a project
  install of `hydo@hydo` beside another plugin), a third folder named by `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, an
  `.agents/skills/onboard` copy, a registered `--to` copy elsewhere and a registered copy that is
  gone, every copy reached 2.9.0. `claude` ran `plugin marketplace update hydo` once and `plugin
  update hydo@hydo` for the user scope and, in the project's folder, for the project scope, each
  with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` naming the folder with the installs. The other plugin's name and
  version and the settings' text appeared in no output, the gone copy's line was dropped, and a
  second `--check` exited 0;
- `hydo skill install --to DIR` and `hydo skill update` recorded their copies in the registry;
- `hydo doctor` named 0.9.0 in two runs with one look at the list, and printed nothing with
  `HYDO_UPDATE_CHECK=0` or `HYDO_OFFLINE=1`.

The unit tests cover the release list, the notes' section, the recognition of each install
kind, the daily look, the options, Claude Code's folders, the plugin entries, and the registry.
On this Mac, `hydo update --check` of the checkout's build against GitHub's real release list
printed:

```text
hydo update: hydo 0.4.0, this hydo was built in the checkout <the worktree>
  hydo: 0.4.0, the newest release (up to date)
  Claude Code ~/.claude: plugin hydo@hydo 2.0.0 -> 2.3.3: claude plugin update hydo@hydo (scope project, project <a project>)
  Claude Code ~/.claude-<second>: plugin hydo@hydo 2.3.1 -> 2.3.3: claude plugin update hydo@hydo (scope user)
```

with exit status 3: the two marketplace installs of the user's two Claude Code folders are
behind, and no copy is in the known folders. Nothing was updated: the user's Claude Code plugins
and `~/.hydo` were not changed. Nothing recorded moved.
