## Milestone 313 (tentative number): faults of the disk's blocks on the Mac and KVM engines

A team that tests its own storage engine with its own simulator said that hydo's disk faults act
on whole requests and whole files. Its storage engine's rules are about sectors. This milestone
adds four faults that a real disk makes, on the data disk of the Mac engine and of the KVM engine,
which share the virtio block device (`hydo/crates/hydo-hvm/src/virtio/block.rs`). The design is
`docs/design/block-faults.md`; the how-to is `hydo guide faults`, "Faults of the disk's blocks".

The host tokens, each decided from `dseed=` and from the requests counted from the workload's
start:

- `torn=<p>[:any]` (needs `disk=cut`): at a power cut, `<p>` percent of the unflushed writes of
  two or more sectors keep a seeded prefix of their sectors, or with `:any` a seeded subset,
  never none and never all;
- `mis=<k>[:<sectors>]`: the k-th write goes `<sectors>` away, or 1 to 16 blocks of 4 KiB away in
  a seeded direction, and the place it was meant for keeps its old bytes;
- `lse=<sector>+<count>[,...][:rot]`: reads of the sectors fail with an I/O error, or with `:rot`
  return 16 seeded damaged bytes per sector; a write of a whole sector repairs it; the sectors stay
  bad across a power cut;
- `hang=<k>[+<ms>]`: the k-th request gets no completion, or with `+<ms>` an I/O error after that
  many milliseconds of guest time.

The guest token `G=<svc>@<at>[+<down>]:bad|rot[,len=][,range=][,file=][,seed=]` aims a latent
sector error at a range of a file of a service's storage. At the fault's stop the controller runs
`sync`, asks busybox `stat` for the file's inode and device, and reads the partition's start from
sysfs. It then reads the ext4 superblock, the group descriptor, the inode and the extent tree
through the agent's existing `read` of the partition's device (`hydo-control`'s
`schedule/sectors.rs`). It sends the engine the new command `DISK lse=...` and drops the guest's
clean page cache. No agent and no image changed, so the agent pin stays.

What makes each fault inert when absent: the faults' state is outside the device state whose C
layout every recorded fingerprint hashes, and it joins a fingerprint only when a token armed it.
A `dseed=` alone arms nothing. The engine writes what the faults did to
`<run dir>/one.block-faults.txt` only when they did something.

A request that never completes: the guest kernel's virtio block driver renews its 30 s timer without
end, and the program waits in an uninterruptible sleep. A workload that times out in a run with
`hang=<k>` ends the run with `VIOLATION [disk.hang]`. When the guest has waited 120 s of its time
on the request, the engine ends the run with `ERROR <phase>: the data disk never answered a
request (hang=), and the guest waited 120 s of its time for it`. `hydo explore --block-faults`
draws one block fault in 60% of the schedules, from its own stream (`BLOCK_SALT`), and a failure
with one has the class `damaged-disk`. hvx refuses every block fault before any VM
(`hydo_hvx::sched::refusal`), and the design page says what its module would need.

**Evidence.** The example `hydo/onboard/examples/disk-faults` (RESULTS.md) runs recs, a small
record store with a careless and a careful variant, on the Mac engine. Every new fault broke the
careless variant: a torn record after `torn=100`, a stale record after `mis=5`, an I/O error and
damaged bytes after `G=...:bad` and `:rot`, an ignored write error after `hang=10+1000`, and
`VIOLATION [disk.hang]` after `hang=10`. The careful variant passed each one. Each of the 21
schedules ran twice with one fingerprint and one control transcript. `hydo explore --seeds 1-20
--block-faults` drew a block fault in 10 of 20 schedules. It found `hang=4` and `mis=3` on the
careless image, and nothing on the careful one.

The old schedules keep their values. The release's Redis example built from this tree to its
recorded sha256 `31e90668…`, and its 7 recorded schedules of `hvm/release-redis` gave their
recorded fingerprints and control hashes on the Mac engine (from `05f433ee427f8e3c` and
`f8953914130df454` for `disk=none | run` to `9e2ce885165b1bc1` and `3a704aaf23b5fa14` for
`disk=cut dseed=1f16055b6d41c6d9 | run C=9 R=no`). The tests of hydo-hvm, hydo-kvm, hydo-control
(its recorded transcripts), hydo-engine, hydo-engine-proto and hydo-hvx passed, and so did the
explorer's `fake_engine`. The explorer's identity goldens (`identity-quick.txt`,
`corpus-full.txt`) and the controller's `corpus-quick.txt` held byte for byte with the example's
two manifests moved aside. They are re-recorded with the manifests in, because every example
manifest is an input of them; the controller's golden only gained the two manifests' lines. The CLI
golden of `hydo guide manifest` is re-recorded for the new text of MANIFEST.md.

On Redis 7.2.4 (the release's example, `appendfsync always`) each schedule ran twice with one
fingerprint:

- `disk=cut dseed=1 torn=100 | run C=12` passed: no write of several sectors was unflushed at
  the cut, because Redis syncs each one.
- `torn=100:any` with `C=12 R=everysec` lost `k:0`, as the run without it does: Redis's unsynced
  data was in the guest's page cache, which a torn write does not reach.
- `mis=10` and `mis=30`, also with a kill and restart at step 15, passed: the misdirected writes
  did not hit the append-only file.
- `hang=30+1000` failed one flush with an I/O error. Redis stopped, as its `always` setting says
  it does, and its restart then stopped at `FATAL AOF MANIFEST FILE ERROR` (`Read AOF manifest
  failed`). The state of the guest's file system after the failed flush was not traced.
- `hang=30` ended `ERROR check: the data disk never answered a request (hang=), and the guest
  waited 120 s of its time for it`: the check's read waited on the disk.

The KVM engine did not run the faults on this Mac. The one-off workflow
`.github/workflows/tmp-disk-faults-kvm.yml` on the branch `tmp-disk-faults-kvm` runs the scripted
tests and the example's schedules twice on three of GitHub's KVM runners; it is committed and not
pushed. No fingerprint epoch change, and nothing recorded moved.

**What is left.** Open item 160.

**On KVM (after the milestone's commit).** The lead pushed the one-off workflow
`tmp-disk-faults-kvm`. Its first run found that `hydo-kvm` named a constant of `hydo-hvm`'s
module `serve`, which only the Mac builds, so the KVM engine did not compile on Linux; the
constant moved to `hydo_hvm::virtio`. Two later runs fixed the workflow's own image name and a read
of a missing notes file. Run 44380177675 then ran the example's 14 schedules twice on an AMD EPYC
7763 and two Xeon 6975P-C hosts. Every schedule gave the Mac engine's verdict and one fingerprint
over its two runs; the two Intel hosts agree (for example the careless store's torn write,
`8442b56bf4c79e4d`, and its misdirected write, `60696e6e8dc9d09a`), and AMD has its own values.

### Milestone 314 (tentative number) - DONE (Apache Iggy server 0.10.0, one server from its image and a client on its Go SDK v0.10.0, on hvx; with `durability: persisted` no acknowledged message was lost, stored twice or read out of order, no stored group offset was lost, and no message of the expiring topic was gone before its time, in 112 blind schedules and 30 directed runs; with the default `replicated` a kill alone loses acknowledged messages, which `hydo explore --configs` labels the documented trade-off (known as issue #4631); a backward clock step stops a partition's message expiry for the step's length, a clock effect by design; no new bug; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-18)

**The example.** `hydo/onboard/examples/iggy` (RESULTS.md) runs one Iggy server from its official
image `apache/iggy:0.10.0` (index `sha256:176125a0…`), imported with `hydo compose` from a
one-service Compose file. Only TCP is on, with one shard, a 512 MiB memory pool, and the segment
cleaner every 5 s. Its data directory is a file system of its own (`storage:`). Iggy refuses a
data directory that holds anything it did not write, so `IGGY_PATH` names a folder inside the
mount, beside the file system's `lost+found`. The client `iggyc` is one static Go program on
Iggy's Go SDK v0.10.0, built on the bare-metal machine; the Rust SDK needs Rust 1.95. `provision:`
creates the topic `t` (3 partitions), the topic `x` (1 partition, an expiry of 20 s, 1 MiB
segments) and the consumer group `g`. Both topics take the build parameter `durability`, by
default `persisted` in `hydo.yaml`. Producers send batches with unique message ids to `t`; one
group member at a time joins `g`, reads with the SDK's partition reader, stores its offsets by
hand and leaves; others send 128 KiB batches to `x`, and a probe reads `x` during the run.

**The checks.** A messages check over `t` claims at-least-once delivery, no duplicates, the log's
order per partition, delivery to both the full read and `g` (`fan_out: every-group`), and no
redelivery after an acknowledged offset store. Its drain reads every partition from offset 0, then
`g` from its stored offsets. The expiry check and the probe judge `x` by Iggy's rule
(`core/partitions/src/segment.rs`, `is_expired`). A message is gone early if it was sent less than
the expiry before the latest wall clock that the run showed. A sealed segment of the leading run of
expired segments must not stay 30 s past its expiry. The latest clock is the uptime plus the
largest offset of the wall clock from the uptime that a command recorded, so a step back never
makes a deletion look early. Two clean runs give one fingerprint on each image, `a23c4e632bba0742`
on the final one.

**What held.** With `persisted`, under kills, pauses, power cuts at steps, the server's power loss,
clock steps of 30 s to 30 days both ways, and on the image with the client's console events, power
cuts and kills at the moment of an acknowledged send or offset store (`A=ig.send_acked`,
`A=ig.commit_acked`, 25 schedules, 10 with `kill-now-iggy`). 9 power cuts at disk flushes
`cf=50` to `cf=1500`, and 6 kills at 0 to 3 ms after an acknowledgement, held too. Exploration 1
(process, storage faults, seeds 1-20) had 7 ERRORs, each a damaged file that Iggy detects and
fences. Exploration 2 (process, seeds 1-40) and exploration 3 (process, `--more-faults`,
reactions, `--kill-now`, seeds 41-80) had none. Exploration 4 (swarm, seeds 81-120) stopped after
24 schedules, when the host's out-of-memory killer ended one of its engines; its 11 schedules
with disk I/O errors or a lying disk failed, the disk's loss, and the other 13 passed.

**The setting.** `hydo/hydo-configs.yaml` explores `durability` from Iggy's default: `hydo explore
--configs`, seeds 1-12, kills and power cuts. `replicated` failed 7 of 12, shrunk to `C=30` and to
`K=iggy@15+1`; `persisted` passed 12. The table labels both failures the documented trade-off
(the server's README, "Replication factor": `replicated` "acknowledges a write before that copy
reaches disk"). Issue #4631 (closed) has the cause, the truncation to the last published WAL
frontier at recovery, and a comment that measured the loss after one `kill -9` of a single node.
After the kill the next offset was 65537, the next block of the offset reservation lease, so no
offset held two messages.

**The clock effect.** The cleaner walks a partition's sealed segments from the oldest and stops at
the first one that has not expired (`leading_expired_end`), by its newest message's timestamp, the
wall clock at the append (`IggyTimestamp::now()`, `SystemTime`). After a step back, the oldest
segment's timestamps lie ahead of the clock, so `disk=none | run T=15:-86400` kept all 4 sealed
segments, 512 messages, to the end; without the step 512 of 544 were deleted. The code and the
documentation delete the oldest sealed segments by timestamp, so this is by design. No issue
names it; #4650 (an idle partition's active segment never seals) is another cause. Not reported.

Retro: Apache Iggy server 0.10.0, hvx, 2026-11-18
- Time to the first clean run: 35 minutes of wall time (20 of them scouting), none of it waiting
  for machines.
- Schedules run before the first finding: no new finding. The configuration run's first schedule
  showed the documented loss of `replicated`. 3 ERRORs of exploration 1 were the expiry check's
  own mistake, a wait of 60 s inside a command timeout of 60 s; its rule for kept segments was too
  strict after a step back, and both were rewritten before exploration 2.
- The findings: 0 new, 1 known and documented (the loss with `replicated`, #4631), 1 clock effect
  by design (the expiry after a step back), 1 documented (detected damage fences a partition).
- What took the most time: the expiry check (40 minutes: a rule for the latest clock that a step
  back cannot fool, and the cleaner's leading run); the configuration exploration's shrinks (14
  minutes); the setup on a shared machine (scripts for one remote job at a time, 15 minutes).
- What hydo lacked: a check cannot read the guest's clock steps or the clock at the moment of an
  event (open item 159); a new `storage:` file system holds `lost+found`, which Iggy refuses (a row
  of the playbook's setup problems).
- Strategies: `hydo explore --configs` showed the documented loss of the default at the first
  seeds; the entries "Settings that trade durability", "Clock steps and the clock audit" and "One
  node's storage faults" of `hydo guide strategies` are updated.

**What is left.** Open item 159.

## Milestone 312 (tentative number): the VictoriaMetrics cluster and its replicas

The onboarding of the VictoriaMetrics cluster version v1.156.0 (2026-11-09, the latest release)
on hvx, by `docs/ONBOARDING-PLAYBOOK.md`. Three new candidates, all clock effects, none posted.
Nothing recorded moved.

**The example.** `hydo/onboard/examples/victoriametrics` (RESULTS.md) runs two `vmstorage`
nodes, one `vminsert` with `-replicationFactor=2` and one `vmselect` with
`-replicationFactor=2 -dedup.minScrapeInterval=1ms`, from the official images
(`victoriametrics/<component>:v1.156.0-cluster`), imported with `hydo compose` from the example's
Compose file. Each node's `/storage` is a file system of its own (`storage:`), and the release is a
parameter (`vm`). The Go client `vmc` imports 2 new series with 3 samples each per write through
`/api/v1/import` and records each acknowledged sample. A messages check (`no-loss`,
`duplicates: forbidden`, `no-phantom` for a wrong value) reads every sample back with
`/api/v1/export`. A query check compares `count_over_time` and `sum_over_time` with the writes,
and an `anytime_` read judges the samples acknowledged 30 s earlier during the faults. Two clean
runs give one fingerprint: `9386f5eab3082c58` on the final image (`da0e7ab0…`), and
`cb0237a41b672c7f` twice with rounds of 1 s.

**Finding 1, new.** A backward clock step deletes the current month's partition on every
vmstorage node. `retentionWatcher` (`lib/storage/table.go:446`) drops every partition whose start
is later than now plus `-futureRetention` (2 days by default, line 464), and `pt.Drop()` removes
its data and index. `disk=none | run T=20:-1728000 W=740c6cfa,p2,q2,r1000` (20 days back from
2026-11-18) loses all 162 samples acknowledged before the step, `fp=ed7eab9cd7aa0756` on every
run; 18 days back passes. v1.141.0, which added the future retention (pull request #10718),
loses them too, and v1.140.0 keeps the partition. Blind in e1's seeds 4, 7 and 18.

**Finding 2, new.** After a backward clock step, new rows and new index entries wait in
vmstorage's memory for the step's length. Their buffers store the flush deadline as
`time.Now().Add(2s).UnixMilli()` (`lib/storage/raw_row.go:248`, `:325`; `lib/mergeset/table.go:208`,
`:278`) and compare wall-clock milliseconds. A read 30 s after `T=10:-3600` misses 12
acknowledged samples with both nodes healthy. `T=10:-3600 K=storage.all@50+2` loses 360
acknowledged samples (`fp=295f21500237d2ee`), and the same kill without the step loses 60.

**Finding 3, new.** A backward clock step leaves a batch with one copy. `BufferedConn`
(`lib/handshake/buffered_conn.go`) compares the deadline that `SendRPCRequestToConn` set from
`time.Now()` with `fasttime`, which a goroutine refreshes once a second. Right after the step
every write to both nodes failed with `i/o timeout`, and vminsert logged `cannot make a copy #2
out of 2 copies`. `T=10:-3600 L=vmstorage1@50+2` then loses 3 acknowledged samples for good
(`fp=f52ca18bd47eb06a`): vmstorage1 held its one copy in memory (finding 2) until its power
loss. Each fault alone loses nothing.

**Known and documented.** A crash of both nodes loses the last seconds (documented). A node that
lost its unflushed samples stays without them, so a later outage of the other node misses them
(issue #2613; the cluster has no repair). vminsert answers before vmstorage has the data (issue
#8677). A new series is invisible for up to 10 s to a cached tag filter, also after
`/internal/force_flush` (issue #5555, pull request #11116). A sample more than 2 days ahead of
vmstorage's clock is dropped after vminsert answered `204` (documented). Damaged files stop
vmstorage or return another value (the environment).

**What held.** Without clock steps, one node's kill, pause, partition, one-way loss, or power
loss lost no acknowledged sample, and every query returned each sample once with its value. In
e2 (40 schedules without `G=`) every failure without a clock step needed both nodes to fail
within a few seconds of each other.

**Explorations.** e1 (process, seeds 1-30, with `G=`, stopped during its shrinks): 21 failures, 11
of them detected corruption. e2 (process, seeds 31-70, `explore-nocorrupt.yaml`, no shrink): 20
failures in 273 s. e3 (swarm, seeds 71-110, no shrink, one worker): 24 failures in 387 s, 10 of them detected
corruption; every violation without `G=` had a clock step or two node faults within seconds.

**Tests.** The explorer's `identity-quick.txt` and `corpus-full.txt` and the controller's
`corpus-quick.txt` are re-recorded. They gain the new example's entries and the chunk digests
after them; the quick identity tier samples every fifth group, so the new manifest also moves
which other examples it samples. `identity-full.txt` is not re-recorded: it already lacked
Blnk's `hydo-paths.yaml` and a Meilisearch regression from earlier milestones. The CLI golden
differs on the bare-metal machine only in the `--check` warning of open item 115.

Retro: the VictoriaMetrics cluster v1.156.0, hvx, 2026-11-18
- Time to the first clean run: 70 minutes of wall time, none of it waiting for machines.
- Schedules run before the first finding: 4 blind schedules of e1 (seed 4 was finding 1) and
  10 directed runs that passed. Before them 3 clean runs failed by the checks' mistakes (the
  console limit, vmselect's 30 s latency offset, the 10 s tag filter cache).
- The findings: 3 new (clock effects that break a promise or a documented limit), 4 known or
  documented, 2 of the environment.
- What took the most time: separating the faults of the explorations' failures (about 1.5
  hours, 40 directed runs); e1's shrinks of detected corruption (1 hour, stopped); the client's
  history records over hvx's 64 KiB console (30 minutes).
- What hydo lacked: nothing warns that a run's history passed the console's 64 KiB; a check's
  long last line splits one finding into signatures (fixed in the client); the explorer shrinks
  detected corruption; one `T=` per schedule (open item 65); the clock audit does not follow
  `fasttime` (all in open item 158).
- Strategies: clock steps found all three; storage faults found nothing without a step. The
  entries "Clock steps and the clock audit" and "One node's storage faults" of `hydo guide
  strategies` are updated.

**What is left.** Open item 158.

## Milestone 311 (tentative number): ClickHouse with two replicas, deduplicated retries and quorum inserts

**The example.** `hydo/onboard/examples/clickhouse` (RESULTS.md) runs ClickHouse v26.10.6.18,
the newest stable release (2026-11-18), as two replicas of one shard, `ch1` and `ch2`, with three
ClickHouse Keeper servers. The images are the official `clickhouse/clickhouse-server` and
`clickhouse/clickhouse-keeper` under their tag `26.10.6` (amd64 `sha256:9084cd79…` and
`sha256:ca269194…`). It was imported with `hydo compose` from the example's own Compose file
and runs on hvx only (x86_64, `guest.cpu: v3`, 4,096 MiB). A static Go client on the HTTP
interface, `chc`, writes blocks of 1 to 30 rows into four `ReplicatedMergeTree` tables. They take
synchronous inserts deduplicated by the block's hash or by `insert_deduplication_token`, async
inserts, and quorum inserts with `insert_quorum = 2`, parallel and sequential. Each insert is
tried up to four times on either replica, and one acknowledged insert of three is sent once more.
A messages check judges them: `no-loss`, `at-most-once`, and `fan-out` over the groups `ch1` and
`ch2`, with one delivery per stored copy of a block. So do two final rules (`converge`,
`blocks`), a read of each acknowledged quorum insert on the other replica, and an anytime read
with `select_sequential_consistency = 1`. The build parameter `fsync` is `0` (ClickHouse's
defaults), `insert` (`fsync_after_insert`, `fsync_part_directory`) or `1` (also the fsync after a
merge and after a fetch). Two clean runs give one fingerprint on each image: `8174700d4ae25fa3`
on the default image (`aaed39f4…`) and `23aed071fdf281b0` with `fsync=1` (`96b2ed99…`).

**Finding 1, a known bug.** On the image with `fsync=insert` (`9b5182d2…`), `disk=cut | run
C=40` leaves the replicas apart for good. `final_converge` fails with `the replicas differ in 21
blocks after the heal` (`b9f68cd13b21c4c3`, twice), `fan-out` fails, and `no-loss` holds. The
power cut loses merged parts that no replica synced. Each replica then queues a fetch of the
merged part, which no replica has. The replica that merged keeps the source parts, and the part
check stops at "Hoping that it will eventually appear as a result of a merge"
(`ReplicatedMergeTreePartCheckThread::searchForMissingPartOnOtherReplicas`), so the other replica
never gets the rows. 13 more minutes of guest time in a `hydo inspect` session changed nothing.
The stuck fetch is known (#29778, #33508, #53143 open); no report names the power cut as its
trigger. A cut at step 20, `disk=none`, and the composition of seed 1 fail too; with `fsync=1`
and on the default image the schedule passes. The schedule is in
`schedules/known-merged-part-lost-at-power-cut.schedule`, outside `hydo/regressions/`, because it
needs the build parameter.

**The settings.** `hydo explore --configs --seeds 1-8 --no-shrink` explored the three values of
`fsync` with the same schedules, four of them with a power cut. With `0` three failed: seeds 1
and 5 lost a block acknowledged with `insert_quorum = 2` (`no-loss`), and seed 6 broke
`converge`. With `insert` seeds 1, 5 and 6 broke `converge` (finding 1). With `1` none failed.
Without shrinks the command's table lists no class and says that no combination failed, so seed 5
went through it once more with shrinks. On `0` it shrank in 81 tries to the power cut and the
quorum inserts alone (`a40341cdfd2dfa90`, twice). The shrink on `insert` was stopped after 8 tries
of 1.5 minutes, and `1` passed. The table labeled the loss on `0` the setting's documented
trade-off, found only with `fsync=0` and not with `fsync=1`. It is not reported.

**What held.** No retried insert was stored twice, also not a second send of an acknowledged
block, with block hashes, tokens and async inserts. Every acknowledged quorum insert was on the
other replica at once. Every read with `select_sequential_consistency = 1` had every block
acknowledged before it. No block was partial, and no block refused before the write appeared.
With the fsync after an insert and a merge on (E2, E3: 40 schedules) and with every fsync setting
on (E4), no acknowledged insert was lost in a run that reached its checks. The faults were kills
of replicas and Keepers, pauses, partitions, one-way loss, clock steps from 30 days back to a
year forward, and power cuts at steps and at disk flushes (`cf=`). E4's six failures each had a
lying disk or disk I/O errors. The clock audit's three schedules passed.

**What hydo lacked.** Seven gaps, in RESULTS.md, "What hydo lacked". hvx takes at most 4 GiB of
root and data disk together, and ClickHouse's programs are 1.4 GB (`root.share_images` and a
1,024 MiB data disk). One explorer worker of a 4 GiB guest held about 7 GB of the host, and the
host's out-of-memory killer ended one run. A group's kill restarts the Keepers one at a time
after each is ready, and a Keeper opens its client port only with a quorum (`ready: "true"`, as
open item 147 says for PD). The guest agent stopped answering in four schedules, three with a
ring partition of the Keepers and one with a kill of two Keepers (`TIMEOUT workload`, not
traced). The importer took port 2181 from the Keeper image's `EXPOSE`, kept the images'
`entrypoint.sh`, which changes owners in the read-only root, and did not propose `guest.cpu:
v3`, without which the programs stop with SIGILL. `hydo explore --configs` without shrinks
lists no class of failure and says that no combination failed. A workload command's output stays
in the guest. hydo's check of tracked files reads a version of four numbers as an address, so the
example names the image tag `26.10.6`.

**Tests.** The explorer's identity-quick and corpus-full goldens and the control corpus-quick
golden are re-recorded for the new example: its inputs and entries are new, the quick identity
golden's sample of examples shifts by one manifest, and the full corpus's later chunks shift by
the new example's schedules. Nothing recorded moved.

Retro: ClickHouse v26.10.6.18, hvx, 2026-11-18 and 19
- Time to the first clean run: 50 minutes of wall time, about 20 of them in image builds.
- Schedules run before the first finding: 1 (seed 1 of E1). None failed by the rules' mistakes.
- The findings: 0 new, 1 known (#53143, with a power cut as its trigger), 1 documented (the
  default fsync settings, labeled by `hydo explore --configs`), and the environment's (a lying disk
  and disk I/O errors in E4).
- What took the most time: seven runs that each waited 900 s after the guest agent stopped
  answering (1 hour 45 minutes); the disk limit, the entrypoint, SIGILL and the pool sizes before
  the first clean run (40 minutes); the shrinks of the settings exploration (1 hour).
- What hydo lacked: the disk limit of hvx (open item 157); memory for two VMs beside other
  sessions (open item 157); the one-at-a-time restart of a group (open item 147, and the
  example's `ready: "true"`); the agent that stops answering after the Keepers lose their quorum
  (open item 157); the import's port, entrypoint and CPU level (open item 157); a command's output
  in the guest (open item 157); a version of four numbers read as an address (the example names
  the tag `26.10.6`).
- Strategies: power cuts of the whole guest found finding 1 at the first seed, and the messages
  check's `fan-out` over one group per replica found it with the rule `converge`. The entries
  "Power cuts of the whole guest", "The messages check's claims" and "Settings that trade
  durability" of `hydo guide strategies` are updated. Clock steps and the clock audit found
  nothing: the audit's places were merges and replica delays, not the deduplication window.


**What is left.** Open item 157.

## Milestone 316 (tentative number): five problems of a user's onboarding with 0.4.0 on the Mac

A user onboarded a project of their own with hydo 0.4.0 on the Mac engine (an M2 Pro) and
reported five problems. The project is private, so each problem was reproduced with public
images and examples only. Each fix is its own commit, so that a patch release (0.4.1) can take
them; none moves a recorded value, and the fingerprint epoch stays 4.

**1. A service in the recovery boot without its tmpfs, and a claim of lost data.** In the user's
recovery boot after a power cut, PostgreSQL's `/dev/shm` (`mounts: - {tmpfs: true, dst: /dev/shm,
size: 64m}`, which `hydo compose` writes for every image service) was devtmpfs's directory
(mode 755, root), although the tmpfs at `/tmp/hydo/oci-tmpfs/<service>/2` existed. PostgreSQL
(uid 999) stopped with `could not open shared memory segment "/PostgreSQL.<n>": Permission
denied`, and the run ended `VIOLATION service cannot recover (committed data unrecoverable)`,
classed `durable-defaults`.

- The mount was not reproduced. The official `postgres:16.4` image from a Compose file with
  `shm_size: 64m` and a `pg_isready` healthcheck, imported with `hydo compose`, ran on the Mac
  engine with `network: bridge`: its first boot and the recovery boots of `C=3`, `C=10` and
  `C=15` had `none /oci/db/dev/shm tmpfs rw,relatime,size=65536k` (a check in the image said so),
  and an exploration of seeds 1-24 failed only on disk faults (`ERROR db restart failed` under
  `disk=ioerr`, and a lying disk's `Structure needs cleaning`). A test in the guest ran the
  service's launcher and three of its `hydo-oci` helpers at once beside a busy loop, 70 times on
  fresh views of the tree: every time the service saw its own tmpfs.
- The launcher has one race that gives the user's symptom inside the service. Its first line
  binds `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`, `/tmp` and `/data` into the service's root when `mountpoint`
  says they are not, outside the lock that guards the `mounts:`. A `hydo-oci` helper (a
  readiness check that `hydo compose` made from a healthcheck) that checks `$R/dev` before the
  launcher binds it, and binds it after the launcher has mounted the tmpfs on `$R/dev/shm`, puts
  a second bind of `/dev` over the first and hides the tmpfs. The service then sees devtmpfs's
  `/dev/shm`, which the launcher's `mkdir -p` made with mode 755. The fix moves the binds under
  the lock and decides with `/proc/mounts`. It changes the launcher of every image service, so
  every image with one gets new bytes, recorded ones too: it waits for a release that raises the
  middle number (open item 162).
- What a patch can fix is the diagnosis. The verdict is the controller's for any service that
  does not start in the recovery boot, and it stays. When the service's last log lines name a
  cause in its environment (permission denied, operation not permitted, a read-only file system,
  a program or shared library that cannot run, memory, an address in use) and none of them
  names damaged or missing data (structure needs cleaning, an I/O error, corrupt, a checksum, no
  such file or directory, and similar words), the diagnosis says that the service did not start
  because of its environment, that the run does not show what "committed data unrecoverable"
  says, and quotes the line (`hydo/crates/hydo-cli/src/inspect/diagnose.rs`,
  `environment_cause`; `docs/design/inspect.md` decision 7). The class stays `durable-defaults`.

**2. Emulators with `network: bridge`.** `emulators: [{use: s3, buckets: [...]}]` with
`network: bridge` was refused: `services[0]: network: bridge gives every service its own network
namespace and address: addr: required`. The expanded `<name>_emulator` service had no `addr:`,
and the entry had no key for one. With an address, the emulator would still have listened on
127.0.0.1 of its own network namespace, where neither its proxy (on 10.89.0.1) nor its readiness
check reaches it. Now, with `network: bridge`, the service takes the entry's new `addr:` (a
format-1 addition), or the first free address of 10.89.1.1, 10.89.1.2, ... that no service, fake
or proxy has, and the emulator listens on 0.0.0.0. A manifest that writes its own `/etc/hosts`
in `root.text`, as `hydo compose` does, gets `<addr> <name>_emulator` and `10.89.0.1 <name>`
for each name it lacks. Without the bridge nothing changes.

**3. YAML anchors in `hydo.yaml`.** A manifest with `x-common: &common` and `<<: *common` in its
services stopped with `hydo.yaml:<n>: unexpected indentation` (open item 121). MANIFEST.md says
that a Compose file is read as YAML 1.1 with anchors; for `hydo.yaml` it said that anchors are
not supported. The YAML subset now reads `&name` before a value, `*name` as a whole value (also
in flows) and `<<` merge keys as PyYAML's `safe_load` applies them: the merged pairs first, a
merged list's mappings in reverse order, then the mapping's own keys, a later pair winning at
the place its key was first seen. An alias needs its anchor earlier in the file, and a plain
value such as a cron line stays a string. A top-level `x-` key is an extension field, as in
Compose, and is dropped when a manifest is read (`hydo_manifest::drop_extensions`).

**4. FIFOs of an image.** hydo-build left every FIFO of an image's layers out (`1 device/FIFO
entries skipped`). A FIFO is now an empty file in the staged tree with its layer's mode and
owners in the tree's meta. The cpio writer writes a FIFO entry for it (the arm64 initramfs and
a disk root's archive), and the x86_64 ext4 pass replaces the file with debugfs's `mknod <name>
p` in the file's folder before it sets the mode and owners. Device nodes stay left out. Before
the change, the images of every recorded image service were fetched by their pinned digests
and their layers read: the voting app's five images, redis 7.2.4 and restate 1.7.13, for each
architecture they are recorded for. None has a FIFO or a device entry, so no recorded image
gets new bytes.

**5. Text that was not true.** MANIFEST.md said that `hydo compose` on a Mac passes `--no-addr`
because the arm64 kernel has no network namespaces; since Milestone 99's second guest kernel the
importer writes `network: bridge` and the addresses there too, as `hydo guide capabilities`
says. The row now says what `--no-addr` is for and that `hydo compose` passes it on no machine.
`hydo explore` on the Mac warned that one worker of 4096 MiB guests needed up to about 4831 MiB
with 4563 MiB available, and the run fitted. The estimate counted the image (479 MiB) beside the
guest's RAM, as on hvx, where the module copies it into kernel memory. The Mac and KVM engines
load the image into the guest's RAM and map that RAM as plain memory that the host gives as the
guest touches it. For them a worker is now its guest RAM and 256 MiB, the warning says "may use
up to about ... as the guests touch their memory", and it names `--workers`. The estimate sizes
no pool. The memory macOS has free now counts the speculative pages too, which `vm_stat`'s
`Pages free` leaves out and `top` counts as free; a Mac's pool, sized from that memory, can grow
by them (84 MiB on this Mac when measured).

**Evidence.** On this Mac, with the released 0.4.0 and with this tree's `hydo` in a copy of the
0.4.0 release tree, each in an install cache of its own (`HYDO_HOME`), and every VM run under the
shared lock:

- FIFO: an alpine image built with `mkfifo -m 0666 /srv/in` and `chown 1000:1000`, whose service
  reads the FIFO, ended `ERROR service start (reader)` on 0.4.0 (`/srv/in is not a FIFO`). With
  the change it is `prw-rw-rw- 1000 1000`, every line written into it reached the reader, and two
  runs gave one fingerprint (`99f5f7bef543d84a`). The same image without the FIFO built to the
  same initramfs and disk sha256 on 0.4.0 and on this tree (`3b67ed9c…`, `61d274de…`). The
  debugfs commands ran with e2fsprogs 1.47.0 in a Linux container, with a space in a path: a FIFO
  inode with the mode and owners, and `e2fsck -fn` clean. No x86_64 image was built.
- Emulators: an s3 emulator on service networks behind a `root.text` `/etc/hosts` was refused by
  0.4.0 with the user's message. With the change it was ready at 10.89.1.1, the hosts file had
  `10.89.1.1 s3_emulator` and `10.89.0.1 s3`, the workload listed its bucket through the proxy by
  the name `s3`, and rclone in the emulator's image wrote four objects to 10.89.1.1 and read them
  back; two runs gave one fingerprint, and a kill of the emulator kept the verdict OK. rclone's
  PUTs through the proxy stored empty objects, on loopback with 0.4.0 as well (open item 162).
- Diagnosis: a service that stops in its recovery boot with PostgreSQL's two log lines gets the
  verdict, the input hash and the control transcript of 0.4.0 (`ctl=c76f0c2a8db0e34e`), and its
  diagnosis now ends with "db did not start because of its environment, not because of lost
  data: its log ends with `FATAL: could not open shared memory segment "/PostgreSQL.7":
  Permission denied` and names no damaged file". PostgreSQL 16.4's recovery failure under a
  lying disk (`Structure needs cleaning`) keeps the claim.
- YAML: every tracked YAML file parsed to the same value as before but seven Compose files, which
  no command reads as a manifest. Their refusals as manifests moved in the equivalence corpora:
  14 answers of hydo-manifest's and 14 of hydo-build's. The emulator key moved 4 answers of
  hydo-manifest's (the list of an entry's known keys).
- Tests: the YAML subset's `anchors_aliases_and_merge_keys`, hydo-manifest's
  `tests/anchors.rs`, cpio's `an_image_fifo_is_a_fifo_entry` and the OCI staging goldens (only
  the FIFO's entries changed), emulators'
  `with_a_bridge_each_emulator_gets_a_free_address_and_its_names`, and diagnose's
  `a_recovery_start_that_fails_on_its_environment_claims_no_lost_data`.

Two things this work met are recorded for later: `hydo compose`'s guess of `guest.ram_mib:
1024` was too small for the PostgreSQL image's initramfs on the Mac (`Initramfs unpacking failed:
write error` at boot, and then a namespace setup that failed with `No such file or directory`),
and the busybox image's 400 hard links each became a whole copy in the initramfs (open item
162). hydo-build's equivalence corpus has six mismatches from before this milestone, for two
mutants with a `contracts:` key that the recorded answers do not list (`error_paths`, M306).

**What is left.** Open item 162.

## Milestone 318 (tentative number): what the third evaluation of `hydo fuzz` found, fixed

The third evaluation of `hydo fuzz` by a new user (Milestone 308,
`docs/design/function-fuzzing-evaluation-3.md`) ranked what stopped a Rust developer. This
milestone fixes the first six items of its list. Each fix is its own commit, so that a release
can take them one by one. None touches an engine, an image, or a recorded value. The tests are
`cargo test -p hydo-contracts --test it fuzz_m318::`, on the new fixture
`hydo/crates/hydo-contracts/tests/fuzz-m318`.

**1. A false `broken` verdict on an element of a list of built values.** half's
`len(self) == 0 || result[0] == self[0]` broke on every call. The harness answered the read
value before the call only for a parameter that a `build` line builds, not for such values
inside a list. So `self[0]` was the constructor's arguments, and a record compared with a
number gave `false`. The harness now answers the read value of every built value inside a
parameter (an element, a field, a variant's field), and the clauses read each through its
`read` line. A built value without a `read` line is undecided, with the line to write. A
comparison of two kinds of value is undecided, never false. Commit `63b72900`. Before, the
fixture's `bits` broke on 198 of 300 calls; now it holds, and `first` is `not judged`.

**2. Results hydo did not read gave the wrong verdict and advice.** heck's eight conversions
return `Self::Owned`, and each was `vacuous` with advice about the inputs. `Self::<name>` now
resolves through `type <name> = ...;` in the crate's `impl` of the trait for the type, the
result type that the `impl`'s method writes, and `ToOwned::Owned` (`String` for `str`, `Vec<T>`
for `[T]`). When a clause's last part is reached and cannot be decided, the clause is `not
judged`, and the report names the place and its type. Commit `f9ae01d8`.

**3. Two enumerations of one name.** humantime's `duration::Error` resolved to `date::Error`,
and a full path did not help. The reading now keeps every structure and enumeration of a name
with its module, and each file's `use` lines. A name resolves to the definition of the
function's module, else to the one a `use` line imports. A path resolves from `crate`, `self`,
`super`, the function's module, an imported first segment, or the root. Commit `b6f4c049`. The
no_std fixture's two structures named `P` resolve too.

**4. Const generics, `&'static` parameters and closures.** A const generic parameter takes its
value from a `with` line (`with N = 8`), also in array lengths, and an `impl` block for an
array type is read whole. A `&'static` parameter gets a value that the harness leaks after it
reads the values at entry. A type parameter bound by `Fn`, `FnMut` or `FnOnce`, and `impl
Fn(...)`, take a generated closure from a few shapes (a constant, the argument, an integer
converted or one past it, a predicate on an integer). A report shows it as `|x| x > 0`, and
`--input` reads it back. A closure whose result hydo cannot generate is refused with advice to
write a property function. Commits `f8db7860` and `e172fe25`; the second fixes the leak when
the result keeps the reference, which the proof run on percent-encoding found.

**5. The default strings.** A random string now takes printable ASCII, the default characters,
or letters with characters whose case mapping changes them (`ß`, `İ`, `ﬄ`, combining marks, a
capital outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, and others), each about a third of the time.
Commit `ee27924a`. The fixture's title case breaks at one such character within 1,000 calls;
before it held.

**6. The `read` line.** The harness imports `ToString`, `ToOwned` and `FromIterator`. A method
that takes its value (`collect`, `into`, `into_*`) reads a clone, and `collect()` and `into()`
get the line's type. A method takes a turbofish, and the types and constructors of `build` and
`read` lines take type arguments (`ArrayVec<u8, 8>`). Commit `f052453c`.

**The proof.** Fresh copies of the evaluation's six crates from crates.io, 71 contracted
functions written again from the evaluation page, seed 1, 1,000 inputs, on the Mac. `main` at
`da3e590e` refused 21 of them and gave 9 wrong verdicts. This milestone refused none and gave
no wrong verdict. All nine known upstream bugs of the evaluation showed (heck 36, 70, 71;
humantime 67, 68, 69, 78, 82; `rust-url` 1132); seven showed before. The table per crate is the
section "After Milestone 318" of the evaluation page. Nothing new was found, and nothing was
posted.

What is left is open item 163.

## Milestone 320 (tentative number): images in private registries

A user onboarded a project of their own with hydo 0.4.0 on a Mac. Its images were in a private
registry. `docker login` had worked, and Docker kept the credential in the macOS keychain through
a credential helper. `hydo compose` still stopped with `registry <host>/postgres:
.../v2/postgres/manifests/18.3: HTTP 401`. hydo asked every registry anonymously, and
`hydo-fetch-image`, which fetch-images.sh runs, had no way to log in either. The user imported
with `--no-resolve`, unpacked `docker save --platform linux/arm64` into each image folder by hand,
and ran `hydo compose` again, which left the images unpinned. The project and the registry are
private, so everything below ran with registries made for the tests.

**Credentials where Docker finds them.** The module `hydo_compose::creds` reads
`$DOCKER_CONFIG/config.json`, by default `~/.docker/config.json`. hydo-config registers
`DOCKER_CONFIG` (`hydo_config::tools::Tools::docker_config`), and every program's `main` hands
the folder to the registry client (`hydo_compose::registry::set_docker_config`). The lookup
follows Docker's order:

1. a `credHelpers` entry for the registry;
2. else `credsStore`;
3. else an `auths` entry: a base64 `user:password` in `auth`, or an `identitytoken`.

A helper is the program `docker-credential-<name>`. hydo runs `get` with the registry's server
address on stdin and reads `Username` and `Secret`, as Docker does; Docker Hub's address is
`https://index.docker.io/v1/`. A helper has 60 s to answer. Its stderr is not shown, and a
failure is named by its exit status only, because hydo cannot tell what a helper prints.

**The registry's flows.** `hydo_compose::registry::Http` answers a 401 once:

- `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm=...,service=...,scope=...`: the credential goes to the realm
  as basic authentication, or an identity token as a refresh token in a form POST. The registry
  gets the token. Without a credential the token is anonymous, as before.
- `WWW-Authenticate: Basic`: the registry gets the credential as basic authentication.

`creds::parse_challenge` reads the header by RFC 7235: quoted values with commas and escaped
quotes, and only the first of two challenges. A credential goes only to the registry it belongs
to and to the token service that registry names, and never over plain HTTP to a host that is not
on the loopback. A redirect, such as a blob in a storage service, takes no `Authorization` header
along. A registry on the loopback (`localhost`, `127.x.x.x`, `[::1]`) is reached over plain HTTP,
as Docker reaches it by default. A credential's `Debug` hides its secret, and no error quotes a
token service's answer.

**Messages.** A refusal names the registry and where hydo looked, without a secret:

```text
hydo-compose: registry 127.0.0.1:<port>/team/app: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v2/team/app/manifests/1.0:
HTTP 401 (unauthorized): hydo found no credential for 127.0.0.1:<port>: <folder>/config.json has no
credHelpers entry for 127.0.0.1:<port>, no credsStore, and no auths entry for 127.0.0.1:<port>. Log
in with `docker login 127.0.0.1:<port>` and run the command again, or take the image from the local
Docker with `hydo compose --from-docker`
```

A credential that the registry refuses gives "the registry refused the credential from the
credential helper docker-credential-<name> (credsStore in <folder>/config.json)". A registry that
does not answer gets the `--from-docker` hint as well.

**`--from-docker`.** For a registry that hydo cannot log in to, `hydo compose --from-docker` saves
each image whose registry refuses or does not answer from the local Docker. The command is
`docker save --platform linux/<arch>` for this machine's guest. The file goes where `hydo.yaml`
names it, and hydo reads the image's settings from it. The lock entry has `from_docker: true` and
pins the file's digest, as a local build's entry does (M214). A later `hydo compose` reads the pin
and needs neither the registry nor Docker. fetch-images.sh saves a missing file again with
`hydo-fetch-image docker`. When the local Docker holds another image under that name, the new
file is kept as `<file>.rebuilt`, and the script exits 1 until `HYDO_ACCEPT_REBUILD=1` takes it.
The check against the pin is the local builds' code, now shared (`localbuild::check_pin`). A
build's message about another digest now says "The new file is" where it said "The new build
is". A Docker before 28 has no `--platform` for `save`. After an
`unknown flag` error hydo saves without it and checks the architecture of the saved image.

**Evidence.** The tests are `hydo-compose`'s `private_registry::` (8 tests) and the unit tests
`creds::tests` (the challenge parser, base64, hostnames, and a `Debug` without the secret).
Every test writes its own Docker config in a temporary folder and runs every program with that
`DOCKER_CONFIG` and a `HOME` of its own. No test read this machine's Docker config or keychain, and
none logged in to a real registry.

- A registry in the test process on 127.0.0.1 serves one image for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64,
  with the token flow or with basic authentication. Against it:
  - an `auths` password went to the token service as basic authentication, and the manifests
    were fetched with the token;
  - an `auths` identity token went to the token service as a refresh token in a form POST;
  - a `credHelpers` helper was asked once, for this registry's address only, while a
    `credsStore` helper and a wrong `auths` entry were present and not used;
  - a `credsStore` helper served a registry without a `credHelpers` entry;
  - a wrong password, in both flows, gave the refusal above with the helper's name, and no
    output held the password, its base64, or the token;
  - a missing entry, a helper without a credential, a missing config file, and a helper that is
    not installed each gave a message that says so.
- `hydo-compose` and fetch-images.sh as programs, with a `credsStore` helper on `PATH`: the lock
  file pinned the index digest the registry serves, `hydo-fetch-image` fetched the arm64 image
  (this Mac's), and its config read back. With an empty Docker config both stopped with the
  advice, and printed no secret.
- With Docker (Colima, Docker Engine 28.4.0, CLI 29.6.1): the `registry:2` image ran with
  htpasswd authentication on 127.0.0.1. The test pushed the two-platform image into it over the
  registry's API, and `hydo-compose` and fetch-images.sh pinned and fetched it with a
  `credsStore` helper. A wrong password gave the refusal. For `--from-docker` the test loaded an
  image named `127.0.0.1:1/hydo-test-from-docker-<pid>:1` with `docker load`. That registry does
  not answer. Without the option the import stopped and named it. With it the file was saved and
  pinned, and a second import needed neither. fetch-images.sh saved the removed file again "as
  pinned". After another image was loaded under the name, the script stopped at the pin, and
  `HYDO_ACCEPT_REBUILD=1` took it. The test removes its container and its image when it ends,
  and it is skipped where Docker does not answer.
- The Compose equivalence corpus moved only in the three answers that print `hydo compose
  --help`. The local builds' tests passed unchanged.

Nothing recorded moved: no image, schedule, or fingerprint depends on the registry client.

**What is left.** Open item 165.

## Milestone 317 (tentative number): an image service's system folders mounted once (fingerprint epoch 5)

Open item 162 left one problem of a user's onboarding with 0.4.0 (Milestone 316) without a cause
in hydo. In the user's recovery boot after a power cut, PostgreSQL's `/dev/shm` tmpfs (`mounts: -
{tmpfs: true, dst: /dev/shm, size: 64m}`, which `hydo compose` writes for Compose's `shm_size`)
was hidden. The service's `/proc/self/mountinfo` showed the order. Mount 35 was the service's
`/dev`, 42 the tmpfs on it, 43 the bind of a seed folder at `/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d`, then 44
a second devtmpfs on the same `/dev`, and 45 the service's volume. PostgreSQL then found
devtmpfs's `/dev/shm` (mode 755, owned by root) and stopped with `could not open shared memory
segment ... Permission denied`. This milestone finds the code that mounts `/dev` the second time,
fixes it for images built from now on, and keys the fix on a new fingerprint epoch, 5. It is for
the release after 0.4.1 (0.5.0).

**The cause.** Every image service has a launcher, `/etc/hydo/oci/<service>/run`, and a helper,
`/etc/hydo/oci/<service>/exec`, which `hydo-oci <service> <command>` runs. hydo-build writes both
(`hydo/crates/hydo-build/src/oci.rs`, `scripts`). Before this milestone each began with one line
that bound `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`, `/tmp` and `/data` into the service's root:

```sh
for d in proc sys dev tmp data; do $BB mountpoint -q $R/$d || $BB mount --bind /$d $R/$d || exit 125; done
```

Only the service's `mounts:` came after it, in a block that runs once per boot under a lock
(`/tmp/hydo/oci-mnt.<service>.lock`) and that `/proc/mounts` decides. The line ran on every start
of the launcher and of every helper, outside the lock. A readiness check that `hydo compose` makes
from a healthcheck (`timeout 5 hydo-oci db pg_isready ...`) is such a helper, and the controller
runs it as soon as it has started the service. So two processes ran the line at the same time.
When one of them had looked at `$R/dev` before the other bound it, and bound it after the other
had taken the lock and mounted the `mounts:`, its bind went over the first `/dev` and hid
everything mounted on it. That is the user's order: the late bind came after the seed folder's
bind and before the volume's, because the process that held the lock was between those two
entries. A run without a power cut has the same race, but its moments differ, as the user's run
without a cut showed.

**The reproduction.** hvx on the bare-metal machine, with public images only. The project
(`devshm`) has seven image services from the official `postgres:16.16-alpine3.24` image on service
networks (`network: bridge`), as `hydo compose` writes them. PostgreSQL has a `/run` tmpfs with
`copy_up`, the `/dev/shm` tmpfs, a seed folder on `/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d`, a volume and a
`pg_isready` readiness check. The six other services run `sleep` with readiness checks through
`hydo-oci`, and some start together (`start_after: started`). The workload inserts rows with
`psql`, and a check, `mounts.once`, counts each service's mounts in `/proc/mounts` and asks
`hydo-oci db stat -f -c %T /dev/shm`. A second form, `devshm2`, starts PostgreSQL first and alone,
so its readiness check runs as soon as the launcher has started, and draws power cuts only. A
third form, `devshm3`, adds a service that runs `hydo-oci db true` in a loop. With this tree before
the fix (the launcher of epoch 4):

- `devshm` (PostgreSQL started with others, after two services) passed `disk=none | run` and
  `disk=none | run C=6`, and an exploration of 80 schedules found nothing.
- In an exploration of `devshm2` (`hydo explore --seeds 1-300`), every schedule failed
  `mounts.once`. The explorer's first boot, which every schedule starts from, had `app3`'s
  `/data` bound twice. In 87 of the 116 recovery boots PostgreSQL's `/tmp` was bound twice, and
  in 54 its `/data`.
- With `devshm3`, eight runs `disk=none | run C=2` to `C=9` failed `mounts.once`. Two recovery
  boots had a second `/dev` on `app3`. `hydo inspect exec <run> --at end` showed it below `app3`'s `/dev/shm`
  tmpfs, so the tmpfs stayed visible there.
- An exploration of `devshm3` with tick jitter (`--timing`) failed 79 of its first 204
  schedules: every one of its 79 recovery boots. In 9 of them PostgreSQL's `/dev` was bound
  twice, and in 21 `app3`'s. In seed 42 (`disk=cut | run C=11`) PostgreSQL's second `/dev`
  came after its `/tmp` and before its `/dev/shm` tmpfs.
- No run here gave the user's exact order, a second `/dev` after the tmpfs. The late bind needs
  one process to stop between its look at `$R/dev` and its bind for as long as the other takes
  for the whole lock block. The double binds show the same race with shorter stops.

**The fix.** From the fingerprint epoch 5 the launcher and the helper share one block, under the
service's lock and once per boot (its done file):

```sh
if [ ! -f /tmp/hydo/oci-mnt.db.done ]; then
  $BB mkdir -p /tmp/hydo; exec 9> /tmp/hydo/oci-mnt.db.lock; $BB flock 9
  hmnt() { $BB grep -q " $1 " /proc/mounts; }
  if [ ! -f /tmp/hydo/oci-mnt.db.done ]; then
    for d in proc sys dev tmp data; do hmnt $R/$d || $BB mount --bind /$d $R/$d || exit 125; done
    ... the service's mounts:, in their order ...
    : > /tmp/hydo/oci-mnt.db.done
  fi
  exec 9>&-
fi
```

The shared tree of `root.share_images` is bound first inside the block (it had the same race), and
a `writable: true` layer is still bound before it, under its own lock. A service without
`mounts:` gets the block too, with the system folders only. A process that finds the done file
mounts nothing, and one that waits for the lock tests the done file again under it. The storage
faults' power loss of one service (`L=`) removes the done file after it has unmounted the
service's file system, as before: the next start binds what is missing and leaves the system
folders, which `/proc/mounts` still lists.

**The epoch.** The launcher is inside the image, so the fix decides the bytes of an image that is
built, never the run of an image that exists. An image built at epoch 4 or before keeps its
launcher. Every image service's image built now gets new bytes, so every recorded run of an image
service is expected to move. By the epoch rule (AGENTS.md) such a change raises `hydo_image::EPOCH`:
it is 5, and `hydo_image::EpochDefaults::oci_mounts_once` says which launcher an epoch builds
(true from 5). hydo-build takes it from the epoch it builds at, as Milestone 269's
`regressions_in_image` does. So "two hydo versions of one epoch build the same image bytes"
(`hydo-image`'s documentation) still holds. Every image built at epoch 5 also has a new record,
`/etc/hydo/image.json` with `"epoch":5`. Nothing changes at run time: no engine, controller, agent
or kernel changed, and an image of epoch 5 runs with the defaults of epoch 4.

**What moves.** The values are not re-recorded here (the batch rule, AGENTS.md open item 105).
Every image of `hydo/onboard/recorded.json` gets new bytes when it is built at epoch 5: hvm 21,
kvm 6 and hvx 43. The images with image services also get the new launcher: `hvm/voting` and
`hvm/redis-oci` (7 runs), and `hvx/redis-oci`, `hvx/restate-oci`, `hvx/voting`,
`hvx/voting-generated` and `hvx/voting-loopback` (14 runs). On hvx the record alone moved none of
the 141 runs at epoch 4, so the 14 runs of the image services are the ones expected to move there;
on the Mac and KVM engines, which hash the image's disk and the guest's RAM, the 76 and 19 runs
are likely to move. docs/REBASELINE.md section 29 names the epoch.

**Evidence.** On hvx, with this tree's programs in a copy of the 0.4.0 Linux release:

- The explorations of `devshm2` and `devshm3` with this tree's hydo, on the projects built at
  epoch 5 with the same seeds: no schedule failed. In the first 55 schedules of `devshm2`
  (22 recovery boots), which all failed before, and the first 230 of `devshm3` with tick jitter
  (87 recovery boots), every system folder and every tmpfs of every service was mounted once,
  and PostgreSQL's `/dev/shm` was a tmpfs. The explorations were stopped there, because the
  shared machine had slowed to minutes per schedule.
- The pinned reproducers gave `a76d7fe857fdb37c` and `efbde7b57264be0f` on their epoch-2 images
  in `~/hydo/build/m204`, and `e153f376096a072c` and `6a5c2fe208174af3` on their epoch-4 images
  in `~/hydo/build/m302`, before and after the fix.
- Images built at epoch 4 keep their values under this hydo with the fix. The release's Redis
  example, built at epoch 4 by this tree before the fix, gave the recorded hvx values
  `2f9186af5e3be2b1` (`disk=none | run`) and `d299dc487ceb5e3c` (`disk=cut | run C=12
  R=everysec`, `k:1` lost) before and after the fix. `devshm` built at epoch 4 gave
  `d6e4551b652cedf6` (`disk=none | run`) and `ce147468e60d12d9` (`disk=none | run C=6`) before
  and after the fix.
- Tests: hydo-build's `oci::tests::a_helper_beside_the_launcher_never_hides_the_shm_tmpfs` runs a
  helper and then the launcher of a PostgreSQL-like service with a stand-in for busybox that
  records the mounts and holds the helper's bind of `/dev` until the launcher has mounted
  `/dev/shm` or waits for the lock. The launcher of epoch 4 ends with two `/dev` mounts, the second
  over the tmpfs; the launcher of epoch 5 binds each system folder once, before the `mounts:`, and
  every mount stays visible. `oci::tests::the_launchers_of_each_epoch` checks the block's order in
  both scripts, with a shared tree, and the launcher of epoch 4 as it was. The OCI staging golden
  (`tests/golden/oci/answers.json`) changed in the 16 launchers and helpers only, and
  `oci_share` checks the shared tree's bind inside the block. `hydo-image`'s `epoch_defaults`
  covers the new default. hydo-build's equivalence corpus keeps its six mismatches from Milestone
  306; this change adds none.

**What is left.** Open item 162 (the user's own project was not run) and open item 105 (the
values of epoch 5).

## Milestone 319 (tentative number): the guest's timer tick on hvx, and the ClickHouse runs that never ended

In the ClickHouse onboarding (Milestone 311) four schedules ended `TIMEOUT workload` after the
engine's limit of 900 s of host time, seven runs in all (open item 157). Three had a ring
partition of the three Keepers, and one a kill of two Keepers and a forward clock step. The
control transcript of each ended at an answered `clock_get`, and the guest printed nothing more.
The report then was that the guest agent stopped answering. It did not: the guest's clock nearly
stopped, and every timeout in the guest waited with it.

**The reproduction.** Seed 20 of exploration E2, `disk=cut dseed=6711e6dcb424bc7a | run
K=keepers.minority.7@36+3 N=keepers.ring@12-21:loss,100% C=40 P=replicas.all@6+3
W=9580664b,p4,q2,r250`, ran with `hydo run` on hvx on the onboarding's image `img-i2`
(`fsync=insert`), from a tree of its own on the bare-metal machine. Two runs ended `TIMEOUT
workload` at a wall limit of 700 s and 500 s (`HVX_EXPLORE_WALL_SECS`, to save time), each with
243 typed commands and the same input hash `inh=109d022965b67fca` and transcript hash
`ctl=805e43e8de53b972`. The last command was the composer's `clock_get` (id 243) at stop 180146,
and the agent answered it. The client's last line came at 126.2 s of guest time.

**Where the time went.** A temporary diagnostic of the engine sampled the vCPU every few seconds
of host time while the run went on. It read the snapshot, the PMU branch clock's counters and,
by the kernel's `System.map`, the guest's `jiffies`:

- Before the partition the run went from 9 s to 120.8 s of guest time in about 5 s of host time.
- After it, the guest retired about 575 million conditional branches in each 5 s of host time.
  So 555 ticks of the branch clock moved the virtual TSC 1.1 s. The guest's own clock moved 60 to
  85 timer ticks of 1 ms: 0.06 to 0.085 s. In 489 s of host time it moved 5.7 s.
- The host's time went into the module's run calls, which run the guest. The engine and the
  controller took almost none.

`hydo inspect start` at stop 180146 showed the guest in that state, and its calls answered (7.5 s
to 110 s of host time each, so the agent ran). An advance of 20 s took 18 s of host time and the
next one of 8 s took 764 s. At 128.9 s of uptime:

- `/sys/devices/system/clocksource/clocksource0/current_clocksource` was `refined-jiffies`. The
  kernel log has `Marking clocksource 'tsc-early' as unstable because the skew is too large` at
  6.27 s and `Switched to clocksource refined-jiffies` at 10.04 s: hvx's virtual TSC counts guest
  work, and the clocksource watchdog compares it with the timer ticks.
- `/proc/timer_list` showed the tick in periodic mode (`tick_handle_periodic`) on the one-shot
  `lapic-deadline` device, `now at 128916129504 nsecs` and `next_event: 128936000000 nsecs`: the
  next tick was set 19.9 ms ahead.
- In 60 ms of guest time two `KeeperHandler` threads of `keeper3` ran 14.2 ms and 13.9 ms. Both
  were runnable all the time and mostly in the kernel (58 user and 153 system ticks). `keeper3`'s
  client port 9181 held a connection from `ch2` in `CLOSE_WAIT`.

**The cause.** `refined-jiffies` counts each tick as 999,848 ns (its rate comes from the PIT's
1,193,182 Hz: 1,193 cycles a tick). The periodic tick on a one-shot device sets each next tick
`TICK_NSEC`, 1,000,000 ns, after the one before, and programs it as the difference from the
clock's present time. The two counts part by 152 ns a tick. After t seconds of uptime the next
tick is due 1 ms + 0.152 ms × t ahead of the virtual TSC: at 128,935 ticks, 19.6 ms, as the
timer list showed. An idle guest does not notice, because the module moves the virtual TSC to
the deadline at a HLT. A busy guest has to run through that virtual time: here about 10 million
branches for each 1 ms of its clock. Two Keeper threads kept the CPU busy after the Keepers lost
their quorum, and the guest's clock ran about 1.2 s in 100 s of host time. The step's timer, each
command's `busybox timeout 50`, and the client's 12 s deadlines were all in guest time. None of
them ended before the engine's limit. The controller waited for those ends and had nothing to
send.

The kernel's command line is built in `run` of `hydo/crates/hydo-hvx/src/engine.rs` (`cmdbase`,
from `boot::ROOTFS_CMDLINE`). Nothing on it named a clocksource, so the guest kernel picked
`refined-jiffies` itself.

**The fix.** `guest.exact_tick: true` (a format-1 addition) makes hvx boot the guest kernel with
`clocksource=jiffies`. The plain jiffies clocksource counts a tick as 1,000,000 ns, the tick's own
period, so each tick is due 1 ms after the one before at any uptime. `hydo build` writes
`/etc/hydo/exact-tick` only with the key, the engine layer passes `--exact-tick on` to hvx for
such an image (`hydo_engine::image::exact_tick`), and `hydo-hvx` adds the parameter. The Mac and
KVM engines ignore the key. The ClickHouse example's `hydo.yaml` sets it.

- On `img-i2` with `clocksource=jiffies` added through `HVX_EXPLORE_CMDLINE_EXTRA`, seed 20
  moved 5.8 s of guest time in each 20 s of host time while the Keeper threads were busy. Then it
  went on quickly. The run ended `HYDO-ORACLE: VIOLATION [converge] the replicas differ in 1
  blocks after the heal` (finding 1, after the power cut `C=40`) with `fp=56cdb36c4bdaf736`. It
  took 1,354 s of host time with its recovery boot and checks, on a loaded machine.
- The image `img-x1`, built from the committed example (`--set fsync=insert`, so with
  `guest.exact_tick: true`), booted with `clocksource=jiffies` on its command line. Seed 20 gave
  `VIOLATION [converge] the replicas differ in 2 blocks after the heal`, `fp=2be840e3c29f36dd`, in
  711 s of host time. A second run gave the same fingerprint, input hash
  (`inh=50392a9848e8a956`) and transcript hash (`ctl=897572c6272fa6fd`). Both runs ended with
  their verdict, not at the engine's limit.
- Seed 33 of E3 (`disk=none dseed=ad03dcc43f85bd09 | run K=keepers.majority.6@21+3 P=keeper1@13+4
  T=23:86400 W=93234449,p4,q2,r1000`, the kill of two Keepers and the forward clock step) ended
  `OK` on `img-x1` in 181 s of host time. It did not run on that image without the key, and seeds
  27 and 40 did not run.

**What moved.** Nothing recorded. An image without the key has the same bytes, the same engine
arguments and the same kernel command line as before, and the controller sends what it sent.
The pinned reproducer `disk=none dseed=4d5cb825dfaab05b | run K=redis@11+1 C=24` on the
epoch-4 old image gave `e153f376096a072c` (VIOLATION, order 11), its recorded value, with this
tree's engine on hvx. The fingerprint epoch stays 4. The new key changed the list of known
`guest` keys in 18 refusals of hydo-manifest's equivalence answers, which are re-recorded.

**Why not the default.** The exact tick changes the guest's time from the boot on, so every hvx
fingerprint of an image with it moves. As the default it belongs to a new fingerprint epoch and a
release that raises the middle number, as M316's launcher fix does (open item 164).

**What is left.** Open item 164.

## Milestone 321 (tentative number): two tests that only Linux ran, and command output without a pipe

CI on `main` failed on Linux after Milestones 317 and 320 were merged. Both failures were in new
tests that the Mac skips or passes, and a third problem was a hang of four hours.

**The launcher test of Milestone 317.** `oci::tests::a_helper_beside_the_launcher_never_hides_the_shm_tmpfs`
named its folder `hydo-oci-once-...` in the temporary folder. It replaces the scripts' `/tmp/hydo`
with that folder, and on Linux the temporary folder is `/tmp`. So the stand-in busybox's own path
was replaced too, and the helper never ran ("the helper never reached its bind of /dev").
`TMPDIR=/tmp` reproduces it on a Mac. The folder is `oci-once-...` now, and the test passes with
`TMPDIR=/tmp`. The launcher's code was right.

**The registry test of Milestone 320.** On Linux an import with a wrong password passed. The test
now prints the registry's log and what the credential helper was asked when that happens. The
log showed no request of the import at all: with only the lock file removed, the import pinned
the image files that `fetch-images.sh` had saved in the project folder. The test now removes
the whole project folder before the wrong password, so the import must ask the registry. hydo's
code was right.

**A read that waited for hours.** A run of `cargo test -p hydo --test it` waited about four hours
in `configs::`: an explorer was in `hydo_engine::host_cpu`, reading the output of `sysctl` from a
pipe that a child of another thread held open (the scripted engine `engine.sh serve`). macOS marks
a new pipe close-on-exec only after it is made, so a child started in that moment inherits its
write end. `host_cpu` and `available_mib` now read the output of `sysctl` and `vm_stat` through a
temporary file, and `wait` ends when the command ends. A unit test runs a command that leaves a
child running: it returns at once, where the pipe waited for the child.

Nothing recorded moved.


## Milestone 322 (tentative number): the release list under GitHub's rate limit

On 2026-11-19, after a day of tests and checks on one Mac, GitHub's API answered every request
without a login with HTTP 403. GitHub allows 60 such requests an hour from one address, and the
answers had `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`. `hydo skill update --check` then printed only `hydo:
https://api.github.com/repos/kakoc/hydo/releases?per_page=100: HTTP 403` and exited 1. A user
could not tell from that line what happened or what to do. `hydo update` and the daily look of
`hydo doctor` read the same list and had the same problem.

**What changed.** The new module `hydo/crates/hydo-cli/src/releaselist.rs` reads the release
list for all three:

- A token. hydo takes `GH_TOKEN`, else `GITHUB_TOKEN`, else the output of `gh auth token
  --hostname github.com` when `gh` is on `PATH`. It asks `gh` only when a request may carry a
  token, waits at most 5 seconds (2 for `hydo doctor`), and reads the answer through a new file
  of mode 0600 that it removes at once, not through a pipe (Milestone 321 says why a pipe can
  wait for another thread's child). The token goes as `Authorization: Bearer` only to a URL
  whose origin is exactly `https://api.github.com` (`token_may_go`). The download host, another
  port, `http://`, and a host such as `api.github.com@example.org` get none. The fetcher drops
  the header on every redirect (`RedirectAuthHeaders::Never`).
- No token is shown. `hydo_config::run::Secret` holds the value, and its `Debug` prints
  `<hidden>`. `hydo_config::Env`'s `Debug` hides `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` too.
- GitHub's limit. A 403 or 429 answer with `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0` is not retried (a 429 was
  retried four times before). The commands print one line and exit with status 4, which means
  that the release list could not be read; 3 still means that something is newer. Any other
  failure to read the list exits with 4 too, where it exited with 1. Offline stays 1.
- The daily look of `hydo doctor`. At the limit it prints nothing about it, keeps its earlier
  answer as it was, and records `limited_until` from `x-ratelimit-reset`. It makes no look
  before that time.
- Fewer requests. Each command reads the list once, and the newest hydo and skill releases come
  from it. Every successful read keeps the list in `~/.hydo/update-check.json`: the versions,
  each release's "Before you upgrade" section, and the newest skill release. The file keeps the
  fields `checked`, `api` and `newest`, so an older hydo's doctor still reads it. A command
  takes a kept answer of the last 10 minutes and says so in its first line, for example `hydo:
  the release list as read less than a minute ago, kept in ...; it is read again after 10
  minutes`. `hydo doctor` takes one of the last day, so the doctor that `hydo update` runs after
  an update makes no request.
- `HYDO_GITHUB_API_STANDIN`, a developer variable, names a loopback origin that hydo treats as
  GitHub's API for the token. A value that is not plain HTTP to a loopback host is ignored. The
  tests check with it which requests carry the token.

The line at the limit:

```text
hydo update: GitHub's limit for requests without a login (60 an hour from one address) was reached, so the release list could not be read; the limit resets in 38 minutes. Set GH_TOKEN to a GitHub token, or log in with `gh auth login`, to lift it. Nothing was changed
```

When the request had a token, the line says that the limit of requests with the token was
reached, and gives no advice to log in.

**Tests.** `hydo-cli`'s `tests/update.rs` has four new cases against its local fake release
server, each with a temporary home. None calls GitHub.

- `at_github_s_limit_the_commands_say_so_and_change_nothing`: a 403 and then a 429 with the
  rate-limit headers. `hydo update --check`, `hydo update --yes`, `hydo skill update --check`
  and `hydo skill update` print the one line with `resets in 38 minutes` and exit 4. Each makes
  one request, and no skill copy, program or download changes. `hydo doctor` then prints
  nothing about it and makes no request, also after the list is readable again. A command reads
  it, and the doctor prints its note from that answer.
- `a_token_goes_to_the_api_host_only_and_is_never_shown`: the API on its own server. A `hydo
  update --yes` with `GH_TOKEN` sent `Bearer <token>` to the API and nothing to the download
  host. A redirect of the API to the other server did not carry it. Without the stand-in, the
  API got no token. The token is in no output and in no file under the case's folder.
- `gh_auth_token_gives_the_token_when_no_variable_does`: a fake `gh` gave the token once, with
  the arguments `auth token --hostname github.com`. With `GH_TOKEN`, `gh` was not asked. For a
  request that may not carry a token, `gh` was not asked either.
- `one_request_for_the_release_list_per_command`: `hydo update --yes` updated hydo and a skill
  copy with one request. The next `hydo skill update --check` and `hydo update --check` took the
  kept answer. Without the file, `hydo skill update` made one request.

The unit tests of `src/releaselist/tests.rs` cover `token_may_go`, the line, `gh_token` (an
error, no output, two words, and a `gh` that hangs and is killed after 300 ms), and the doctor's
look at the limit. The first start of a new script took up to 1.7 s on this Mac while the other
cases ran, longer than hydo waited for `gh` in one run. So the `gh` case starts its fake once
before the command.

**The real check.** One `hydo update --check` against GitHub, with a temporary home, from this
tree's build (version 0.4.0) on this Mac, where `gh` is on `PATH`:

```text
hydo update: hydo 0.4.0, this hydo was built in the checkout <the worktree>
  hydo: 0.4.0 -> 0.4.1: nothing (see the commands below)
  ...
rc=3
```

A `hydo skill update --check --to <folder>` right after it printed `hydo: the release list as
read less than a minute ago, kept in <home>/.hydo/update-check.json; it is read again after 10
minutes` and `onboard: not installed (release 2.4.0)`, with no second request. The kept file had
the keys `api`, `checked`, `newest` (`0.4.1`), `releases` and `skill` (`2.4.0`). GitHub's limit
was not reached during the check, so the line at the limit ran against the fake server only.

Nothing recorded moved. `hydo update --help`, `hydo skill --help` and `hydo guide update` have
new text.
