## Milestone 340 (tentative number): shrinks from snapshots

The user said "go" on 2026-11-23 to the second recommendation of Milestone 337
(`hydo/explore/RESEARCH-shared-prefix.md`): shrink candidates continue from snapshots that
earlier runs of the shrink took, instead of running from S1 what they share with those runs. The
design is `docs/design/shrink-snapshots.md`. `hydo explore --shrink-from-snapshots` turns it
on. After the proofs it is on by default with the KVM engine only (the end of this section).

**What was built.**

- The points where runs part. The host controller counts the workload's step ranges and the
  composition's rounds that it started (`Controller::ranges_started`, an effect on the host
  state only, so no command and no transcript changed). The runner compares the count before
  and after each step. When it grew, the link takes `SNAP` before any of the step's commands
  reaches the engine (`Link::at_range_start`). A first version asked a copy of the controller
  before the step; the copy of the controller's whole state at every stop cost more than it
  found.
- The book of snapshots (`hydo_control::prefix`). A worker keeps 8 and a run takes 4 for a guest
  under 2 GiB, 4 and 2 from 2 GiB on, and hvx keeps 2. A composed workload's run spreads its
  snapshots over its rounds. A candidate continues from the deepest snapshot of the same
  engine schedule that its controller reaches (`agent::check_branch`, the state search's offline
  check), with `RESUME`; every other candidate runs from S1. A continuation that fails drops its
  snapshot and runs from S1.
- The pool. The reruns of a failure take snapshots, and the shrink candidates take and use them
  (`Worker::run_prefix`, `Worker::prefix_gain`). A free worker takes, among the jobs that would
  start now, the one it continues from the deepest snapshot, and never waits for one.
- `--check-continued` runs every run that took or used a snapshot again from S1 without
  snapshots. It compares the RESULT line without its wall seconds and every file of the run but
  the engine's own console. The run from S1's result counts. `shrink-snapshots.json` and one
  line on stderr give the counts. `--shrink-from-s1` and `HYDO_SHRINK_SNAPSHOTS` (`hydo-config`)
  choose; `HYDO_SHRINK_SNAPSHOTS_KEEP` sets the two numbers for measurements.
- The Mac engine. A snapshot that is not the host's S0 or S1 gets a RAM base of its own,
  without the RAM tree hash that names a shared base, and guest RAM stays mapped as it was until
  the run's end. On a 1 GiB guest a mid-run snapshot took 0.27 s before, of which the hash was
  0.20 s and the new mapping with its instruction-cache upkeep 0.03 s. After both changes it
  took 0.11 s to 0.14 s. Runs without mid-run snapshots do as before.

**Exactness on the Mac engine.** The images were the Redis quickstart of the release 0.4.1
(`explore-ob-redis-arm64.cpio.gz`, `31e90668…`, fingerprint epoch 4) and the repository's
`redis-composed` example with the quickstart's Redis files, built by the released 0.5.0
(`c63f273f…`, epoch 5). Each exploration ran three times with 2 workers: with
`--shrink-from-s1`, with `--shrink-from-snapshots`, and with `--check-continued`.
`events.jsonl` and `exploration.json` were compared without the wall times, the worker numbers,
the repeat counts, and the command line. The engine and the snapshots changed between the
builds: the first took snapshots before the step with the RAM tree hash, the second without the
hash, the third (the commit's, without the rounds) after the step without a new mapping.

| exploration | runs that took or used snapshots | continued | compared with S1 | differed | records |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Redis, `--strategy random --shrink-causes 3`, seeds 1-40 (three builds) | 39 to 43 | 5 to 8 | 22 to 24 each | 0 | the same 102 run records, 8 failures, 6 minimal schedules |
| redis-composed, the same options (three builds) | 353 to 368 | 33 to 41 | 98 to 105 each | 0 | the same 324 run records, 11 failures, 9 minimal schedules |

Every compared run gave the same RESULT line (fingerprints, `ctl`, the engine's counts, the
verdict), the same `<tag>.log` and the same control transcripts as its run from S1.

**Time on the Mac engine.** The seconds are the engine's seconds of the shrink candidates, from
`events.jsonl`, on a Mac that other sessions shared. The Redis row's snapshots are from the
`--check-continued` run of the last build, whose recorded seconds are those of the runs from S1.

| exploration | from S1 | from snapshots | snapshots taken, their seconds | guest clock not run again |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Redis, seeds 1-40 | 5.0 s (36 candidates) | not measured with the last build | 39, 4.3 s | 5.7 % |
| redis-composed, seeds 1-40 | 73.5 s (246 candidates) | 86.8 s | 90, 10.5 s | 2.8 % |

The shrinks took longer with snapshots. A Redis run takes 0.1 s to 0.3 s, and a snapshot of its
1 GiB guest about 0.12 s, so a snapshot costs more than a continued run saves. The composed
example's candidates mostly change the composition (`W=...,x<rounds>`, `n<rounds>`,
`o<commands>`), and such a candidate parts from its parent at a round, not at a step range.
With snapshots only at the step ranges 2.8 % of the guest clock was skipped. So the commit also
counts each round of a composition as a point and spreads a composed run's snapshots over its
rounds. That version ran in the scripted tests only: the shared Mac VM lock stayed with another
session from 12:07 to past 14:12, and its runs were stopped unrun. A tree over every
point where two runs' commands part, on any worker, would skip 21 % on the same exploration
(7 % on the quickstart's), by the control transcripts. One worker with 16 snapshots kept and
12 per run skipped 2.5 %, so the workers and the counts were not what limited it.

**hvx.** hvx refuses a snapshot of a schedule with `cf=`, `pp=`, `xt`, `q=` or `tj=`, and the
refusal leaves the point out. TiKV's exploration `explore-ex4` of Milestone 287 (the research
note's largest shrink, 1,124 s) had 18 shrink candidates: 13 with `cf=` and 5 without. So 5 of
18 could continue there. An hvx snapshot holds every page of guest RAM that is not zero in host
memory, and the engine keeps 8 names with S0 and S1. Without a module change it is not worth it.

**KVM.** The one-off workflow `.github/workflows/tmp-shrink-snap-kvm.yml` ran on the branch
`tmp-shrink-snap-kvm` (commit `b84fad0e`, on the milestone's commit `ed511da2`, which has the
points at the composed rounds too), run 45181990563. The branch is deleted. Each of four
GitHub runners (three Xeon 6975P-C, one AMD EPYC 7763) built the published 0.5.0 release's
Redis example. It explored seeds 1-40 with 2 workers and `--shrink-causes 3`, three times per
strategy: from S1, from snapshots, and with `--check-continued`.

| strategy | compared with S1, per runner | differed | records, per runner | continued | snapshots, their seconds | guest clock not run again |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| random | 18 | 0 | 94 events the same in all three | 5 to 7 of 32 or 33 runs | 16 to 19, 0.0 s to 0.1 s | 4.7 % to 6.9 % |
| swarm | 23 | 0 | 132 events the same in all three | 4 or 5 of 54 or 55 runs | 28 to 30, 0.1 s | 2.9 % to 3.7 % |

So 164 runs that took or used a snapshot matched their runs from S1, on both vendors. A KVM
snapshot keeps the pages written since S1 in the engine's memory, so it cost a few milliseconds.
The engine's seconds of the reruns and shrink candidates from S1 and from snapshots:

| runner | random | swarm |
|---|---|---|
| Xeon 6975P-C (1) | 10.6 s, 10.0 s | 17.7 s, 17.2 s |
| Xeon 6975P-C (2) | 10.7 s, 10.0 s | 17.8 s, 17.5 s |
| Xeon 6975P-C (3) | 10.7 s, 10.0 s | 17.5 s, 17.3 s |
| EPYC 7763 | 10.6 s, 10.3 s | 18.3 s, 17.6 s |

The shrinks took 1 % to 7 % less time in all eight pairs.

**The defaults.** On by default with the KVM engine, where every compared run matched and the
shrinks took less time (`run::shrink_snapshots_default`). Off on the Mac engine, where every
compared run matched too but the shrinks took longer, and on hvx. `--shrink-from-s1` and
`HYDO_SHRINK_SNAPSHOTS=0` turn it off; hydo-bench's pools never turn it on. No test of CI
continues a candidate on a real KVM host.

Nothing recorded moved: no recorded value, explorer golden, or control corpus changed. The
explorer's fake-engine scenario `repeats_take_the_earlier_result` also explores the stack with
`--shrink-from-snapshots --check-continued`: the scripted worker keeps no snapshots, and the
files are the same. The scripted agent's test `a_shrink_candidate_continues_from_its_parents_range_start`
shows the snapshots at the range starts and a continued candidate with the transcript of its run
from S1.

## Milestone 341 (tentative number): 0.5.0's features on the engines that had not run them

Several features of 0.5.0 ran on one engine only. The user agreed on 2026-11-23 to run them on
the others. This milestone ran them on hvx, on the Mac engine, and on KVM in a one-off workflow,
fixed what was wrong, and records what held. No engine, image, or recorded value changed.

### How the runs were made

- hvx: the bare-metal machine, the published 0.5.0 Linux release installed with `install.sh
  --no-module` into a tree of its own, and the examples of this tree. Every VM ran through
  `hvx-run` under umask 022. The release's Redis example built the image `23c3b280…`, the
  recorded one, and `disk=none | run` gave `cce52f9e8565f6e2`, its recorded value.
- The Mac engine: the installed 0.5.0 release, under the shared VM lock.
- KVM: the workflow `.github/workflows/tmp-m341-kvm.yml` on the branch `tmp-m341-kvm`, with the
  published 0.5.0 Linux release, run 45170910149 on GitHub's runners.

### The statistics of Milestone 336 on hvx

`hydo explore --seeds 1-40 --strategy swarm --workers 2` of the Redis example wrote
`stats.json` with every part:

- The curve: 4 distinct verdicts, which grew at runs 1, 5, 12 and 20, and 2 property outcomes,
  at runs 1 and 5. "Flat over the last 10 runs: no new verdict or property outcome since run 20
  of 40."
- The cost: 40 first runs took 25.8 s of the engine, 19 re-runs 10.2 s, and 23 shrink runs
  13.2 s. Re-runs and shrinks took 44 % of the workers' busy time. A first run took 0.65 s on
  average (median 0.6 s, the longest 1.4 s). The clock is hvx's own unit, 29,954 per first run.
  The host CPU was 84 s for 31.8 s of wall time. The explorer's process held 5,038 MiB at most
  and an engine 13 MiB, because hvx's engine runs inside the explorer's process (open item 169).
- The faults drawn: disk faults in 31 runs, power cuts in 21 (at 15 workload steps), crashes of
  `redis` in 19 (at 8 steps), and the setting `R=` in 18. No schedule drew a pause or a clock
  jump, and the statistics name `--new-faults` for them.
- The estimate: an hour on 2 workers fits 5,410 first runs. The exploration measured 4,703 an
  hour.

The same seeds as `--shard 1/2` and `--shard 2/2`, and `hydo explore --merge` of the two, gave
the same curve, the same runs with the same new keys, and the same faults drawn. The merge has 43
shrink runs against 23, because each part shrank its own failures (open item 153). Its workers
keep their part numbers.

### The repeats and the error shrinks of Milestone 339 on hvx

The exploration of the last section answered 9 runs from earlier results, 5.0 s of the engine. With
`--rerun-repeats` the same 82 run records (tag, schedule, verdict, fingerprints) and the same 4
minimal schedules came back. Two errors of the system were shrunk, and each minimal schedule
gave one fingerprint on both confirmations:

| Error | From | Tries | Minimal schedule | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ERROR redis restart failed` | seed 12 | 5 | `disk=ioerr:1 dseed=fd403ef8d08fa636 \| run K=redis@16+1` | `264951ea4e91998a` |
| `ERROR restart after the faults (redis)` | seed 20 | 3 | `disk=ioerr:1 dseed=ce2af709f01aac0 \| run` | `441d4e62c64662f2` |

**TIMEOUT on hvx.** hvx's `TIMEOUT workload` is the engine's wall limit, `HVX_EXPLORE_WALL_SECS`
(900 s by default), not the manifest's `workload.timeout`. A guest call that passes
`workload.timeout` is killed, and the run goes on. So a short `workload.timeout` does not bound
the cost of a TIMEOUT shrink: each candidate that keeps the error runs to the wall limit. The
proof used a copy of the release's Redis example with two changes. Its `workload.timeout` is
20 s, and after a failed `SET` the client spins in the shell (`[ "$r" = OK ] || while :; do :;
done`). The guest's clock then moves at about two thirds of the wall clock: 20 s of guest time
took 30 s of wall time. With `HVX_EXPLORE_WALL_SECS=20`:

- `hydo run "disk=none | run K=redis@5+3"` ended `TIMEOUT workload` after 20.0 s, with the
  fingerprint `0000000000000000`.
- `hydo explore --seeds 1-20 --strategy random --workers 2` ran 20 schedules in 368 s. 11 first
  runs ended `TIMEOUT workload`, and 12 runs were answered from earlier results (64.5 s of the
  engine). It shrank three TIMEOUT failures:
  - seed 1, `disk=ioerr:1 dseed=910a2dec89025cc1 | run K=redis@0+2`, in 4 tries to the disk
    errors alone;
  - seed 2 in 3 tries to `disk=none dseed=0 | run K=redis@9+1`;
  - seed 12 (`disk=lying:2 ... | run K=redis@6+3 C=7`) in 10 tries to `disk=none dseed=0 | run
    K=redis@6+1`.
- The engine's seconds by role: first runs 224.6 s, re-runs 220.5 s, shrink runs 104.6 s, and
  the confirmations of the minimal schedules 121.0 s. Each run that kept the error took the 20 s
  limit, so with the default limit one such candidate takes 15 minutes.

### Two fixes

**A TIMEOUT has no fingerprint** (commits `99b4da45` and `165477d6`). hvx's engine ends a run
that passes its wall limit before it hashes the end state, and writes the fingerprint
`0000000000000000`. The two
confirmations of a minimal TIMEOUT schedule then compare two zeros, and `report.md` said
"fingerprint, two runs: `0000000000000000` / `0000000000000000` (identical)". The web page said
"same fingerprint". Now `report.md` says that the runs have no fingerprint, because each ended at
the engine's limit before its end state was hashed, so only the verdicts repeat. The limit is
hvx's wall time or the exit budget of the Mac and KVM engines, whose runs also end with zeros
(the section "The KVM runs"). The page
says "same verdict" with the same reason. `hydo_results::has_fingerprint` and
`Shrink::confirmed_without_fingerprint` decide it; a run without a result does not count as a
timeout. `exploration.json` did not change. The new test of hydo-results is
`a_shrink_whose_confirmations_timed_out_has_no_fingerprint`.

**`hydo explore --schedule` does not shrink** (commit `77d913ff`). `hydo guide faults` said that it
runs a schedule and shrinks a failure. It runs the schedule once, and open item 38's text of
Milestone 187 says so too. The guide now says that it runs the schedule once, and that a person
finds the tokens a failure needs by leaving tokens out by hand.

### The recursive `/sys` of Milestone 338 on hvx

`hydo/onboard/examples/redis-oci/hydo-sys.yaml` is the redis-oci example with one more check,
`oci.sys_cgroup_files`. It runs `hydo-oci redis sh -c "cat /proc/self/cgroup; ls /sys/fs/cgroup;
test -e /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.procs"` in the image service. The image built at epoch 5 is
`396d54dc…`:

- `disk=none | run` gave `OK invariants=2 held`, `5c12fb8373b148f3` twice. The check listed
  `cgroup.controllers cgroup.max.depth cgroup.max.descendants cgroup.pressure cgroup.procs
  cgroup.stat ...` in the service's root.
- `disk=none | run K=redis@5+2` gave `OK invariants=2 held`, `aecd1c7dd916f1eb`. After the
  service's restart the folder still had its files, because the launcher's block binds once per
  boot.

### The s3 proxy of Milestone 329 in a VM

0.5.0 re-pinned `hydo-world` with Milestone 329's fix: x86_64 `40973bdb…`, arm64 `9fbdbee4…`.
The new example `hydo/onboard/examples/checkout/hydo-s3.yaml` runs one s3 emulator and a client,
`s3probe` (Go, standard library only, built by the example's `build.sh` for amd64 and arm64).
Each workload step is one round through the proxy:

- a PUT of 7 bytes and its HEAD, which must name `Content-Length: 7`;
- a PUT of 3,000,000 bytes, its HEAD, and a GET whose answer must have `Content-Length:
  3000000` and the same bytes;
- a PUT with `If-None-Match: *` on a new key (200) and on the same key again (412);
- a PUT with `If-Match` and the object's ETag (200), and one with another ETag (412).

A 412 that an `H=` rule gives is checked against the server's own port. After the proxy's 412 to
`If-None-Match`, the server has no such key. After its 412 to `If-Match`, the server keeps the
first bytes. The check `s3.rounds_read_back` reads each acknowledged round's objects from the
server. Every schedule held, and each gave one fingerprint over two runs:

| Schedule | hvx (`ba2a859f…`) | the Mac engine (`0eb05b06…`) |
|---|---|---|
| `disk=none \| run` | OK, 40 answers as S3 gives them, `1a5efe89b6ea0e9d` | OK, 40, `c27377375a768e64` |
| `disk=none \| run H=s3.put_if_absent@1-2:status=412` | OK; round 1's conditional PUT got 412 from the proxy, and the server had no key; `60cf779c3e6158cc` | the same, `951cd681ce4e0cfb` |
| `disk=none \| run H=s3.put_if_match@2-3:status=412` | OK; round 2's `If-Match` got 412 from the proxy, and the server kept `first-2`; `1d3625b1ae992896` | the same, `0b3c48624df9ce24` |

The checkout example itself, buggy, kept its verdicts with 0.5.0's `hydo-world`. `disk=none |
run` was OK, with 8 receipts stored through the s3 proxy (hvx `4b6b7992e35890ff`, the Mac
`8eb002a4f0d34699`). `H=stripe.payment_intent@3-4:status=500,effect=yes` gave `VIOLATION
[stripe.charged_at_most_once] ... ref o3 took effect 3 times` (hvx `fa8275c08b747d39`, the Mac
`055ef90b2ac11ead`).

### The filmstrip and the read-back of Milestone 334 on the Mac engine

It did not run. On this Mac, `hydo build hydo-walk.yaml --set variant=buggy` fetched the
Playwright image (966 MB) and started the helper VM that makes the 3,200 MiB root from 2,420 MiB
of files. The Mac had 18 GB free, shared with other sessions. The build was stopped with 5.9 GB
written, when the free space fell under the 12 GB that the sessions keep free. Vikunja's image
needs as much. KVM ran web-shop's walk (the section "The KVM runs").

### The KVM runs

The workflow `tmp-m341-kvm` runs four parts, each on two hosts, with the published 0.5.0 Linux
release (`.github/workflows/tmp-m341-kvm.sh`):

- `explore`: the Redis example's exploration of seeds 1-40, again with `--rerun-repeats`, and as
  two shards and their merge, compared by a script. Then a copy that writes and syncs without end
  after a failed `SET`, under a small exit budget (`HYDO_KVM_RUN_EXITS=3000000`), so that a run
  ends `exit budget exhausted` and is shrunk.
- `walk`: web-shop's walk (`hydo-walk.yaml`, the variant `buggy`) with `I=1`, the power cut
  `C=3` with and without `disk=cut`, Milestone 284's minimal schedule, and an exploration of
  seeds 1-10 with `--protocol-faults`.
- `vikunja`: Milestone 334's three Vikunja schedules.
- `oci-s3`: `hydo-sys.yaml` and `hydo-s3.yaml`.

Run 45170910149 ran the eight jobs. The hosts were an Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C and an AMD EPYC
7763 (`explore`), a Xeon 6975P-C and an EPYC 7763 (`walk`), and Xeon 6975P-C hosts (`vikunja`,
`oci-s3`). Every schedule gave one fingerprint over its two runs. A KVM fingerprint holds for one
CPU vendor or model (open items 102 and 153), so each host's values are its own.

**`explore`.** The Redis example's image was `23c3b280…` on both hosts. `disk=none | run` gave
`d2e4da56c54ce2a1` on the AMD host, the recorded KVM value, and `b5b0234c48d0d4f6` on the Xeon
Platinum 8573C. The exploration of seeds 1-40 gave the same verdicts on both hosts:

- The statistics: the curve was flat over the last 10 runs, with verdicts that grew at runs 1,
  2, 12, 19 and 20, and property outcomes at runs 1 and 2. The engine's clock is VM exits, 13,155
  per first run. 40 first runs, 17 re-runs and 27 shrink runs took 10.7, 4.0 and 6.4 s of the
  engine on Intel (13.8, 5.0 and 8.0 s on AMD), and shrinks took 46 % of the busy time. An hour
  on 2 workers fits 14,081 first runs on Intel and 11,201 on AMD.
- `--shard 1/2`, `--shard 2/2` and `--merge` gave the same curve, the same runs with the same new
  keys, and the same faults drawn as one exploration.
- The repeats answered 9 runs, and `--rerun-repeats` gave the same 84 run records.
- Five failures were shrunk, each to the same minimal schedule on both hosts. Among them are the
  two errors of hvx's exploration, with hvx's minimal schedules: `ERROR redis restart failed` to
  `disk=ioerr:1 dseed=fd403ef8d08fa636 | run K=redis@16+1`, and `ERROR restart after the faults`
  to `disk=ioerr:1 dseed=ce2af709f01aac0 | run`.

The copy that writes and syncs without end after a failed `SET` ran with
`HYDO_KVM_RUN_EXITS=3000000`. `disk=none | run K=redis@5+3` ended `ERROR workload: exit budget
exhausted while the workload's steps 5 to 7 ran` after 38 s (Intel) and 57 s (AMD), with the
fingerprint `0000000000000000`. The random exploration of seeds 1-20 shrank four such errors, the
same on both hosts: seed 1 to `disk=ioerr:1 dseed=910a2dec89025cc1 | run`, seed 2 to `disk=none
dseed=0 | run K=redis@9+2`, seed 10 to `K=redis@14+1`, and seed 12 to `K=redis@6+1`. Seeds 1 and
12 shrank to hvx's TIMEOUT schedules. The repeats saved 82.6 s and 115.5 s of the engine. The
confirmations of an exit-budget error have zero fingerprints too, so the report's words of
commit `99b4da45` name both limits since commit `165477d6`.

**`walk`.** The web-shop walk image was `f95bf05a…` on both hosts.
