## Milestone 342 (tentative number): Prometheus behind an agent, its snapshots and its scrape times

The onboarding of Prometheus v3.16.0 (2026-11-05, the latest release) on hvx, 2026-11-23. The
example is `hydo/onboard/examples/prometheus`; its RESULTS.md has the evidence.

**The example.** An exporter (the client's own `promc serve`, a new series at every scrape), a
Prometheus agent that scrapes it every second and forwards with remote write, and a central
Prometheus server, all from the official image `prom/prometheus:v3.16.0` (index
`sha256:e0498764…`) in one hvx guest of 2,048 MiB. `hydo compose` imported the Compose file. The
server receives remote write, scrapes itself, keeps out-of-order samples up to 10 minutes back
and one day of data, and cuts blocks of one minute (`--storage.tsdb.min-block-duration=1m`, a
hidden flag for tests) with chunk files of 16 MB. Its data directory and the agent's are file
systems of their own. The client writes 2 new series per remote write, one in order and one 60 s
back, sends each fourth write twice, takes snapshots and reads them back with `promtool tsdb dump`
inside the server's image, and records the blocks that the server lists. Five build parameters
choose the rules of the explorations (`ooo_snapshots`, `scrape_times`, `powerloss`), the scrape
alignment (`adjust`) and the server's configuration (`server_config`).

**The checks.** `samples`: every acknowledged sample is queryable with its value; after a power
cut, or the server's own power loss in the image built with `powerloss=yes`, only a sample of a
block that the server listed after its acknowledgement, in the same run of the server, must be
there. A sample a day older than the head's newest one may be gone (retention). The same rule
covers every scrape that a read found. `snapshots`: a snapshot holds every sample acknowledged
before it, also after a power cut. `scrape` (`eventually`, 120 s after the heal): the agent's new
scrapes reach the server. `times`: two scrapes a second apart carry two timestamps.

**What was found.**

1. **New: a snapshot with the head lacks every out-of-order sample of the head.** In every run
   without faults on the default image, each snapshot lacked the out-of-order samples that the
   server had not compacted into a block yet, up to 207 of them, and held every in-order one.
   `DB.Snapshot` (`tsdb/db.go` line 2586) writes the head through `NewRangeHead` (lines 2611 to
   2616), whose index lists only the in-order chunks (`appendSeriesChunks`, `tsdb/head_read.go`
   line 363). The querier adds the out-of-order head with `NewHeadAndOOOQuerier` (lines 2681 to
   2684); the snapshot does not. With the default blocks of 2 hours a snapshot can lack up to about
   3 hours of out-of-order samples, which then are only in `wbl/`. The same on `main` at
   `f1486b67`. No issue or pull request names it (30 phrases). Regression
   `snapshot-without-ooo-head`, `disk=none | run`, fingerprint `a5a53e35802ad822` twice.
2. **Known (prometheus#8312, closed by a bug scrub), with a new cause.** After `T=20:-300` the
   scrape loops stamped every scrape with the last aligned time before the step, until the clock
   passed it: 199 of 240 pairs of scrapes a second apart shared one timestamp, and the server
   dropped 81,585 of its own samples as duplicates, although its out-of-order window of 10 minutes
   covers the step. `scrape/scrape.go` line 1460 aligns when `scrapeTime.Sub(alignedScrapeTime)
   <= tolerance`, which a negative difference always is; a maintainer in #8312 described the
   alignment as two-sided, and the bug scrub named the out-of-order window as the remedy. With
   `--no-scrape.adjust-timestamps` no pair shared a timestamp. The clock audit named this
   function second. Regression `scrape-times-frozen-after-clock-step`, fingerprint
   `bd59337c12da9aa9` twice.
3. **Known (prometheus#11496, open), with a new trigger.** The remote-write watcher sends only
   samples later than its start (`tsdb/wlog/watcher.go` lines 286 and 560). Without the alignment
   of finding 2, a step back of 5 minutes held the agent's new series back: the check `scrape`
   held 70 s after the heal instead of at once.

Documented or by design: the server's own power loss loses its unsynced head (the WAL syncs a
segment at each head compaction only), a step back of more than the out-of-order window makes
the server refuse every new sample (and the agent drops each refused batch whole, #9214), a
forward step of a year lets retention delete every older block, and `G=` on a block file also
damages the snapshots that hard-link it. `promtool tsdb dump` reads a snapshot only with a `wal`
folder (open pull request #20416).

**What held.** With the two findings' checks left out (`ooo_snapshots=skip`, `scrape_times=skip`), no rule broke in 104 blind schedules (e1 24, e2 40, e3 6, e3b 25, e4 9) and 35 directed runs: power cuts at 19 flushes `cf=60` to `cf=1140` and 11 drawn ones, `kill-now-prometheus` and cuts 5 to 40 ms after a new block, three power cuts at steps, and three strict power losses of one service. Two failures were damaged files that snapshots share through hard links (the environment). Two engines were ended by the host's out-of-memory killer beside another onboarding.

**hydo.** Two small additions: `hydo guide services` names `/bin/hydo-oci` for programs that a
command starts, and `hydo guide strategies` has the new entry "A snapshot or a backup read back
at once" and the Prometheus evidence in three entries. No code of hydo changed. The new example
enters the explorer's and the controller's corpora; their goldens were not re-recorded in this
commit (open item 170).

Retro: Prometheus v3.16.0, hvx, 2026-11-23
- Time to the first clean run: 55 minutes of wall time (scouting 25, setup 30), none of it
  waiting for machines.
- Schedules run before the first finding: none. Finding 1 failed the first clean run that read a
  snapshot back; finding 2 came from the clock audit's place and a directed step of 5 minutes.
  Four failures of the explorations were the rules' own mistakes, all after a power loss of the
  server alone or a damaged file.
- The findings: 1 new (the snapshot), 2 known with a new detail (#8312, #11496), 4 documented or
  by design, 2 environment (damaged files shared by snapshots).
- What took the most time: the rule after a power loss of the server alone (three versions, 40
  minutes); memory beside another onboarding (two engines ended by the host's out-of-memory
  killer, and one worker from then on); the client's records of in-order and out-of-order samples
  after a clock step (20 minutes).
- What hydo lacked: a check cannot read its run's faults; one clock for all services; a
  command's output stays in the guest; `hydo-oci` by its path (guide text); memory per hvx worker.
  Open item 170.
- Strategies: a new entry "A snapshot or a backup read back at once" (finding 1); "Clock steps
  and the clock audit" (the audit named finding 2's function); "The features behind a flag"
  (the out-of-order window); "One node's storage faults" (snapshots share damaged files; the
  power loss of one server needs the server's start in the rules); "Power cuts at the k-th disk flush" and "Reactions at console events" (Prometheus held).

## Milestone 343 (tentative number): GreptimeDB in cluster mode, region failover and the object store

The onboarding of GreptimeDB v1.3.1 (2026-11-13, the latest release) on hvx, by
`docs/ONBOARDING-PLAYBOOK.md`, with the published hydo 0.5.0 Linux release. One new candidate,
not posted. Nothing recorded moved.

**The example.** `hydo/onboard/examples/greptimedb` (RESULTS.md) runs the production shape of a
cluster, small in memory: one etcd as the metasrv's store, a metasrv with region failover on, two
frontends, two datanodes with the write cache on, the region WAL in one Kafka 3.9 broker that
syncs each record, and the data on S3 through hydo's S3 emulator. It was imported with `hydo
compose` from the example's Compose file, whose configuration files are in `config/`. Kafka
needed a line for the guest's hostname `(none)` in `/etc/hosts` and runs as root. The Go client
`gtc` writes 3 rows per write through both frontends into a deduplicating table and an
append-mode table, each of 3 regions. It also runs `ADMIN flush_table`, `compact_table` and
`migrate_region`, and DDL statements on tables `d<n>`. A messages check (`no-loss`,
`duplicates: forbidden`, `no-phantom`), a count check, an `eventually_` DDL check, an
`eventually_` leader check and an anytime read judge them. Two clean runs give one fingerprint on
the final image (`3fb799a5…`): `2330e7fdc5c43f46`. The guest has 3,072 MiB, and the services'
peaks add up to about 1,360 MiB.

**Finding 1, new.** A short or zeroed copy in a datanode's manifest cache stops the datanode at
every start. At its start the cache records each local file's own size
(`mito2/src/cache/manifest_cache.rs` lines 190 and 193). `fetch_manifests` reads a delta from the
cache first (`manifest/storage/delta.rs` line 211) without comparing the listing's size. With the
default `compress_manifest = false` the decoding in `get_from_cache_decoded`
(`manifest/storage/utils.rs` line 38) cannot fail, so the short JSON reaches the parser. One
region that does not open stops the datanode (`datanode/src/region_server.rs` line 1517).
`disk=none | run G=datanode0@11+1:trunc,seed=71f5a076 W=6311ab23,p4,q2,r1000` cuts a cached
delta to 686 bytes, while S3 keeps its 1,076 bytes. It ends in `ERROR datanode0 restart failed`
with `fp=f9ec66d7caa0cd80` twice, and the same kill without the damage passes. Pull request
#10179 (in v1.3.1) refills a cached entry that does not decode, and its test leaves out the
uncompressed default ("Truncation only applies to compression envelopes"). Blind in e3's seed 13
and e4's seed 23. A power loss of a datanode, six times, lost cached copies whole and left none
short. The regression is `regressions/manifest-cache-truncated.schedule`. No report found; nothing
posted.

**Not bugs.** An unanswered `DROP TABLE` took effect later, which the first DDL check did not
allow: a mistake of the rules, fixed (`u~<what>~<table>`). A power cut of the guest made the S3
emulator lose an SST object that it had acknowledged: rclone's local backend writes without an
fsync. A datanode or a frontend that did not start while Kafka or the metasrv was down: hydo's
restart ignores the restart policy (open item 111). Damaged Kafka segments stopped Kafka.

**What held.** Every acknowledged row stayed readable, once and with its value, in both tables.
So it held through kills, pauses past the failure detector, partitions, and one-way loss of every
service, and through failovers and migrations. It held through one node's power loss and damaged
SST files, clock steps from 30 days back to a year forward, S3 errors and drops, and pauses inside
a write's WAL append. Every acknowledged DDL statement took effect. The datanode counts its
region lease on the monotonic clock, so a paused datanode refused the writes that reached it
after the metasrv had moved its regions.

**Explorations.** e3 (process, seeds 1-20, with protocol, cluster and storage faults): 3 errors in
11 minutes, finding 1 and two of hydo's restarts. e4 (swarm, seeds 21-80, with reactions and
`--kill-now` at the client's events): 5 errors in 26 minutes, finding 1 again, three damaged
Kafka segments and one of hydo's restarts. About 60 directed runs.

**Tests.** The explorer's `identity-quick.txt` and `corpus-full.txt` and the controller's
`corpus-quick.txt` are re-recorded for the new example's inputs.

Retro: GreptimeDB v1.3.1, hvx, 2026-11-23
- Time to the first clean run: 45 minutes of wall time, about 15 of them in image builds.
- Schedules run before the first finding: about 60 (45 directed runs, 2 of the halted
  explorations, and seeds 1 to 13 of e3). The DDL check's mistake failed 2 directed runs before it.
- The findings: 1 new (a gap in the fallback of the manifest cache), 0 known; the rest were the rules'
  mistake, the environment, or hydo's restart.
- What took the most time: two explorations that hung on hvx's 16 MiB of agent lines (about 45
  minutes); the hypothesis of a write applied twice by the retries, 19 directed runs without a
  duplicate (about 50 minutes); Kafka's first start without a line for the hostname (about 20
  minutes).
- What hydo lacked: a durable S3 emulator, an error-log scan that fits hvx's line budget, a clock
  audit that follows a project's own clock, and a restarted service's earlier log (all in open
  item 171, with open items 111, 141 and 152).
- Strategies: one node's storage faults found finding 1; pauses past the failure detector, clock
  steps and protocol faults found nothing. The entries "One node's storage faults", "Pauses of a
  service past its failure detector", "Clock steps and the clock audit", "Protocol faults on
  fakes and emulators", "Power cuts of the whole guest", "Error logs as findings" and "The
  features behind a flag" of `hydo guide strategies` are updated.

**What is left.** Open item 171.

## Milestone 344 (tentative number): the write routes of a project's API

`hydo rules scan --kind writes [DIR] [--json] [--max N] [--all]` lists every route of a
project's API that writes, each with its handler, from the project's own sources. Nothing
recorded moved, and no VM ran.

**Why.** An onboarding writes one workload command per client operation. An operation that no
command calls is not tested under faults. On Meilisearch the index swap, the dump, and the payload
of a document addition held the three bugs that hydo found (M295), and those operations came from
reading the sources by hand. `hydo rules scan` found no routes before.

**What it reads.** The module is `hydo/crates/hydo-cli/src/writescan.rs`. It reads text, as the
clock audit does, and leaves out what the audit leaves out: test files, test code inside a
source file (M324), examples, vendored code, and generated code.

- HTTP routes with the methods POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE:
  - Rust: axum's `.route(<path>, post(h))` and `get(a).post(b)`, actix-web's
    `web::resource(<path>).route(web::post().to(h))` and attributes, and the route tables of an
    attribute macro (`"<path>" => [post(h)]`, `sub(Type)`), also inside `macro_rules!`;
  - Go: net/http's `"POST /p"`, gorilla/mux's `.Methods(...)`, chi, gin, labstack's router, httprouter,
    fiber, and Prometheus's route package;
  - JavaScript and TypeScript: express, fastify, koa, hapi's route objects, and NestJS's
    decorators;
  - Python: FastAPI and Flask decorators, and Django's URL patterns with each view's methods;
  - Java and Kotlin: Spring's mappings and JAX-RS.
- RPC methods whose names do not say that they read: `.proto` services with their
  `google.api.http` mappings, a Go type that embeds `Unimplemented<Service>Server`, and a Rust
  `#[async_trait] impl Service for T` whose methods take a `Request<...>`.
- OpenAPI 3 and Swagger 2 operations, also through `$ref` files.

The prefixes come from the calls that enclose a route, the groups that a file assigns, and mounts
by name. A route that two places declare is listed once. A POST route or an RPC method whose name
says that it reads is left out and counted (`--all` lists them). Each route has a class: `data`,
`admin` (a snapshot, a dump, a compaction), `session` (a sign-in or a token) or `runtime`
(health, metrics, profiling, a reload). The list is grouped by resource and ranked by class.
`--json` has every route with its rank, its handler's file and line, and why it counts, for
`hydo rules check` and the skill. The scan without `--kind` prints one line per route in its
section `writes`. The design and the proof are the section "The write routes" of
`docs/design/rule-suggestion.md`; the reference is `hydo guide rules`, "List the routes that
write". The onboarding skill's step that writes the workload, and its inventory, run it.

**The proof.** The scan ran on the sources of six examples at their tags, on this Mac, in 2 to
11 seconds each. 20 routes per project, spread evenly over the ranked list, were judged by their
handlers (all 14 for Prometheus).

| project | tag | files read | routes that write | resources | reads left out | handlers found | right in the sample |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Meilisearch | v1.57.0 | 576 | 83 | 23 | 10 | 83 | 19 of 20 |
| Iggy | server-0.10.0 | 2,038 | 38 | 17 | 2 | 38 | 20 of 20 |
| Prometheus | v3.16.0 | 616 | 14 | 7 | 12 | 14 | 12 of 14 |
| GreptimeDB | v1.3.1 | 1,834 | 53 | 29 | 26 | 53 | 19 of 20 |
| Hatchet | v0.120.5 | 2,411 | 99 | 36 | 12 | 99 | 20 of 20 |
| Memos | 26.11.0 | 742 | 49 | 24 | 4 | 49 | 19 of 20 |

109 of 114 judged routes write. The five others: Meilisearch's `POST /indexes/{index_uid}/fields`
(a list with a filter), Prometheus's `POST /labels` and `POST /series` (queries), GreptimeDB's
Flight `DoAction` (not implemented), and Memos's `Transcribe` (it stores nothing). Every write
that the examples' RESULTS.md pages name was listed: Meilisearch 8 of 8 (with the swap, the edit
by function, the dump and the snapshot), Iggy 5 of 5, Prometheus 2 of 2, GreptimeDB 1 of 1 (its
SQL endpoint), Hatchet 5 of 5, and Memos 5 of 5. Meilisearch's 83 routes hold 44 per-setting
routes of a route table inside `macro_rules!`; without them the list has 39.

The first runs found the scan's own errors, which are fixed:

- an array `[post(h)]` was taken for an attribute;
- two route tables named `CompactApi` in two modules shared one mount;
- `$` counts as a character of a name, so `$route` was missed;
- `PUT` and `DELETE` of one path merged;
- a tonic `impl<T: X> Service for Y` lost its trait's name;
- a Go type that embeds several services listed its helpers;
- a function whose parameters take more than six lines had no definition;
- OpenAPI's `operationId` `workflow:delete` did not match the Go handler `WorkflowDelete`.

**What is left.** Open item 175.

## Milestone 345 (tentative number): reactions aimed at one event, options the engine cannot use, and one list of several explorations' problems

The user said "do" on 2026-11-23 to three explorer changes learned from automated onboardings.
Each part is its own commit. None moves a recorded value: they are host-side changes, and a
schedule without the new forms sends the same commands as before. The fingerprint epoch stays 5.

**1. Reactions aimed at one event.** `--reactive` draws one reaction per schedule over every
event and six fixed delays (`--kill-now`: ten). A window of one or two milliseconds after one
event then gets a few hits in a thousand schedules, as Meilisearch's index swap did. The new
form tries a grid instead:

```sh
hydo explore --reactive-at <event>[#<k>][@<step>][,...] [--react-delays A..B[/STEP] | A,B,C] [--react-actions kill-now,kill,cut,...]
```

- The names. The options join `--react-events` in one family, so every `--react-` option shapes
  a reaction; a bare `--delays` would say nothing about what it delays. `--reactive-at` keeps the
  name the request gave.
- The grid. Seed `n` is cell `n - 1`, in the order event, delay, action, so every moment after the
  event meets every action before the next moment. `kill-now` and `kill` name one action per
  service; the default is `kill-now,kill,cut`, each only where the manifest's `faults:` and the
  engine keep it (the probe renders a schedule with the action and looks for it). An action named
  by hand that they would drop is refused. The default delays are `0..50`, the range of
  `--kill-now`'s draws. A grid of more than 100,000 cells is refused.
- The schedules. A seed of the first round is the plain workload with its one reaction
  (`disk=cut` for a power cut), so nothing else moves the moment. Seeds past the grid try it
  again with the seed's composition, walk and timing streams. Without `--seeds` the exploration
  runs the grid once; `hydo explore` no longer adds its default `--seeds 1-20` then. Each
  schedule is an ordinary one: it is run again, shrunk, replayed and saved. `--reactive`,
  `--kill-now`, `--sweep`, `--steer` and `--search` do not go with it. The explorer's first line
  says that it draws no fault, and the next line describes the grid in words.
- A later record of an event. `A=<event>#<k>...` acts at the k-th record of the event from the
  arming point. The full form is `A=<event>[#<k>][@<step>][+<ms>]:<action>`; `#1` is not written,
  as `@0` and `+0` are not. The host's reaction counts the event's records. The kill at the
  event's moment gets a relay script that counts them in the guest: for the first record the
  script is Milestone 305's byte for byte (`relay_script(1) == RELAY`), so every earlier
  schedule sends the same command. The shrinker tries the first record in place of the k-th.
  The words of a schedule say "for the 3rd time".
- The moment a write is applied. MANIFEST.md and `hydo guide faults` say how to give it an
  event: the client polls the operation's status and writes a record when the server reports it
  started or finished. A reaction to a service's own log line was not built. busybox's `tail -f`
  reads a file once a second, which is late for a window of a few milliseconds, and a service's
  output goes to its log file, not to the console that the relay sits over. Such a reaction would
  need a relay of its own over each service's output.

The proof ran on the Mac engine, on the Meilisearch example built with this tree at the
fingerprint epoch 5 (`cb5eb6c3…`), with 2 workers of 1,536 MiB. On this image the saved
regression `A=meili.swap_acked@20+14:kill-now-meilisearch` passes: the window moved with the
image's bytes, as its RESULTS.md says it does.

- `hydo explore --reactive-at meili.swap_acked@20` gave the grid of 153 schedules (51 delays,
  three actions) in 4 minutes 24 seconds, with its shrinks. Finding 1, the swap that runs twice
  (`VIOLATION [swap] sa and sb are swapped otherwise than # succeeded swaps say`), came first at
  seed 29, `A=meili.swap_acked@20+9:kill-meilisearch`. It came again at seeds 32, 34 and 37:
  `kill-meilisearch` at 10 ms and `kill-now-meilisearch` at 11 and 12 ms. The edit that runs
  twice came at seeds 5, 8, 11, 13 and 16 (`kill-meilisearch` at 1 to 3 ms,
  `kill-now-meilisearch` at 4 and 5 ms). Every power cut broke `docs` or `dumps`, findings 2 and 3. All 60 failures failed again
  the same way, and each signature shrank to its one reaction.
- The blind exploration of Milestone 309 on the same image, `--strategy process --reactive fault
  --react-events meili.swap_acked,meili.edit_acked,meili.add_acked --kill-now --seeds 1-360`, ran
  the swap twice first at seed 101, and at 5 of its 360 seeds (101, 138, 158, 160 and 307), in
  12 minutes 29 seconds. The aimed grid found it at its 29th schedule, at 4 of 153 cells.
- `--reactive-at meili.swap_acked`, armed from the start, ran the swap twice first at seed 20
  (`kill-meilisearch` 6 ms after the first swap's `202`) and again at seed 25
  (`kill-now-meilisearch` at 8 ms), in 4 minutes 43 seconds.

**2. Options the engine or the image cannot use.** `hydo explore` already refused a few options
before any VM: `--more-faults` on the Mac and KVM engines, `--block-faults` on hvx, `--vcpus 2`
on the Mac, `--cluster-faults` without `groups:`, `--upgrades` without `versions:`. Other options
drew schedules that the engine then refused one by one, or drew nothing. The new module
`hydo_explore::refuse` asks before the first run, with the existing rules:

- For each option that draws a kind of its own (`--timing`, `--preempt`, `--more-faults`,
  `--turns`, `--pause-workload` and `--pause-thread`, `--block-faults`, `--storage-faults`), it
  draws the first 64 schedules with only that option on and asks `hydo_engine::refusal_on`, the
  rule each engine applies before a VM (Milestone 208), with the exploration's vCPUs and the
  image's epoch. A refused draw refuses the option with the engine's reason and one example.
  `--timing` with `--vcpus 2` on KVM is such a case: its tick jitter is one vCPU's.
- `--storage-faults` on a manifest without a service with `storage:`, or whose `faults:` allows
  neither `corrupt` nor `powerloss`, and `--block-faults` on an image without a data disk, are
  refused: they would draw nothing.
- `--react-delays` and `--react-actions` without `--reactive-at` are refused.

Each refusal is one line with the option, the reason and what to use instead. The probe prints
every line it has, and the explorer stops with status 5, as Milestone 328's refusals do, with
the JSON line for a program. The probe costs no VM. Every option of the explorer's own refusal
test (`--timing --preempt --new-faults`, and `--more-faults` on hvx) passes on the three engines.

**3. One list of several explorations' problems.** `hydo report A B C` and `hydo report --html A
B C [-o FILE]` read several explorations of one image and list each problem once. The rounds
keep their own documents: `hydo explore --merge` merges the shards of one exploration, which
share one command line, and these rounds do not. Each round's problems come from its own story,
the same words as its own report. Two failures are one problem when their class group and
signature agree, the key that each exploration shrinks by, and the keys that one round's report
shows as one problem stay one. A problem is shown as the first round that found it shows it,
with that round's minimal schedule, its command, and its own problem number for `hydo inspect
diagnose`. A line under its title names every round and seed that showed it, and the top of the
list names each round with its seeds and the options that tell it from the others. The error
lines of new kinds are one problem with the rounds that wrote them. Two images (by their sha256)
are refused. The page is the first folder's `report-merged.html`.

On the three Meilisearch rounds of part 1, `hydo report hydo-out/blind hydo-out/aim20
hydo-out/aim0` listed 5 problems, where the three reports list 5, 3 and 3, 11 in all. The swap
and the edit that run twice, one problem in each report, read "in 3 of 3 explorations: 1 (seeds
101, 123, 138, 151, 158, 160, 185, 307 and 1 more), 2 (seeds 5, 8, 11, 13, 16, 29, 32, 34 and 1
more) and 3 (seeds 20 and 25)". A line names at most 8 seeds and counts the rest. The documents
lost after a power cut, the empty dumps and the new error line showed in all three rounds, and a
lost snapshot after a kill and a cut in the blind round only. A key that two rounds share takes
the first round's words: the aimed rounds' lost documents after a cut joined the blind round's
problem, whose minimal schedule also pauses the service. `hydo report --html` of the three wrote
a page of 16 KiB.

**Tests.** `hydo-schedule`'s language test reads and refuses the `#<k>` forms. The controller's
reaction tests run a later record with the host's reaction and with the relay, and a unit test
runs the relay's counting line in `sh`. The explorer's `reactive::an_aimed_exploration_tries_every_cell_in_turn`
checks the grid's order, its canonical schedules and the second round on the Meilisearch
manifest; `refusals::options_the_engine_or_the_image_cannot_use_are_refused` checks the
refusals and that the engines' own options pass. `hydo::explore_refusal` runs an aimed
exploration on the scripted engine (8 schedules without `--seeds`) and the refusal of
`--storage-faults` with status 5. `merged::a_problem_two_rounds_found_is_listed_once` merges
two rounds. No explorer or controller golden moved.

**What is left.** Open item 173.

## Milestone 346 (tentative number): a ready-made claim that an acknowledged write ends as acknowledged

A `type: messages` check takes a new claim, `acked_outcome`: every send that the system
acknowledged ends in a final state that the check's `final:` reads back, and that state agrees
with the acknowledgement. The user said "do" on 2026-11-23. Nothing recorded moved.

**Why.** A check of this kind found the Meilisearch example's lost document additions without a
hint: an addition acknowledged with `202` ended `failed` with an internal error after a power
cut. The same kind of check caught an index deletion reported `failed` with `index_not_found`
after it had taken effect. Each project wrote the check by hand, and the rules are easy to get
wrong: an agent's check of the Iggy example counted an error of an unknown outcome as a failure.

**The declaration** (a format-1 addition, `hydo/schema/project-v1.json`, the schema example
`messages-acked-outcome`):

```yaml
    final: /bin/mlc readback
    claims:
      acked_outcome:                      # none | success | a mapping
        client_errors: [index_not_found]  # codes, or patterns with *
        effect: recorded                  # none | recorded
```

`hydo build --check` refuses the claim without a `final:`. The results show `acked_outcome` in
the declaration only when it is declared, so every earlier declaration shows as it did.

**The records.** A new operation of the messages history, `status <channel> <item>...`, written
by the read-back. Each item of its completion carries the final state in `s=` (`ok` succeeded,
`fail` failed, `info` no final state), the system's error in `e=`, and with `effect: recorded`
whether the operation's effect is in the system's state, `f=1` or `f=0`. A read without an
answer is the operation's `info`. The Rust SDK writes it with `Messages::status`,
`Item::final_state`, `Item::error` and `Item::effect`. The shared case
`sdk/cases/history/messages` has four new lines, and the Go, Python and JavaScript SDKs replay
it unchanged (their tests pass).

**The claim**, reported as `<check id>.acked-outcome`, judges the last answered read of each id:

- An acknowledged send breaks it when it ends `s=info`, or `s=fail` with an `e=` that
  `client_errors:` does not name.
- A send with an unknown outcome may end in any state.
- With `effect: recorded`, `s=ok` with `f=0` and `s=fail` with `f=1` break it for any send,
  also with a client error. An item without `f=` is judged by its final state alone.
- An acknowledged id without an answered read is undecided; with no answered read at all the
  claim is undecided, and the run's verdict is an ERROR.

A violation names up to five ids with their system ids and final states, and its witness holds
each one's send and status record. The checker is `claims::acked_outcome` in hydo-history's
module `messages`. A status operation creates no group, so it changes no other claim.

**The tests.** `hydo-history`'s `messages::` has six new scripted tests of the claim: a hold with
succeeded and client-caused failures, the failures that break it, the effect with and without
`effect: recorded`, the undecided cases, the declaration's refusals and its JSON, and the
witness in `run_checks`. `hydo-manifest`'s `format::` takes the new schema and the example case,
and `hydo-schema-compat` finds the schema an addition to the released one. The Rust SDK's
`messages_records_the_shared_case` writes the shared case's new lines; the Go, Python and
JavaScript SDKs' case tests pass unchanged.

**The Meilisearch example** (`hydo/onboard/examples/meilisearch`, Mac engine, this tree's hydo
over the 0.5.0 release's guest files, images at the fingerprint epoch 5). The client records each
task request as a send of its request id with the task's uid as its system id, and writes
`m<uid>:<request id>` to `$HYDO_ACKED`. `mlc readback`, the final: of the new check `queue`,
drains the queue and writes each acknowledged task's final state, its error's code, and the
effect of an addition (every document stored with its body) and of an index deletion whose
creation succeeded (the index is gone). The check declares
`acked_outcome: {client_errors: [index_not_found], effect: recorded}`. In its own commit the
client gained `parallel_driver_delidx`: the creation of an index `x<cmd>` and its deletion,
enqueued one after the other, with the event `meili.delete_index_acked`.

| schedule | `queue.acked-outcome` | fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| `disk=none \| run` | held over 173 acknowledged tasks | `34d6b1999155c0a5` (twice) |
| `disk=cut \| run A=meili.add_acked@20+2:cut` (finding 2) | broken: `add.155 (system id 178) was acknowledged and ended failed with internal, but its effect is there; add.157 (system id 180) ... failed with internal, not an error the client causes` | `3e5b31f5dd34a1fb` |
| `disk=none \| run A=meili.delete_index_acked+13:kill-now-meilisearch` | broken: `delidx.4 (system id 14) was acknowledged and ended failed with index_not_found, but its effect is there` | `b72d43f0a3a2d63c` (three runs) |
| `disk=none \| run A=meili.delete_index_acked+7:kill-now-meilisearch` | broken: `mkidx.4 (system id 13) was acknowledged and ended failed with index_already_exists, not an error the client causes` | `f3bf73fdaf6b40f3` (three runs) |
| `disk=none \| run A=meili.swap_acked@20+10:cut` | broken: `add.157 (system id 179) was acknowledged and ended succeeded, but its effect is not there` | `e21f719584c4b44e` |

On the image before the deletion driver (the second commit's), finding 2's schedule broke the
claim twice with `fp=fecb31f6821fff20`, and the clean run held over 159 tasks with
`fp=b9c674012d4c2dc7`.

What the effect showed. Finding 2's failed additions have their documents stored: the first boot
indexed them, and the restart ran their batch again after the payload files were gone. So on
this image the failure comes from finding 1's split of two commits, not from a lost payload. With
the cut 10 or 16 ms after a swap the payload was lost before the first run, and the claim names
a succeeded addition whose documents are missing. The index deletion and the creation run twice
after a kill between their two commits, a fourth form of finding 1 (RESULTS.md, finding 4). The
deletion's `index_not_found` is in `client_errors`, so only the effect breaks the claim there.
Delays of 4 to 6, 12 and 14 ms held. The old check `final_tasks`, which counts every failure as
broken, broke on the same runs; the claim states the rule without a hand-written check, and it
held where `final_tasks` called a succeeded addition with `indexedDocuments` 0 broken although
its documents are stored (`+14`, `A=meili.add_acked@20+40:cut`).

**What moved.** No value of `hydo/onboard/recorded.json`: the example is not in it. The example's
own values (RESULTS.md) are new, because the client and the composition changed. The saved
regressions on the new image:

- `payload-lost-at-a-power-cut` and `swap-runs-twice-after-a-kill` keep their violations.
- `swap-runs-twice-after-a-crash` (`A=meili.add_acked@20+40:cut`) still fails, by findings 2
  and 3; the swap no longer runs twice there. Its comment says so.
- `dump-empty-after-a-power-cut` passed with `C=30`, because no dump came before step 30 in the
  new composition. It is `C=55` now (`fp=547d6d5f16276222`, twice).
- `index-deletion-runs-twice-after-a-kill` is new.

The explorer's `identity-quick.txt` and `corpus-full.txt` are re-recorded for the example's new
inputs. The controller's corpus held unchanged.

**What is left.** Open item 174, and open item 66 is updated.

## Milestone 347 (tentative number): two gaps of a user's test project

Status: done on 2026-11-23. Nothing recorded moved, and the fingerprint epoch stays 5.

A user's test project on a Mac found two gaps of `hydo compose`:

1. An image tag whose index has only a linux/arm64 build failed without `--from-docker`. The
   registry reader (`hydo_compose::registry::resolve_image`) refused every image without a
   linux/amd64 build, with `no linux/amd64 image`, on every machine. Now it refuses only an
   image with neither build. The service's settings (its command, user, ports, healthcheck and
   volumes) come from the amd64 build, or from the arm64 build when the image has only that
   (`settings_platform`), as they already did for a local build made on a Mac. A one-shot job's
   user comes from the same place. `hydo compose` warns that such an image runs on the Mac engine
   only. On an x86_64 machine fetch-images.sh stops at its amd64 file with `fetch-images.sh:
   <image> has no linux/amd64 build, so it does not run on this machine`, instead of fetching the
   tag for an architecture the image does not have. An image without platform entries (an image
   given by digest with `--no-resolve`) writes the same lines as before.
2. `hydo compose --help` and the usage line of `hydo compose` without a file did not name
   `--from-docker`; both do now, and the help says what it does.

MANIFEST.md's row for `image:` says what an image with only an arm64 build gives.

**Tests.** `registry::an_arm64_only_image_is_imported` answers from a registry in the test with
an index of one arm64 build: the reader keeps it, the manifest takes its `Cmd` and `EXPOSE`, and
fetch-images.sh has the stop line. The CLI's recorded answers of `compose`, `compose --help` and
`guide manifest` are re-recorded (`HYDO_BLESS=1`), with the digest of the guide's files in
`agents.jsonl`. `compose_equals_python` keeps every one of its 185 cases.

**What is left.** The user's own project did not run with the fix. An image with only an amd64
build on a Mac is unchanged: its hydo.yaml names the x86_64 file only.

## Milestone 348 (tentative number): five gaps of recent onboardings

Status: done on 2026-11-23. Nothing recorded moved, and the fingerprint epoch stays 5.

The onboardings of ClickHouse (M311), Prometheus (M342), GreptimeDB (M343) and the aimed
explorations of Meilisearch (M345) named five gaps. Each fix is its own commit.

1. **`hydo-oci` by name (`guest.path`).** The commands that hydo starts in the guest had no
   `PATH`. The kernel gives init none, and busybox's shell exports none. A shell command found
   `hydo-oci` through the shell's own default, but Go's `exec.Command("hydo-oci", ...)` in the
   Prometheus client failed with `executable file not found in $PATH` (open item 170). The
   format-1 addition `guest.path: true` makes the host controller give every command it starts
   `PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin`
   (`hydo_image::COMMAND_PATH`, busybox's own default). The manifest's `env:` can still set
   another. The variable is in each command's environment, so in guest RAM, and in every
   fingerprint and control transcript. So what an absent key means is keyed on the image's
   fingerprint epoch (`hydo_image::EpochDefaults::command_path`): off at every epoch up to 5,
   and on from the next one, 6. The host controller's environment was chosen over an `export`
   in the image's `prelude.sh`. The prelude is part of the image's bytes, so that way would
   change every image built from now on; the controller's way changes nothing until a manifest
   asks for it.
2. **A failing workload command's output.** A composed command's output stays in the guest's
   `/tmp/hydo/compose/log.<entry>`, so the examples' clients copied their errors to the console
   (open items 157 and 170). The controller already reads that file after each command. Now a
   command that ends with an exit status other than 0 and 100 gives one `HYDO-CMD-OUT
   {"id":..,"entry":..,"rc":..,"lines":[..],"omitted":n}` note, the first time in a boot. A
   command that reports a violation (exit 100) gives the `HYDO-CHECK-OUT` note of its finding
   `compose.<id>.no_violation` instead, so `result.json` keeps the lines in `details.output`, as
   M225 does for a failing check. Both keep the last 20 lines, each cut to 300 bytes, at most
   2,000 bytes. A note is in the run's console log (`one.log`), and no transcript's hash and no
   fingerprint covers it. The diagnosis replay of M239 also reads the output: of a plain
   `workload.run` (`workload.log`), or of up to 4 composed commands that failed in the verdict's
   conversation, named by the controller's `HYDO-CMD end` reports. It writes their last 64 KiB
   to `logs/workload.log` and `logs/command.<id>.log`.
3. **The error-log scan past hvx's 16 MiB.** On hvx a boot whose agent lines passed the 16 MiB
   that the engine keeps lost the agent's later replies, and the run waited for its wall limit
   with no word but a line of `engine.log` (open item 171). The engine now ends the boot at the
   first stop after the buffer filled, with `ERROR agent lines full <phase>: ...`. The verdict
   names the error-log scan of large service logs as the usual cause, and says to lower the
   services' log level or to set `errors: false`. The diagnosis takes the verdict's words. Failing
   early was chosen over a bound on the scan: the host controller does not know its engine, and
   the Mac and KVM engines keep 32 MiB of console per boot, so a bound for hvx would change their
   scans too. A run that filled the buffer never reached a verdict before, so no recorded run
   changes.
4. **An option that draws nothing.** M345's probe asked the engine about each option's draws
   after the explorer's rendering, which drops what the manifest's `faults:` or the engine does
   not keep, so an option whose draws were all dropped was not refused (open item 173). Now the
   explorer compares its first 64 rendered schedules with and without each drawing option:
   `--new-faults`, `--more-faults`, `--cluster-faults`, `--protocol-faults`, `--upgrades`,
   `--pause-workload` or `--pause-thread`, and `--corrupt-several`. An option that changes none
   of them is refused, one line each, with the exit status 5. The range of `--cf-range auto`
   comes from a probe run after the check, so the check gives `--more-faults` a placeholder
   range. The point runs of `--sweep`, a given schedule,
   `--no-faults` and `--reactive-at` draw no seed's faults and are not checked. `--new-faults`
   with `--strategy process` or `swarm-pos` gets a warning only, because those strategies draw
   pauses, clock steps and one-way losses themselves. About 100 lines of the examples' hydo.yaml
   headers, RESULTS.md pages and design notes give that pair, and a refusal would have made
   them wrong. The lines that recommend a command to a user drop `--new-faults` from the process
   strategy: `hydo guide strategies`, `hydo guide error-paths`, `hydo guide faults` and the
   playbook.
5. **The saved Meilisearch regression.** Open items 148 and 173 said that
   `swap-runs-twice-after-a-kill.schedule` (`+14`) passes on the image built at epoch 5. That was
   M345's image. M346 changed the client, and on its image the regression fails again (its
   RESULTS.md table, "Since Milestone 346"). On the Mac engine, with this tree's hydo and the
   example built again (`ce20b437…`), `disk=none | run A=meili.swap_acked@20+14:kill-now-meilisearch`
   gave `VIOLATION [swap]` in two runs, `fp=5401620771ff668b` and `wfp=ff2e49cab7d84f41`, the
   value of M346's table. `+12`, which M345's grid named, passes on this image
   (`wfp=19611eda9fb10bd2`). So the regression and its `# expect: violation` line stay as they
   are. The run without faults gave `wfp=34d6b1999155c0a5`, also M346's value.

**Proof on the Mac engine.** The runs of item 5 also showed item 2. In the `+12` run, 96 of
159 composed commands failed while Meilisearch was down, and `one.log` had 10 `HYDO-CMD-OUT`
lines, one per command, such as `mlc: POST /indexes/docs/documents: no answer: ... connection
refused`. `hydo inspect diagnose <the +14 run> --evidence` wrote four `logs/command.<id>.log`
files beside `logs/meilisearch.log`. The fingerprints above are M346's, so the notes moved none.

**Tests.** `command_path::` runs a conversation with and without the key: with it, every command
the controller starts has the `PATH`; without it, or with `false`, none has one.
`hydo_image`'s defaults test says that no epoch up to 5 has the default on. `command_out::` checks
the note's bounds, and the diagnosis's unit test checks which `HYDO-CMD end` reports name a
file to read. `phase_end` has a unit test in the hvx engine, which builds on Linux only; clippy
checked it for the `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` target. `refusals::an_option_that_draws_nothing_is_refused`
refuses `--cluster-faults` and `--upgrades` on the Redis example, warns of `--new-faults` with
the process strategy, and refuses nothing of 14 examples' own command lines. The project
schema and the CLI's recorded answer of `hydo guide manifest` are re-recorded (`HYDO_BLESS=1`).
Every control transcript of the controller's corpora held unchanged. In `m123-quick.txt` only
the count of records that contain ` seed=` moved, from 308 to 314: six new `HYDO-CMD-OUT` notes
quote the output of the scripted agent's failing commands. The line is re-recorded in the
record's commit.

**What moved.** No value of `hydo/onboard/recorded.json`, and no example's value.

**What is left.** Open item 176, and open items 148, 157, 170, 171 and 173 are updated.

## Milestone 349 (tentative number): Garage, three nodes, and what a listing says

The onboarding of Garage v2.5.0 (2026-10-24, the newest release) on the Mac engine, by
`docs/ONBOARDING-PLAYBOOK.md`, with the hydo of `main` at `45aa2be3` (0.5.0 and Milestones 344
to 347). Two new candidates and one bug fixed on Garage's `main-v2` but in no release. Nothing
was posted. Nothing recorded moved.

**The example.** `hydo/onboard/examples/garage` (RESULTS.md) runs production's shape: three
nodes with `replication_factor = 3`, the default `consistency_mode = "consistent"` and LMDB, each
node's metadata and data on a file system of its own. It was imported with `hydo compose` from
the example's Compose file; the configuration is `config/garage-fsync-<true|false>.toml`, chosen
by the build parameter `fsync` (`true` by default, Garage's default is `false`). The Go client
`gac` (the AWS SDK for Go v2) connects the nodes, applies the layout and makes the key and the
bucket through the admin API v2. It runs PutObject, overwrites, DeleteObject, DeleteObjects,
multipart uploads with their completion or their abort, and CopyObject, each through a node that
the seed picks, and reads each acknowledged write through another node. The checks are a
`type: messages` check with M346's `acked_outcome` and `effect: recorded`, a listing check, an
uploads check, and an `eventually_` check that every node answers. Two clean runs give one
fingerprint on the final image (`d25c3a50…`): `e80b6137f1d1a827`.

**Finding 1, fixed on `main-v2`, not released.** After a backward clock step, CopyObject onto an
existing or a deleted key is acknowledged and has no effect. `handle_copy_metaonly`
(`src/api/s3/copy.rs` line 293) takes `now_msec()` as the copy's version timestamp, while every
other write takes `next_timestamp` (`put.rs` line 720). `disk=none | run T=17:-3600` fails on
every run. Commit `4dde841d` (2026-11-22, the quota fix of #1621) uses `next_timestamp` there too.
Blind in 23 of the 200 blind schedules.

**Finding 2, new.** After a node comes back from a kill, a pause or a power loss, ListObjectsV2
lists the keys deleted while it was down, through any node, for up to 10 minutes, while GET
answers 404. Each node applies the listing's filter `IsData` to its own copy
(`src/table/data.rs`, `read_range_aux`, lines 152 to 161) before the coordinator merges the copies
(`src/table/table.rs`, `get_range_internal`), so the nodes that hold the deletion return nothing
for the key. `get_range` does no read repair, and the anti-entropy sync of the object table runs
every 10 minutes. ListMultipartUploads lists an aborted upload the same way (`IsUploading`).
`disk=none dseed=0 | run K=garage1@1+1 W=757a66d9,p4,q1,r500,oanytime_read` and `disk=none
dseed=0 | run N=nodes.isolate.3@21-29:delay,500ms W=6d4d3721,p3,q2,r500 L=garage1@23+1` are the
regressions. Blind in 52 of the 200 blind schedules, from seed 2.

**Finding 3, new, minor.** Each node saves its peers' addresses once a minute
(`DISCOVERY_INTERVAL`), by truncating and writing `peer_list` without a sync
(`src/util/persister.rs` line 79). A cluster formed with `garage node connect`, as the page
"Deployment on a cluster" does, then does not form again after a power loss of every node in its
first minute. With `hydo build --set peerwait=no`, `disk=cut | run C=3` ends `VIOLATION
[available] not satisfied 120.56s after heal`. The default build waits for the lists in
`first_init`, so that the explorations' power cuts test the data.

**Not bugs.** With `fsync=false` a power cut lost an acknowledged PutObject (`hydo explore
--configs` labeled it the documented trade-off). A damaged LMDB file stops its node, as "Known
issues" says. A damaged `node_key` leaves its node out of the cluster: Garage does not compare the
key's two halves.

**What held.** With both fsync settings on, every acknowledged write but the copies of finding 1
stayed as acknowledged and was readable through another node at once. That held through kills,
pauses up to 80 s, partitions and one-way loss, one node's power loss, damaged data blocks of one
or two nodes, and 48 power cuts of the whole guest 0 to 30 ms after an acknowledgement. LMDB keeps
`MDB_NOMETASYNC` with `metadata_fsync = true`, which may undo the last transaction (issue #1571
names it), but Garage's next commits come within milliseconds.

**Explorations.** e1 and e3 (process, seeds 1-80, cluster and storage faults), e6 (swarm, seeds
81-120, `--kill-now` reactions at the client's events), e7 (process, seeds 121-200, with
`--corrupt-several` and reactions), e2 and e4 (M345's `--reactive-at` grids, 132 schedules), and
e5 (`--configs`, both values of `fsync`, 20 seeds each). All on one worker of 1,024 MiB, at 160 to
860 runs an hour.

**Tests.** The explorer's corpus and identity goldens (quick and full) and the controller's
corpus golden are re-recorded for the new example's inputs (`HYDO_BLESS=1`).

Retro: Garage v2.5.0, the Mac engine, 2026-11-23
- Time to the first clean run: 50 minutes of wall time, 20 of them waiting for free disk.
- Schedules run before the first finding: 1, a directed clock step; blind, seed 2 of e1. None
  failed by the rules' mistakes but the first clean run, whose listing check named the first
  command's keys.
- The findings: 2 new (the listing, and the lost peers), 1 fixed but not released (the copy), 1
  documented (`fsync=false`), and the environment (damaged LMDB files and keys).
- What took the most time: the power cuts that left the cluster without peers, which first looked
  like hydo's or the checks' error (about 30 minutes); two waits for free disk (about 20
  minutes); separating the faults of the uploads listing (about 10 minutes).
- What hydo lacked: `hydo rules scan --kind writes` found no route in Garage, the clock audit
  does not see versions ordered by wall-clock timestamps, and an `acked_outcome` check without
  deliveries makes every passing run count as vacuous (open item 177).
- Strategies: a new entry, "A listing compared with a read of each key", found finding 2. The
  entries "Clock steps and the clock audit", "Power cuts of the whole guest", "A scan of a
  reaction's delay" and "Settings that trade durability" of `hydo guide strategies` are updated,
  and the first table has a row for object stores.

**What is left.** Open item 177.

## Milestone 350 (tentative number): the three gaps of the Garage onboarding

Status: done on 2026-11-24. Nothing recorded moved, and the fingerprint epoch stays 5.

The Garage onboarding (M349) named three gaps of hydo in the section "What hydo lacked" of its
RESULTS.md. Each fix is its own commit. The proofs read the sources of Garage v2.5.0, of the six
projects of M344 at their tags, and of Valkey 9.1.3, Temporal 1.32.2 and River v0.51.2, cloned
from their repositories, with a debug build on this Mac. No VM ran.

1. **The write routes of an enumeration of endpoints.** `hydo rules scan --kind writes` found no
   route in Garage. Garage's S3 router is a Rust `enum Endpoint` whose variants are the
   operations. A match on the request's method calls `from_get`, `from_put` and the others,
   whose arms name the variants from the query and the headers (`EMPTY header
   "x-amz-copy-source" => CopyObject`). The admin API lists each variant after its method in a
   macro's table (`POST CreateKey (body),`). The scan now reads both shapes in Rust:
   - a match on the request's method (`Method::PUT => ...`) whose arm names a variant, or calls
     a function of the file whose arms name the variants;
   - a table in a macro's invocation that names a variant after `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or
     `DELETE`.

   An operation's handler is the first call of the arm that matches its variant
   (`Endpoint::PutObject { key } => handle_put(ctx, req, &key).await`), or of the block of an
   `if let Endpoint::CreateBucket {} = endpoint`. When no arm names the variant, the handler is
   the first method of a type named for it (`impl RequestHandler for CreateKeyRequest`). Garage's
   S3, K2V and admin routers each have an `Endpoint`, so an arm in the files nearest to the
   router wins. An operation that no code handles is left out: Garage answers "not implemented"
   to most of S3's bucket settings. The path is `<Enum>::<Variant>`. The resource is the
   variant's first noun (`bucket` of `PutBucketCors`), and the class comes from the variant's
   words, not from the enumeration's name.
2. **Versions ordered by the wall clock.** The clock audit looked only for durations. Garage's
   CopyObject takes its version's timestamp from `now_msec()` (`src/api/s3/copy.rs` line 293),
   while PutObject keeps it above the key's newest version (`next_timestamp`, `put.rs` line
   720). The audit has a second kind of place now, the shape `order`: a reading of the clock
   kept as the order or the version of data.
   - The reading is the value of a name about an order (`timestamp`, `ts`, `version`, `seq`,
     `revision`), or of a variable that the function then stores in such a field.
   - It reads the clock now: no time made from a stored value (`time.Unix(0, 0)`), no getter
     that the duration audit follows, and no stamp formatted for a log.
   - A reading kept above the earlier value (`max(prev + 1, now_msec())`) is no place.

   A place is `high` when the code compares two values of the name: a merge (`other.ts >
   self.ts`), a maximum or a sort key (`.map(|v| v.timestamp).max()`), or the fields of a
   function named `cmp_key`. The places are ranked as the durations are, in a section of their
   own with its own 5 shown, so the durations keep their ranks. Each gets three schedules: a step
   back of 5 minutes and one of an hour in the middle of the workload, and a step back of 5
   minutes after a restart of the service that runs the code. `--json` gives them as
   `clock_orders`, and the scan without `--kind` counts them in a line of its own.

   Garage's `now_msec()` returns `SystemTime::now()` over three lines of a chain, and the audit
   read a Rust tail expression on its last line only. It now starts at the chain's first line,
   unless the chain measures a duration (`.elapsed()`). The limits had a second friction: the
   audit explained Garage's places with "10 minutes by default (src/block/manager.rs:49)", a
   constant of another file. The name it took was `Duration`, of `Duration::hours(24)`. Now a
   type is no limit, and a plain word such as `timeout`, `idle` or `interval` is read in the
   place's own file only. A name of two words or in capitals is still read in every file, as
   Valkey's `repl_min_replicas_max_lag` is. A literal of Rust (`Duration::hours(24)`,
   `Duration::from_secs(600)`) gives the limit when no name does. A Rust `fn new` counts as a
   function now; the rule against Java's `new X(...)` had left it out.
3. **A messages check with one claim that judged nothing.** A `type: messages` check gives one
   finding per claim. Garage's check declares `acked_outcome` and records no deliveries, so its
   implicit `no-phantom` judged nothing while `acked-outcome` judged about 80 operations a run.
   `hydo explore` then counted all 48 passing runs of e4 as vacuous passes. Now a claim with
   nothing to judge makes the pass vacuous only when no claim of the same check judged an
   operation (`hydo_explore::results::vacuous`). The history checker's own warning, that the
   claim holds vacuously, stays.

**Proof of item 1.** On Garage v2.5.0 the scan read 205 files and listed 42 routes in 10
resources (34 `data`, 8 `admin`), each with its handler. It left out 3 POST operations whose
names read: `ReadBatch`, `PollRange` and `PreviewClusterLayoutChanges`. Every write of the
workload's table in RESULTS.md is in the list with its handler:

| operation | handler |
|---|---|
| PutObject | `handle_put` (`src/api/s3/put.rs:58`) |
| DeleteObject | `handle_delete` (`src/api/s3/delete.rs:56`) |
| DeleteObjects | `handle_delete_objects` (`src/api/s3/delete.rs:66`) |
| CopyObject | `handle_copy` (`src/api/s3/copy.rs:47`) |
| CreateMultipartUpload | `handle_create_multipart_upload` (`src/api/s3/multipart.rs:35`) |
| UploadPart | `handle_put_part` (`src/api/s3/multipart.rs:121`) |
| CompleteMultipartUpload | `handle_complete_multipart_upload` (`src/api/s3/multipart.rs:290`) |
| AbortMultipartUpload | `handle_abort_multipart_upload` (`src/api/s3/multipart.rs:573`) |
| CreateBucket | `handle_create_bucket` (`src/api/s3/bucket.rs:168`) |

The other bucket operations are DeleteBucket and the bucket's CORS, lifecycle and website
settings. The admin API's writes of `first_init` are there too: `ConnectClusterNodes`,
`UpdateClusterLayout`, `ApplyClusterLayout`, `ImportKey`, `CreateBucket` and `AllowBucketKey`,
each with its `<Variant>Request::handle`. The six projects of M344 gave the same JSON as before,
byte for byte: Meilisearch 83 routes, Iggy 38, Prometheus 14, GreptimeDB 53, Hatchet 99 and
Memos 49.

**Proof of item 2.** With the example's hydo.yaml the audit names 4 functions of Garage that
keep a wall-clock reading as a version, all `high`. The copy's `now_msec()` is the second:

```text
4 functions keep a wall-clock reading as the order or the version of stored data.
...
2. src/api/s3/copy.rs:293, in handle_copy_metaonly [high]
     let new_timestamp = now_msec();
   It keeps a wall-clock reading as timestamp, and the code orders data by comparing two values of it (src/api/s3/put.rs:723). ...
     back           disk=none | run T=20:-300
     back-long      disk=none | run T=20:-3600
     back-after     disk=none | run K=<service>@2+3 T=10:-300
```

The other three are the timestamps of a key's permissions on a bucket (`src/api/admin/bucket.rs`
line 253 and `src/garage/server.rs` line 387), and the constructor of Garage's last-writer-wins
register (`src/util/crdt/lww.rs` line 66). `put.rs` line 724 and the register's `update` keep
their reading above the earlier one, and the audit leaves them out. M349's finding 1 is the
schedule `back-long` at step 17: `disk=none | run T=17:-3600`. With `now_msec()` followed, the
durations of Garage grew from 4 functions to 9, among them the delays of the garbage collection
of blocks (`src/block/rc.rs`). Those two places name `BLOCK_GC_DELAY`, 10 minutes, which `rc.rs`
imports from `manager.rs` line 49. The places of the request signatures no longer name it.

The known places of the three public cases keep their ranks:

| project | the known place | rank with hydo.yaml (without) | functions with an order place |
|---|---|---|---|
| Valkey 9.1.3 | `refreshGoodReplicasCount`, `shouldStartChildReplication` | 2 and 4 (4 and 6) | 0 |
| Temporal 1.32.2 | `reconnect` in `db_handle.go` | 1 (3) | 4 |
| River v0.51.2 | `river_leader.sql` | 2 (2) | 0 |

Temporal's 4 order places stamp versions with `time.Now().UnixNano()`, such as the ephemeral
data of `service/matching/user_data_manager.go` that `mergeEphemeralDataLocked` merges by its
`Version`. Nobody judged them further. The rule for limits moved a few places of the reports
lower, below the top 5. A place whose explanation has a value from the code went from 30 to 29
on Valkey, from 16 to 15 on Temporal, and from 1 to 0 on River. Valkey's `clientMatchesFilter`
had named `idle, 10 seconds by default (src/anet.c:201)`, and River's place had named `Duration,
1 minute by default` from River's Java client.

**Proof of item 3.** The unit test
`a_messages_claim_with_nothing_to_judge_beside_one_that_judged_is_no_vacuous_pass` gives Garage's
pair of claims, `no-phantom` with 0 operations judged and `acked-outcome` with 80, and gets no
reason. Two claims of one check that both judged nothing give two reasons. A claim of another
check that judged operations does not cover a claim with nothing to judge. No exploration ran
again.

**Tests.** `writescan::tests::enumerations_of_endpoints_with_their_handlers` reads both shapes,
an `if let`, a request type's handler, an operation without a handler, and a POST that reads.
`clockscan::tests::a_reading_kept_as_a_version_is_an_order` has the copy, the put that keeps its
reading above the newest version, a time of creation, the three-line `now_msec()`, a Go merge,
and a stamp for a log. `a_limit_is_no_type_and_no_plain_word_of_another_file` checks the limits,
and `hydo::rules::the_clock_audit_names_versions_taken_from_the_wall_clock` checks the report,
the JSON, and the scan without `--kind`.

**What moved.** No value of `hydo/onboard/recorded.json`, no example's value, and no golden.

## Milestone 351 (tentative number): Kvrocks, a master, two replicas, and WAIT

The onboarding of Apache Kvrocks 2.17.0 (2026-09-19, the newest release) on the Mac engine, by
`docs/ONBOARDING-PLAYBOOK.md`, with the hydo of `main` at `b8c698d7` (0.5.0 and Milestones 344
to 349). Two new candidates. Nothing was posted. Nothing recorded moved.

**The example.** `hydo/onboard/examples/kvrocks` (RESULTS.md) runs a master and two replicas from
the official image, each node's RocksDB data and configuration on a file system of its own, with
`rocksdb.write_options.sync yes` and `use-rsid-psync yes` (the build parameters `sync` and
`rsid`; Kvrocks's defaults are `no`). It was imported with `hydo compose` from the example's
Compose file; `config/start.sh` writes each node's configuration into its volume at the first
start, because Kvrocks rewrites it. The Go client `kvc` (go-redis v9, without retries) writes
strings, `SET ... PXAT` keys, hashes, counters, lists, sets, sorted sets, `MULTI`/`EXEC`
transactions and Lua scripts, and confirms each with `WAIT 2`. It reads each confirmed write on
both replicas. It fails the master over to a replica as Redis Sentinel does, with one late write
to the old master, and runs `FLUSHMEMTABLE` so that the data reaches SST files. The token `M`
switches the client to the mode where the master's reply alone acknowledges a write and no
failover runs. The checks are a `type: messages` check with M346's `acked_outcome` and `effect:
recorded`, `eventually_converge` (the replicas hold what the master holds), `eventually_wait`
(`WAIT 2` answers 2 after the heal), `final_atomic` and `final_counters`.

**Finding 1, new.** A node that has just rejoined by a full synchronization does not start again
after a power loss. `ReplicationThread::fetchFile` (`src/cluster/replication.cc` lines 1040 to
1112) writes the master's checkpoint with `WritableFile::Append` and no sync, `SwapTmpFile` and
`Storage::RestoreFromCheckpoint` (`src/storage/storage.cc` lines 500 to 554) rename the files and
the directories into place without a sync and destroy the old database. A power cut of the guest
or of the node alone in the next seconds leaves the fetched SST files at length 0, and the node
stops at every start with `Corruption: Sst file size mismatch between expected 2080 and file
system 0`. `disk=cut dseed=0 | run W=6311ab23,p4,q3,r500 A=kvrocks.failover_done+5500:cut` is the
directed regression; blind, e2 found it in 10 of 60 schedules, shrunk to `disk=cut dseed=0 | run
C=40 W=d6d260d0,p3,q2,r500,oanytime_read`. The cause is unchanged on `unstable` at `ff8bb662`.

**Finding 2, new, a clock effect.** After a backward step of the wall clock, `WAIT 2` on an idle
master answers 0 for the step's length, and `INFO replication` reports a lag, although both
replicas hold every write. `sendReplConfAck` (`src/cluster/replication.cc` lines 666 to 682)
sends an acknowledgement that is not forced only when `util::GetTimeStamp()`, the wall clock, has
moved a second past the last one, and an idle master forces none. `disk=none dseed=0 | run
M=master T=17:-300 W=740c6cfa,p1,q3,r500` is the regression; blind in 9 of 40 schedules with the
master's reply as the acknowledgement, shrunk to the clock step alone.

**Not bugs.** With Kvrocks's default `rocksdb.write_options.sync no` a power cut lost 8 of 70
acknowledged writes (e4, seed 1), the documented cost; with `yes` none was lost. In e4 one
failure was the expiry check's mistake: a key had expired as set before a backward clock step,
and the read-back required it after the step. The client now records the latest clock the run
saw. 16 schedules damaged `CURRENT`, an SST file, a WAL or the node's configuration with
`G=`, and the node then stopped at its start: detected damage. `CONFIG REWRITE` writes without a
sync (the open apache/kvrocks#3710); no run showed it.

**What held.** With both durable settings, every write that `WAIT 2` confirmed stayed as
acknowledged through kills, pauses, partitions, failovers with late writes, one node's power loss,
damaged files, power cuts and clock steps, but where finding 1 stopped a node. Every read of the
replicas after `WAIT 2` saw the write, every transaction and script was whole on every node, no
counter passed its `INCR`s, no deadline came early, and no replica served a value that no write
sent.

**Explorations.** e1 (the first image, seeds 1-20), r1 to r3 (`--reactive-at
kvrocks.failover_done` with power cuts 0.5 s to 23 s later, 43 schedules), e2 (process, seeds
21-80, cluster and storage faults), e3 (the master's reply as the acknowledgement, seeds 1-40),
and e4 (`--configs`, `sync` and `rsid` one at a time, seeds 1-20). e4 was stopped after its
second combination, before `use-rsid-psync no`, because the Mac had 5 GB of free disk and a full
swap. All on one worker of 1,024 MiB, at 240 to 560 runs an hour. RESULTS.md has the table.

**At the fingerprint epoch 6.** After the branch moved onto `main` at `e1b47cef` (Milestones 350,
352, 353 and 354), the example's image was built again at epoch 6 with the client's fixed expiry
check (`ee70237d…`). Every value moved with the image. Two clean runs give `bc3e6d306a811a13`.
`hydo repro --regressions` gave 3 of 3 as expected: finding 1's directed regression
`35d9039868e11329` (twice, once more in a `hydo run`), its blind regression `2dc94c8301e58369`,
and finding 2's `c964be0dc09a2a55`. The schedule that had failed by the check's mistake passes.
The clock audit and the scan of write routes of `e1b47cef` still found nothing in Kvrocks.

**Tests.** The explorer's corpus and identity goldens (quick and full; `identity-full.txt` did
not change) and the controller's corpus golden are re-recorded for the new example's inputs
(`HYDO_BLESS=1`). With a target folder of this branch's own: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo test
-p hydo-explore --test it` (60 passed), `-p hydo-control` (120 and 41 passed), `-p hydo-agents
--test it` (14 passed), `-p hydo --test it -- docs:: equivalence::` (23 passed), `sh
ci/vale.sh` and `sh ci/consolidate-tests.sh --check` pass. The whole `-p hydo --test it` gave 72
passed and 2 failed: `onboard::the_fetch_step_names_the_release_fetcher_when_it_is_not_on_path`
and `update::a_checkout_build_is_left_alone_with_the_commands`. Both expect a hydo built in its
checkout's `target/`, and this one was built in a target folder outside the checkout (open item
179). No Rust code changed in this milestone.

Retro: Kvrocks 2.17.0, the Mac engine, 2026-11-24
- Time to the first clean run: 1 hour 50 minutes of wall time from the start, none of it
  waiting for machines.
- Schedules run before the first finding: 43 aimed cuts, of which the first 13 could not reach
  it (no SST file in the checkpoint, or no failover in the run); blind, seed 22 of e2. One
  failure was the expiry check's mistake (e4).
- The findings: 2 new (the unsynced full synchronization, and `WAIT` after a backward clock
  step), 1 documented setting (`sync no`), and the environment (detected damage).
- What took the most time: making the full synchronization carry SST files and happen in every
  run (about 40 minutes); a reaction that never fired and passed (about 15 minutes); separating
  the data's agreement from the acknowledgements' in the checks (about 15 minutes).
- What hydo lacked: the scan of write routes and the clock audit found nothing in C++, a
  reaction whose event never came passed silently, `--reactive-at` with `--seeds` runs one
  point per seed, the diagnosis of a failed restart after `L=` quotes no log, a regression
  cannot carry a build parameter, and no reaction cuts one service's power (open item 179).
- Strategies: a new entry, "Failovers by the client, with a late write", found finding 1. The
  entries "Power cuts of the whole guest", "Clock steps and the clock audit" and "A scan of a
  reaction's delay" of `hydo guide strategies` are updated, and the first table names Kvrocks.

**What is left.** Open item 179.

## Milestone 352 (tentative number): aimed reactions, refusals and the claim `acked_outcome` on KVM

Status: done on 2026-11-24. Nothing recorded moved, and the fingerprint epoch stays 5.

Milestones 345, 346 and 348 ran on the Mac engine only (open items 173 and 174). This milestone
ran them on the KVM engine, on GitHub's runners, and records what held. No code changed.

### How the runs were made

The one-off workflow `.github/workflows/tmp-m345-m346-kvm.yml` and its script ran on the branch
`tmp-m345-m346-kvm` (commit `37c014fc`, on `main` at `b8c698d7`, which has Milestones 345 to
349). It ran as run 45371753189, and the branch is not merged. Three `ubuntu-24.04` jobs ran it.
Each job built the branch's `hydo`, and took the 0.5.0 release's guest files with `hydo setup
--get 0.5.0`. The KVM engine runs in the `hydo` process, so the controller of Milestones 345 to
348 was the branch's. The job then built the Meilisearch example
(`hydo/onboard/examples/meilisearch`) for x86_64 and ran the proofs, each schedule twice.

The hosts were two Intel Xeon 6975P-C and one Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C. GitHub gave no AMD host.
Every host built the image `3de31c71…`, and every host gave the same fingerprints, the same
failures, and the same shrinks. On Intel a KVM fingerprint of an image built at epoch 3 or later
leaves out DR6's host bits (Milestone 252), so the two models agree.

### The claim `acked_outcome` of Milestone 346

| schedule | verdict | `queue.acked-outcome` | fingerprint (`wfp`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `disk=none \| run` | OK, 159 of 159 commands succeeded | held over 173 acknowledged tasks | `890cecf05c958416` (`f1e85a586253c8ed`) |
| `A=meili.delete_index_acked+13:kill-now-meilisearch` (the saved regression) | OK | held over 8 | `29b491ad67043204` |
| `A=meili.swap_acked@20+14:kill-now-meilisearch` (the saved regression) | OK | held over 70 | `98aedc015867eec2` |
| `A=meili.delete_index_acked+6:kill-now-meilisearch` (found by the grid below) | `VIOLATION [tasks]` | broken: `delidx.4 (system id 14) was acknowledged and ended failed with index_not_found, but its effect is there` | `8385564e5978c59b` (`865d132dbc333ef3`) |

Each schedule gave one fingerprint in its two runs on each host. The clean run held over 173
tasks, as on the Mac. Both saved kill regressions pass on KVM: the window after an event sits at
another delay on each engine, as it moves with the image's bytes on one engine.

### The aimed grids of Milestone 345

`hydo explore --backend kvm --workers 2 --reactive-at meili.swap_acked@20` ran the grid of 153
schedules (51 delays, three actions) in 17 to 23 minutes. 21 first runs failed, and each failed
again with its own fingerprint.

- The swap that runs twice (finding 1, `VIOLATION [swap]`) came at 6 cells:
  `kill-meilisearch` 0, 1 and 2 ms after the swap's `202`, and `kill-now-meilisearch` at 3, 8
  and 9 ms. The first was seed 2, `disk=none dseed=0 | run A=meili.swap_acked@20:kill-meilisearch`.
  It shrank to itself, and both confirmations gave `42d6871a086075e1`. `hydo run` of it gave
  the same value twice on each host, the value of the explorer's first run.
- 15 of the 51 power cuts, from 2 ms to 50 ms, broke `edits`: an edit runs twice (`cnt's k has
  n=20 after 19 succeeded edits`). On Milestone 345's image the Mac's power cuts broke `docs` or `dumps`. No run
  of this grid broke `acked_outcome`.

`hydo explore --backend kvm --workers 2 --reactive-at meili.delete_index_acked --react-actions
kill-now,kill` ran 102 schedules in 7 to 10 minutes. 8 first runs failed, each with
`VIOLATION [tasks]`, and each failed again with its own fingerprint:

- `kill-now-meilisearch` at 1 to 5 ms and `kill-meilisearch` at 3 ms: the creation of `x4` runs
  twice, and the claim names `mkidx.4 ... ended failed with index_already_exists, not an error
  the client causes`. This is the Mac's form at 7 ms.
- `kill-now-meilisearch` at 6 ms and `kill-meilisearch` at 8 ms: the deletion runs twice, and
  the claim names the deletion's effect, the Mac's form at 13 ms.

Both forms have one signature, so the explorer shrank one of them, seed 3 (`+1`), to itself.

### The refusals of Milestones 345 and 348

Each of these stopped with status 5 in 0 to 6 seconds, before any run, with one line that names
the option and the reason:

- `--timing --vcpus 2`: the KVM engine refuses the tick jitter `tj=` with several vCPUs.
- `--more-faults`: `cf=` runs on hvx only.
- `--cluster-faults`, `--upgrades` and `--protocol-faults`: the manifest has no groups, no
  versions, and no fakes or proxies. With `--json` the explorer printed `{"refused": ...,
  "status": 5}`.
- `--react-delays 0..5` without `--reactive-at`.
- `--reactive-at` with `--kill-now --reactive fault`.
- `--react-actions kill-nobody`: the manifest and the engine leave that reaction out.

`--strategy process --new-faults` warned that `--new-faults` adds nothing to the strategy, and
ran its one seed (status 0).

The explorer's runs came before Milestone 350. Every passing first run carried the warning that
it checked nothing: 132 of 153, and 94 of 102. It came from the claim `no-phantom`, which had
no deliveries to judge. Milestone 350 changed that rule.

**What is left.** Open items 173 and 174 are updated.

## Milestone 353 (tentative number): the fingerprint epoch 6

Status: done on 2026-11-24. The fingerprint epoch is 6. No value of an older epoch moved, and the
epoch-6 values wait for the 0.6.0 pass.

This is the first step of hydo 0.6.0. Two defaults had waited for an epoch change, because each
moves the runs of every image that has it:

- `guest.outcomes_after_cut` (Milestone 184). Without the key, the recovery boot after a power
  cut starts with an empty `$HYDO_OUTCOMES`. A check that looks up the ids listed there then
  reports every acknowledged id lost, or passes without checking anything. Open item 62 kept the
  key opt-in until an epoch change, and the epoch 2 (Milestone 204) did not take it in. 28
  manifests of 21 examples set it by hand.
- `guest.path` (Milestone 348). Without it, the commands that hydo starts have no `PATH`, so a
  program that such a command starts does not find `hydo-oci` by name. Milestone 348 keyed it as
  on from epoch 6 and left the epoch where it was.

The lead's recommendation, accepted for this step, was to turn both on at epoch 6.

**The change.** `hydo_image::EPOCH` is 6. `hydo_image::EpochDefaults` gets `outcomes_after_cut`,
true from epoch 6 on both architectures, and `command_path` was already true from epoch 6. The
host controller's plan keeps the manifest's value of `guest.outcomes_after_cut` as an `Option`
(`Plan::outcomes_after_cut`), as it does for `guest.cgroup2` and `guest.path`.
`agent::plan_of_image` puts in what an absent key means at the image's epoch. Every place that
reads the key reads the plan's value: the outcomes kept at a power cut, the report line at the
cut and at the run's end, and the write into the recovery boot's file. No other crate reads the key. A plan read from a
manifest alone, as the controller's corpora read theirs, keeps the manifest's value, so their
recorded transcripts stay the same.

The project schema keeps `"default": false` for both keys, because `hydo-schema-compat` allows no
change of a released default; the descriptions name the epoch. MANIFEST.md (the commented tour,
"Outcomes after a power cut", "Services from a Docker/OCI image") and the guide topics
`composer`, `invariant-patterns`, `services` and `strategies` say the new defaults.

**The examples that set the key by hand** keep the line, and their bytes, until the pass:
`blnk` (`hydo.yaml`, `hydo-contracts.yaml`, `hydo-paths.yaml`, `hydo-values.yaml`),
`clickhouse`, `dragonfly`, `formance-ledger`, `garage`, `greptimedb`, `hatchet`, `iggy`
(`hydo.yaml`, `hydo-configs.yaml`), `lago`, `meilisearch`, `memos`, `mender` (`hydo.yaml`,
`hydo-devices.yaml`), `rauc`, `restate`, `river`, `saleor`, `surrealdb` (`hydo/hydo.yaml`,
`upgrade/hydo.yaml`), `swupdate` (`hydo.yaml`, `hydo-devices.yaml`), `temporal`, `valkey` and

**What moves.** docs/REBASELINE.md section 30 has the list. Every image built at epoch 6 has new

controller starts carries `PATH`, which is in guest RAM and in the control transcript. Every

**Proof on the Mac engine.** The release's Redis example (`examples/redis` of the installed 0.5.0

The shared cargo target folder of this work was also used by another session from another
