## Milestone 354 (tentative number): the s3 emulator keeps its writes across a power cut

Status: done on 2026-11-24, on the Mac engine. A format-1 addition, opt-in. Nothing recorded
moved, and the fingerprint epoch stays 5.

**The problem.** `emulators:` with `use: s3` runs `rclone serve s3` 1.76.0 over `/data/<name>`.
rclone's local backend writes an object's file and closes it without an `fsync`
(`backend/local/local.go`, `Update`), and no option of the backend makes one. `rclone serve s3`
writes an object under a temporary name and renames it into place before it answers
(`cmd/serve/s3/backend.go`, `PutObject` and `commitObject`). A completed multipart upload is a
rename of the streamed file (`multipart.go`), and a copy is a read and a PUT. So the data and the
renames of every write wait in the guest's page cache and in ext4's journal for the next
writeback. A power cut of the guest then loses objects that the emulator acknowledged. For that
reason the GreptimeDB example of Milestone 343 left `cut` out of its faults (open item 171).

**The way.** Four ways were compared (`docs/design/emulators.md`, "Objects that survive a power
cut"). rclone has no option. A mount option `sync` is a flag of the whole file system, so every
service's writes on the data disk would become synchronous. A sync in hydo's proxy before it
forwards an answer is a change of `hydo-world`, a pinned guest program, so every image built after
its re-pin would get new bytes. The chosen way is one command: ext4's attribute `S` on the
emulator's folders. The entry's new key `durable: true` (a format-1 addition, `false` by default)
ends the service's `setup:` with `&& chattr +S /data/<name> /data/<name>/<bucket> ...`, with
busybox's `chattr`. On a file with the attribute each `write(2)` returns after the data and the
inode are written and the disk's cache is flushed (`generic_write_sync`). In a folder with it each
create, rename, unlink and mkdir commits the journal first (`IS_DIRSYNC`). New files and folders
inherit it. So the temporary file, its rename, and a DELETE's unlink are on the disk before rclone
answers. The validator refuses the key on `stripe` and `smtp`, and it refuses a value that is not
a boolean. Without the key the setup is the one of Milestone 242, so no image changes.

**The proof.** The new example `hydo/onboard/examples/checkout/hydo-s3-cut.yaml` runs s3probe's
new mode `cut-step <n>` in each of 4 steps, through the s3 proxy:

- a PUT of 64 bytes (`o<n>a`) and a PUT of 1 MiB (`o<n>b`);
- a copy of `o<n>a` (`o<n>c`, `x-amz-copy-source`);
- a multipart upload of 5 MiB and 1 KiB, completed (`o<n>m`);
- a DELETE of the round before's `o<n-1>a`.

Each acknowledged write is a word in `$HYDO_ACKED` (`put:o2a`, `copy:o2c`, `mp:o2m`, `del:o1a`),
and then the SDK event `s3.acked`. The check `s3probe cut-check` reads every word from rclone's
own port in the recovery boot: an object has its bytes, and a deleted key answers 404. The same
file with `durable: false` is the image without the change. The runs used the Mac engine, the
hydo of this tree, and the engine and guest files of the 0.5.0 release. Each schedule ran twice
on each image, and each pair gave one fingerprint:

| Schedule | `durable: false` | `durable: true` |
|---|---|---|
| `disk=none \| run` | OK, 19 writes, `f34d92e89cce6a1d` | OK, 19 writes, `af9757495fc433ff` |
| `disk=cut \| run C=3` | VIOLATION, 10 of 14 writes lost, `6d19b0e30e92a637` | OK, 14 writes, `913ad97e4f50437a` |
| `disk=cut \| run C=4` | VIOLATION, 13 of 19 lost, `d06d02e14d31d4ef` | OK, 19 writes, `a49afd22824e9090` |
| `disk=cut \| run A=s3.acked@2+5:cut` | VIOLATION, 10 of 12 lost, `687f41f069d3399c` | OK, 10 writes, `a2c42221aa293e9d` |
| `disk=cut \| run A=s3.acked@3:cut` | VIOLATION, 11 of 15 lost, `4053f698800d2958` | OK, 15 writes, `db6a871eaa8c0fa1` |

Without the attribute every lost object answered 404 in the recovery boot. Its rename never
reached the disk. At `C=3` the run lost ten writes. They were the three of step 0 and of step 1
that no DELETE removed, and the four objects of step 2. The reaction `A=s3.acked@2+5:cut` cuts
5 ms of guest time after the first acknowledged write of step 2. Before that cut the run with the
attribute acknowledged 10 writes, and the run without it 12, because each write takes longer
with it. The run without faults made 6,070 engine stops with the attribute and 841 without it.
It took 1.9 s of the engine against 1.0 s.

The DELETE is judged only together with its object: in the runs without the attribute each
deleted object was lost with its create, so a lost unlink did not show. In the runs with the
attribute every deleted key answered 404 after the cut.

**Tests.** `emulators::a_durable_s3_emulator_marks_its_folders_synchronous` checks the setup, that
nothing else of the expansion changes, and the two refusals. The project schema has the key
(`HYDO_BLESS=1 cargo test -p hydo-manifest --test it format::`). The explorer's corpus and identity
goldens and the controller's corpus golden are re-recorded with the new example. The recorded
answer of `hydo guide manifest` is re-recorded with the new text. hydo-manifest's equivalence
corpus gains four mismatches: mutants with an unknown key on an emulator entry. Their message
lists the known keys, which the recorded answers do not have.

**What is left.**

- hvx and KVM did not run the example. The attribute is a property of the guest kernel's ext4,
  the same on every engine. The x86_64 busybox 1.37.0 of the 0.5.0 Linux release has `chattr`
  (its `chattr_main`).
- A multipart upload that is not completed is still lost at a cut: rclone keeps the upload's
  record in memory. So is the user metadata that rclone keeps in memory. No run tested either.
- `durable` stays opt-in. It could be the default of the next fingerprint epoch, keyed on the
  image's epoch as `guest.path` is (Milestone 348).
- GreptimeDB's example did not run again with `durable: true` and `cut` (open item 171).

## Milestone 355 (tentative number): seven gaps of the Kvrocks onboarding

Status: done on 2026-11-25, on the Mac engine and on this Mac's copies of seven projects'
sources. The Kvrocks onboarding (Milestone 351, on its own branch) named what hydo lacked in the
section "What hydo lacked" of its RESULTS.md. Each fix below is its own commit. Two are format-1
additions: the build parameters of a regression, and the reaction `powerloss-<svc>`. One is a
results addition: `unfired_reactions` of an exploration's summary. Nothing recorded moved, and
the fingerprint epoch stays 6.

**1. A reaction that never fires says so.** In the onboarding, three schedules of
`A=kvrocks.failover_done+...:cut` passed, and nothing said that no failover had run, so no cut
came. The explorer warned only when no record of the run named the event at all
(`results::unseen_events`, a misspelt id). Now, at the end of the workload's steps, the
controller writes one note for each reaction that did not act:
`HYDO-REACT-UNFIRED {"token":..,"event":..,"nth":k,"at":step,"armed":bool,"seen":n,"cut":bool}`.
`seen` counts the records of the event after the reaction was armed, from the count of records
that the main sequence keeps when it arms the reaction. A note is for people: no control
transcript's hash and no fingerprint covers it, as for `HYDO-CHECK-OUT`.
`results::unfired_reactions` turns each note into a warning of the run, such as `the reaction
A=client.step3_acked@10:kill-redis never fired: no record of its event client.step3_acked came
after it was armed before step 10; the run did not test it`. Other forms name the k-th record
that a reaction waits for, a power cut that ended the steps first, and a step that the run never
reached. The warning is in `result.json`, `hydo run` prints it, and `hydo report <run dir>` shows
it under "What hydo saw". An exploration counts its first runs with such a warning in
`unfired_reactions` of its summary (a results addition; `hydo explore --merge` adds the parts'
counts). It prints the count with one example, and `hydo report`, `report.md` and the web page
name it. These runs no longer count as vacuous passes, also the ones that `unseen_events` names.

On the Mac engine, a Redis project with an event at step 3 (the proof project below) ran
`disk=none | run A=client.step3_acked@10:kill-redis`: OK, with the warning above in the output of
`hydo run`, in `result.json` and in `hydo report`. The aimed exploration `--reactive-at
client.step3_acked@10 --react-delays 0..1 --react-actions kill --seeds 1-3` printed `in 3 of 3
first runs a reaction never fired`, and `exploration.json` has `unfired_reactions: 3`. In the
controller's test of a reaction that never fires, the run's records are those of the run without
the reaction, apart from the declaration and the note. The controller's corpus and identity
goldens did not move.

**2. What `--seeds` means with `--reactive-at`.** `--seeds 1-3` ran the grid's first three cells,
and the guide read as if it ran the grid three times. Milestone 345 defined it: seed `n` is cell
`n - 1`, seeds past the grid run it again with each seed's composition, and the options alone fix
the order of the cells, so seed `n` names the same schedule in every exploration of the same
options, also in shards and with `--time-limit`. That is the right meaning, because a seed is one
schedule everywhere else, and a shard splits seeds. So the code keeps it, and the words now say it
exactly: `hydo guide faults`, MANIFEST.md, `hydo explore --help`, and the explorer's first lines
(`Seed k runs cell k of the grid: seeds 1-153 run it once with the plain workload, and seeds
154-306 run it again with each seed's composition`). Seeds that are not whole rounds of the grid
get one more line, for example `--seeds 1-3 runs cells 1 to 3 of the grid's 153, one cell per
seed. To run the whole grid once, give --seeds 1-153; three times, --seeds 1-459.`
(`aim::seeds_words`).

**3. The clock audit follows a project's own wrapper of the clock in C++.** The audit named no
function in Kvrocks 2.17.0's 255 source files. Kvrocks reads the clock through
`util::GetTimeStamp` (`src/common/time_util.h`), a template that returns
`std::chrono::duration_cast<Duration>(std::chrono::system_clock::now().time_since_epoch()).count()`,
and `GetTimeStampMS()`, which calls `GetTimeStamp<std::chrono::milliseconds>()`. The audit already
followed a small function with a name about time that returns a reading, in every language it
reads, and through as many levels as the functions call each other. It missed these for three
reasons of C++ text. In C and C++ files a reading now starts at its namespaces, a call with
template arguments is a call, and a cast of one reading (`duration_cast<...>(`,
`time_point_cast<...>(`, `static_cast<...>(`) keeps it a reading unless its argument is a
difference. A function that returns a reading is no limit any more.

With the example's `hydo.yaml` the audit names 22 functions in Kvrocks. The fourth is the place
of finding 2, `src/cluster/replication.cc` line 670 in `sendReplConfAck` (lines 666 to 682):
`if (force || (now - last_ack_time_secs_) >= 1)`, `high`, with `now` traced to
`util::GetTimeStamp()` and `system_clock::now()`. The JSON and text reports of the clock audit on
Valkey 9.1.3, Temporal 1.32.2, River v0.51.2 and Garage v2.5.0, each with its example's
`hydo.yaml`, are byte for byte those of the binary before the change, so their known places keep
their ranks.

**4. The scan of write routes reads command tables.** `hydo rules scan --kind writes` read one
file of Kvrocks and found no route: the commands of a Redis-compatible server are a table in C or
C++. The scan reads such tables now (`writescan::command_entries`), by their shape. An entry is a
call or an initializer whose first argument names a command, with an integer arity and an
argument that flags it: a string of flag words (`"write"`, `"read-only"`) or flag constants
joined with `|` (`CMD_WRITE`, `CO::WRITE`). A file with three entries or more is a table, and
only such a C or C++ file counts among the files read. Each write entry is a route `CMD <NAME>`.
Its handler is the class of the call's template argument, a function argument named for a
command, or the argument of `.HFUNC(...)`. Its resource is the entry's group, or the stem of the
table's file without `cmd_` or `t_`.

On Kvrocks 2.17.0 the scan reads 21 files and lists 142 write commands in 18 resources, 137
`data` and 5 `admin`, each with the class and the line of its handler. That is every entry of its
tables flagged `write`; the hand count of 143 had a commented-out entry of the Cuckoo filter too.
On Valkey 9.1.3 it lists the 118 commands of `src/commands.def` with `CMD_WRITE`. The JSON and
text reports of Meilisearch v1.57.0, Iggy server-0.10.0, Prometheus v3.16.0, GreptimeDB v1.3.1,
Hatchet v0.120.5, Memos 26.11.0 and Garage v2.5.0 are byte for byte those before the change.

**5. The diagnosis of a failed restart after one service's power loss quotes the service's log.**
For `ERROR kv2 restart failed (after its power loss)` the `hydo: diagnosis:` line named only the
error. `verdict_service` read `ERROR <svc> restart failed` but not the reason in parentheses that
the restart of a storage fault adds. So the diagnosis did not know the service, read no log of it
first, and quoted nothing. It reads the form now, and the summary says `while it was restarted
after its power loss`. On the Mac engine, the proof project built with `--set refuse=yes` (its
service refuses a second start, as a node whose files a power loss damaged does) gave:

- `disk=none | run L=redis@5+2`: `ERROR redis restart failed (after its power loss)`, and
  `hydo: diagnosis: redis exited while it was restarted after its power loss, before its
  readiness check passed (exit status 1); its log ends: Failed to open the database: Corruption:
  the marker of an earlier start is there`;
- `disk=cut | run C=5`: `VIOLATION service cannot recover (committed data unrecoverable)
  (redis)`, with the same quote from the recovery boot, as before.

**6. A saved regression names the build parameters it needs.** Finding 2 of Kvrocks needed the
client's other mode, first built as a parameter, and became a token so that one image carries
all three regressions. A regression file may now have a line `# params: <name>=<value> ...`, and a
`test.regressions` entry the key `params:` (format-1 additions). `hydo build` refuses a name that
`params:` does not declare. When the build has other values, it warns and names the `hydo build
--set ...` that makes the image of the regression. `hydo repro --regressions` (and `hydo ci run`)
replays such a regression only on an image whose `/etc/hydo/params` has its values. On another
image it prints `SKIP` with the build command and counts it apart. A file without the line reads
as before, and its entry in `<image>.regressions.json` has no new key. The regressions stay out of
the image, so the image's bytes do not change with the line. On the Mac engine the proof project
had two regressions, `plain` and one with `# params: refuse=yes` and `# expect:
fp=8b08a99152bfdfbf`:

- `hydo build`: the warning, and the image's sha256 the same as before the regressions were added
  (`c7a4263a…`, the disk `887eb24e…`);
- `hydo repro --regressions` on that image: `PASS plain`, `SKIP restart-refused-after-a-power-loss
  ... it needs the build parameters refuse=yes (this image: refuse=no)`, and `1 of 1 regressions as
  expected, 1 left out`;
- on the image of `--set refuse=yes`: both PASS, the second with its recorded fingerprint;
- a line `# params: nosuch=1`: `hydo build --check` stops with `# params: names nosuch, which
  params: does not declare (params: refuse)`.

**7. A reaction cuts the power of one service.** A reaction could cut the whole guest, kill or
stop a service, but not take one node's power, and finding 1 with one node's power loss came only
from blind `L=` schedules. The action `powerloss-<svc>` (`A=<event>[#<k>][@<step>][+<ms>]:
powerloss-<svc>`) does at the reaction point what `L=<svc>@<step>+<down>` does before a step: the
service stops, its own file system shuts down and is mounted again, and the service stays down
until the heal's restart pass, as after `kill-<svc>`. The name follows the fault kind `powerloss`
of `faults:`. The service needs `storage: {dir:, size_mib:}`, and the controller's check of names
refuses the action otherwise. The run reports the record of `L=`. `--react-actions powerloss`
names one action per service with `storage:`, and the explorer keeps the action where `faults:`
allows `powerloss`. It runs on the engines where `L=` runs, because it is the same controller
code. On the Mac engine `disk=none | run A=client.step3_acked+50:powerloss-redis` logged `POWER
LOSS of redis at the reaction A=client.step3_acked+50:powerloss-redis (/dev/vda5 shut down and
mounted again ...)`, restarted Redis at the heal, and passed; `hydo repro` gave its fingerprint
`7f93836fa6c29e4b` again. `--reactive-at client.step3_acked --react-actions powerloss` ran its
grid of two cells.

**The proof project.** The Redis example of the installed 0.5.0 release, copied into the scratch
folder, with `storage: {dir: redis, size_mib: 96}` on its service, `powerloss` in `faults:`, a
console record `client.step3_acked` after the acknowledged write of step 3, and a build parameter
`refuse` that makes the service refuse its second start. It ran with this tree's `hydo`,
`hydo-build` and `hydo-hvm` beside the release's guest files, under the shared Mac VM lock.

**Tests.** The controller's `react::a_reaction_that_never_fires_is_inert` checks the note and
that nothing else changes, and
`storage::a_reactions_power_loss_shuts_the_file_system_down_at_the_event` checks the power loss at
the event. `results::a_reaction_that_never_fired_is_named`,
`aim::seeds_that_are_not_whole_rounds_say_what_they_run`,
`clockscan::cpp_follows_a_projects_own_wrapper_of_the_wall_clock`,
`writescan::command_tables_list_their_write_commands`,
`diagnose::a_failed_restart_after_a_power_loss_quotes_the_service_log`,
`runs::a_regression_of_other_build_parameters_names_its_image` and
`composer::a_regression_file_names_its_build_parameters` check the other parts. The results and
project schemas are re-recorded with the new fields (`HYDO_BLESS=1`), and so is the recorded
answer of `hydo guide manifest` in the CLI's golden, with the new text of MANIFEST.md. The
`hydo` tests `onboard::the_fetch_step_names_the_release_fetcher_when_it_is_not_on_path` and
`update::a_checkout_build_is_left_alone_with_the_commands` fail with a target folder outside the
checkout, as every build of this worktree has; they do not touch these parts.

**What is left.** Open item 180.

## Milestone 356 (tentative number): Apache Pulsar, its transactions, and a timeout on the wall clock

The onboarding of Apache Pulsar 5.0.1 (2026-10-26, the newest release, with BookKeeper 4.18.1 and
ZooKeeper 3.9.6) on hvx, 2026-11-25, by `docs/ONBOARDING-PLAYBOOK.md`, with this tree's hydo
(0.5.0 and Milestones 340 to 354, the fingerprint epoch 6) in a copy of the 0.5.0 Linux release's
guest files. The example is `hydo/onboard/examples/pulsar`; its RESULTS.md has the evidence. One
known bug of the official Go client and one new clock effect of the transaction coordinator.
Nothing was posted. Nothing recorded moved.

**The example.** `hydo/onboard/examples/pulsar` (RESULTS.md) runs production's shape as Pulsar's
own multi-node Compose file (`docker-compose/kitchen-sink`) deploys it: three ZooKeeper servers,
three bookies and two brokers, each JVM with a small heap, the serial collector and the first JIT
tier, in one hvx guest of 5,120 MiB. `hydo compose` imported the example's Compose file. Each
ZooKeeper server's data and each bookie's journal and ledgers are on a file system of their own;
the configuration is the image's own files with the keys of `conf/` set (`conf/pconf.sh`):
ensemble 3, write quorum 3, ack quorum 2, `journalSyncData=true`, deduplication and transactions
on, and ledgers that roll over after 100 entries. The build parameters `ackquorum`, `jsync` and
`client` choose the settings and the client. The client `pulsarc` (`client/main.go`, on
pulsar-client-go) produces two messages per command with explicit sequence ids and sends a
message again after its process ended, consumes a shared subscription and a failover one with
the broker's receipts, unloads partitions through the admin API, and runs transactions with a
message acknowledged inside; 1 transaction in 8 is left open, as a crashed client does. A
`type: messages` check (no loss, one stored copy, every subscription), a second one for each
key's order on the failover subscription, a final check that each transaction is all or
nothing, and an `eventually_` check that no partition keeps an open transaction after the heal
judge it. Two clean runs on the final image (`16f3c0f9…`) give one fingerprint, `811b19bbb54fcf71`.

**Finding 1, known.** With pulsar-client-go v0.21.0 every message of an aborted transaction is
delivered. The client puts the transaction's id into `CommandSend` only
(`pulsar/internal/batch_builder.go` lines 233 to 236, `commands.go` lines 357 to 360), and the
broker's dispatcher drops an aborted message by the id in its metadata
(`AbstractBaseDispatcher.java` lines 188 to 209). It broke the first run without faults.
pulsar-client-go#1498 names it, and pull request 1499 (approved, open) fixes it; the example
builds its default client from that pull request's head (`client/go.fix.mod`). With
`--set client=release`, `disk=none | run` fails on every run (`fp=8cf005d04d8a1961`).

**Finding 2, new, a clock effect.** The coordinator times a transaction out on the wall clock:
`TransactionTimeoutTrackerImpl` reads `Clock.systemUTC()` (line 55) for the deadline and for the
check (lines 65, 112 to 119). After a step back inside the timeout of a transaction that its
client left open, the transaction stays open for the step's length, and its partitions hold back
every later message for every subscription (`TopicTransactionBuffer`'s max read position).
`disk=none | run T=32:-600` left 18 acknowledged messages undelivered and showed a committed
transaction with one of its two messages; on the final image it breaks the open-transaction
check (`fp=bcfa5492766b3941`). A step before the transaction began or after its timeout
passes. Blind at e1's seed 4 (a step back of 30 days) and in two schedules of e2.

**Finding 3, new.** A broker opens a transaction coordinator's store and starts its timeouts only
when a client connects to that coordinator (`TransactionMetadataStoreService.handleTcClientConnect`,
lines 109 to 145, from `ServerCnx.handleTcClientConnectRequest`). After a power cut of the whole
guest the recovery boot runs no transactional client, so a transaction that a crashed client
left open before the cut is never aborted, and its partitions deliver nothing after it: a
committed transaction showed one of its two messages. `coordinatorStats` answered 500 on both
brokers; one transactional client in that state loaded the coordinators and the transaction was
aborted at once. `disk=cut dseed=0 | run C=16 W=adbbc231,p4,q1,r500` gave a committed transaction with one of
its two messages; on the final image `disk=cut | run C=34` breaks the open-transaction check
twice (`fp=0aa2f73c75dcea55`). Blind as e3's
seeds 51 and 52 and e2's problem 4, with and without its clock step.

A later check for the upstream report found why `C=34` gave `no partition's transaction buffer
answered`. In that recovery boot bookie2's AutoRecovery stopped on a `BadVersionException` of an
under-replication znode, BookKeeper ended the bookie with exit status 0, and `restart:
on-failure` left it down; with two bookies no ledger of ensemble 3 could be created. The saved
regression is `disk=cut | run C=35` now (`fp=c26c630a0f1df04e` twice, once from a fresh checkout
of `3bac22f8`). All bookies run, two partitions hold back behind the open transaction `(1,11)`,
the acknowledged `m57.1` is never delivered, and the committed `x59` delivers neither message. In a
`hydo inspect` session `coordinatorStats` answered `Transaction coordinator not found!` until one
transactional client loaded the coordinators, which aborted `(1,11)` at once. The cuts before
steps 30 and 32 fail the same way.

**By design and the environment.** An acknowledgement with the broker's receipt can come back
after a broker crashes: the broker writes a subscription's position at most once a second
(`ManagedCursorImpl`, the mark-delete rate limit) and the Java client's `isAckReceiptEnabled`
documentation says so; `after_ack: no-redelivery` broke at the first power cut on a copy of the
manifest (`fp=42acd95fa46b424f`), and the check claims `after_ack: allowed`. A damaged file of a
ZooKeeper server (six schedules) or 32 flipped bits of a bookie's file (one) stop that server at
every start.

**What held.** No acknowledged publish was lost, deduplication stored every message once, and
the failover subscription kept each key's order, through kills, pauses past ZooKeeper's session
timeout, partitions and one-way loss of nodes and groups, one node's power loss or damaged
files, power cuts at steps and at disk flushes, 15 power cuts aimed 0 to 40 ms after an
acknowledged send, an acknowledgement or a transaction's end, and the clock steps that came
near no open transaction. `journalSyncData=false` lost nothing in three power cuts, also 5 ms
after an acknowledged send; why was not traced.

**Explorations.** 84 blind schedules on one worker of 5,120 MiB, on the images before the
final check: e1 (process, cluster faults, seeds 1-5, stopped in its shrink of finding 2), e2
(process with cluster, storage and more faults, seeds 6-40), cf1 (`--configs --configs-mode
one`, its default combination only, stopped), e4 (`--reactive-at` power cuts 0 to 40 ms after
three events, 15 schedules, none failed), e3 (swarm with new faults, seeds 46-56, stopped by a
memory guard), and e5 (seeds 76-87, three failures of the first version of the open-transaction
check). About 50 directed runs separated the faults and checked the settings.

**hydo.** No code of hydo changed. The guide's strategies have the Pulsar evidence in five
entries and the first table. `docs/USE-CASES.md` names the transaction checks under
"Transactions across messages". The new example enters the explorer's and the controller's
corpora: their goldens are re-recorded with `HYDO_BLESS=1` in a copy of the tree without git on
the bare-metal machine, and checked there.

Retro: Apache Pulsar 5.0.1, hvx, 2026-11-25
- Time to the first clean run: 1 hour 10 minutes of wall time (scouting 30 minutes, the build
  of this tree's hydo on the bare-metal machine 5 minutes, the import and the folder 35 minutes);
  the first run without faults found finding 1.
- Schedules run before the first finding: none; finding 1 broke the first run without faults.
  Finding 2 came from reading the coordinator after the clock audit, then blind at e1's seed 4.
  Finding 3 came blind in e2 and e3. No failure was a mistake of the rules after the console
  records were made short.
- The findings: 2 new (the coordinator after a restart; the timeout on the wall clock, a clock
  effect), 1 known (the Go client's aborted messages), 1 by design (acknowledgements after a
  broker crash), and the environment (damaged files of ZooKeeper and of one bookie).
- What took the most time: hvx's 64 KiB of console, which cut the first records off without a
  warning (40 minutes); the shrinks of clock steps and the explorations' memory on the shared
  machine (about an hour of stopped or wasted runs); finding 3's cause, which needed three
  inspections of the end state (40 minutes).
- What hydo lacked: no warning when the console passes 64 KiB on hvx; a claim cannot be a
  build parameter for `hydo explore`; `kill-workload/` does not reach a composed workload; one
  operation per process also when the history is the only reason; the write-route scan sees
  no binary protocol. Open item 181.
- Strategies: "How each unknown outcome ends" (a client that leaves transactions open, and the
  check that each one ends), "Clock steps and the clock audit" (finding 2), "Power cuts of the
  whole guest" (finding 3), and "The messages check's claims" (`after_ack` by design, and the
  order claim on a failover subscription) are updated, and the first table names Pulsar.

**What is left.** Open item 181.

## Milestone 357 (tentative number): a ClickHouse mutation of a dropped column after a power cut

Status: done on 2026-11-25. Nothing recorded moved, and the fingerprint epoch stays 6.

A candidate from an automated onboarding of ClickHouse v26.10.6.18 on one server, verified by hand
on hvx and reduced to the variant `hydo/onboard/examples/clickhouse/single/` (RESULTS.md, section
"One server: a mutation of a dropped column after a power cut"). A table syncs its inserted parts;
the workload adds a column, inserts, modifies the column, drops it, and updates the row.
`disk=none | run` passes. `disk=cut | run C=6` fails twice with `fp=b1992b2c7f5ea453` (hydo 0.5.0,
an image built at epoch 5): the `MODIFY COLUMN`, the `DROP COLUMN` and the `ALTER UPDATE` stay not
done with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`, because the mutated parts were never synced, came back with their
mutations unfinished, and the table's metadata no longer has the column. With `--set
merge_fsync=1` the same cut passes. A kill in Docker with the mutated parts removed gave the same
stuck queue, and `KILL MUTATION` freed it. The cause is in `MutateTask.cpp` (`splitAndModifyMutationCommands`
keeps a column the table no longer has) and `MutationsInterpreter.cpp`; the closest report,
#120975, is closed with a fix of a test only. The example's RESULTS.md has the duplicate search.

**What is left.** Open item 157. The variant ran on hvx only, with hydo 0.5.0.
## The 0.6.0 re-recording pass

Status: done on 2026-11-25 on hvx, KVM, and the Mac. No milestone number. The pass
re-records the values of `hydo/onboard/recorded.json` at the fingerprint epoch 6 of Milestone
353, under the rule "Re-recording runs in batches" (AGENTS.md). It raises no version, builds no
release, and publishes nothing. docs/REBASELINE.md section 31 has every value and decision.

**How it ran.** `hydo-bench rebaseline` ran this tree's programs over the guest files of the
published 0.5.0 Linux release (`2b5d45fd…`, unpacked under umask 022 and set up with `hydo
setup`). No guest kernel and no pinned guest program changed since 0.5.0. The order services of
the stack images came from the repository's commits `d26ed1d` and `0112b48` as archives
(`HYDO_STACK_SRC`). The Qdrant example's two test programs were the pinned ones of an earlier
pass's inputs, checked by sha256. Every VM went through `~/bin/hvx-run`, and the module stayed
`91D86B693F4D4035C368F9B`.

**hvx.** A first `--check` (6,968 s) built every image once and ran every schedule; each run
whose values moved ran a second time from a fresh boot. All 141 runs moved, each run gave one
result twice, and four verdicts changed. After the decisions below, `--write --thorough
--accept-verdicts` (9,398 s) built all 43 images twice with the same bytes and ran all 141
schedules twice from fresh boots with the same values. Every fingerprint and every `ctl` value
moved, because each command that the controller starts carries `PATH`.

| Verdict change | Decision |
|---|---|
| `hvx/stack-errors-fix` `disk=ioerr:5 dseed=1 \| run`: the failed restart is mysql's, not redis's | accepted: the same class, as at epoch 4 |
| `hvx/nats-flaky-buggy` `q=18813` on 2 vCPUs fails | the turn sweep's boundary `q=18407` (OK) and `q=18496` (VIOLATION) replaces `q=18813` and `q=18870`; the fixed test passes at `q=18496` |
| `hvx/etcd-3.5.5` `disk=cut dseed=1 \| run C=20` passes | `C=21` gives the first symptom of etcd issue 14685 and replaces it for both releases |
| `hvx/etcd-hc-3.5.5` `K=etcd1@10+1 P=etcd3@26+1`: the history check holds | `K=etcd2@25+1 P=etcd1@27+1`, the plain image's schedule of the second symptom, breaks it; it replaces the schedule for both releases |

The searches ran one VM at a time on the pass's images. They were the default turn sweep of the
nats image (25 runs and 4 repetitions) and 46 etcd schedules. The RESULTS.md pages of the two
examples list their results. 48 recorded hvx runs cut the whole guest's power, and their recovery boots
now get the first boot's outcomes. Only etcd's `C=20` changed its class among them. Its check
compares the members' revisions and reads no outcome, and the cuts before steps 21 and 22 still
break it, so the timing moved its window. Three other verdict lines of power cuts differ in their
words and keep their class: miniflux's `C=20 S=off`, the composed Redis history's `C=12
R=everysec`, and etcd 3.5.6's `C=21`.

**The pinned reproducers.** The epoch-6 images, the list's `stack-old` and `stack-fix`, are kept
in `~/hydo/build/rel060`: `disk=none dseed=4d5cb825dfaab05b | run K=redis@11+1 C=24` gives
`db33d71069816103` (VIOLATION, order 11) and `c421af1ccb714225` (OK). With the pass's programs
the epoch-2, epoch-4 and epoch-5 images in `~/hydo/build/m204`, `m302` and `rel050` gave their
recorded values: `a76d7fe857fdb37c`, `efbde7b57264be0f`, `e153f376096a072c`,
`6a5c2fe208174af3`, `b6e78273b1d21304` and `b531d6bcaa8489b7`. So the epoch-6 defaults reach no
image built before.

**The goldens and the tests.** In full mode on the bare-metal machine, hydo-explore's `it`
passed 59 of 60 tests, its `fake_engine` 31 of 31, and hydo-control's `it` 120 of 120. The
corpus and identity goldens needed no new recording. The one failure,
`identity::local_outputs_are_no_inputs`, needs a git checkout, and the tree there was an archive.
`hydo`'s `docs::`, hydo-bench's `recorded::` and hydo-control's `silent::` pass with the new list.
The quickstarts still cite the values of the published 0.5.0 release. So `tests/docs.rs` names

of hvx, six of KVM and of the images, and four of the Mac.
0.6.0's release step 6a moves the pages to the epoch-6 values and removes the entries.

**KVM.** The bare-metal machine never runs KVM, so the one-off workflow
`.github/workflows/tmp-rel060-kvm.yml` ran on GitHub's runners (branch `tmp-rel060-kvm`, run
45517605164, with the published 0.5.0 release's guest files and this tree's programs). Six jobs

## Milestone 358 (tentative number): the features of `main` since 0.5.0 on hvx and KVM

Status: done on 2026-11-25 on hvx and KVM. One fix, of the hvx engine that a checkout's hydo
starts. Nothing recorded moved, and the fingerprint epoch stays 6.

Milestones 345 to 355 ran on the Mac engine, and Milestone 352 ran 345, 346 and 348 on KVM. This
milestone runs them on hvx and on KVM, as Milestone 341 did for 0.5.0. It records what held and
fixes what was wrong.

### How the runs were made

- hvx: the bare-metal machine, in a tree of its own made from `main` at `d1931461`. The tree's
  `hydo`, `hydo-hvx`, `hydo-build`, `hydo-compose` and `hydo-fetch-image` ran over the guest
  files of the published 0.5.0 Linux release (`2b5d45fd…`, through `HYDO_RELEASE_DIR`). Every
  VM ran through `hvx-run` under umask 022, one at a time, with one explorer worker. The module
  stayed `91D86B693F4D4035C368F9B`.
- KVM: the workflow `.github/workflows/tmp-m358-kvm.yml` on the branch `tmp-m358-kvm` (commits
  `f12dd2db` and `d524d18a`, on `d1931461`), run 45612798752 on GitHub's runners. Eight jobs ran
  four parts, `redis`, `oci`, `s3` and `meili`, on two hosts each. Each job built the branch's
  `hydo` and took the 0.5.0 release's guest files and its `examples/redis`.
- One script, `.github/workflows/tmp-m358-kvm.sh` on that branch, makes the projects and runs
  each schedule twice on both engines. A pair with two fingerprints, or a run without a result,
  fails its part. The Go programs were built on this Mac for hvx; the jobs build them with the
  runner's Go.

Three projects were made for the proofs, beside the examples:

- `r355`: the 0.5.0 release's Redis quickstart with `storage: {dir: redis, size_mib: 96}`,
  `powerloss` in `faults:`, a record `client.step3_acked` after the acknowledged write of step 3,
  and a build parameter `refuse`. With `refuse=yes` the service refuses its second start, as a
  node whose files a power loss damaged does. A second check, `env.path`, fails when a command
  that hydo starts has no `PATH`. Its regressions are `plain` (`disk=none | run`, `expect: ok`)
  and `restart-refused-after-a-cut` (`# params: refuse=yes`, `expect: violation`, `disk=cut |
  run C=5`). It is Milestone 355's proof project, written again.
- `redis-oci-path`: `redis-oci/hydo-sys.yaml` with a Go program, `pathprobe`, and the check
  `oci.path_by_name`. The program runs `exec.Command("hydo-oci", "redis", "redis-cli",
  "ping")`, the call that failed in the Prometheus client (open item 170).
- `lines`: one service that writes 400,000 error lines of 87 bytes to its log, with `errors:
  true`.

### The fix: a checkout's hydo ran the hvx engine of another version

On the bare-metal machine `hydo` cannot open `/dev/hvx` itself, so it starts the engine as a
program under sudo. A hydo built in a checkout took that program from its root. That root is the
install cache or the release tree of `HYDO_RELEASE_DIR`, so this tree's hydo ran the 0.5.0
release's `hydo-hvx` with this tree's host controller, and said nothing. The first round of hvx
runs (redis, oci and s3) had that pair. The `lines` project showed it. With the 0.5.0 engine its
run waited 900.2 s for the wall limit and ended `TIMEOUT check`; Milestone 348's engine ends it
at once (the section on the agent lines below).

Commit `192af3fc` makes such a hydo take the `hydo-hvx` in its own folder when there is one
(`hvxenv::engine`). `HYDO_HVX_EXPLORE` still decides first, and a release or a cargo install
keeps its engine. The unit test is
`hvxenv::tests::a_checkout_build_takes_the_engine_built_next_to_it`. The build, the test and
clippy ran on the bare-metal machine. In a tree with the fix and without `HYDO_HVX_EXPLORE`, the
process list showed the tree's `target/release/hydo-hvx` under sudo. `lines` then ended `ERROR
agent lines full check` in 27 s, twice, and the Redis quickstart gave `2f5a6dc34e0c8ba6` twice.

Every later hvx run used the tree's engine, named by `HYDO_HVX_EXPLORE`. The only engine changes
since 0.5.0 are Milestone 340's snapshots of shrinks, which are off on hvx, and Milestone 348's
end of a full buffer. So the second round of the redis and oci parts gave every fingerprint and
`ctl` value of the first round again, and the s3 part every one of the schedules that both
rounds ran.

### The fingerprint epoch 6 (Milestone 353)

The quickstart's Redis built at epoch 6 is `8fae6946…`, the image of `hvx/release-redis` in
`hydo/onboard/recorded.json`, with `"epoch": 6` in its record. Each schedule gave one
fingerprint twice:

- `disk=none | run`: OK, `acked=20`, `2f5a6dc34e0c8ba6` (`ctl` `21f6fe353462b188`);
- `disk=cut | run C=12`: OK, `acked=12`, `47ae607ed0a15c48` (`ctl` `b8dfb4051945f4ab`).

These are the list's hvx values. The first boot's transcript ends with `hydo-explore-outcomes:
0=ack 1=ack ... 11=ack`. The recovery boot's control transcript has one write of
`/tmp/hydo/outcomes` with the lines `0 ack` to `11 ack`, before it starts Redis. Every command
of both boots carries `PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin`.

### `guest.path` and a Go program (Milestone 348)

`redis-oci-path` (`afe58cd8…` on hvx, with the image file `2a18d78d…` that `hydo-fetch-image`
saved) held its three checks. `pathprobe` printed `found /bin/hydo-oci with
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin; redis-cli ping answered
"PONG\n"` in every run. `disk=none | run` gave `c1971f9ae985a430`, and `disk=none | run
K=redis@5+2` gave `3e8696991ebfb915` (`acked=18`), each twice. In `r355` the check `env.path`
held in every run.

### The note of a reaction that never fired, `powerloss-<svc>`, and `# params:` (Milestone 355)

The images of `r355` are `5bee04f5…` (`refuse=no`) and `78c48827…` (`refuse=yes`). Each schedule
gave one fingerprint twice on hvx:

| Schedule | Verdict | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| `disk=none \| run` | OK, `acked=20` | `6bb7610d40759e15` |
| `disk=none \| run A=client.step3_acked@10:kill-redis` | OK, with the warning below | `f51e7e953de9f23f` |
| `disk=none \| run A=client.step3_acked+50:kill-redis` | OK, `acked=7`, no warning | `b4f974f433df1729` |
| `disk=none \| run A=client.step3_acked+50:powerloss-redis` | OK, `acked=7` | `f6b2b78e5af5b2e5` |
| `disk=none \| run L=redis@5+2` (`refuse=yes`) | `ERROR redis restart failed (after its power loss)` | `371fe35ee1ff1fc8` |

- The warning reads `the reaction A=client.step3_acked@10:kill-redis never fired: no record of
  its event client.step3_acked came after it was armed before step 10; the run did not test it`.
  It is in `hydo run`'s output, in `result.json` and in `hydo report`. The reaction that fired
  has none. The run with the reaction that never fired has another fingerprint than the run
  without it, because the reaction's step 10 splits the workload's calls there.
- `hydo explore --reactive-at client.step3_acked@10 --react-delays 0..1 --react-actions kill
  --seeds 1-3` printed `in 3 of 3 first runs a reaction never fired`, and its summary has
  `unfired_reactions: 3`. Seed 3 is the second round's first cell. Without a composition its
  schedule is seed 1's, so the exploration took seed 1's result.
- The power loss logged `hydo-ob: POWER LOSS of redis at the reaction
  A=client.step3_acked+50:powerloss-redis (/dev/vda5 shut down and mounted again; what was not
  written back is lost)`, and Redis started again at the heal. `--reactive-at client.step3_acked
  --react-delays 0,50 --react-actions powerloss` ran its two cells, `A=client.step3_acked:powerloss-redis`
  and `+50`, and both held.
- The diagnosis after one service's power loss read `redis exited while it was restarted after
  its power loss, before its readiness check passed (exit status 1); its log ends: Failed to open
  the database: Corruption: the marker of an earlier start is there`.
- `hydo build` of `refuse=no` warned that `restart-refused-after-a-cut needs the build parameters
  refuse=yes`, and named `hydo build --set refuse=yes`. `hydo repro --regressions` on that image
  gave `PASS plain` and `SKIP restart-refused-after-a-cut`, and `1 of 1 regressions as expected,
  1 left out`, with the exit status 0. On the image of `refuse=yes` it gave `PASS plain`
  (`a1fdf35589f7d060`) and `PASS restart-refused-after-a-cut` (`5afcf6fef935b54d`), `2 of 2`.
  `<image>.regressions.json` names the parameters for the second regression only.

### `ERROR agent lines full` on hvx (Milestone 348)

In `lines` the error-log scan reads the service's log of 35 MB through the agent. With the tree's
engine, `disk=none | run` ended in 35 s and 32 s with `ERROR agent lines full check: the agent
wrote more than 16 MiB of lines in this boot, which the hvx engine does not keep; the error-log
scan of large service logs (errors:) is the usual cause: lower the services' log level, or set
errors: false`. Both runs gave `494ccd9e15bdace4` (`ctl` `8e3203c3bbd73cba`), and the diagnosis
line has the verdict's words. With the 0.5.0 engine the same run waited 900.2 s and ended
`TIMEOUT check`, with the same fingerprint and `ctl`.

### Meilisearch: aimed reactions, `acked_outcome`, the notes, and the vacuous passes

The Meilisearch example built at epoch 6 with this tree is `3994a902…` on hvx, with the client
`mlc` built on this Mac (`a6138b92…`).

- `disk=none | run`: OK, 159 of 159 commands succeeded, and `queue.acked-outcome` held over 173
  acknowledged tasks, twice with `88a4e3f64fe74822`. `result.json` has no warning that the run
  checked nothing, although `no-phantom` judged 0 deliveries (Milestone 350).
- `disk=none | run A=meili.swap_acked#40:kill-meilisearch`: OK with the warning `its event
  meili.swap_acked came 16 times after it was armed from the start of the workload, and it acts
  at record 40 of the event; the run did not test it`. It gave the clean run's fingerprint, with
  another `ctl`, twice.
- `disk=none | run A=meili.add_acked@10+20:powerloss-meilisearch`: `VIOLATION [tasks]`,
  twice with `54a210d05c581415`. The claim reads `add.32 (system id 43) was acknowledged and
  ended failed with internal, not an error the client causes`, with the new error line `Failure
  to delete the content files associated with task #. Error: No such file or directory`. That is
  the example's finding 2, a payload lost at a power cut, here from one service's power loss.
  `one.log` has 10 `HYDO-CMD-OUT` notes, such as `mlc: POST /indexes: no answer: ... connect:
  connection refused`.

The aimed grid of Milestone 345 at the index deletion, `--reactive-at meili.delete_index_acked
--react-actions kill-now,kill`, ran in parts on one worker:

- `--react-delays 0..50`, the default range: 102 schedules in 330 s, none failed. On KVM the
  failing cells lay between 1 and 8 ms (Milestone 352).
- `--react-delays 51..200`: 300 schedules in 1,194 s, 14 failed, and each failed again with its
  own fingerprint. `kill-meilisearch` 112 to 116 ms after the deletion's acknowledgement runs the
  deletion twice. The claim reads `delidx.4 (system id 15) was acknowledged and ended failed with
  index_not_found, but its effect is there`, KVM's form at 6 and 8 ms. `kill-now-meilisearch` at
  192 to 200 ms runs the creation of `x4` twice instead: `mkidx.4 (system id 13) ... ended failed
  with index_already_exists`.
  A third part, `--react-delays 201..260 --react-actions kill-now` with `--no-shrink`, failed
  all 60 cells the same way, and each failed again with its own fingerprint.

`hydo run` of `disk=none dseed=0 | run A=meili.delete_index_acked+112:kill-meilisearch` gave
`VIOLATION [tasks]` twice with `c9327412a6f0befe`, the explorer's value. Its `one.log` has 10
`HYDO-CMD-OUT` notes. `hydo inspect diagnose <run> --evidence` wrote `logs/meilisearch.log` and
four command logs: `command.parallel_driver_add.log`, `command.parallel_driver_delidx.log`,
`command.parallel_driver_snap.log` and `command.parallel_driver_swap.log`.

No first run of these grids counts as a vacuous pass: `vacuous_passes` is absent from every
summary. Before Milestone 350, 94 of KVM's 102 such runs did (Milestone 352). Every reaction of
the grids fired.

The refusals of Milestones 345 and 348 stopped with the exit status 5 before any VM, each with
its JSON line under `--json`. They were `--block-faults` (hvx's disk is in its module),
`--cluster-faults`, `--upgrades`, `--protocol-faults`, `--react-delays` and `--react-actions`
without `--reactive-at`, and `--react-actions kill-nobody`. `--reactive-at` with `--kill-now
--reactive fault` stopped first for the missing `--react-events`, and with `--react-events` for
its own reason: the grid and the random reactions do not go together. `--strategy process
--new-faults` warned and ran its seed.

  power loss came at another moment.
- **The aimed grid at the index deletion** (`0..50` ms, `kill-now,kill`) ran in 761 s and 821 s.
  7 of 102 first runs failed, each again with its own fingerprint: `kill-now-meilisearch` 4 to 8
  ms and `kill-meilisearch` 10 and 11 ms after the deletion's acknowledgement. Each ran the
  creation of `x4` twice (`mkidx.4 ... ended failed with index_already_exists`). The deletion's
  own effect, which M352 found at 6 and 8 ms on an image built at epoch 5, did not come. The
  explorer shrank seed 9 to itself, `disk=none dseed=0 | run
  A=meili.delete_index_acked+4:kill-now-meilisearch`, and `hydo run` gave `2a7b8c891134964d`
  twice. `hydo inspect diagnose --evidence` wrote four command logs. No passing first run of the
  95 counts as a vacuous pass, where M352 counted 94 of 102.

### What did not run, and what is left

- No Intel host ran the Meilisearch part, and no AMD host ran `durable: true` with the same
  `s3probe` as an Intel host.
- A window after an event sits at other delays on each engine (open item 173). On hvx the
  default delays of `--reactive-at`, 0 to 50 ms, missed the deletion's window, which starts at
  112 ms. On KVM the epoch-6 image showed only the creation that runs twice.
- The saved Meilisearch regressions (`+13` and `+14`) did not run on hvx.
- Open item 182 has what is left of the fix.

The commit with the fix is `192af3fc`; the branch `tmp-m358-kvm` adds the workflow on
`d1931461`. Open items 116, 173, 174, 176 and 180 are updated, and open item 182 is new.

## Milestone 359 (tentative number): a new user's trial of 0.6.0's features on NSQ

Status: done on 2026-11-25 on the Mac engine. Nothing recorded moved, and nothing was posted.
A tester who had not used hydo tried the features new since 0.5.0 from the guide alone, on NSQ
v1.3.0 with `--mem-queue-size=0`. The hydo was the release build of `main` at `d1931461`.
The page is `docs/design/0.6.0-user-trial.md`: per feature what was done, the time, what
worked, each friction with its exact message, a verdict, and the frictions ranked.

The features were `hydo onboard` from a Compose file, the write and clock scans, a messages check
with `acked_outcome` and `effect: recorded`, `--reactive-at`, `hydo stats` and `hydo report` of
two rounds, `powerloss-<svc>` from a reaction, and `hydo save` with `hydo repro --regressions`
and `# params:`. The s3 emulator did not apply, because NSQ uses no object store.

The three frictions that cost most:

1. A messages check ended in `ERROR check jobs.no-loss could not be evaluated: no group that had
   to receive the acknowledged messages has a drained record`, although the drain had written its
   `drained` record. It happened when every acknowledged message had been received once.
2. `no-loss` with `acknowledgement: explicit` does not judge a message that a consumer received,
   never acknowledged, and that never came back. Only the tester's read-back for
   `acked_outcome` caught such a loss.
3. `hydo save` wrote no `# params:` line for an exploration of an image built with `--set`, and
   kept no file for findings whose names matched an earlier file (`exists, kept`).

The trial found three candidates in NSQ, each replayed with its fingerprint. A kill of `nsqd`
loses the messages of a topic before its queue's first metadata sync, because go-diskqueue
v1.1.0 starts an empty queue when the metadata file is missing. A kill loses a message that a
consumer holds in flight. After a step back of the wall clock, every publish to an existing topic
waits until the clock passes the last message id's time (`nsqd/guid.go`, `nsqd/topic.go`).

## Milestone 360 (tentative number): the frictions of the 0.6.0 trial

Status: done on 2026-11-25, on the Mac engine with the trial's NSQ project and in the tests.
The trial of Milestone 359 (`docs/design/0.6.0-user-trial.md`) ranked what a new user met. Each
fix below is its own commit, in the order of that ranking, and each says what it changed for the
user. Nothing recorded moved: every change is in the host's checks, reports and commands, and the
fingerprint epoch stays 6. The proof project is a copy of the trial's `hydo/` folder of NSQ
v1.3.0, built with this tree's `hydo`. That `hydo` was a build in a target folder outside the
checkout with `HYDO_RELEASE_DIR=~/.hydo`, which is also the proof of fix 7.

**1. A messages check's ERROR names the real cause.** The trial's ERROR said `no group that had
to receive the acknowledged messages has a drained record`, while the drain had written
`drained jobs work`. The cause was the rule of the groups that must receive a message. A named
group had to receive only the messages sent after its first completed `sub` or `recv`. The trial's
client records no `sub`, and its consumer's first `recv` waits for the first message, so the group
joined after every message sent before that receive. In a run whose messages were all sent early,
no group had to receive any of them, and the claim had nothing to judge.

Two changes. First, a group that received a message now has to receive it, because the delivery
proves that the group gets it (`index::must_groups`). Second, when no acknowledged message can be
judged, the ERROR names one of three causes (`claims::no_drained_group`): no drained record, drained
records of other channels only, or drained groups that received none of the messages sent before
they joined. The third names the record to write, `sub <channel> <group> from=start`. A held
`no-loss` also counts the acknowledged messages it did not judge, with the reason: the trial's
clean run read `20 judged` for 24 sends without a word.

On the Mac engine the trial's clean run `disk=none | run` judged 24 of 24 sends in `no-loss`. The
trial's aimed schedule `disk=none dseed=0 | run A=nsq.msg_received:kill-nsqd` sends `m0` to `m3`
before the consumer's first receive completes, and the consumer receives only `m0`. Before, no
group had to receive any of them, which is the ERROR that stopped 5 of the trial's 36 aimed runs.
Now `no-loss` held with `1 judged, 1 undecided` and the words `3 acknowledged message(s) not
judged: sent before any group of the channel joined, and received by none`. Both runs gave the
fingerprints that they gave before the change (`f14563fde5c29fc3` and `28aea04d29d339c3`). The
test `messages::a_group_that_received_a_message_had_to_receive_it` holds the trial's history
shape and each of the ERROR's forms.

**2. `no-loss` with a lease judges a received message that never came back.** With explicit
acknowledgements, `no-loss` counted any delivered message as delivered, and `lease` judges only a
delivery that comes again too early. So the trial's in-flight loss passed both claims. `hydo guide
messages` says that an unacknowledged message comes back when its lease or visibility timeout runs
out, and a `lease` is the declaration of that promise. So `no-loss` judges it when the check
declares a `lease`. A message whose deliveries in a drained group no acknowledgement accepted (an
`ok` ack, or a reject) and that was not delivered again is lost when the drain's record comes after
the last delivery's lease ended. The delivery and the record must be in the same boot, with no
clock step between. Before the lease's end, across a power cut, across a clock step, and with an
acknowledgement whose outcome is unknown (`info`, which may have been accepted), the message is
undecided. Without a lease the claim stays as it was, and `processing: once` judges such a
message (it already did). The declaration did not change, so no shared case of
`sdk/cases/history/messages` changed, and the SDKs keep their tests.

The trial's client records its `FIN` to a killed `nsqd` as `info`, because the error does not say
whether the server read it. So in the run above `m0` is undecided, not lost, and `acked_outcome`
stays the claim that breaks there. The test names the four outcomes: lost after the lease,
undecided before its end, undecided with an `info` acknowledgement, and held without a lease.

**3. `hydo save` writes the image's build parameters and keeps every finding.** A file was named by
the class and the start of the verdict, and the first file of a name was kept: a second finding
with one check got no file, and only `exists, kept` said so. Now a finding whose name is taken by
another finding gets the next free name, `<name>-2.schedule`. A file that holds the same schedule
and the same `# params:` words is kept, so a second save of one exploration writes nothing. When the
exploration's image was built with values other than the defaults of its manifest's `params:`
(the image's `/etc/hydo/params` against its `/etc/hydo/hydo.yaml`), each file gets a `# params:
name=value` line with those values, after its first line. An image built again since the
exploration (another sha256) gives a warning instead, and an image that is gone gives no line.

On the Mac engine the aimed round `hydo explore --reactive-at nsq.msg_received@2 --react-delays
0..500/500 --react-actions kill,powerloss --seeds 1-12 --workers 3` had three shrunk failures of
one file name. `hydo save` into the proof's `regressions/`, which held the trial's files, printed
`... -di.schedule holds this finding already, kept` (the trial had saved that schedule), wrote
`-di-2.schedule` and `-di-3.schedule`, and ended `2 regressions saved, 1 kept`. A second save wrote
nothing (`3 kept`). Then `hydo build --set memq=10000` replaced the image, and a save
of the same round printed the warning `... was built again since the exploration`. With the round's
`exploration.json` given the new image's sha256 (so that the round reads as an exploration of the
`memq=10000` image; no VM ran for it), `hydo save` wrote each file with `# params: memq=10000`
on its second line and ended `3 regressions saved with # params: memq=10000 (the image's build
parameters)`. The unit test
`runs::tests::save_keeps_every_finding_and_names_the_build_parameters` covers the names and the
values. The golden answers of the second `hydo save` in `tests/golden/cli.jsonl` moved for the new
words (re-recorded with `HYDO_BLESS=1`).

**4. A problem's command, steps and title come from one schedule.** Since Milestone 328 a failure
of the safe settings has a class of its fault families (`process`), and the explorer shrinks one
failure per class group (`advice::shrink_group`) and signature. The exploration's story found a
problem's minimal schedule by the class group, but decided whether the problem was shrunk by the
shrink's own class. So a problem of the class `process` showed its whole failing run as "See it
again" and as its steps, beside a title made from its minimal schedule. Both now use the class
group. The aimed round's problem shows `See it again: hydo run "disk=none dseed=0 | run
A=nsq.msg_received:kill-nsqd"`, its minimal schedule. The test
`htmlreport::tests::a_process_problem_shows_its_minimal_schedule` fails without the fix.

The trial's second case was the merged problem whose title named a power loss that the tester did
not find in its command. Its minimal schedule, which the trial saved, ends `... W=:p1,r100,...
L=nsqd@1+1`: the power loss is there, after the long composition word, and the steps and the title
were true. Nothing changed for it.

**5. The property table counts the long violation records.** The table reads each `HYDO-ASSERT`
line up to 1,023 bytes, the line of the C header it was ported from. hydo's own records of history
and messages checks have sorted keys, so `details` comes first, and a violation's long details cut
`id`, `ok` and `t` off. The table dropped such a record: it counted the claims that held and few
of those that broke. A record longer than the line is now written again with `details` last
before the cut (`results::long_record`), and a shorter line is read as before. In the aimed round
the table reads `jobs.acked-outcome 4 8 FAIL`, and 8 of its 12 first runs failed that claim; the
trial's table had read `19 4 FAIL` beside 15 failing runs.

**6. `hydo stats` of two folders, and a reaction's power loss.** `hydo stats A B` printed B alone.
It now refuses two folders with one line: `hydo stats: one exploration at a time, and
hydo-out/aimed and hydo-out/clean are two: run hydo stats on each ...`, with `hydo explore
--merge` for the shards of one exploration and `hydo report A B` for their problems. The faults
drawn counted the reaction `powerloss-<svc>` as a reaction not in `faults:`, and the same page then
said that power losses of one service were never drawn. Such a reaction now counts as a power
loss of that service at its event's step (`stats::faults_of`). `hydo stats hydo-out/aimed` reads
`power losses of one service: 4 of 12 runs; on nsqd 4` and `crashes: 8 of 12 runs`, and power
losses are not among the kinds that were never drawn.

**7. A build in a target folder outside the checkout knows its checkout.** `ctx::checkout_of` looked
for `<checkout>/target/` among the program's folders, so a build with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` elsewhere
was no checkout build, ignored `HYDO_RELEASE_DIR`, and found no guest files (open item 179). Cargo
marks every target folder with a `CACHEDIR.TAG` file. A program inside such a folder is now the
build of the checkout of the crate's source path that cargo gave the build, when that folder is a
hydo checkout (`ctx::checkout_of_built`). A copy of the program in a prefix or a release keeps its
own root. The tests `onboard::the_fetch_step_names_the_release_fetcher_when_it_is_not_on_path` and
`update::a_checkout_build_is_left_alone_with_the_commands` pass with this milestone's target folder
outside the checkout, and every proof above used such a build.

**8. `hydo ci run` reports a regression of other build parameters as left out.** `hydo ci run`
replays the saved regressions with the code of `hydo repro --regressions`, so a regression whose
`# params:` names other values than the image's did not run. But it was counted as replayed and as
expected, and `junit.xml` showed it as a passing test. Now the counts leave it out, `report.md`
says `N of M as expected, K left out: they need other build parameters` and names each with the
build it needs, and `junit.xml` has it as a skipped test (`runs::left_out`). `hydo explore` replays
no saved regression: the explorer reads the regressions only for the saved compositions of
`W=@<key>`, so it has nothing of `# params:` to honour. The test
`ci::report::tests::a_regression_of_other_build_parameters_is_left_out` covers the report and
`junit.xml`.

**9. `hydo explore --reactive` draws a power loss of one service.** A quarter of the fault
reactions that `--kill-now` does not take are now `powerloss-<svc>` of a service with `storage:`,
when `faults:` allows `powerloss` and the schedule has no `cf=`. The choice comes from a stream of
its own (`gen::POWERLOSS_SALT`), and nothing is drawn from it for a manifest without such a service,
so such an exploration draws the schedules it drew before; the reactive stream's golden did not
move. On the Meilisearch example's space, 156 of 613 fault reactions of seeds 1-1000 took the
service's power, and every other part of each schedule stayed as it was
(`reactive::a_fault_reaction_can_take_one_service_s_power`).

**What is left.** The smaller frictions of the trial's section 9 are not fixed: the import's unused
`data.dirs` and its placeholder against the first service, the clock scan's `<database>` for a
known service, the Go SDK's missing call for `drained`, `hydo inspect diagnose --text` that prints
JSON, and the title `Nsq` for NSQ. Open item 183 lists them with what else is left.

## Milestone 361 (tentative number): the equivalence corpora pass on every machine

The two equivalence tests compare the validator and the builder with recorded answers. They are
`hydo-manifest`'s `equivalence::same_as_hydo_build` and `hydo-build`'s
`equivalence::print_and_check_outputs_match_hydo_build`. Each answer comes from a repository
manifest, a fixture case, or a mutant. A mutant is a repository manifest with one or two seeded
edits. Since Milestone 239 the tests failed (open items 115 and 165). On `main` at `4f988c40`
they failed on 58 and 57 answers on this Mac. Their answers also depended on the machine, on the
checkout, and on where the test program was built. This milestone finds every cause, makes the
tests independent of the host, and records the answers again. No product code changed: every
change is in the three test programs and their goldens.

**The 58 and 57 mismatches.** Each Rust message that lists known keys was checked against its
recorded digest. The script took the keys out of the list one set at a time and hashed the
message again. A message whose digest then matched the recording differs only in its list of
known keys:

- `hydo-build`: 39 answers lack `exact_tick` and `path` among the `guest:` keys (21), `if_header`
  of a fake's route (6), `errors` and `if_header` of a proxy's route (6), and `error_paths` of a
  `contracts:` entry (6).
- `hydo-manifest`: 32 answers lack `path` (18), `if_header` (8), `durable` of an emulator entry
  (4), and `errors` and `if_header` (2).

The other 18 and 26 answers belong to mutants of `hydo/onboard/examples/meilisearch/hydo/hydo.yaml`,
which Milestone 346 changed. The tests make the mutants from the files as they are now, so after
an edit a mutant is another manifest than the recorded one, under the same name. With the folder
`hydo/` of Meilisearch checked out from before Milestone 346, the counts were 39 and 32, every one
a list of known keys. So no mismatch was a real difference between the two code paths, and no
code was fixed.

**Why the count changed between runs (open item 165).** On 2026-11-23 one run of the merge of
Milestone 346 counted 57 and the next run 39. The test reads the checkout that its program was
built from, and hydo-manifest's test also read `VERSION` from the checkout that holds the
program. The count is 57 with the Meilisearch folder after Milestone 346. It is 39 with the
folder before it. So the run that counted 39 read the Meilisearch folder of a checkout without the
merge, for example through a test program built in that checkout. The record of that day does
not name the program. Nothing inside the test varies: on this Mac each test passed three times
in a row with the same answers. Three more things made the answers depend on the place:

- A git-ignored file of the checkout. An image that `fetch-images.sh` saved turns the refusal
  `image ... does not exist` into an acceptance, and a binary that a build left beside an example
  removes a `root.files` warning. With an empty Dragonfly image file and two empty Blnk binaries
  in the checkout, the old hydo-manifest test counted 61 mismatches instead of 58.
- The host's own files. The `--check` warning about missing `root.files` sources counts the
  sources that exist. A Nix store path such as `/nix/store/svzgg47md9362vjrq5x9k1djln2pkihj-redis-7.2.4`
  exists on the bare-metal machine and not on the Mac. A `~/hydo/build/...` source exists in the
  bare-metal machine's home (open item 115).
- The pinned input digests of a folder plan covered the git-ignored files of its `hydo/` folder.
  The recorded digests of Blnk's and Vikunja's folders matched no tracked state of them.

**What changed.**

- Each of the two tests copies the repository's own files into the temporary directory and
  answers every request from that copy. The copy holds the files of `git ls-files --cached
  --others --exclude-standard`, with their modes and symbolic links, about 41 MB in 3,893 files.
  The copy is `<root>` in the answers, so a git-ignored file cannot reach an answer. The pinned
  digests are taken from the copy too.
- hydo-manifest's test passes the copy's `hydo/onboard` as `onboard_dir`, so the version comes
  from the copy's `hydo/VERSION`, wherever the program was built.
- The `root.files` warning is left out of the compared `--check` lines when a source of the
  manifest lies outside the copy and the scratch folder. Such a source is an absolute path, a
  `~/` path, or a relative path that leaves them. The warning of a manifest whose sources are
  all in the copy stays, for example Blnk's `../bin/...`. The function is `host_neutral` in both
  tests. The warning's own logic keeps its unit test,
  `the_check_names_missing_sources_of_root_files`.
- Each repository file's mutants have a seed of their own, from the digest of its pinned name,
  and are named by its place in the pinned list: `m<place>.<k>.json` and
  `mutant<place>.<k>.json`. An edit of one file now changes only its own mutants. A mismatch of a
  mutant names its file, and says when that file changed since the recording.
- The `hydo` program's `equivalence::cli_matches_golden` leaves the same warning out of some
  `hydo build --check` cases. Such a case's manifest names an absolute source, or a relative
  source that is no tracked file and lies outside the case's folder. A `~/` source stays,
  because each case has its own HOME. This was the last part of open item 115.

**The recorded answers that changed.** Both goldens were recorded again with `HYDO_BLESS=1`, and
each diff was checked against the old golden by request:

- `hydo-manifest/tests/golden/answers.txt`. Of the 1,798 requests that are no mutants and are in
  both goldens, 1,731 kept their answers. 59 changed only in the digest of their `--check` lines:
  the 30 manifests with sources outside the repository, on both architectures where they load.
  8 changed in the list of known keys (the fixture cases `v-guest-15`, `v-guest-unknown`,
  `w-fake-31` and `w-proxy-7`). 107 requests are new, from the 41 files tracked since the last
  full recording (the Prometheus, GreptimeDB, Pulsar and other examples). 23 read-backs of the
  image path kept their answers under a new name, because their name holds the request's
  index. All 10,411 mutant lines are new, from the new seeds.
- `hydo-build/tests/golden/answers.txt`. Of the 5,422 requests that are no mutants, 5,340 kept
  their answers. 58 `--check` runs changed only in stdout: the warning of a manifest with
  outside sources is left out. 24 changed in the list of known keys (fixture cases 299, 315, 367
  and 378, each on both architectures and with three flags). 328 requests are new, from the
  newly tracked files. All 7,440 mutant lines are new.
- `hydo-cli/tests/golden/cli.jsonl`. Three answers lost the warning line: `build
  examples/shop/hydo.yaml --check` (its source `../../../../build/shop-fixed` is a git-ignored
  folder of the checkout), `build examples/stack/hydo.yaml --check` (a Nix store path), and the
  Mac's `build examples-mac/redis/hydo.yaml --check` (29 Nix store paths).

**Proofs.** On this Mac with a private target folder:

- hydo-manifest's and hydo-build's tests passed twice in a row, and a third time with the empty
  Dragonfly image, two empty Blnk binaries and `build/shop-fixed` placed in the checkout.
- Before the change, the copy alone gave the same 58 and 57 mismatches as the plain test. The
  filter alone changed only the answers that this section names.
- `cargo test -p hydo --test it equivalence::cli_matches_golden` failed on exactly the three
  answers of `cli.jsonl` in the list of changes before the new recording, and passed after it.

On the bare-metal machine, in its own folder `~/hydo-m361` with its own target folder, the tree
of this milestone ran without a VM. That machine's `/nix/store` holds 4 entries of
`redis-7.2.4`. Both tests passed twice in a row (183 s and 165 s each), and
`equivalence::cli_matches_golden` passed once, with the goldens recorded on the Mac.

**What is left.** Open items 115 and 165 are closed; open item 165 keeps its other entries. The
read-backs of the image path still carry the request's index in their name, so a new pinned file
renames the later ones in the next recording. Their answers do not change.

## Milestone 362 (tentative number): NSQ, a kill of `nsqd` in a new queue's first seconds

The NSQ project of the 0.6.0 user trial (Milestone 359) became the example
`hydo/onboard/examples/nsq` (RESULTS.md), by `docs/ONBOARDING-PLAYBOOK.md`, with the published
hydo 0.6.0 on the Mac engine. Of the trial's three candidates, one is new and two are known.
Nothing was posted, and nothing recorded moved.

**The example.** One `nsqd` and one `nsqlookupd` of NSQ v1.3.0 from the official image, as nsq.io's
Docker page runs them, with `--mem-queue-size=0`, the setting that NSQ's guarantees page names
for writing every incoming message to disk. `nsqd`'s data path is a file system of its own;
`--mem-queue-size` and `--sync-every` are the build parameters `memq` and `sync_every`. The trial's
Go client `nsqc` speaks the HTTP API and the TCP protocol itself and records each publish,
receipt and `FIN` with the Go SDK's `hydohist`. Its drain records the channel's group as
`sub jobs work from=start`, because `nsqd` hands a topic's earlier messages to its first channel.
Without it, `no-loss` judged none of the messages that finding 1 lost, since they were sent before
any receive (open item 183). A `first_` command's records did not do it: they stay in
provisioning, before the snapshot that each run starts from. The check is the trial's messages check: `delivery: at-least-once`, a
`lease` of 60 s, and `acked_outcome` with `effect: recorded`, where the effect is a consumer's
`FIN`. `eventually_publish` checks that a publish works after the faults.

**Finding 1, new.** A kill of `nsqd` in the first seconds of a new topic or channel loses every
message of it. go-diskqueue v1.1.0 writes a queue's `.diskqueue.meta.dat` only at its first
sync, after 2,500 messages or at a tick of 2 s once there was activity (`diskqueue.go` lines 433,
503, 656 and 697 to 702). `New` ignores the missing file (lines 131 and 132), so the restarted
queue starts empty at file 0, position 0, although the data file holds the messages, and
`writeOne` writes the next message over the first one (lines 388 to 405). The check of
out-of-sync metadata from go-diskqueue#31 runs only when the file exists. `hydo inspect` right
after the restart showed `jobs.diskqueue.000000.dat` with `m0` to `m5` and no metadata file. The
regressions are the trial's blind `K=nsqd@4+1 W=...` and the aimed `A=nsq.msg_received:kill-nsqd`,
where neither the topic's nor the channel's queue had its metadata. A kill 2.8 s after the first
publish and the same kill with `--sync-every=1` lost nothing. A power cut can lose the first
metadata file after its sync too: `persistMetaData` renames a synced temporary file into place
and syncs no directory (lines 524 to 528). The blind `disk=cut dseed=0 | run C=20 W=...` published
one message about 3 s before the cut; the last stop before the cut had the metadata file, and the
recovery boot had only the data file and `jobs.diskqueue.meta.dat.<n>.tmp`, so the message was
lost although its data file had been synced. NSQ's `master` (`85cf10c0`) still
requires go-diskqueue v1.1.0, and go-diskqueue's `master` (`ff2a02e5`) has the same code. No issue
names a missing metadata file at a start. The draft report waits for the lead.

**Finding 2, known (nsqio/nsq#1386).** A kill 2.2 s after a consumer took a message, before its
`FIN`, loses that message: it is in flight only in memory, and the channel queue's sync has
written the read position past it (`3`, `0,32`, `0,128`). A clean exit writes in-flight messages
back (`Channel.flush`, `nsqd/channel.go` lines 214 to 250). A maintainer confirmed it in #1386 and
#1142, and the guarantees page says that delivery at least once assumes that `nsqd` does not fail.
The trial took its aimed schedule `A=nsq.msg_received:kill-nsqd` for this finding. That kill comes
before either queue's first sync, so it shows finding 1: 4 of 4 messages lost at `+0` and at
`+1000`, and only the one in flight at `+2200`.

**Finding 3, known (nsqio/nsq#1124), a clock effect.** After a backward step of the wall clock
every publish to a topic that had a message waits until the clock passes the last id's time:
`NewGUID` returns `ErrTimeBackwards` (`nsqd/guid.go` line 57), and `Topic.GenerateID`
(`nsqd/topic.go` lines 491 to 503) tries again every millisecond. #1124 is open with the label
`bug`; #1249, a change to ids without the clock, was closed unmerged.

**The runs.** The final image `explore-ob-nsq-arm64.cpio.gz` (`4fe61962…`) gives
`d29eb914ebcefac1` on two clean runs. Each regression gave one fingerprint over two fresh runs,
and `hydo repro --regressions` gave 5 of 5 as expected with the same values: finding 1
`d39f53f08499f0e1`, `2b20291d317536f9` and, after the power cut, `501a3f509a3aca0f`, finding 2
`cc4f5ae54b811cdc`, and finding 3 `b5b2092116480f0d`. RESULTS.md has the separating runs and their fingerprints.

**The exploration.** `hydo explore --seeds 1-20 --strategy process` of the final image ran on 3
workers in 713 s. 14 of 20 schedules failed: 6 power cuts (finding 1, seed 1 shrunk to `C=20`
alone), 3 kills of `nsqd` (finding 1), and 5 backward clock steps (finding 3, shrunk to
`T=7:-1265`). Kills of `nsqd` after the queues' first syncs, pauses, network faults and steps
back before the topic's first message passed. A first version of the client recorded a `FIN`
without an answer within 5 s as no final state, and a pause of `nsqd` then failed
`acked-outcome` although `nsqd` took the `FIN` after the pause (seed 13): a mistake of the rules.
The client now leaves such a message out of the read-back unless a consumer finished it later,
and the pause passes.

**Tests.** The new example enters the explorer's and the controller's corpora. Re-recorded with
`HYDO_BLESS=1`: the explorer's corpus goldens (full and quick), its identity goldens (quick and
full), and the controller's quick corpus golden, which adds the example's entries only. With a
target folder of this task's own: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo test -p hydo-explore --test
it` (61 passed), `-p hydo-agents --test it public_content::`, `-p hydo --test it -- docs::
equivalence::cli_matches_golden` (15 passed), the controller's corpus tests, `sh ci/vale.sh`
and the voice lint of the draft pass. No Rust code changed.
